2856.t:
In 1970, Yogiji Mahārāj was touring in Africa. In Kenya, the milk from the dairy used to come in a thick paper packet. One day during {!kathā!}, the topic of milk was being discussed. Swāmishri [Yogiji Mahārāj] asked, “How is milk packaged in a paper container? Show me.”
Bhaskarbhāi brought a packet of milk to show Swāmishri. Seeing the packet, Swāmishri inquired with curiosity, “Was the milk filtered before packaging? How does the milk come out of the packet?”
Bhaskarbhāi cut one corner of the packet and a stream of milk came out.
In a childlike manner, Swāmishri said, “Yes! What would have happened if I had not seen this? I have come to Africa twice but never saw this.”
Then, Swāmishri said, “Read {!prathamnu triju!} [Gadhadā I 3] on remembering the divine actions and incidents of God.” He then said, “The packet was held and it was cut… all this should be remembered.”
[Y.M. : 6/36]

4417.t:
On Māgshar sud 14, Samvat 1876, about four-and-a-half hours after sunset, Shriji Mahārāj was resting on a cot in the courtyard of His quarters in Gadhadā. Muktānand Swāmi started singing {!kirtans!} in the {!bihāg!} tune while playing the {!sarodā!}. About 10 or 12 {!pārshads!} were sleeping near Mahārāj. They said, “Brahmānand Swāmi is singing. Muktānand Swāmi’s voice is soft whereas Brahmānand Swāmi’s voice is loud.”
Shriji Mahārāj requested Devji Bhakta of Pachcham to see who was singing. After going to the sādhus’ residence and asking from the doorway, Devji Bhakta said that Brahmānand Swāmi is singing. Shriji Mahārāj said, “Let go verify whether Brahmānand Swāmi is indeed singing.”
Using the pretext of verifying who is singing, Shriji Mahārāj went to give {!darshan!} to Muktānand Swāmi. Other {!munis!} were sleeping while only Muktānand Swāmi was engaged in singing affectionately along with Sadguru Ādhārānand Swāmi. Having realized Shriji Mahārāj arrived, both stood up and placed a cot with cushions in the courtyard where Shriji Mahārāj sat down and said, “We came to check who is singing.” All the other sādhus said, “Muktānand Sami sings daily as according to his {!niyam!}.” Shriji Mahārāj replied, “I have a great liking for singing {!kirtans!} and I never get tired of listening to {!kirtans!}. I have the same eagerness to listen to discourses.”
From henceforth, the dialog of the first Vachanāmrut of Gadhadā I 1 starts.
[H.C.S. : 21/1]

4458.t:
In Gadhadā I 1, Muktānand Swāmi asks the question, “What type of body does a devotee of God attain when he leaves his physical body, which is composed of the five {!bhuts!}, and goes to the abode of God?”
Shriji Mahārāj answers, “… By the wish of God, a devotee attains a divine body composed of Brahma… this is how they reach the abode of God…”
One would wonder why Muktānand Swāmi, an astute {!sādhu!}, asks a question about leaving the physical body when Shriji Mahārāj visits him in the middle of the night – a question that does not relate to the previous questions (about constant contemplation on God’s form and the form of {!māyā!}). 
Muktānand Swāmi’s question may seem unrelated to the previous questions but it is related to the event of that time. The incident surrounding this Vachanāmrut is as follows:
Hirābā (Dādā Khāchar’s sister Pānchubā’s daughter) became seriously ill, causing everyone sorrow. When Mahārāj heard the news, He visited Pānchubā’s quarter and consoled them, saying, “Hirābā was a {!Brāhmin!} during her past life, whose house I visited during my {!van-vicharan!}. She served me intensely; hence, the fruit of that service is her birth in Satsang in your family. She had a desire to obtain the bliss of my {!murti!}. That wish has been fulfilled so she will now go to {!dhām!}. No one needs to grieve.”
Saying this, Mahārāj retired to the Akshar Ordi and Hirābā immediately went to {!dhām!}. Everyone in Dādā Khāchar’s {!darbār!} began weeping. When Mahārāj heard the weeping, He asked [Mulji] Brahmachāri, “Who is crying?” Brahmachāri replied, “Pānchubā’s daughter Hirābā went to {!dhām!} so they are crying.”
Mahārāj said, “I have placed her in my Akshardhām, so in such a joyous moment should one cry or rejoice?” So saying, Mahārāj became disheartened.
[B.S. : 4/177]
From this narrative, it becomes clear that the clouds of mourning that were cast in Dādā Khāchar’s {!darbār!} were due to Hirābā’s passing away to Akshardhām. Muktānand Swāmi must have also felt some remorse. Therefore, with the intent to console Dādā Khāchar’s family in any way, Muktānand Swāmi must have asked about what happens to a {!satsangi!} devotee after he passes away: “What type of body does a devotee of God attain when he leaves his physical body, which is composed of the five {!bhuts!}, and goes to the abode of God?” Muktānand Swāmi’s intent is for Dādā Khāchar’s family to hear from Shriji Mahārāj Himself that Hirābā’s passing away is fortunate as she is in Akshardhām with a divine body.

4459.t:
Immediately after Muktānand Swāmi’s question, Harji Thakkar asks Shriji Mahārāj, “Some have been practising {!satsang!} for quite some time, yet they do not harbour the same profound love for the Satsang fellowship as they do for their own body and relatives. What is the reason for this?”
It is worthwhile to understand the background to Harji Thakkar’s question. As noted above, everyone in Dādā Khāchar’s family were mournful of Hirābā’s death. During this time, Mulji Brahmachāri went to get Mahārāj’s {!thāl!} from the {!darbār!} as was the usual routine. The {!thāl!} was covered with a cloth so Mulji Brahmachāri didn’t realize it simply contained {!bhadku!} (a type of porridge made from dried grains). However, when he placed it in front of Mahārāj and removed the cloth, Mahārāj asked in surprise, “Brahmachāri, what is this?” Brahmachāri was bewildered. But recalling Hirābā’s death, He said, “Since everyone in the {!darbār!} is still in mourning, they sent {!bhadku!} today as may be their practice during mourning.”
Amusingly, Mahārāj asked, “How long will this last?” Brahmachāri replied, “13 to 14 days at least.” The mourning led to a lapse in serving Mahārāj! Harji Thakkar seems to be aware of this incident since he lived in Gadhadā. Naturally, this question must have arose in his mind since Shriji Mahārāj has been residing in Gadhadā from around Samvat 1860 or 1861 till this point – a span of 16 years. Therefore, Harji Thakkar uses the words, “some have been practicing satsang for quite some time…”, implying a great duration of time when asking: “What is the reason for not harbouring the same profound love for Bhagwān as one does for their own body and relatives?”
[B.S. : 4/177]

4522.t: At 8 am on December 10, 1967, Yogiji Mahārāj was discoursing on Gadhadā I-3. During the discourse, Arjunbhāi came with a bugle. Seeing the bugle, he said, “Play it.” He had the bugle played twice. Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Remember this incident.”\r\n[Y.M. : 4/584]

4527.t:
6 January 1964, Mumbai.
Explaining Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 5 during the morning discourse in Akshar Bhavan, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Meditate on Shri Krishna Bhagwān together with Radhika. Is the concept of [worshipping] the choicest devotee not included here? The whole Satsang reads about this. Nobody asked [at the time], ‘Who is Mahārāj’s ideal devotee?’ If they did ask, then Mahārāj would have shown them. If one could not understand Mahārāj to be supreme, then how would they have been able to accept this concept of his choicest devotee? It is due to the merits from our past lives that we have been able to understand this.
“When {!ghee!} and honey are added to a banana, its taste is enhanced. When such a taste is experienced, one’s own eyes freeze with delight. Has Gunātit changed? He is definitely present. Mahārāj and Swāmi are always present. Akshar is Gunātit. Mahārāj resides within him.”
[Y.M. : 3/568]

4529.t:
11 December 1968, Mumbai.
At 4.15pm, Yogiji Mahārāj was participating in a question-answer session with youths during their Saturday assembly, which was taking place on the first floor of Akshar Bhavan in Mumbai. In answer to a question, he said, “Mahārāj has said in Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 5, ‘One should meditate on Shri Krishna Bhagwān together with Radhika. ‘{!Ārādhitā iti Rādhā!}’. Here, Mahārāj has subtly mentioned that one should meditate upon Akshar along with Purushottam.
“When one wishes to show someone the moon in the sky, they would say, ‘Look at this house and above it you can see the moon.’ Hence, one first needs to fix the goal. Once this is done, why would we need to look at the house? The goal is the moon. Similarly, the talk here is of meditating on Mahārāj along with his choicest devotee.
“When a builder wishes to build an archway, he applies a mould [template] first and then commences construction on the archway [final product]. Once the archway is completed, the mould is removed. However, people become fixated on the mould [template] and forget the archway. Similarly, there is no liberation without developing firm conviction in Akshar and Purushottam. Bapa [Shāstriji Mahārāj] will not take one who lacks this faith to Akshardhām.”
[Y.M. : 5/308]

4533.t:
5 August 1963, Mumbai. 
On the day of Rakshabandhan, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “If one thinks about one’s own shortcomings, one will never think about the shortcomings of others. They would only [their] see virtues...”
“When harsh words are uttered and even if one has not made a mistake, this happens to prevent a mistake in the future. Appreciate that the {!Sant!} rebukes us in order to improve us and so that we do not make mistakes in the future. At the moment nobody rebukes us and everything seems fine. But if one who seems inferior to us or one who is elder to us rebukes us, then think of their virtues. If one retaliates then one will regret it.
“What is meant by harsh words? It means the harshest of the harsh. It would burn the attachments of anyone [who receives it]. Read Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 37. One would then understand that the person who rebuked us is in fact a well-wisher. I am not saying this, Mahārāj is. Even if harsh words are uttered and one does not feel sadness within, then he will rank first [spiritually]. One who feels bad ranks second. By not looking at the flaws within others, one experiences peace. Sitting on an elegant throne is not a measure of greatness.
“One who lacks wisdom and looks at the flaws of others may be in Satsang, but he regresses daily. One may read the Vachanāmrut, but if at the time he feels, ‘I understand that Vachanāmrut’, then this is the latent pride of one’s virtues. Become brave and remain as a servant of a servant and give up pride of one’s own virtues.”
[Y.M. : 3/515]

4535.t:
10 April 1970, Dar-es-Salaam, Tanzania.
During the afternoon discourse at 1pm, whilst carrying out a {!nirupan!} on Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 6, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “When one attains the company of God and the {!Sant!}, one must learn to look at everyone else’s virtues as well. Dattātreya saw the virtues of 24 gurus and so he was known to be wise. What virtues could the prostitute and others possess? Yet he took one virtue from each of them.
“Everyone has flaws, but if one imbibes good qualities from others and leaves everything else aside, then he is known to be wise. If one sees virtues only in oneself, then one cannot be called wise.
“What is greatness? Peace within the heart is greatness. Even if thousands of people bow their heads before one, that is not considered to be a sign of greatness. One who is truly great does not think ill of anyone. If one has attached oneself to the {!Sant!}, and the {!Sant!} rebukes one without reason, one lacking the above thought will take it the wrong way. However, we should feel the {!Sant!} is rebuking us to improve us. By thinking in this manner, one will progress.”
[Y.M. : 6/133]

4543.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “By remaining in the company of the {!Motāpurush!}, one’s affection for the body is removed and one attains the virtue of devotion with servitude. To behave with servitude is one of the divine virtues of God. When one attains this virtue, one becomes complete. One should contemplate on the words of Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 14. Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 7 was Shāstriji Mahārāj’s favourite Vachanāmrut. One should read such Vachanāmruts, contemplate on them and develop a strong resolve to imbibe their words. As a result, the {!Motāpurush!} becomes pleased on one.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 18/3]

4553.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “One should contemplate on the words of Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 14. Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 7 was Shāstriji Mahārāj’s favourite Vachanāmrut. One should read such Vachanāmruts, contemplate on them and develop a strong resolve to imbibe their words. As a result, the {!Motāpurush!} becomes pleased on one.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 18/3]

4555.t:
28 December 1961, Mumbai. 
Addressing the {!sādhus!} in the morning {!mangal!} discourse, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “One who has perfected Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 7 has perfected them all. The mind is the ruler of each and every individual – one should change this ‘{!guru’!} to the {!Sant!}. One can ensure that this birth is one’s last only through fighting against one’s mind. One should look down on the pleasures of this world with disdain and detachment in order to discern that there is no happiness in this world. We will ultimately experience misery if we do not do as God and the {!Sant!} wish. Conversely, if we do as they wish, then we experience eternal peace. One maintains a feeling of euphoria if God and the {!Sant!} look upon one gracefully.
“To serve is to enhance the reputation of the fellowship after completing one’s education. Krishnacharan Swāmi used to say to me, ‘Shāstriji Mahārāj will be your tutor.’ Shāstriji Mahārāj said to me, ‘You have kept Mahārāj and Swāmi [at the forefront] – {!brahmavidyā!} is encompassed within this.’ One should do as God and the {!Sant!} wish, without harbouring an inferiority complex. True service is that which is done in accordance with the wishes [of God and the {!Sant!}].”
[Y.M. : 3/266]

4564.t: 4 April 1959, Advāl.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj often used to have the Vachanāmruts Gadhadā I 15, Gadhadā I 16, Gadhadā I 17 read during the afternoon discourses after lunch. He would say, “Gadhadā I 17 – Do not utter discouraging words. Gadhadā I 16 – We should possess discretion. One who understands these three Vachanāmruts has nothing left to accomplish for his {!moksha!}. We should treasure these Vachanāmruts and aim to imbibe them.” \r\n[Y.M. : 2/536]

4573.t: Whilst discoursing on Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 9, Pramukh Swāmi Mahārāj said, “We cannot see the form of God that resides above [in Akshardhām] and we do not believe in the form of God that we see in front of us; how then can we be happy?”\r\n[Satsang Saurabh : 1/69]

4580.t: 10 July 1961, Mumbai. \r\nYogiji Mahārāj wrote an inspiring letter from Mumbai for the Swāminārāyan Prakāsh for the Satsang community. He wrote, “Become the servant of servants. The attributes of a true servant have been described in Gadhadā I 14 and Gadhadā II 62; one should read and think about this. Therefore, {!sādhus!} and devotees should keep the strength of Mahārāj and Swāmi, and perfect devotion with servitude.” \r\n[Y.M. : 3/206]

4582.t: 9 December 1961, Mumbai. \r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “Shāstriji Mahārāj often used to have these Vachanāmruts read in the afternoon: Gadhadā I 15, Gadhadā I 16, Gadhadā I 17, Gadhadā I 21, Gadhadā I 58. Sometimes, he would discourse on them for three hours.” \r\n[Y.M. : 3/252]

4589.t: 29 May 1965, Bochāsan.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj started to recite Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 16 by heart before saying, “One who perfects this one Vachanāmrut will never be swayed by negative influences in Satsang. Even if only a little knowledge is imbibed, it must be maintained throughout one’s life. This is the Vachanāmrut that needs to be understood. Not much else needs to be understood. Everyone should take this Vachanāmrut and imbibe it for themselves – not preach to others.”\r\n[Y.M. : 4/69]

4591.t:
21 November 1960, Gondal. 
At 6am in the Akshar Deri, explaining Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 16, Yogiji Mahārāj asked, “What is meant by discerning between {!sat!} [truth] and {!asat!} [untruth]?” 
He replied:
“1. Look at your own flaws and see the virtues in others. 
2. Understand the words of the {!Sant!} to be the highest truth. 
3. Rid oneself of negative thoughts and harbour positive thoughts. Thinking about the flaws of others is the definition of negative thoughts.”
[Y.M. : 3/133]

4736.t:
Once, Gopālānand Swāmi was discoursing on Gadhadā I-20 in Amdāvād. Sarvanivāsānand Swāmi heard Gopālānand Swāmi’s explanation and Swāmi’s words impacted him greatly. He decided: I want to do {!samāgam!} of Gopālānand Swāmi and eradicate all my shortcomings. When Gopālānand Swāmi was ready to return to Vadodarā, Sarvanivāsānand Swāmi also got ready to leave with him.
Sarvanivāsānand Swāmi was a gem among the {!sādhus!} in Amdāvād; therefore, Acharya Ayodhyāprasādji Mahārāj begged him to stay, “I’ll make you the {!mahant!} of Amdāvād, give you 20 pairs of Shriji Mahārāj’s footprints [{!charanārvind!}], give you attendants and a carriage; but do not leave Amdāvād.” However, Sarvanivāsānand Swāmi was not trapped in these temptations and left with Gopālānand Swāmi. He listened to Gopālānand Swāmi’s talks and became enlightened like him. After Gopālānand Swāmi reverted back to Akshardhām, the devotees who had affection for Gopālānand Swāmi felt as if he was still present through Sarvanivāsānand Swāmi.
Having observed Sarvanivāsānand Swāmi’s tale, Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “And what is bondage to the world? Sarvanivāsānand Swāmi overcame an infinite times more bondage and associated with a great {!Sādhu!}.”
[S.V. : 2/109]

4860.t: 9 December 1961, Mumbai. \r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “Shāstriji Mahārāj often used to have these Vachanāmruts read in the afternoon: Gadhadā I 15, Gadhadā I 16, Gadhadā I 17, Gadhadā I 21, Gadhadā I 58. Sometimes, he would discourse on them for three hours.”\r\n[Y.M. : 3/252]

4861.t:
Once in Samvat 1915, Gunātitānand Swāmi came to Samadhiyālā [Bhojā Bhakta’s village]. Everyone ate the {!dudhpāk-puri!} that was prepared and offered to Thākorji. In the afternoon {!kathā!}, Jāgā Bhakta was reading Gadhadā I-21 while Gunātitānand Swāmi was resting nearby.
Bhāyābhāi asked Jāgā Bhakta, “In this Vachanāmrut, what are the two forms of Akshar that Mahārāj talks about? Which form is the one that remains in Mahārāj’s {!sevā!} and which is the one that came on this earth with Mahārāj?”
Overhearing the question, Gunātitānand Swāmi sat up and said, “Bhāyābhāi, what did you ask?” Bhāyābhāi repeated his questions.
Gunātitānand Swāmi answered, “Where do you have to go find Akshar? The one who sits in front of you is Akshar – the one who remains is Mahārāj’s {!sevā!} and the one who came on the earth along with him. Consider it your great fortune that we have come to your village. Otherwise, where is Akshar and where is Samadhiyālā village [i.e. What is Samadhiyālā village compared to the greatness of Akshar]?”
[G.S. : 1/515]

4862.t:
10 December 1961, Mumbai. 
During a question and answer session on Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 21 with Yogiji Mahārāj, the latter explained, “Why did Shriji Mahārāj sit in contemplation for some time? It was because those present may not have been able to understand his discourse.
“Non-violence means to not hurt any {!jiva!}.
“The highest form of non-violence is to take {!jivas!} above {!māyā!}. Celibacy should be observed in eigth ways. The highest form of celibacy is to understand one’s form to be {!Gunātit!}. Understand oneself to be the ātmā, above the three bodies and three states. Then one will not be affected by any words.
“{!Ātmanishthā!} encompasses maintaining stability in happiness and misery.
“The highest form of {!ātmanishthā!} is to keep firm faith in Akshar.
“What is detachment? There are many deities, but have attachment to only one - Sahajānand Swāmi.
“Ultimate detachment is to be attached solely to Akshar and Purushottam.”
[Y.M. : 3/255]

4864.t:
Samvat 1969, Sārangpur. Rānābhāi Darbār of Jhinjhar said some harsh words to Sādhu Harikrishnadās who was doing {!sevā!} in Sārangpur. Harikrishnadās requested Rānābhāi to meet Shāstriji Mahārāj. After prostrating, he sat before Shāstriji Mahārāj and said, “I’ve heard many, many things about you; however, hearing words like: ‘you are all outcasts from Vartāl and all of you are {!bandiyā’!} from those who oppose you, I never came for your {!darshan!}.”
Swāmishri subtly laughed and said, “You have great {!sanskārs!} from your previous life, hence you have been able to come here. Bring the Vachanāmrut.” Shāstriji Mahārāj had him read Gadhadā I-21 in which Shriji Mahārāj explains the two forms of Akshar, Gadhadā I-71 in which Shriji Mahārāj said Bhagwān manifests on the earth along with his Akshardhām, Gadhadā II-59 in which Shriji Mahārāj says only those who have accumulated a great number of merits from performing good deeds receive the opportunity to serve Bhagwān’s {!Sant!}, and Vartāl 5 in which Shriji Mahārāj says that if one performs services of the Sant [one possessing highest qualities] similar to the services one performs of God then even if he was a devotee of the lowest calibre and was destined to become a devotee of the highest calibre after two, four, ten, or even after 100 lives, he will become a devotee of the highest calibre in this very life.
Shāstriji Mahārāj had all these Vachanāmruts read and explained that such a Sant with the highest qualities is Gunātitānand Swāmi who is the eternal Aksharbrahma; and the fundamental principle of {!upāsanā!} is to offer {!upāsanā!} having identified one’s self as Akshar.
Hearing the clear principles from the Vachanāmrut, Rānābhāi understood {!upāsanā!} perfectly.
[S.M. : 1/383]

4865.t:
Samvat 1970, Sārangpur. A great aspirant, Kuberbhāi, came to Sārangpur mandir but heard that Swāmishri [Shāstriji Mahārāj] had just left for the Charotar region a few days earlier. He was heartbroken having missed Shāstriji Mahārāj. Realizing Kuberbhāi to be a great aspirant, Vignāndās Swāmi asked him his reason for coming. Kuberbhāi said, “My name is Kuberbhāi from Bhavnagar. I am a {!satsangi!} but I have some questions related to why Shāstriji Mahārāj separated from Vartāl and established his own {!sansthā!}.”
Vignāndās Swāmi patiently listened and replied that Shāstriji Mahārāj’s principles are according to the scriptures and Shriji Mahārāj’s principles. He had Gadhadā II-9, 24, 30; Gadhadā I-21 and 71 read and explained the principle of Akshar-Purushottam from these.
Kuberbhāi’s eyes opened having listened to this principle. He was a true and fearless aspirant, so all his false preconceptions evaporated and he understood the knowledge of Akshar and Purushottam. He also realized that if this sādhu [Vignāndās Swāmi] is this knowledgeable, then how great must Shāstriji Mahārāj be?
He took the vows of {!panch-vartmān!} and wore a new two-fold {!kanthi!} as a symbol of Akshar and Purushottam, and thus became a brave new devotee of Shāstriji Mahārāj.
[S.M. : 1/401]

4871.t: Without the digit ‘1’ placed in front of it, the number ‘0’ has no value. Similarly, God is the digit ‘1’ and devotional activities such as singing {!kirtans!}, performing prostrations, etc. are equivalent to the number ‘0’. When one remembers God while performing these devotional activities, one experiences their true fruits. However if one does not remember God whilst performing these devotional activities, one will not experience their fruits. This is the essence of this Vachanāmrut – the {!paramhansas!} titled it using the unique example of the digit ‘1’.

5786.t:
March 1863, Ghoghāvadar.
In Ghoghāvadar, Jāgā Bhakta read five Vachanāmruts, namely: Gadhadā I 23, Gadhadā II 30, Gadhadā II 45, Amdāvād 2 and Amdāvād 3. 
Extremely pleased with his selection of Vachanāmruts, Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “Oh, ho! It’s like I had never heard these Vachanāmruts. Please read them again.” Jāgā Bhakta read them again. 
Gunātitānand Swāmi then said, “Listening to these Vachanāmruts, it is clear that without imbibing these principles in our lives, no liberation is possible in infinite years. This is true not only for us, but one may be an {!āchārya!}, or the son of God, or an {!ishwar!}, or some minor or major god, but liberation is impossible without imbibing these principles. Why? Because this is also Mahārāj’s principle.” 
[S.V. : 3/13]

5787.t:
In Samvat 1919, Gunātitānand Swāmi started his journey toward Vartāl for the {!samaiyo!} of Chaitra sud 15 [{!Punam!}]. He stayed one day in Gondal and then arrived in Goghāvadar, a village nearby. He stayed at the Shiv Mandir on the river bank. While resting in the afternoon, he had Jāgā Bhakta read the Vachanāmrut. Jāgā Bhakta read five Vachanāmruts: Gadhadā I-23, Gadhadā II-30 and 45, Amdāvād 2 and 3. Hearing these Vachanāmruts, Swāmi sat up and said, “It is as if I had never heard these Vachanāmruts.” He said, “Read them again.” Jāgā Swāmi read them again.
Then Swāmi said, “Listening to these Vachanāmruts, I have concluded that even after millions of years, without behaving in this way, there is no final release. So, for us, there is no alternative but to do this. Also, even if one is an {!āchārya!}, a son of Bhagwān, an {!ishwar!}, or some small or big deity, still there is no release without behaving in that way. Since, that is Mahārāj’s belief.” Based on this, Swāmi recited some couplets quoted by Mahārāj: ‘{!Nijātmānam brahmarupam…’!}, ‘{!Brahmabhutah prasannātmā…’!}, ‘{!Parinishthitopi nairgunye…’!}, ‘{!Atmāramāshcha munayo’!}.
After reciting many such couplets, he said, “When one becomes like this, then Bhagwān resides in one’s heart.” Then, looking at a devotee, he said, “You do have a {!murti!}, but without a {!mandir!} where will you install it? So, if you want to install Bhagwān, then learn to prepare a {!mandir!} as described here, then Bhagwān will stay.”
Then he continued, “When the {!sādhus!} went to get the {!murtis!} for this mandir [Junagadh], the sculptor asked, ‘What type of {!murtis!} shall I make for you?’ Then the sādhus said, ‘Make them according to these designs.’ Then the sculptor said, ‘These {!murtis!} are suitable only for a mandir worth hundreds of thousands of rupees.’ Then the sādhus said, ‘We’ve come to take {!murtis!} in accordance with such a mandir.’ So the sculptor said, ‘Then I’ll make them.’ Then the sculptor sculpted the {!murtis!}. Similarly, without becoming {!brahmarup!} where will we install Purushottam? So, if you want to install Purushottam, you have to become {!brahmarup!}.” Having said this, he got up. Then he held a devotee’s wrist and while walking told him, “Beware, never have any [worldly] desires.” Then that devotee’s desires stopped. And Swāmi said, “If one can remain like this all the time, doubts, strong attachments to one’s karma, desires, affection for worldly relations, body-consciousness, etc. and countless other strong material bonds are destroyed and one can continually stay focused on Bhagwān.”
[S.V. : 3/13]

5823.t:
In Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I-25, Shriji Mahārāj says, “Recently, I granted {!samādhi!} to a devotee in which she saw intense divine light. Seeing that light, she began to scream; ‘I’m burning!’…”
The reason for Shriji Mahārāj’s gracious words is as follows:
Around the month of Posh of Samvat 1876, Lādkibāi came for Mahārāj’s {!darshan!} from Meghpur. Ever since Mulji Bhakta was killed in Meghpur, Mahārāj had not visited Meghpur. Therefore, Lādkibāi went for Mahārāj’s {!darshan!} whenever Mahārāj visited nearby villages. Due to her intense love for Mahārāj, her {!indriyas!} were always drawn toward Mahārāj’s {!swarup!}. When she arrived in Gadhpur, she immediately entered the {!samādhi!} state. In the {!samādhi!} state, she saw frightful incoming waves of light similar to enormous crashing waves of an ocean. She heard terrifyingly loud thuds as if the whole {!brahmānd!} will split apart. This experience caused Lādkibāi to shriek whilst in {!samādhi!}, “Mahārāj, save me. I’m burning, I’m burning…”
Hearing Lādkibāi’s screams, Jivubā, Lādubā and other women also started to tremble. Jivubā asked, “Mahārāj, what is happening to her?”
Mahārāj’s answer has been captured in the discourse delivered in this Vachanāmrut.
[B.S. : 4/184]

5846.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi had Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 26 read and said, “This, too, is one that can enable one to transcend all material qualities and limitations [attain {!nirgunbhav!}].”\r\n[S.V. : 6/31]

5847.t: On the morning of 21 January 1964, Yogiji Mahārāj was discoursing on Gadhadā I 26. In the narrative, it is mentioned that Shriji Mahārāj was seated in the afternoon time. So Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Mahārāj must have sat down after eating. Where was the time for rest? If Mahārāj rested, the whole {!brahmānd!} would turn upside down… Now he will talk about the cause [{!kāran!}].” Saying this he had the rest of the Vachanāmrut read, but no where was {!kāran!} mentioned.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “Bring the Vachanāmrut. {!Kāran!} was not mentioned?” He started to examine the Vachanāmrut himself. Harshadbhāi gave him his glasses. Finally, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “This is a subtle talk. {!Kāran!} has not been referred to explicitly. But when one can see Bhagwān in their heart, then the {!kāran!} [body] is destroyed – one should understand this way. This has been mentioned by a {!Motāpurush!}. {!Iti Vachanāmrutam!}.”\r\n[Y.M. : 3/583]

5853.t:
In Samvat 1928, Vartāl {!Mandir’s!} Harikrishna Mahārāj’s {!murti!} gave {!darshan!} to Girdharbhāi and told him, “Today, the {!Param Ekāntik Satpurush!} is Bhagatji Mahārāj. Serve him.”
Having learned who the true {!Ekāntik Satpurush!} is, as per Vartāl 19, Girdharbhāi sought out Bhagatji Mahārāj. 
The following day, Bhagatji was sitting in the assembly hall next to his room, discoursing to the {!sādhus!} and devotees. When Girdharbhāi arrived, he noticed the sādhus and devotees sitting around Bhagatji. Girdharbhāi did {!darshan!} of Bhagatji Mahārāj and sat in the back. Knowing what had taken place through his omniscient powers, Bhagatji said to him, “Girdharbhāi, please come and sit at the front.” Girdharbhāi came forward and sat in the front.
At that same time, Kothāri Govardhanbhāi happened to pass by and was surprised to see Girdharbhāi there. He approached Bhagatji and said, “Prāgji, you may easily discourse to your obedient disciples in Junagadh, but Girdharbhāi is not someone who will be easily convinced. He has travelled extensively and is experienced. If you can convince him, then you are truly great.”
Bhagatji laughed when he heard these words. He replied, “Kothāri Mahārāj! I will speak to him only if you want me to, but please do not get angry later!”
“I will not, so do not worry. In fact, it is my wish that you speak to him freely without reservation,” the {!kothāri!} replied.
After the {!kothāri!} left, Bhagatji Mahārāj had Girdharbhāi read Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I-27 and Bhagatji Mahārāj explained it to him.
After Bhagatji Mahārāj’s explanation ended, the assembly was left spellbound. The whole assembly then got up to leave, but Girdharbhāi remained seated and gazed at Bhagatji. Eventually, he touched Bhagatji’s feet and prayed, “Mahārāj, please keep the grace you had on me today, forever.” Bhagatji smiled and blessed him.
This marked the beginning of Girdharbhāi’s conviction in Bhagatji and the start of his spiritual association with him. Kothāri Govardhanbhāi also developed deep respect for Bhagatji. He now knew that Girdharbhāi would no longer wish to remain as a householder. He arranged for Girdharbhāi to be initiated into the {!sādhu!}-fold at the hands of Adbhutānand Swāmi and he was named Vignāndās Swāmi. The more Vignāndās Swāmi associated with Bhagatji, the more his saintly personality developed. He became a gem amongst the {!sādhus!}.
[B.M. : 170]

5856.t:
On the Kārtik sud 11 {!Ekādashi Samaiyo!} of 1954 in Vartāl, it was decided that Vignāndāsji, Keshavprasādji, Yagnapurushdāsji, Nārāyancharandāsji, Purushottamdāsji, and Kothāri Bechar Bhagat would be excommunicated from Vartāl. This group of sādhus left Vartāl and travelled from village to village until they arrived in Mahuvā.
A very enjoyable assembly was held in their presence. Since these sādhus had been sent away from Vartāl for speaking of Prāgji Bhakta’s greatness, everyone was curious to know more about Prāgji Bhakta. They also wished to know how these {!sādhus!} had spoken about Bhagatji’s greatness to the other devotees. Vitthalbhāi, Fulchandbhāi, and Dāmā Sheth all attended the assembly in the mandir.
“Please, can you tell us the way in which you understand Bhagatji and what you have seen in him,” Fulchandbhāi asked Bechar Bhagat.
	“We believe him to be an {!ekāntik!} devotee. He has Aksharbrahma Gunātitānand Swāmi’s blessings upon him. We believe that Gunātitānand Swāmi is Akshar based on the incidents Bhagatji has shared with us. Furthermore, we experience internal peace due to his association,” replied Bechar Bhagat.
“It seems that you have left this Satsang and trusted him fully. He could even throw you down a well. Please justify your claims of his greatness on the basis of the Vachanāmrut.”
Bechar Bhagat kept silent and instead, Nārāyancharan Swāmi said, “Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 27 describes the attributes of the {!Satpurush!}. We believe that Bhagatji is one who has those attributes.”
“Please tell us exactly what has been said in Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 27,” Vitthalbhāi asked. 
Bewildered at this question, Nārāyancharan Swāmi looked at Bhagatji. Bhagatji simply pointed his finger at Shāstri Yagnapurushdāsji, who was seated among the Gadhadā {!sādhus!}.
“This young {!sādhu!}will expose everything as it is, so please ask him,” Bhagatji said, indicating that they should ask Yagnapurushdāsji.
“Please tell us,” everyone requested to Yagnapurushdāsji.
Shāstri Yagnapurushdāsji realized that this was an excellent opportunity to reveal Bhagatji’s form as it really is. He also felt that Bhagatji wanted him to expand on the qualities and virtues of the {!Satpurush!}. In earnest, he began to address Vitthalbhāi and the other devotees.
In this way, Shāstriji Mahārāj explained how Prāgji Bhakta is an {!Ekāntik Satpurush!} based on this Vachanāmrut to everyone’s amazement.
[B.M. : 248]

5863.t:
Samvat 1952, Gadhadā.
During the Jal-Jhilani {!samaiyo!} at 2:00 p.m., Bhagatji made his way to Acharya Vihārilālji Mahārāj’s residence, where an assembly was in progress. During the discourses, Āchārya Mahārāj asked Moti Bhagat to read Vachanāmruts, Gadhadā I 27 and Gadhadā III 21.
Āchārya Mahārāj then said, “Both of these Vachanāmruts seem to apply to Bhagatji. This is evident because Pavitrānand Swāmi insulted Bhagatji when Bhagvatprasādji Mahārāj went to Mahuvā. However, in the intense summer heat, Bhagatji would still sit on the sand opposite the tent and only get up after the evening discourse had finished. He is the only person in whom I have seen such enthusiasm for discourses and {!darshan!} of the {!sādhus!}. Everyone else was also convinced and felt, ‘There is no one else like this’ when they witnessed his elevated state of humility and saintliness. I was also amazed to see his spiritual state. Only a golden thread remain firm throughout all seasons, whilst threads made from wax soften during the summer heat. Similarly, in Satsang, only those who possess such a spiritual state remain stable when insulted; whereas others end up leaving Satsang permanently.”
“All of this is due to Swāmi’s grace,” Bhagatji replied.
[B.M. : 434]

5865.t:
1929, Sārangpur.
Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 27 was being read in the assembly: “The countless wonders which have occurred in the past, those which are currently taking place, and those which will occur in the future are all only due to the manifest form of God that I have attained.”
Hearing this, Kuberbhāi of Bhavnagar asked Shāstriji Mahārāj, “Oh compassionate one! In this, who should one understand as the manifest form of God? Everyone understands their own guru to be the manifest form of God and they believe him to be the all-doer. In reality, who should one believe to be the all-doer?”
Very pleased to hear Kuberbhāi’s question, Swāmishri replied, “Your question is such that it can remove the ignorance of countless people in Satsang. In this supreme Satsang, everyone believes their own guru to be the best and as the all-doer. However, such an understanding dishonours the forms of Shriji Mahārāj and [Gunātitānand] Swāmi. Mahārāj alone is the all-doer. Mahārāj has three powers: {!kartum, akartum!} and {!anyathakartum!}. From these three types of powers, Mahārāj only uses his {!kartum!} and {!akartum!} powers through the {!Sant!} who is associated with him, in whom he resides and through whom he works. Through the profoundness of his powers, he merges countless people into himself and behaves as the form of Virat. At this time, no matter how obstinate a {!jiva!} may be, even if it is ungodly or a mountain of sin, he even places such obstinate {!jivas!} at the level of the highest devotee merely through his grace. Mahārāj used this power through [Gunātitānand] Swāmi. It was through this power of Mahārāj that Swāmi made countless impious {!jivas!} pious. He changed them from within and made them behave according to his wishes.”
Having said this, Swāmishri went on to give an example in order to explain this in detail: “[Gunātitānand] Swāmi wanted to build a new {!mandir!} in Bagasara after demolishing the old one that was there. He needed to procure the corner plot of the tailor’s house situated in the {!mandir!} compound. The owner of the house, however, was a Kāthi Darbār who was averse to Satsang. In addition, the townsfolk had coerced him into hating the Satsang. Therefore, he flatly refused to part with this corner plot for the mandir. Adjacent to that were the houses of some {!Brāhmins!}. If they could be secured, then the {!mandir!} could also be expanded. The {!sādhus!} asked the {!Brāhmins!}. They said, ‘We have obtained these houses as a gift from the Darbār. We cannot sell them without his permission.’ However, the Darbār never gave permission. Different groups of {!sādhus!} approached the Darbār, but he insulted them with harsh words. In this way, there was no resolution to this issue.
“Eventually, they all told Swāmi in Junagadh what had happened. Swāmi said, ‘Tell the Darbār through one of his {!satsangi!} relations. As one has affection for one’s relatives, he will listen.’ Ālā Khumān, the Darbār of Kundla, was a {!satsangi!} related to him. They asked the Darbār through him for the tailor’s corner plot and for the several houses belonging to the {!Brāhmins!}; however, the Darbār did not listen to Ālā Khumān either. Ālā Khumān conveyed Swāmi’s message two to three times, in person and with humility. Even then, the Darbār refused to agree. In the end, Ālā Khumān refused to even drink the water of Bagasara.
“Once, when Swāmi was passing by that way, he went to Bagasara. Having left his belongings in the old {!mandir!}, Swāmi took a couple of {!sādhus!} and devotees with him to meet the Darbār. The {!sādhus!} told him, ‘Swāmi! Please don’t go. The Darbār is evil and will insult you.’ Swāmi replied, ‘What is praise and insult for us sādhus? We will remember Mahārāj and tell him. If he agrees, then fine; if not, then what do we have to lose?’ So saying, Swāmi made his way to the palace.
“On seeing Swāmi, the Darbār immediately came downstairs. Swāmi turned to him and cast his divine gaze. The Darbār changed from within! He offered prostrations to Swāmi and said with folded hands, ‘Swāmi! My guardian! What is the reason for you coming here today?’ Swāmi told him about the land for the {!mandir!}. Immediately he said, ‘Swāmi! Never mind the houses of the {!Brāhmins!}, but you can have my {!Darbār!} as well! I will do whatever you say. Ālā Khumān did ask me two or three times with regards to this, but I refused to give the houses. Now he has stopped drinking water from my village. I will call him and sign the necessary documents in his presence so that he is also satisfied.’
“Pleased with this promise, Swāmishri blessed him. When Ālā Khumān arrived two or three days later, the Darbār signed the documents in his presence and donated the houses.
“Thus, by changing the Darbār from within, Swāmi completed this task that no one else could – something which was impossible for everyone else. The power to change someone from within is Mahārāj’s power. Mahārāj demonstrated this power through Swāmi – who was Mahārāj’s manifest form. The underlying principle is that the Sant has become the manifestation in which Mahārāj resides. Mahārāj uses this power through him in order to align {!jivas!} towards Himself. Therefore, the all-doer is Mahārāj alone. Nevertheless, Mahārāj makes use of his {!kartum!} and {!akartum!} powers through the {!Sant!} who is His manifestation. Therefore, understand the attributes of the {!Sant!} who has attained this association with Mahārāj through Vachanāmruts Gadhadā I 27 and I 62 as well as Gadhadā III 26 and III 27. Recognize this {!Sant!} who works and travels according to Mahārāj’s wishes, and understand that Mahārāj is present in Satsang through that {!Sant!}.”
Swāmishri’s answer to Kuberbhāi’s question was to the point and easily understood by everyone.
[S.M. : 1/591]

6522.t:
In this Vachanāmrut, Shriji Mahārāj says, “Only by keeping profound association with the {!Satpurush!} can one develop intense love for God.” Somlā Khāchar asks in response, “We are intensely engaged in such profound association, yet why does such intense love not develop?”
Shriji Mahārāj counters with: “It is true that you engage yourselves in such profound association, but as well as associating with Me, you also associate with the world. As a result, intense love for God does not develop.”
Mahārāj responded this way to Somlā Khāchar not because Somlā Khāchar failed in observing {!niyams!} and abiding by {!dharma!}. Mahārāj actually praised Somlā Khāchar’s virtue of always behaving consistently (i.e. constantly observing {!niyam-dharma!}) in Gadhadā III 24. So why did Mahārāj insinuate Somlā Khāchar “also associates with the world.”
A story passed down by word of mouth reveals the fact that, being a {!kāthi darbār!}, Somlā Khāchar’s primary deity of worship was Surya-Nārāyan. After coming into Satsang, he developed faith in Shriji Mahārāj; yet, he would pray to Surya-Nārāyan with folded hands daily at sunrise: “{!He Hari Sūraj-Nārāyaṇ!}! {!Dātaṇ fāṭā ne pāp nāṭhā, bhekhnī ṭek ne bānānī pat rākhjo!}.” (By having your {!darshan!} in the morning, my sins are burned away. Keep me in company of sādhus and protect those who take refuge in you.) Such a small infraction in his {!pativratāni tek!} (vow of fidelity) caused Shriji Mahārāj to deliver a reproach to Somlā Khāchar. This is how the story has been narrated by word of mouth. No doubt, after Mahārāj pointed this out to Somlā Khāchar, his {!bhakti!} toward Mahārāj must have improved.

6523.t: 7 December 1961, Mumbai.\r\nDuring the afternoon discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Our mother and father is Swāminārāyan. Our village is Akshardhām. Us {!tyāgis!} [renunciates] should imbibe this Vachanāmrut within our lives.”\r\n[Y.M. : 3/249]

6524.t:
Samvat 1953, Junagadh. Harilālbhāi, Shivlāl Sheth’s grandson, had arranged for a month-long Satsangijivan {!pārāyan!} in Junagadh. Four {!purānis!} read the {!kathā!} in turns during the month. When the {!pārāyan!} ended, everyone was faced with a dilemma: which {!purāni’s pujān!} should be done first? Everyone discussed among themselves who it should be and had concluded that it should be the senior and experienced {!purāni!} Haridās. His {!pujān!} was going to be done first when the talk went to Harilālbhāi, who was known to speak his mind. He instantly said, “Whoever’s {!kathā!} was most effective should be honoured first. By listening to Shāstri Yagnapurushdāsji’s {!kathā!}, I experienced great joy; moreover, everyone else also listened with keen interest. Therefore, his {!pujān!} should be done first.”
Those who bore malice started a turmoil. In order to insult Shāstriji Mahārāj and disparage his guru, Ghanshyāmdās stood up and said, “Today, the one who has made a tailor and a shoemaker his guru has become prominent; such is the adverse time.”
Shāstriji Mahārāj was still seated on the dais, gathering the pages of the scripture when Ghanshyāmdās made his retort. Shāstriji Mahārāj roared like a lion in defence, “The right to become a guru is not reserved for {!sādhus!} only. Mahārāj has said: as long as he continues to harbour vanity of his caste or {!āshram!}, he will never imbibe the virtues of a {!sādhu!}. (Gadhadā I-44) Where is your {!sādhutā!} if you identify a devotee of Bhagwān only by his caste due to your self-conceit? Prāgji Bhakta and Jāgā Bhakta have received the blessing of Gunātitānand Swāmi. Mahārāj will not tolerate such derogatory words spoken against them.” Ghanshyāmdās was subdued by Shāstriji Mahārāj’s defence and couldn’t speak any further. The others also became silenced.
After Shāstriji Mahārāj walked off the stage, he addressed the assembly again and said, “Only because of malice and to disparage Prāgji Bhakta and Jāgā Bhakta did this {!sādhu!} speak. However, many of the senior {!sādhus!} here knew how Prāgji Bhakta and Jāgā Bhakta served and pleased Gunātitānand Swāmi. If after having known their greatness we do not defend them in order to save our face, then we are considered {!vimukh!} according to Shriji Mahārāj’s words.” Shāstriji Mahārāj sat down having said that.
[S.M. : 1/180]

6805.t: 25 June 1970, London. In the evening, whilst returning from Akshar Hill to the {!Mandir!}, Doctor Swāmi was reading Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 19. Upon listening to it, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Shāstriji Mahārāj possessed the four characteristics of {!dharma, ātmanishthā, vairāgya!} and {!bhakti!}. If one understands the {!Sant!} to be flawless through one’s mind, acts according to the {!Sant’s!} command with one’s body, and sings the {!Sant’s!} praises with one’s speech, then one will develop the aforementioned four characteristics.”\r\n[Y.M. : 6/323]

6807.t:
In this same Vachanāmrut, Vālā Dhruv of Vaso asks, “Mahārāj, how can the feelings of I-ness and my-ness towards one’s body and its relations be eradicated?”
The history that has been passed down through the generations is as follows: A close female relative was raped by a wicked person. This incident happening to a noble family caused Vālā Dhruv to become distressed and he could not find any way to heal from his depression. It has been said that to free himself from the shackles of this traumatic experience, Vālā Dhruv asked this question.
This piece of history seems to be valid because of Shriji Mahārāj’s peculiar answer: “Moreover, out of those 8.4 million life forms previously undertaken, there is not a single mother, sister, daughter or wife who observes the vow of fidelity any longer. So how can one who believes such relations to be one’s true relations ever overcome the feelings of I-ness and my-ness?...”
Here, Shriji Mahārāj mentions all four types of relations a male can have with a female: mother, sister, daughter, and wife. Therefore, the close female relative who was raped must have been one of these four. It has been said that the assault was on his sister. Vālā Dhruv’s sister was a {!mumukshu!} who readily served {!sādhus!}. One {!vairāgi bāwā!} took advantage of her subservient nature – leaving a disturbing mark on Vālā Dhruv.
Moreover, Shriji Mahārāj answers Vālā Dhruv’s question specifically using {!pativratā dharma!} (vow of fidelity – refraining from the physical contact of a male that is not related to oneself) from among other {!dharmas!} women are to observe. Therefore, we can confidently presume that a sinful deed occurred where {!pativratā dharma!} was transgressed.
Shriji Mahārāj has advised how to eradicate I-ness and my-ness in many Vachanāmruts (such as Gadhadā I 8, Gadhadā I 21, Gadhadā III 19); however, nowhere has He used this sort of logic: “Moreover, out of those 8.4 million life forms previously undertaken, there is not a single mother, sister, daughter or wife who observes the vow of fidelity…” Only here does He give this thought process because Vālā Dhruv is suffering from the distress of his sister having transgress {!pativratā dharma!}.

7428.t:
21 January 1964, Mumbai. 
In the afternoon, Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 28 was being read. Explaining the essence of this Vachanāmrut, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “When one perceives flaws in others, one falls from Satsang. When you have free time, try to understand this Vachanāmrut. Leave everything aside and read the Vachanāmrut.”
“Flaws are inherently present within people, but do not look at these and only look at their virtues. All sādhus are great, all devotees are great, and all are {!upasaks!} of Swāminārāyan! We are all one and not different.”
“Oh! How fortunate I am to be in Satsang. If I had fallen into bad company, what would have happened to me? If one perceives virtues in this way, then he becomes great. True greatness is when we experience peace in our hearts and not by attaining worldly status. If one attains the former type of greatness, he can never fall.”
[Y.M. : 3/583]

7430.t:
26 April 1970, Mombasa. 
Yogiji Mahārāj was staying at the house of Ravibhāi Pandyā. In the afternoon at 1:20pm, Yogiji Mahārāj read Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 28. Explaining the essence of this Vachanāmrut, he said, “One should remain as the servant of a servant. Once Gunātitānand Swāmi was seated on a horse. A Muslim had come with the intention of killing him. He asked, ‘Are you the great one?’ Gunātitānand Swāmi replied, ‘No, only Allah [God] is great.’ The Muslim was touched by Swāmi’s servitude towards God and bowed before him.”
“What is peace? When there is tranquillity within the heart.”
“Who has attained greatness? One who remains as a servant of servants; not one who has attained a prominent status.”
[Y.M. : 6/178]

7470.t:
In Nadiād, Shāstriji Mahārāj explained the principle of Akshar-Purushottam to Dolatrām Pandyā [a senior devotee belonging to the Vartāl {!Mandir!} committee]. Dolatrām Pandyā said, “Swāmi, you have rid me of my misunderstanding. The fact that Akshar and Purushottam are Swāmi and Nārāyan is now lodged in my heart. However, please explain to me how that Akshar is Gunātitānand Swāmi and only Gunātitānand Swāmi.”
Shāstriji Mahārāj recounted all the incidents of Shriji Mahārāj that showed Gunātitānand Swāmi is Akshar. Then he said, “Greatness is due to one’s faith in the manifest form of Bhagwān and the observance of his commands. [Gadhadā I 31] Therefore, study both Gopālānand Swāmi’s talks and Gunātitānand Swāmi’s talks [their respective scriptures] and decide whose talks brings out the greatness of Shriji Mahārāj to a greater extent.”
Dolatrāmbhāi then came to understand that Gunātitānand Swāmi was the greatest of Shriji Mahārāj’s {!paramhansas!}.
[S.M. : 1/415]

7517.t:
In this Vachanāmrut, Shriji Mahārāj explains the glory of the {!Gunātit Satpurush!}, who understands God as the all-doer and as eternally possessing a form. He describes the 11 honours (characteristics) of such a {!Satpurush!}, which the {!paramhansas!} have noted within this Vachanāmrut. They are as follows: 
1. He is dear to me
2. {!Kāl!} is unable to administer its power over him 
3. {!Karma!} is unable to administer its power over him 
4. {!Māyā!} is unable to administer its power over him
5. I (Shriji Mahārāj) place the dust of his feet on my head
6. In my (Shriji Mahārāj’s) mind I am afraid of harming him
7. I (Shriji Mahārāj) long to have his darshan
8. One who wishes for liberation through the grace of God is wise, just like one who wishes to cross the ocean with the aid of a ship
9. After leaving his body, he attains a divine form and forever remains in God’s service and in his presence
10. His {!darshan!} is equivalent to the {!darshan!} of God himself 
11. His {!darshan!} alone redeems countless wretched souls

7521.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “Only devotion offered after fully recognising the form of God is accepted as devotion by God. And without fully recognising God, it is as though we are trapped and forced to perform some work. Service performed without recognising God cannot be called devotion.” Then he had Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 37 read. \r\n[S.V. : 5/181]

7680.t:
The title of this Vachanāmrut is “The Observance of the Moral Do’s and Don’ts” ({!Vidhi-Nishedhnu!}, where {!vidhi!} are the moral do’s and {!nishedh!} are the moral don’ts). In this Vachanāmrut, Shriji Mahārāj is heavily expounding the necessity of {!vidhi-nishedh!}. He is establishing the necessity using solid and pure logic from the support of scriptures and the {!vartan!} of sages of the past. In conclusion, as if He’s giving his final judgment, Mahārāj says: “Therefore, the prescribed moral do’s and don’ts are indeed true, not false. Whosoever falsifies them will be consigned to {!narak!}.”
Glancing at the history of the {!sampradāy!}, we obtain the following motive for this Vachanāmrut:
Prior to this discourse, Shriji Mahārāj had Gopi Bhatt recount the {!guru-paramparā!} of the {!Sampradāy!} that day. Gopi Bhatt had detailed that, “Ātmānand Swāmi’s {!shishya!} was Govindmuni. Govindmuni’s {!shishya!} was Ānandmuni. Ānandmuni’s {!shishya!} was Gopālmuni and his {!shishya!} was Ātmānand Swāmi. Ātmānand Swāmi was my father and his {!shishya!} was Rāmānand Swāmi, who you accepted as your guru…”
Shriji Mahārāj was pleased to hear Gopi Bhatt’s narrative and gifted him fine clothes, jewels, and a horse.
Afterward, Shriji Mahārāj called and asked Shukmuni, “Please write a letter to all the {!paramhansas!} stating that the British rule now prevails and the circumstances are favourable for the {!sādhus!} to behave as according to traditional customs. According to our customs, we should adopt the practice of keeping a tuft of hair [{!shikhā!}], sacred thread [{!sutra!}], and {!tilak!}.” Accordingly, Shukmuni wrote the letter to all the {!paramhansas!} residing at various places.
[B.S. : 4/187; H.C.S. : 20/7-16]
In Samvat 1863, Shriji Mahārāj initiated 500 {!paramhansas!} due to the oppression of {!bāwās!}. He allowed them to abandon the {!shikhā!} and {!sutra!} and travel uncharacteristically. On this day, 13 years had passed when Mahārāj gave them the {!āgnā!} to recommence the traditional practices and the moral do’s and don’ts because the fear of oppression was no longer present.
For 13 years, the {!paramhansas!} had behaved purely in their mind rather than observing physically. It is quite possible that since Mahārāj permitted them to lapse in the moral do’s and don’ts, they became accustomed to that way of life. Hence, some found it difficult to completely route back to moral observances. In Gunātitānand Swāmi’s talks, he mentions, “We have never happily observed Mahārāj’s {!āgnās!} readily, despite that we cannot comprehend fully; on the contrary, Mahārāj understood completely. What {!āgnā!} is that?… No one would consent to building {!mandirs!}, no one accepted eating from a {!pattar!} [wooden bowl], etc. After much insistence, He made us accept His words.”
[Swāmini Vāto – 2/63]
From this discourse by Gunātitānand Swāmi, it becomes clear that, after 13 years of freedom from observing do’s and don’ts related to {!dharma!} and {!bhakti!}, many {!sādhus'!} minds were not in concurrence with Shriji Mahārāj’s insistence. Shriji Mahārāj had no choice but to forcefully expound this practice as can be seen by the strict words and His final judgment.

7776.t: 1887 [Samvat 1943], Mahemdavad. \r\nShāstriji Mahārāj said, “Only one who possesses a sharp intellect attains Brahman. Therefore, one who recognises the {!Satpurush!} - the gateway to liberation - safeguards his own liberation; even though he may not be proficient at managing worldly affairs or interpreting the scriptures, he should be considered as possessing a sharp intellect. Conversely one may be extremely adept at worldly affairs or may know the precise meaning of the {!shastras!}, but does not tread the path of liberation. Hence, that person does not recognise the {!Satpurush!}, who is the gateway to liberation and so he possesses a blunt intellect. Therefore, only one who understands the {!Satpurush!} to be the manifest form of God is intelligent, righteous and knowledgeable.” \r\n[S.M. : 1/89]

7779.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi said “Should those who did not associate with Mahārāj when he was present and those who do not associate with the great {!Sādhu!} now, be understood as wise? True intelligence is only that which is gained by learning from a great {!Sādhu!} and is useful in attaining liberation; otherwise, it is not intelligence. Mahārāj used to say, ‘Nath Bhakta is wise and Diwānji is foolish.’”\r\n[S.V. : 2/23]

7792.t:
August 1857, Junagadh.
Gunātitānand Swāmi said to Yogeshwardas Swāmi, “Read the Vachanāmrut.” Therefore, he read Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 54. 
Swāmi was pleased and said, “Please read it again.” In this way, he had this Vachanāmrut read aloud five times before saying “Oh! It feels like I should hear this Vachanāmrut all day long. Look, Mahārāj has described the gateway to {!moksha!} in this Vachanāmrut. Those whose karmas are barren will not understand this Vachanāmrut.”
[G.S. : 1/502]
[B.M. : 513]

7793.t:
Samvat 1950, Amdāvād.
Realizing Bhagatji Mahārāj’s wish and insistence on discoursing, Shāstriji Mahārāj started his talk, “Rarest of the rare is taking birth in a human body. More than that, attaining Satsang is even rarer. But the rarest among everything is attaining the company of an {!Ekāntik Sant!}, thoroughly realizing who he is and associating with him. When one achieves this, then he has done everything and has nothing left to do on the path of liberation.” So saying, Shāstriji Mahārāj recited:
{!Prasangam-ajaram pāsham-ātmānaha kavayo viduhu |!}
{!Sa eva sādhushu kruto moksha-dvāram-apāvrutam ||!}
[Bhāgwat : 3/25/20]
“If a person maintains profound love towards the Ekāntik Sant of Bhagwān just as resolutely as he maintains profound love towards his own relatives, then the gateway to liberation opens for him.” So saying, Shāstriji Mahārāj sat silently.
Bhagatji Mahārāj said, “He spoke a short amount but he said the essence of all scriptures.” Then he came to Swāmishri and said, “{!Rang chhe, Swāmi!}!” And put his hands on Swāmishri’s head.
One devotee said, “You are a {!gruhasth!} [householder] and should not put your hands on a {!sādhu’s!} head. Yet, why did you?”
Bhagatji Mahārāj responded, “I did not put them on his head; Sahajānand Swāmi did!” The devotee was silenced by Bhagatji Mahārāj’s response.
[S.M. : 1/162]

7794.t: September 1896 [Samvat 1952], Gadhadā.\r\nBhagatji looked at one of the {!sādhus!} seated in the assembly. The {!sādhu!} then recited some Vachanāmruts by heart – Gadhadā I 54, Gadhadā II 54 and Gadhadā III 21. Having heard this, Bhagatji turned to Purushottamdas of Vaso and said, “The topic is life’s ultimate goal.” He then added, “{!Ātmabuddhi!} towards the {!Ekāntik Sant!} of God is the unique endeavour for {!moksha!}. Shriji Mahārāj has given the key to {!moksha!} to such a {!Sant!}; therefore, that {!Sant!} is known as the gateway to {!moksha!}. Serve such a {!Sant!} by thought, word and deed, and perfect {!ekāntik dharma!}, but never fall into the habit of criticizing people. Previously, those who had negative thoughts towards the devotees of God have fallen from even the most exalted status.”\r\n[B.M. : 552]

7796.t:
Samvat 1966, Bochāsan.
In the {!samaiyo!} of Chaitra sud 15, Shāstriji Mahārāj said, “{!Swadharma, gnān, vairāgya!}, and {!bhakti!} coupled with knowledge of Bhagwān’s greatness – an {!Ekāntik Sādhu!} who possesses these upholds {!Bhagwat Dharma!} and association with him opens the gateway to liberation.” Then Swāmishri recited ‘{!Prasangam-ajaram pāsham’!} and said, “Mahārāj has shown the gateway to liberation in this Vachanāmrut. To identify one’s {!ātmā!} with an Ekāntik Sant is Mahārāj’s principle. Those whose {!karmas!} are barren will not understand this talk.”
Dayābhāi of Chhāni said, “Swāmi, we all have 90% [15 {!ānā!} = 15/16] affection for you and only 10% [1 {!āno!} = 1/16] affection for our own body [self].”
Swāmishri laughed and said, “If that is so, then you are all sitting in Akshardhām.”
[S.M. : 1/342]

7797.t:
Samvat 1961.
Shāstriji Mahārāj was in Chānsad trying a milk-based remedy for canker sores. Mansukhbhāi Vaidya was called to Chānsad to treat Swāmishri. One morning, Swāmishri was sitting on a mat in the south-facing room of the Mandir. Devotees from Chānsad, Bhādaran, Dabhoi, Ānand, Bil, Sokhadā, etc. were seated in front of him. Kāshibhāi of Bhādran asked Swāmishri, “What are the means to liberation?”
Shāstriji Mahārāj had Gadhadā I 54 read by him and came across Muktānand Swāmi’s question: “How is that {!Bhāgwat Dharma!} upheld? Also, how can the gateway to liberation be opened?”
Swāmishri said, “The question you asked is the same question Muktānand Swāmi asked. Mahārāj answered: {!Bhāgwat Dharma!} is upheld by maintaining profound love towards the {!Ekāntik Sant!} of God, who possesses the attributes of {!swadharma, gnān, vairāgya!}, and {!bhakti!} coupled with knowledge of God’s greatness. Maintaining profound love towards such a {!Sant!} also opens the gateway to liberation.”
Swāmishri then turned to Hāthibhāi and said, “If you do this much, the gateway of liberation will open.”
Hāthibhāi folded his hands and replied, “With this answer, Shriji Mahārāj showed us everything is included in this one solution.”
Swāmishri told Kāshibhāi to read Gadhadā I 57 next. Again, Muktānand Swāmi’s question came, “Mahārāj, what is the most extraordinary means of attaining liberation?” Mahārāj had answered: “The knowledge of Bhagwān’s form [{!swarup!}] and the knowledge of Bhagwān’s greatness [{!māhātmya!}] are the two extraordinary means to attain liberation.”
From this dialogue, Swāmishri said, “Knowledge of Bhagwān’s form and knowledge of Bhagwān’s greatness can only be learned from a {!sādhu!} who has a direct relationship with Bhagwān. Mahārāj has said in Gadhadā III 27: ‘…the attributes of the Sant - being free of lust, avarice, egotism, taste, attachment, etc. - are also described in the scriptures. The {!Sant!} who possesses these attributes has a direct relationship with Bhagwān. Therefore, one should develop the conviction of Bhagwān based on his words. In fact, to have firm faith in the words of the {!Sant!} is itself the conviction of Bhagwān.’ Moreover, Bhagwān’s greatness and knowledge of his form spreads only though the {!Sant!} who has a direct relationship with Bhagwān.”
Finally, Swāmishri had Kāshibhāi read Gadhadā III 36 and explained, “Shriji Mahārāj asked all the {!paramhansas!} and devotees, ‘What is the most extraordinary spiritual endeavour for the liberation of the {!jiva!}, which, if practised, will surely guarantee liberation and prevent all other obstacles from hindering that liberation? Also, what is the greatest obstacle in that endeavour for liberation, on account of which one would certainly fall from the path of liberation? Please answer both questions.’ No one was able to answer Mahārāj’s question, so Mahārāj said, “The most extraordinary spiritual endeavour for liberation is to understand Purushottam Bhagwān, who is seated amidst the mass of light of Brahma, as eternally having a form. Furthermore, understanding that all avatārs emanate from him, one should accept the refuge of the manifest form of Bhagwān by any means possible. One should also offer {!bhakti!} to that Bhagwān while observing {!dharma!}, as well as associate with a {!Sant!} possessing such {!bhakti!}. That is the most extraordinary spiritual endeavour for liberation. One encounters no hindrances along that path.”
[S.M. : 1/253]

7802.t: After having Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 54 read, Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “Oh! I feel like listening to this Vachanāmrut all day long and still do not feel it is enough, since it describes the gateway to {!moksha!} and also explains true spiritual knowledge.” Saying this, he had it read three times and said, “Those whose karmas are barren will not understand this talk. For them, fundamentally, they view the great {!Sādhu!} as an enemy. That is known as destructive spiritual knowledge. So now, only attach [yourself] to this {!Sādhu!}. That such a time has come and still one does not stay with God or with the great {!Sādhu!} or listen to their talks, but instead listens to worldly talks is the {!jiva’s!} perversity.”\r\n[S.V. : 6/209]

7807.t: Bhagatji Mahārāj said, “Out of the 262 Vachanāmruts, Shriji Mahārāj has called Gadhadā I 54 and Gadhadā II 54 the Vachanāmruts of {!moksha!}. He also asked Dinanath Bhatt to consider both of these as particularly relevant to him.\r\n[B.M. : 513]

7816.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “After purifying one’s inner faculties, one should think that whatever important talks take place are due to this {!Sādhu!}. The fact that this Satsang, God and his {!Sādhu!} have been recognised in itself is described as the gateway to {!moksha!}.” After reciting the {!shlok!}, ‘{!Prasangamajaram pāsham!}...’ he said, “Without a door, even if the head is banged against the wall, it is not possible to enter. So, attach the jiva with such a {!Sādhu!}...”\r\n[S.V. : 6/85]

7821.t: Samvat 1955.\r\nWhen Shāstriji Mahārāj was staying in Junagadh, a {!Shāstri!} by the name of Kamalnayan came from the Drāvid region and met him. Shāstriji Mahārāj took him for Jāgā Bhakta’s {!darshan!}. The {!Shāstri!} asked many questions related to {!moksha!}. Swāmishri translated them into Gujarāti and Jāgā Swāmi answered them based on Gadhadā I 54. He explained to the {!Shāstri!} the path to liberation with support from both Gadhadā II 54 and Gadhadā III 2.\r\n[S.M. : 1/206]

7828.t:
04 May 1964, Vāsnā Kotariyā. 
After breakfast, during the morning discourse, Yogiji Mahārāj explained Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 55. He said, “When one stays together with the {!Sant!}, then what are unfavourable circumstances?”
“The {!Sant!} is pure; however, it is bad company which causes one’s mind to become polluted. People engage in negative talks. If a great action is being carried out and someone utters even a single negative word, then the action fails! We must develop the highest level of firmness. We want to be successful. Instil this thought in your soul and develop conviction, fraternity and oneness. One attains great merits and strength by doing this. If one does not follow commands, then one’s resolve will decrease. If one perceives a fault in a devotee of God and it impacts one, it is due to sins committed in one’s past life. One must remain alert, ever ready and think that ‘I want to burn these thoughts to ashes.’ Remain courageous in this way. Remain alert like the police. If the police do not regulate the traffic, then cars will have accidents and the police officer would be suspended. Similarly, if one perceives flaws in other devotees of God, Mahārāj will remove one from Satsang. If one does not perceive flaws, then he will not regress. One who understands this much will understand the essence of all 262 Vachanāmruts. Therefore do not allow oneself to think negatively.” 
[Brahmaswarup Yogiji Mahārāj: 3/632]

7978.t:
02 June 1965, Adās. 
During the evening discourse at the house of Chunibhāi, Yogiji Mahārāj had Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 56 read and said, “The four types of devotee, {!ārta!}, {!jignāsu, arthārthi!} and {!gnāni!} all have the same conviction but their understanding differs. Why is a {!gnāni!} the best out of these? He behaves as {!brahmaswarup!}, not as the body. Whereas, desires and imperfections remain in the other three.
“When one perceives flaws in others, then imperfections remain within. To keep desires other than God is a big flaw. Flaws even remain as a result of his own virtues, if one thinks, ‘There is no one who possesses the same level of detachment as me.’ This is arrogance; it is a grave flaw and he will not progress.
“On the other hand, [a true aspirant] will not remain complacent, but will continue to serve. He keeps strength of his thought. One who is humble is liked by all. To tolerate is the characteristic of saintliness. Do not keep even an iota of arrogance. Chunibhāi Master is one such person who is humble. He performs a lot of service. One must look within one’s heart. Ego is one and the masters are many. That is where the problem lies.
“Arrogance may appear good from the outside, but when difficulties arise, then one feels, ‘I cannot cope with this.’ If one does not have arrogance, then his devotion may not be apparent. One who is humble is powerful. One who is humble is the best. If you shout at children, their minds are not affected. Similarly, one should act in the same way as a child, putting one’s ego aside.” 
[Y.M. : 4/73]

8110.t:
Samvat 1992, in the month of second Bhādarvā, a grand {!pārāyan!} was held in Amdāvād in the auspicious presence of Shāstriji Mahārāj. Arjunbhāi Ranchhodbhāi Chāvdā, who was familiar with Akshar-Purushottam Upāsanā, came for the {!kathā!}. He had listened to talks of great {!sādhus!} from Junagadh, such as Nārandāsji, Tyāgvallabhdāsji, and Dharmaprasāddāsji.
Once, Arjunbhāi went for {!darshan!} to the {!Junā!} Swāminārāyan {!Mandir!} in Gondal. In the assembly, Gadhadā I 62 was being read. He asked Nārandās Swāmi, “If the redemptive attributes, such as {!satya, shauch!}, etc. are imbibed by a Sant, can that Sant be called Bhagwān’s form?”
Nārandās Swāmi, who had received Gunātitānand Swāmi’s grace, said, “Certainly, whoever possesses these attributes is the form of Bhagwān.”
While listening to Swāmishri’s pure speech in Amdāvād, Arjunbhāi recalled the former dialog with Nārandās Swāmi many years prior and realized that Shāstriji Mahārāj is indeed the manifest form of Bhagwān.
Later, he asked Shāstriji Mahārāj many questions. Swāmishri answered his questions and said, “I want to explain the principles of a few Vachanāmruts during the {!samaiyo!} in Bochāsan.” Arjunbhāi had gone to Bochāsan and solidified the belief that the 39 redemptive attributes are present in Shāstriji Mahārāj. He was overjoyed having found the truth that he was seeking after so many years.
[S.M. : 2/11]

8135.t: After reading Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 63, Gunātitānand Swāmi talked extensively on the glory of God: “The {!jiva!} remains weak because the glory of God is not understood as stated here.” \r\n[S.V. : 1/305]

8137.t: After reading Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 63, Gunātitānand Swāmi talked extensively on the glory of God: “The {!jiva!} remains weak because the glory of God is not understood as stated here. Lust, greed, taste, attachment and ego are all like the ocean, but they will become small like the footprints of a cow by God’s grace. This is the glory of God; so never allow the {!jiva!} to become weak. Lakshmiji and God are in our service just as parents are naturally in the service of their children. Whatever we wish will happen. However, we have knowingly suppressed your powers as this attainment is rare even for great deities.”\r\n[S.V. : 1/305]

8143.t: “What is meant by the manifest form of Brahma”\r\nYogiji Mahārāj explained the answer lucidly: “Gunātitānand Swāmi is the manifest form of Brahma. According to Vachanāmruts Gadhadā I 63 and Gadhadā I 71, Akshar is essential in Satsang, but this Akshar was not revealed. Shriji Mahārāj himself stayed in Bhādra for over a month and sang the glory of Akshar and himself stated that Gunātitānand Swāmi is Akshar. Thereafter, during a festival at Junagadh Mandir, Gopalānand Swāmi had the devotees from Bhādra narrate these incidents. In this way, the concept of Akshar remained secret within the Satsang and only a few people were aware of it. This was not discussed in public until Sadguru Gopalānand Swāmi revealed it. That Aksharbrahma is immortal and is the form of the manifest Brahma.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 2/15]

8296.t:
July 1969, Gondal. 
During the discourse, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “The {!Satpurush!} always wishes for our betterment. He breaks the attachment we have towards this world as the affairs of this world are binding. As the {!jiva!} becomes entangled in worldly affairs, it forgets the true purpose of why it has come on this earth. The {!Sant!} awakens one from this slumber.” 
“There were two {!satsangi!} brothers in a village. One was staunch and the other had a mundane understanding. When the younger brother [an ordinary {!satsangi!}] passed away, he became a ghost. The older brother [a staunch {!satsangi!}] would sit in the {!mandir!} daily and spend his time engrossed in {!Satsang!}. When the older brother was about to pass away, Mahārāj came to collect him in a divine vehicle. When this happened, the younger brother [as a ghost] came and stood there. The older brother was attached to his younger brother and looked at him. Mahārāj saw this and removed him from the divine vehicle. They both became ghosts.” 
“The family members saw him. They said, ‘You said you would go to Mahārāj’s abode, so why are you now a ghost?’ He said, ‘I was attached to my younger brother so Mahārāj removed me from the divine vehicle and I became a ghost. Do not worry, I will not harass anyone; however, when you next serve a {!sādhu!} food, please place two lādus in this plate so we can partake of the {!prasād!}.’”
“One day, Bālmukund Swāmi of Junāgadh came to visit their house. He saw them and said, ‘How come you are still here? Go to Badrikāshram.’ With these words, he sent them both to Badrikāshram.”
“In this way, even if a little attachment remains, Mahārāj will not take one to his abode. So make sure no attachments remain.”
[Y.M. : 5/386]

8299.t: 03 June 1965, Adās. \r\nDuring the morning discourse at the house of Chunibhāi, Yogiji Mahārāj explained Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 67. He said, “If one perceives virtues in the {!Satpurush!}, then such virtues will be acquired. If we sit to take a photo and shut our eyes, what will the outcome be? How we look in the photo will be dependent on our posture. Similarly, one becomes as one sees the {!Satpurush!}. One should eradicate the barrier between him and us by understanding him to be the all-knower and flawless. Do as he says as this is how the virtues he possesses can be acquired. Nirgun Swāmi would read this Vachanāmrut a lot. He would not let anyone get up while he was reading it.”\r\n[Y.M. : 4/75]

8300.t:
10 September 1967, Mumbai. 
During the morning discourse, whilst explaining Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 76, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “What great {!divyabhāv!} Mahārāj had! That is why he said to Muktānand Swāmi ‘That answer is correct.’ 
If one starts to think, ‘I know everything and am doing everything’ then virtues will not enter such a person. Only if he repents within will virtues sprout.”
[Y.M. : 4/526]

8301.t: After narrating Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 67 from memory, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “To attain the virtues of the {!Motāpurush!}, one should become a humble servant, tolerate any misery due to one’s own flaws and maintain focus on his [Motāpurush’s] endless virtues. However, one will never attain the virtues of the Motāpurush through one’s own perceived knowledge and pretence of being over-wise.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 9/50]

8302.t: After reading Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 67, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “How can a spiritual aspirant acquire the virtues of the {!Motāpurush!}? Muktānand Swāmi answered the question, but he omitted the word ‘remorse’. Remorse is a great tool on the spiritual path. If one understands oneself to be extremely insignificant before God and his {!Bhakta!} and sings the glory of God and the {!Motāpurush!}, one will acquire all their virtues. If one possesses the following things, one will certainly acquire the virtues of the {!Motāpurush!}: considers oneself to be insignificant, maintains a sense of servitude and understands the glory of the {!Motāpurush!}.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 24/46]

8304.t: 23 March 1959, Vasana.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “Everyone wishes to acquire the virtues of the {!Satpurush!}, but they do not repent within their hearts. When one does so and recognises one’s own flaws, such virtues will be acquired. The {!Satpurush!} is the source of wisdom and yet we say he is not wise. One should keep {!gunātitbhav!} in whatever the {!Satpurush!} does. In this way if one keeps full divinity in the {!Sant!} then one will acquire his virtues.”\r\n[Y.M. : 2/522]

8305.t:
26 March 1956, Sārangpur.
Yogiji Mahārāj said, “When can one be said to possess a rapport with the {!Motāpurush!}? If one acts as per Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 62, that is when it can be said that one has a full rapport with [the {!Motāpurush!}] For these virtues to be acquired, one must imbibe Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 67 in one’s life. One should feel repentance [due to one’s own flaws] and think, ‘I do not understand anything.’ If one comes to the {!Motāpurush!} without any preconceived resolutions in one’s mind, then one will acquire the virtues of the {!Satpurush!}. We do not feel such repentance hence:
{!Am be buti, tam be buti, buti bhelambhelā, chhāyā vinānu jhād batāvo, to tum guru ham chelā.!}
[Meaning: I'm clever, as are you, we are both wise; so show me a tree that does not give shade, and I will consider you to be my guru.]
Do not act over-wise in front of the {!Motāpurush!}. Those that have tried to do so in front of Mahārāj and Shāstriji Mahārāj were left behind [on the spiritual path]. Acting overwise means not setting aside the whims of your mind. If one thinks, ‘I will only accept that you are great if you show me a tree without shade’ then how will one acquire the virtues of the {!Satpurush!}?”
[Y.M. : 2/42]

8307.t: October 1960, Bhādra.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “Remorse is like patching together two ends. However, such a person would still be affected by adverse circumstances. Repentance is like a smooth joint. One will not find any rough edges. He will not suffer from adverse circumstances and will acquire virtues [of the {!Satpurush!}].”\r\n[Y.M. : 3/125]

8311.t: 27 July 1957, Mumbai. \r\nDuring the discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “All the 262 Vachanāmruts are excellent, but this Vachanāmrut is one that can be perfected; if its principles are imbibed in one’s heart, then one will never develop {!nāstik!} feelings and one’s strong conviction in God will become firm.\r\n[Y.M. : 2/275]

8312.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Harikrishnadās was a {!kothāri!} in Sārangpur. He said to Shāstriji Mahārāj, ‘There’s no sugar available in Sārangpur so let us not do {!annakut!}.’ However, Shāstriji Mahārāj had great affection for {!Thākorji!} and replied back, ‘Buy half kilo of sugar with 1 rupee, but do {!annakut!}.’” \r\nYogiji Mahārāj continued, “I heard this with my own ears. Do not put less in {!thāl!} [to save money]. Always use the best ghee. {!Santo!}, do not believe the {!murtis!} are mere paintings on canvas. The {!murtis!} are Shriji Mahārāj himself. We should do {!pujā!} and {!ārti!}. To gain the fruit of {!pujā, ārti!} and {!thāl!} one should perform these activities with the understanding that Shāstriji Mahārāj is manifest and sitting with us. And you will feel that God does exist [{!āstik-bhāv!} will develop]. However, if one offers prostrations with a hidden {!nāstik-bhāv!} [feeling that God does not exist], then Mahārāj will protest and you will not be liberated.”\r\n[Y.M. : 4/211]

8313.t: 30 May 1965, Bochāsan. \r\nAfter pujā, Yogiji Mahārāj instructed Harshadbhāi [Dave] to read Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 68 and said, “There is no doubt that God resides in the {!Sant!}.
