This flaw of ego remained even in those considered great, because the understanding of the {!Sant’s!} greatness had not entered their {!jiva!}. To highlight his dislike of ego and to make devotees humble, Mahārāj asked great {!sādhus!} such as Brahmānand Swāmi, Shukānand Swāmi and Surā Khāchar, ‘What flaw do you possess which would make you suffer a setback?’ They replied, ‘Mahārāj, we have the flaw of egotism. As a result, if a {!sādhu!} of equal status insults us, we become disturbed.’” [Gadhadā III 28]
Kothāri Bechar Bhagat gathered the significance of all these discourses and said to Bhagatji, “I am ready to do exactly as you say.” Bhagatji told him to ask Kothāri Govardhanbhāi for forgiveness. Kothāri Bechar Bhagat went to Govardhanbhāi, prostrated to him, and asked for forgiveness. Bhagatji then said to Govardhanbhāi, “Please keep the {!kothāri!} in Vartāl by any means.”
“We can keep him there as a {!sādhu!},” Govardhanbhāi replied.
Bhagatji agreed to this. Bechar Bhagat was initiated as a {!sādhu!} by Āchārya Mahārāj and named Mahāpurushdās Swāmi.
[B.M. : 188]

12111.t: 22 March 1966, Mumbai. \r\nDuring the morning {!maṅgaḷ!} discourses whilst discoursing on Vachanāmrut Loyā 17, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Perfect Vachanāmrut Loyā 17. Each line should be imbibed in our lives. If one’s foundation becomes strong, the mind will not desire anything. Do it today. This is very simple. You, Kishorebhāi! Have you memorised it? It is not for householders? But now it is. This is the sanctified Vachanāmrut of [Gunātitānand] Swāmi. With the grace of Shāstriji Mahārāj and Bhagatji Mahārāj, it will be perfected.” \r\n[Y.M. : 4/236]

12113.t: Explaining Vachanāmruts Gadhadā I 55 and Gadhadā I 57, Yogiji Mahārāj asked, “What are the most extraordinary means to attain liberation?” He responded, “The answer is understanding the glory and knowledge of God’s form. One should understand and identify the {!Sādhu!} to be God-realised, within whom God resides in totality and thus maintain constant {!divyabhāv!} in him. To understand his glory and remain in a state of bliss is true knowledge. Understand that it is through his wish that the rain falls, the sun and moon rise and set. According to Vachanāmruts Gadhadā I 27 and Loyā 17, if one fully understands God’s glory in all aspects, the sense organs are not led astray and are permanently blunted. However, one should not do as they please under the pretext that, ‘I have found God, so what can harm me?’ Behaving in this manner is contrary to the premise of understanding the knowledge of God’s greatness. The true definition of having the association of God means obeying his commands and staunchly adhering to the moral and spiritual instructions.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 2/6]

12114.t: Discoursing on Vachanāmrut Loyā 17, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “How can one remain good even if circumstances are adverse? One shouldn’t have affection for just two people and dislike another two. Just as one has affection for one’s wife and children, one should have affection for all the devotees of God. Only then can one remain good.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 24/274]

12405.t: 7 August 1955, Tororo, Uganda. \r\nSpeaking on Vachanāmrut Loyā 17, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Gunātitānand Swāmi passed away in Samvat Year 1923 (1867 CE). From Samvat Year 1920 (1864 CE) onwards, he would have this Vachanāmrut read. Every single day for three years, he made sure this Vachanāmrut was read aloud. We all have to perfect this. \r\n[Y.M. : 1/615]

12410.t: 25 November 1962, Bochāsan. \r\nDuring the discourses on Sunday, Yogiji Mahārāj said to Mavji Bhagat, “Perfect Vachanāmrut Loyā 17. Gunātitānand Swāmi had this Vachanāmrut read continuously for three years.” \r\n[Y.M. : 3/407]

12420.t: 8 December 1961, Mumbai. \r\nDuring the morning {!maṅgaḷ!} discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Vachanāmrut Loyā 17 should be read and discoursed upon every week. Spare two hours. [Gunātitānand] Swāmi used to have this read even in rural villages. Internal conflict can only be eradicated through knowledge. \r\n[Y.M. : 3/251]

12421.t: 6 August 1965, Mumbai. \r\nDuring the morning {!maṅgaḷ!} discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj asked, “Who has yet to memorise Vachanāmrut Loyā 17? Before sleeping, before eating, it should always be recited.”\r\n[Y.M. : 4/96]

12427.t: 10 July 1961, Mumbai.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj wrote in a letter of blessings for Swāminārāyan Prakāsh, “The important Vachanāmruts – Loyā 17, Kāriyāni 1, Gadhadā II 59 and Gadhadā II 28 – should all be perfected.”\r\n[Y.M. : 3/206]

12433.t: While having Vachanāmrut Panchālā 1 read, Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “When can we say that such thoughts have been attained? When nothing comes into our focus except for God and Akshardhām, then it can be said that the thought has truly been attained.”\r\n[S.V. : 8/165]

12443.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “One with such attachment beholds God continuously. So, if one has this union [with God and his {!Sādhu!}], then it is fine, and when it is not present, then one needs {!sānkhya!}. And when one realizes the perishable nature of everything up to Prakruti, one can live without hindrance.” Based upon this, Vachanāmrut Panchālā 2 entitled ‘{!Sānkhya!} and {!Yoga!}’ was read. Swāmi then added, “For this reason, learn this.”\r\n[S.V. : 6/85]

12453.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Profound love for the {!Satpurush!} is the greatest of all means [to have darshan of one’s {!ātmā!}]. When does one’s love become unified with the {!ātmā!}? The definition of unifying love with the {!ātmā!} is when one is able to first remove one’s own worldly desires and then apply this love to the {!Satpurush!}. One should contemplate on the words of Vachanāmrut Panchālā 3 to understand this principle.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 6/28]

12455.t:
After celebrating the Chaitri festival of 1879 on 6 April 1879 (Chaitra sud 15, VS 1935), Acharya Mahārāj proceeded to Ānand accompanied with Pavitrānand Swāmi. Bhagatji Mahārāj also attended this festival and he stayed nearby for two months in Vartāl.
There was a custom from the time of Bhagwān Swāminārāyan of chanting the {!dhun!} of ‘Nar-Nārāyan, Swāminārāyan’ after the evening {!ārti!}. Some of the newer sādhus and devotees had, however, changed this tradition and started chanting the ‘Swāminārāyan, Swāminārāyan’ {!dhun!} instead. Pavitrānand Swāmi insisted on the old tradition and chanted ‘Nar-Nārāyan, Swāminārāyan’ on his own.
Once, during {!dhun!}, Pavitrānand Swāmi shouted, “Why are you all not singing the traditional {!dhun!} that was started in the time of Mahārāj?”
“Before a camel dies, it still looks towards Mārwād,” [Implying that it cannot leave its habits despite facing death] boldly replied Aksharpurush Swāmi.
This blatant insult hurt Pavitrānand Swāmi badly. As no one, not even Acharya Mahārāj had stopped the sādhus or told them off, he felt that everyone had consented to this. This incident shocked him so much that he fell ill. The following day, Pavitrānand Swāmi returned to Vartāl from Ānand with his attendant {!sādhu!}. He said to his attendant {!sādhu!}, “Please go and see if you can find a great {!sadguru!}. If you can, please ask him to come and discourse to me.” The attendant {!sādhu!} went out to find Prāgji Bhakta. He relayed this to Pavitrānand Swāmi and said, “Prāgji Bhakta is speaking to a group of {!sādhud!} and devotees in the assembly. I will call him if you want.”
Pavitrānand Swāmi had Prāgji Bhakta called and requested, “Prāgji, please discourse some important Vachanāmruts so that I can be at peace.”
Bhagatji knew what had taken place and asked Vignāndās Swāmi to read Vachanāmrut Panchālā 3. He then began his explanation of this Vachanāmrut. Pavitrānand Swāmi was delighted by Bhagatji’s explanation and said, “Prāgji, what you have said is correct. The only true {!sādhu!} I have seen is Gunātitānand Swāmi. I have had {!darshan!} of the 500 {!paramhansas!}; however, none of them can be compared to Gunātitānand Swāmi in terms of saintliness. Truly, I have seen only one like him…
“Prāgji Bhakta, undoubtedly, you have gained the unique pleasure of such a sādhu because you have pleased him by serving him by thought, word, and deed. He showered his abundant grace upon you and helped you to perfect {!ekāntik dharma!}. I am totally convinced about this because there is no other devotee as humble as you. I recall that in the year 1865 (VS 1921), I decided to never ever sit with you again. You replied, ‘If Gunātitānand Swāmi is Mul Akshar, I want to sit with you and discourse.’ Now the tables have turned. You have so much authority, that you can command me. This is all due to Gunātitānand Swāmi…”
“Prāgji, I experience infinite peace by your {!darshan!} because you are sustaining the true succession of Gunātit.”
[B.M. : 175]

12460.t:
After celebrating a {!samaiyo!} in Bochāsan in Samvat 1989, Shāstriji Mahārāj graced Gānā due to Harmānbhāi’s request. Maganbhāi Narsinhabhāi Patel was with Shāstriji Mahārāj. After two days, Shāstriji Mahārāj went to Rās with Harmānbhāi and Maganbhāi and spent four days there. One morning, the two came for Shāstriji Mahārāj’s {!darshan!}. Shāstriji Mahārāj laughed and asked, “What did you two talk about at night?”
The two were astonished to hear this question because they had talked till 2am and had decided not to tell Shāstriji Mahārāj about their conversation. If Shāstriji Mahārāj tells us what we talked about, then they could solidify the belief that Shriji Mahārāj is manifest through Shāstriji Mahārāj.
Shāstriji Mahārāj gave a suggestive look and said, “Today, I want to rid you of the doubts that you have remaining in recognizing the manifest form of Bhagwān.”
He asked for the Vachanāmrut and had Panchālā 4 read, “The ways of Bhagwān and the {!Sant!} are the same. Recognizing them and attaching one’s self to them is the extraordinary means to liberation.”
In this way, Shāstriji Mahārāj solidified their conviction in the manifest form of Bhagwān.
[S.M. : 1/635]

12461.t: After having Vachanāmrut Panchālā 4 read, Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “If [one] has cultivated firm faith like this and realized God’s divine traits and human traits as one and decided, ‘The joy experienced in Akshardhām is greater than that experienced in all the other abodes’, what difficulty remains in following the codes of conduct? And how can one lapse? Once would not. If one truly has that {!nishchay!}, then even if one tries to to lapse in one’s code of conduct, one would not be able to do so.”\r\n[Aksharāmrut : 4/9]

12469.t: January 1962, Mumbai.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj says, “{!Nirdoshbhāv!} remains for those who praise [us]. But if [someone] snatches one’s food away and even if he does not let one eat, [not being affected by it] is true {!nirdoshbhāv!}. He becomes {!ekāntik!} and attains first place... If [we] keep our eye on the target, then day by day [we will experience] uplifting joy. Food might be really good but if one has been suffering from a fever for seven days, then he does not enjoy it. Similarly, if an illness in the form of {!manushyabhāv!} arises, then happiness is not experienced.”\r\n[Y.M. : 3/277]

12470.t:
In May of 1963, Yogiji Mahārāj came to Panchālā. In the {!darbār!} of Panchālā, Yogiji Mahārāj held a {!pārāyan!} on the Vachanāmrut. One day, during the {!pārāyan!}, Yogiji Mahārāj was responding to letters. Panchala 4 was being read: Muni Bāwā asked a question to Brahmānand Swāmi, “Initially, one may have the conviction of Bhagwān and may engage in worship and remembrance; but later, on seeing the human-like actions of Bhagwān, doubts arise in that conviction. What is the cause of this?”
Brahmānand Swāmi then began to answer that question but was unable to do so satisfactorily.
Then, having thought for some time, Shriji Mahārāj spoke…
After this much was read, Yogiji Mahārāj stopped writing letters and said, “Muni Bāwā asked this question because Mahārāj had performed human-like actions. Therefore, Mahārāj thought for a while before answering.”
[Y.M. : 3/479]

12474.t:
In 1881 [VS 1937], Acharya Vihārilālji Mahārāj sent Bhagatji Mahārāj to Nadiād with Bhumānand Swāmi. While Bhagatji and Bhumānand Swāmi were in Nadiād, someone asked a question in the assembly about {!avatārs!} [incarnations] and the {!avatāri!} [source of the incarnations]. No one was able to provide a satisfactory answer, so Bhumānand Swāmi said, “Call Prāgji Bhakta here; he will be able to answer the question.”
Bhagatji had Panchālā 6 read and then explained, “Shriji Mahārāj has spoken about his own form in this Vachanāmrut, using the guise of Shri Krishna. He has said, ‘It has become apparent that there has not been any {!avatār!} as powerful as Shri Krishna, because Shri Krishna exhibited in various ways the characteristics of all of the other countless forms of himself’.”
“The authors of the {!shāstras!} have also agreed on this. This is evident because the form of Parabrahma Purushottam has been described in these {!shāstras!} as powerful, miraculous, brilliant, valiant, and lustrous as well as possessing many other characteristics. The Vedas also sing the glory of that form. The power, miracles, lustre, and characteristics of the form of Purushottam were seen in Shri Krishna and not seen or even heard of in the previous incarnations. At that time, there was no form as powerful as his and hence everyone proclaimed that Shri Krishna is the Purushottam Parabrahma described in the {!shāstras!}.”
“However, Shriji Mahārāj also exhibited many divine exploits during his stay on earth. He manifested the 24 incarnations from his own form and then merged them back into his own form. He displayed these extraordinary miraculous powers to Parvatbhāi, Swarupānand Swāmi, and Vyāpkānand Swāmi. Moreover, he granted {!samādhi!} to numerous spiritual aspirants; and during that {!samādhi!}, he showed them their chosen deities in their respective abodes. He also made tens of thousands of people free from the bondage of the sense pleasures and attached them to his form. There are those who saw Mahārāj’s life with their own eyes. There are also those who have heard about his life from the eminent people in Satsang. By faith in the words of these people, it is obvious that the characteristics of Purushottam Parabrahma mentioned in the {!shāstras!} are present in Shriji Mahārāj. Therefore, Shriji Mahārāj is Parabrahma Purushottam. Mahārāj has further revealed in this Vachanāmrut, ‘That {!avatār!} [Shri Krishna] reigns as supreme. Only some powers have been revealed through the other {!avatārs!}. This {!avatār!} [referring to himself] however, has revealed all divine powers and strength.’ Therefore, Mahārāj’s incarnation is the greatest of all. Mahārāj mentions further in this Vachanāmrut, that one should keep faith towards the {!pratyaksh!} [manifest] form of Shri Krishna. This is because only this [manifest] incarnation is supreme and only this [manifest] incarnation has displayed all of the divine powers. Thus, Shriji Mahārāj alone is supreme, Parabrahma Purushottam, and the cause of all incarnations.”
Bhagatji’s precise explanation totally convinced all the {!sādhus!} and devotees who were present in the assembly that the source of all incarnations was none other than Shriji Mahārāj himself.
[B.M. : 180]

12485.t: After having Vachanāmrut ā 7 read, Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “By understanding this manifest God to be free from all flaws, nothing remains to be done. If miracles are witnessed, one woulr not be able to remain in line – as what happened to Shekhji – and one would become mad. Therefore, deficiencies may still appear to be present. By understanding God as flaw-free, one also becomes flaw-free. The flaws that are experienced are of the material elements and only God is truly flaw-free. Also, place and time do not affect God, but they do affect the {!jiva!}. Since the body is formed from the {!prārabdha karmas!}, when impure {!prārabdha karmas!} bear fruit, place and time do have an impact. But by knowing the form of God as flaw-free, one is also in the process of becoming flaw-free.” \r\n[S.V.: 5/124]

12487.t: Yogiji Mahārāj was asked a question, “How can one become {!brahmarup!} whilst still alive?”\r\nYogiji Mahārāj replied, “It is said in Vachanāmrut Panchālā 7 that Akshardhām is the form of God –  {!‘Dhāmnā svena sadā nirastakuhakam’!}. In accordance with this, Gunātit is Mul Akshar, an absolute true form. Mahārāj remains supremely above all in his distinct {!vyatirek!} form. Only by understanding the glory of Gunātit can one understand the complete glory of Mahārāj as he exactly is. By associating with Gunātit, one becomes {!brahmarup!}; only then does one become worthy of serving Parabrahma.\r\n[Yogi Vāni 25/43]

12488.t: 5 March 1863, Junagadh.\r\nIn Samvat 1919, Sādhu Vishnuprasāddāsji, Sādhu Hariswarupdāsji, Sādhu Hariprasāddāsji, etc. had come to Junagadh from Vartāl to celebrate Fuldol. At that time, Gunātitānand Swāmi was speaking about Mahārāj’s opinion and doctrine during the festival. Explaining this topic, he said, “Previously, there were many types of Mahārāj’s rājipo and in the first phase: eating tasteless balls of food, wearing jute cloth, keeping a distance far from villages such that one couldn’t even hear a dog bark, studying, building {!mandirs!}, etc. So, there were many types of rājipo. Right now, what does rājipo lie in? In the Vachanāmrut titled 'Māyā of a Magician', God’s form has been said to be flawless; Mahārāj’s form should also be understood accordingly and in the same way, the form of the {!Sant!} should be understood. If the wishes of God are abided by and the company of a true {!Sādhu!} is sought, then Mahārāj is happy, happy and happy on that person.”\r\n[B.M.: 90]

12489.t: 5 September 1956, Sukhpur.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj says, “When God assumes a form on Earth, he acts like a human, as per Panchālā 7. In this, if we become the offspring of the magician, only then would we understand the magic of the magician; but if we are part of the audience, we would not be able to figure anything out. Similarly, if one comes into association with God and the {!Motāpurush!}, only then would one be able to recognise the form of God as it is. Other than that, one cannot recognise him.”\r\n[Y.M.: 2/109]

12526.t: November 1951, Gondal. \r\nOnce when Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 4 was being read, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “I have perfected this Vachanāmrut. When I read this Vachanāmrut for the very first time, at that time I thought that as long as one is attracted to the enticing {!panchvishays!}, one has not realised God’s glory. Since that very moment, I renounced any such enticements [forever].” \r\n[Y.M. : 1/355]

12528.t: During the morning {!mangal!} discourse, Yogiji Mahārāj spoke briefly on Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 4, “For one who understands the greatness of God and the {!Sant!}, then just as the partridge bird constantly looks at the moon, similarly, one continuously looks for service. Everyone performs service when they are told to, but one who looks for and does service on their own accord is great. One who understands greatness cannot stay without offering performing devotion.”\r\n[Y.M. : 6/461]

12535.t:
12 March 1963, Mumbai. 
Once, Yogiji Mahārāj said in Kapolvadi, “...One will only gain entry into Akshardhām if one is chaste in one's conviction. All demigods are due to this God… If one feels confused, one should contemplate on Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 16 and Gadhadā II 5.
“One will only develop affinity for the {!Sant!} after understanding the true nature of God's form; otherwise, one will end up falling off [the path of liberation]. One should affirm the nature of the true form of God in one’s mind, after which one is sure to experience insurmountable joy. It is others that are the ones running after scraps, while we experience ultimate joy.
“Mahārāj will explain [this concept] to us through his inspiration. One should stick to one place. ‘If there are indeed two Gods, they will sort things out between them; what are we to gain from that?’ One should not even think along these lines. If one has truly understood this and subsequently imbibed it into their life, then all misunderstandings are cleared. One can only truly understand through faith… since you have affinity [towards me], renounce the whims of your mind.”
[Y.M. : 3/448]

12537.t: After having the Vachanāmruts Gadhadā II 5 and Vartāl 13 read, Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “Keep your {!indriyas!} and {!antahkaran!} in your {!hrudayakash!} so your focus remains on God. You may not realize while alive, but endeavours do not go in vain. When you leave this body you will see [the fruits].”\r\n[S.V. : 5/152]

12538.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi says, “Scriptures describe God as unbiased, but that is not [strictly] true. Since, God belongs to the devotees, but not to non-devotees. Therefore, he is not unbiased.”\r\n[S.V. : 1/251]

12554.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Two Vachanāmruts are worth imbibing in one’s life. Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 7 and III 11: An understanding like that of Sitāji. One may not understand all the Vachanāmruts, but one should always refer to their favourite Vachanāmruts [of their spiritual inclination] and imbibe their words.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 29/45]

12555.t:
November 1888, Bhādrod.
During the month of Kartik, Samvat Year 1945, a total of twelve {!sādhus!} and {!pārshads!}, including Shāstriji Mahārāj, were forced to leave from Vartāl because they were propagating the {!mahimā!} of Prāgji Bhakta. 
Following this, this group of sādhus went to associate with Bhagatji Mahārāj and stayed in the village of Bhādrod, near Mahuva. 
One morning, after they had bathed and performed pujā, Bhagatji said, “Today, everyone should read out the respective Vachanāmruts which match their personal inclinations.”
Vignāndas Swāmi read Gadhadā II 54, Bechar Bhagat read Gadhadā I 54, Yagnapurushdasji read Gadhadā II 7, Keshavprasad Purani read Gadhadā I 36, Purushottam Swāmi read Sārangpur 7, Nārāyancharan Swāmi read Sārangpur 10, and Shankar Bhagat read Amdāvād 2. 
[B.M. : 353]

12556.t: 28 December 1961, Mumbai.\r\nAddressing the {!sādhus!} during the morning {!maṅgaḷ!} discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “If Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 7 is perfected, then all the Vachanāmruts are perfected.”\r\n[Y.M. : 3/266]

12557.t: After having Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 7 narrated, Yogiji Mahārāj said, ‘What are the qualities of one who possesses saintliness? To endure, tolerate and be powerful, yet remain humble. Muktānand Swāmi asked Mahārāj about the means one should adopt to eradicate vicious natures and Mahārāj replied, ‘If one intensely serves a great {!sādhu!} and obediently perseveres in their observance of the injunctions of God, then God will look upon one with an eye of compassion and one’s vicious natures will be eradicated immediately.’ Muktānand Swāmi was a {!sādhu!} who was endowed with the superlative virtues of saintliness, yet Mahārāj still referred to a great {!Sant!}. Who is that great {!Sant!}? It is Gunātit. What is intense service? It is to perform service beyond limits. One would diligently obey any command without any doubts. For example, one may be sweeping up rubbish and be commanded by the {!Satpurush!} to learn Sanskrit. One then learns and becomes a great scholar, but is then commanded to sweep up rubbish again. One would do so without asking any questions or harbouring any doubts. By performing service according to the words of the {!Sant!}, one earns the grace of God. The key point here is that only by serving the {!Sant!}, does one receive the grace of God and has their vicious natures eradicated.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 24/128]

12558.t: Yogiji Mahārāj was once asked a question, “How can one eradicate one’s own flaws?”\r\nYogiji Mahārāj replied, “The answer lies in Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 7. If a person lacks {!vairāgya!}, but intensely serves the {!Sant!}, and obediently perseveres in one’s observance of the injunctions of God, then God will look upon one with an eye of compassion, and one’s vicious natures will be eradicated. In comparison, if one were to endeavour in other ways, those vicious natures may be eradicated, but after a great deal of time and effort; either in this life or in later lives. By intensely performing service [of the {!Sant!}], one receives the grace of God. This method is the only way to receive such grace.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 25/20]

12571.t: 25 January 1964, Mumbai. \r\nAfter Vachanāmruts Gadhadā II 7 and Gadhadā II 8 were read in the morning, Yogiji Mahārāj further explained, “A hallmark quality of saintliness is to tolerate. One should become happy from within if insulted. One can only perform true service if one maintains the feeling of considering all to be free of flaws. One fully dedicates one’s mind and body for this cause.\r\n[Y.M. : 3/586]

12589.t: 21 June 1968, Gondal. \r\nDuring the afternoon discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “One wants to eradicate one’s vicious natures, yet one lacks detachment. It is a bit like saying that one wants to rid oneself of their hunger, yet one lacks the desire to eat. Muktānand Swāmi was pointed in the direction of the {!Gunātit Sant!}. Who is to be served according to this talk? The {!Sant!}. Who looks upon one with grace? God. [The {!Sant!}] would ask one to lift heavy stones on a day of fasting. When Shāstriji Mahārāj was present, one would have to engage in strenuous service even on a fasting day. One would have to toil hard all day. The grace of Shāstriji Mahārāj would only be gained when all the {!sādhus!} worked tirelessly. Shāstriji Mahārāj blessed all of them, ‘Go, you will now become free of all flaws.’ However, if one sleeps all day, then one does not become a worthy recipient of grace. We had once gone to Bhavnagar for a month. We used to adhere to the vow of not sleeping on the day of fasting. The {!sādhus!} of the Junagadh [{!Junā Mandir!}] used to act accordingly. It goes without question that one thus becomes worthy of receiving the grace [of God].”\r\n[Y.M. : 5/137]

12590.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Which actions of ours do you perceive {!manushyabhāv!} in? If I desire, I can sleep on the floor and my body would not ache. I would bathe with cold water. I would not eat. I would not allow my arms and legs to be cared for and yet nothing would happen. Hence, we might reveal what seems to be body-conscious traits, but one should not believe these. If we did not reveal them, how would you have an opportunity to serve?\r\n“As per Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 7 and II 59, one only excels by performing service. That is why we offer you the opportunity for service by caring for our arms and legs, bathing us and cooking our food. Otherwise if you sat idle, you will never excel. If you wish, I will not ask you to perform any service. One should always maintain {!divyabhāv!}, but one cannot excel without performing service. Do you all want to see a blaze of light? If so, I can ask Swāmi (Shāstriji Mahārāj) to show you a blaze of light, and he will. But then you will become {!sakām!} (have desires to see such things). Hence, it is better to always desire acquiring the spiritually knowledgeable state.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 10/115]

12591.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “When one attains the association of the {!Satpurush!} and perseveres in performing service as per his command, one’s worldly desires are eradicated. Only then does one become free from worldly desires and attachments. One can become free from worldly desires and attachments through spiritual endeavours, but it is similar to trees - there is no happiness in that [i.e. Trees are unable to act on desires so we may call them {!nirvāsanik!} but they cannot experience the bliss of God and the {!Sant!}]. By adopting the latter method, the sages and ascetics were affected by adverse circumstances. Therefore, in terms of ultimate liberation, it is a completely different matter altogether. To achieve this, one would need to imbibe the teachings of Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II-7.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 22/28]

12594.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 7 talks about God’s eye of compassion. God resides within the {!Sant!} and looks upon one with an eye of compassion.’ Consequently, one’s vicious natures are crushed. If one serves the {!Sant!} as per his commands, one will receive his {!rājipo!}.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 27/95]

12595.t: Shāstriji Mahārāj’s favourite Vachanāmrut is Gadhadā II 7, Yogiji Mahārāj’s favourite is Vachanāmrut III 2 and Pramukh Swāmi Mahārāj’s favourite is Vachanāmrut III 7. \r\n[Yogi Gita Marma : 188]

12605.t: April 1956, Amdāvād.\r\nOne evening, Yogiji Mahārāj explained Vachanāmruts Gadhadā II 7 and Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 8. Senior devotees such as CT Patel, Harshadbhāi, Ambālālbhāi and others were seated there. Swāmishri said, “If one performs service, do it so that no one else finds out, but not for show. This is called service performed in secret. This kind of service will considerably strengthen one spiritually. One’s heart will be filled with the light of realisation and inner peace will be experienced.”\r\n[Y.M. : 2/50]

12644.t:
May 1961, Gondal.
Once, a topic was raised in Gondal, “One’s base natures are eradicated either through the great {!Sant!} in this world or in Shwetdweep.”
At that time, Kumud Bhagat (Rāmcharan Swāmi) asked, “Why did such desirous thoughts sprout in the sages’ minds despite having performed many austerities?”
Yogiji Mahārāj answered by saying, “Only if one perfects Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 7 can one become free from desires.”
“Can one become like so through one’s own efforts?”
Swāmishri answered succinctly, “Yes, one can. However, it is similar to trees - there is no happiness in that [i.e. Trees are unable to act on desires so we may call them {!nirvāsanik!} but they cannot experience the bliss of God and the {!Sant!}].”
Ishwarcharan Swāmi asked, “Why did such adverse circumstances affect the sages?”
Swāmishri replied, “Ultimate liberation is completely unique. One must imbibe Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 7 to achieve that.”
[Y.M. : 3/173]

12657.t:
November 1960, Okhā.
Yogiji Mahārāj said, “One can attain an elevated spiritual state if the {!Sant!} looks upon one with grace.” Based on this, Swāmishri explained the meaning behind Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 7. 
Thereafter, he asked, “What is a characteristic of one whom the {!Satpurush!} has graced and who subsequently is able to act according to the inner wishes [of the {!Satpurush!}]?” 
[Swāmishri himself answered], “One has dedicated one’s mind. One does as the {!Satpurush!} commands, without doubting anything even in the slightest, day in day out. Such a person can be said to have completely dedicated one’s {!ātmā!} [to the {!Satpurush!}]. One would not doubt [the {!Sant!}], even if the {!Sant!} makes one renounce the whims of one’s mind or completely reverses any decisions that one has made.”
[Y.M. : 3/134]

12671.t:
1 April 1970, Mwanza, Tanzania. 
During Swāmishri’s stay at the bungalow of Rāmubhāi, Yogiji Mahārāj had Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 7 read in the afternoon. He then said, “What is a characteristic of one who is truly saintly? To tolerate. Does one tolerate the words, ‘You are very good?’ No! One should tolerate harsh insults such as, ‘You are a dim-witted fool’. This is a true characteristic of saintliness.
“[The state of a poor man] is a bit like saying that one wants to eradicate one’s hunger yet one does not want to eat food. In the same way, one wants to rid oneself of one’s vicious natures yet is lacking incredibly in detachment. Mahārāj shows a third pathway - serving a {!Motāpurush!}. Is there anyone senior to the asker of the question, Muktānand Swāmi? This is despite the fact that he was regarded as one of the most senior throughout Satsang. If one continues to apply their own logic in following the commands of the {!Gunātit Satpurush!}, it cannot be labelled as true service. There are four types of disciples – one serves according to the wishes of the {!Satpurush!}, the second only does what one is shown, the third doubts everything that the {!Satpurush!} says, and the fourth just runs away. The first is 100%, the second 66%, the third 33% and the fourth...well, he is just about pulling along.
“What is intense service? To understand that the {!Motāpurush!} is free of all flaws… just as the body has achieved oneness with the {!ātmā!}, one should not keep any distance from the {!Satpurush!}. Only then will one become worthy of imbibing the qualities of the {!Satpurush!}.”
[Y.M. : 6/120]

12686.t: In 1972, about 700 devotees toured south India with Pramukh Swāmi Mahārāj and other {!sādhus!}. Every day in the morning, {!kathā!} took place. One {!nirjalā!} Ekādashi day, Pramukh Swāmi Mahārāj explained Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II-8 for five hours. The devotees in all the compartments heard Swāmishri’s explanation through the overhead speakers. \r\n[Yogi Gita Marma : 181]

12690.t: January 1964, Mumbai. \r\nVachanāmruts Gadhadā II 7 and Gadhadā II 8 were read during the morning discourses, based upon which Yogiji Mahārāj said, “True introspection is to look at the manifest form of God. True meditation is to look at the manifest form of God and stay within the boundaries of his commands.”\r\n[Y.M. : 3/586]

12691.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi has said, “Those who perform an [{!Ashwamedh!}] {!yagna!} send a horse out into all ten directions and must become victorious [in all battles] in order to complete the {!yagna!}. In the same manner, one who has won over the ten directions in the form of the ten {!indriyas!}, i.e. has attached oneself to the {!Sant!} - who never becomes attached to the sensual pleasures - is said to have completed the {!gnān-yagna!}. [Attaching oneself to the {!Sant!}] is analogous to completing the [{!Ashwamedh!}] {!yagna!} by merely taking the horse around one’s courtyard.”\r\n[S.V. : 5/127]

12692.t:
28 December 1967, Mumbai. 
During the afternoon discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “One who is a true devotee of Akshar-Purushottam is constantly engaged in a {!gnān-yagna!}. Such a {!gnān-yagna!} is not for one who sits idly. A true {!gnān-yagna!} is for one to be constantly engaged in service.
“What is true association? True association means one who experiences an ever-increasing closeness to the {!Gunātit Purush!}. Oneness is the key. The {!Satpurush!} is the true pathway to attain God.
“What is the highest spiritual state? The attainment of {!Gunātit!}. Once this is attained, all of the other qualities follow.”
[Y.M. : 4/595]

12696.t:
Whilst explaining the benefits of {!Ekādashi!}, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “There are many benefits of fasting.
1. One’s indigestion will be cured.
2. One’s strength is boosted.
3. The {!ātmā’s!} strength increases.
4. The {!Motāpurush!} becomes pleased.
5. One attains realisation of God.
6. God is very fond of one who performs austerities.
7. The {!indriyas!} and {!antahkarans!} can be conquered through restraining the body and meditating upon the {!ātmā!}.
8. One remains energetic and alert.
9. By fasting, one is able to wake up early and thinks twice about oversleeping. 
10. One will not fall ill due to flu and fevers.
11. The body will acquire power.
Hence there are many benefits. By fasting every five days, one develops good habits and by fasting, one attains merits in doing so too.”
[Yogi Vāni : 24/19]

12701.t: 15 August 1967, Mumbai.\r\nDuring the morning {!mangal!} discourse, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “{!Tāmsi yagna!} is if one accuses others of joining a cult, resulting in them being consigned to hell and subsequently being beaten. One should not engage in gossip or other misuse of one’s senses. This falls into the category of bad company within Satsang. {!Gunātit!} is like the fire of {!Brahma!}. One should associate with {!Brahma!} through contemplation. If a blacksmith does the job of a confectioner, he himself will be called a confectioner – the same goes here. Being born unto {!Brahma!} is the final stage of knowledge. Introspection can be defined as looking within or looking at the manifest form of God. Many ascetics sit there in apparent meditation and introspection; however this is still categorised as extrospection. True introspection is only achieved after attaining God and the {!Sant!}.”\r\n[Y.M. : 3/521]

12708.t: 3 April 1959, Advāl.\r\nOn the day of {!Ekādashi!}, the devotees from Advāl were all seated in the afternoon discourses. The topic of discussion was Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 8. Swāmishri said, “Just as one offers barley seeds and sesame seeds in a sacrifice, one should sacrifice the instincts of one’s senses. Which sacrifice? How should one perform it? Can one perform it for free or does one have to pay? What does sacrificing mean? Sacrificing means that one has completely immersed oneself in the form of God. The {!gopis!} used to say, “I am Krishna, I lifted the Govardhan mountain…” Thus, one attains such oneness with God and ends up completely immersing oneself in the form of God. We should immerse our instincts in the form of {!Gunātit!} – this is true ‘association through sacrifice’. What does sacrificing mean? It means to dissolve oneself in the shape and form of {!Gunātit!}. The true fruits of all of this is when our instincts shape around the {!Sant!}… true {!gnān-yagna!} is when one acts introspectively and one engages in the discourses of God. What is the fruit of education? We get a good job. What is the fruit of such a sacrifice? We can realise God.”\r\n[Y.M. : 2/533]

12709.t: 11 September 1967, Mumbai.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “When one performs a single {!Ekādashi!} fast, one gains merits equivalent to those gained by feeding 60,000 sages daily for 100,000 years. How much merit is this? This is a whole load! On that [{!Ekādashi!}] day, one should feel euphoric.”\r\n[Y.M. : 4/527]

12730.t: 1950, Atlādrā.\r\nDuring his final illness, one night Shāstriji Mahārāj became cold and felt uneasy. Shāstriji Mahārāj said, “Out of all the Vachanāmruts, Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 9 is supreme. Following that, Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 13 and then Gadhadā III 30 and Gadhadā III 38. They are equivalent to one’s life force.” \r\n[S.M. : 2/344]

12731.t:
Samvat 1911, Vartāl. 
A {!chhāvani!} [{!shibir!}] was arranged in the presence of Gunātitānand Swāmi over a 6-month period. Each morning, after the {!shangār ārti!}, Swāmi spoke at his seat. Everyone flocked to listen to him.
During the final days of the {!chhāvani!}, Swāmi thought that when he leaves, this custom of morning {!kathā!} after {!shangār ārti!} will stop. Swāmi wanted this practice to continue after he leaves, so he decided to change his routine. He instead began the custom of going to Āchārya Mahārāj’s room after {!shangār darshan!} so the {!kathā!} continues there. The other {!sādhus!} followed Swāmi’s lead. Āchārya Mahārāj asked, “Swāmi, shall we go to your seat?”
Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “No. From today we will talk here.” Swāmi then began to explain Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II-9: “To believe that Mahārāj is like the other {!avatārs!} is committing blasphemy against his form according to this Vachanāmrut. This can be understood only from the great [{!sādhus!}]. We should get rid of everything in our hearts except for Shriji Mahārāj.”
Shukmuni Swāmi said, “Mahārāj said this Vachanāmrut with me in mind, and I alone selected this Vachanāmrut [for printing]. I compiled this Vachanāmrut, I wrote this Vachanāmrut, but only today have I understood it.”
Hearing Shukmuni Swāmi’s words, Āchārya Mahārāj said, “Swāmi, despite having witnessed or heard the divine incidents of Mahārāj [of his divinity], why does the {!jiva!} hesitate to speak or write about them?” 
This was an implicit insinuation that Shukmuni Swāmi hesitated to openly say Mahārāj was supreme.
Gunātitānand Swāmi explained, “A horse broke its leg in a dream and would not put it on the ground. A vet was called. He said, ‘This horse broke its leg in a dream.’ Someone asked, ‘What should be done?’ The vet said, ‘Prepare 200 horses and fire cannons and guns. When it is startled, it will forget its dream.’ Similarly, people have been confused by the words of the scriptures, so when we continuously bombard them with words of Mahārāj’s supremacy like this, their confusion will clear up and they will understand Mahārāj’s supremacy in their heart.” 
[S.V. : 3/19]
[G.S. : 1/374]

12737.t:
In Samvat 1913, Gunātitānand Swāmi explained the supremacy of Shriji Mahārāj in Amdāvād. Uttamānand Swāmi and other {!sādhus!} said they had never heard this before and asked Gunātitānand Swāmi where he heard such talks. Gunātitānand Swāmi had Ānandānand Swāmi, a senior and experienced {!paramhansa!}, sit in a chair beside him. Swāmi asked Ānandānand Swāmi to agree with him if what he says is true. Then, he started to narrate old incidents of Shriji Mahārāj:
#1.)	In Loj and Māngrol, Mahārāj put his hand on Ānandānand Swāmi’s shoulder and sang Kabir’s {!kirtan!}: “{!Koti Krishna jode hāth, koti Vishnu name māth, koti Shankar dhare dhyān, koti Brahmā kathe gnān, sadguru khele vasant!}” Then, Mahārāj asked Ānand Swāmi who that {!sadguru!} [mentioned in this {!kirtan!}] was. In this instance, Mahārāj said that {!sadguru!} is himself.
#2.)	Samvat 1867, Sārangpur. Mahārāj was playing {!holi!} and sang Kabir’s {!kirtan!} again as he did above. This time, he touched Gunātitānand Swāmi’s chest with his {!chhadi!} and asked, “Who is that {!sadguru!}?” Muktānand Swāmi and Ānand Swāmi replied that that {!sadguru!} is You [as per the incident above]. This time, Mahārāj said, “I am the supreme Purushottam Bhagwān and that {!sadguru!} is Gunātitānand Swāmi.”
#3.)	In Nāgadkā, Vyāpkānand Swāmi witnessed Mahārāj manifest the 24 {!avatārs!} from his {!murti!} and merge them back into his {!murti!}.
#4.)	While Parvatbhāi was ploughing the field, Mahārāj gave him the {!darshan!} of the 24 {!avatārs!} from his {!murti!} and merged them back into himself.
#5.)	In Mangrol, Swarupānand Swāmi saw Mahārāj as the form of Krishna; then in {!samādhi!}, He revealed himself Purushottam [separate from Krishna], and solidified his conviction.
#6.)	Mahārāj asked Swarupānand Swāmi, “Swāmi, we will send you to Golok.” Swāmi replied, “{!Is khadde me to pade ja hai!}.” [“I am in the same pit here.” - implying the bliss of Golok is the same bliss as here [{!mrutyu-lok!}], so there is no reason to go to Golok; but the bliss of Akshardhām is superior.]
#7.)	When Mahārāj installed Nar-Nārāyan Dev in Amdāvād, Mahārāj held your hand in the south-facing balcony and said, “The king of Bharat-Khand is Nar-Nārāyan. His {!murti!} is not installed anywhere, so I have installed it here; however, there are countless such Nar-Nārāyans and countless Krishna-Nārāyans who worship the manifest Sahajānand Swāmi.”
Recounting each incident one by one, Swāmi asked Ānandānand Swāmi if they were true. Each time Ānandānand Swāmi agreed.
Then, Gunātitānand Swāmi had Balmukund Swāmi read Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II-9 and said, “How can we equate Mahārāj to the other {!avatārs!}? If we do, we will have committed blasphemy against Mahārāj.”
Finally, Gunātitānand Swāmi said to Ayodhyāprasādji Mahārāj, “We are telling you the virtues and greatness of your father. You have great affection for me but to whom will you give the keys to your safe - Keshavprasādji [i.e. your son] or me? [Meaning: Who will you give your inheritance to?] Ayodhyāprasādji Mahārāj said, “I can only give it to him [Keshavprasādji].” Swāmi said, “Similarly, Mahārāj gave me the keys to his supremacy, so the talks of liberation will have to be heard from me.”
[G.S. : 1/435]

12738.t:
Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “Without knowing Mahārāj as Purushottam, it is not possible to go to Akshardhām. Without becoming {!brahmarup!}, it is not possible to stay in the service of Mahārāj.”
Shivlāl then asked a question, “How should Mahārāj be known as Purushottam? And how can one become {!brahmarup!}?” 
Swāmi then said, “Know that Mahārāj is supreme, the source of all {!avatārs!} and the cause of all causes.” Based on this, he had Vachanāmruts Gadhadā II 9 and Gadhadā III 38 read and said, “Today, in Satsang, the {!sādhus, āchāryas, mandirs!} and {!murtis!} are all supreme. So what is there to say in Mahārāj being supreme? One should understand that he is supreme. And one can become {!brahmarup!} by believing this {!Sādhu!} to be {!brahmarup!} and associating with him through one’s mind, deed and speech. Then one becomes {!brahmarup!}.” Based on this, he had Vachanāmrut Vartāl 11 read and said, “When one becomes like this, then one stays in the service of Purushottam.”
[S.V. : 3/12]

12739.t: After reading Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 9, Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “If one knows Mahārāj as Purushottam, but due to adverse circumstances leaves Satsang, even then one attains Akshardhām. However, if one does not have this spiritual wisdom to recognize Mahārāj as Purushottam, even if he remains in Satsang, he will attain another abode - but not Akshardhām.”\r\n[S.V. : 1/261]

12740.t: After instructing that Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 9 be read, Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “As described in this Vachanāmrut, one who knows Mahārāj as Purushottam and leaves Satsang will still go to Akshardhām. However, one who stays in Satsang, may observe {!dharma!} and may be a celibate, but does not know Mahārāj as Purushottam will go to another abode.”\r\n[S.V. : 5/304]

12741.t:
Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “Purushottam Sahajānand Swāmi is the cause of all {!avatārs!}. One will go all the way to Akshardhām by offering {!upāsanā!} to him, and one will go to other abodes by worshipping other {!avatars!}. The Bhāgwat states that Prahlād is in the {!Harivarsh Khand!}. One will go to Vaikunth if one believes Mahārāj to be like Rāmchandraji; however, that leads to many problems, what use is that? None of that is of significance. If one believes Mahārāj to be like Shri Krishna, one will go to Golok, where there are cows, calves and {!gop-gopis!}; what use is that? Therefore, no place has the bliss of Akshardhām. Therefore, we must understand Mahārāj to be Purushottam. It says in the Vachanāmrut, ‘I will make you as you understand me to be.’ We get to Akshardhām by knowing him [Mahārāj] as Purushottam. Whoever reaches Akshardhām, never goes back; however, everything else up to Prakruti-Purush is dissolved by time.”
One person said, “We should stay where God keeps us. All the abodes of God are the same. Why do you unnecessarily argue?”
Swāmi replied, “The stars and the moon cannot be described as being the same. Even Mahārāj has said that one must understand there is a clear distinction between the past incarnations of God and the source of them all – just as there is a distinction between the king and his minister, and there is a difference between the arrow and the archer. The minister may be very powerful and give orders; he may be great, but when he goes to the king, he is able to take his seat only after offering many salutes. The king’s orders prevail over him. That is the difference between the {!avatars!} and their source.”
Based on this, he had a Vachanāmrut read and said, “One who equates Akshardhām with other abodes, and one who says that Mahārāj and other {!avatars!} are the same should be known to have committed a worse sin than the five grave sins; such company should be avoided.”
[S.V. : 6/20]

12742.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi says, “One who has affection for God and his great {!Sādhu!} has nothing left to do. Based on this, think about the Vachanāmruts Gadhadā II 9 and Vartāl 11. They both convey the same message.\r\n[S.V. : 5/338]

12743.t: January 1957, Bodi.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “{!Swarupnishthā!} [conviction of God] and understanding of his glory are equivalent to the bridegroom and other endeavours are equivalent to the party of the bridegroom. When one understands the two Vachanāmruts of {!swarupnishthā!} – Gadhadā II 9 and Gadhadā III 38, one’s conviction will become firm. Keep one’s conviction and refuge firm.” \r\n[Y.M. : 2/185]

12750.t: January 1957, Bodi.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “{!Swarupnishthā!} [conviction of God] and understanding of his glory are equivalent to the bridegroom and other endeavours are equivalent to the party of the bridegroom. When one understands the two Vachanāmruts of {!swarupnishthā!} – Gadhadā II 9 and Gadhadā III 38, one’s conviction will become firm. Keep one’s conviction and refuge firm.” \r\n[Y.M. : 2/185]

12751.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “Mahārāj told Gopālānand Swāmi in his dream, ‘If you do not spread the knowledge that I am Purushottam [i.e. that he is distinct from the other {!avatārs!} and is {!sarvopari!}], then I will keep you in the current body for one thousand years.’” Then Swāmi said, “Mahārāj had also told me [that he is {!sarvopari!}], I realized it from [reading] Mahārāj’s old documents and knew it even before that. When I openly spoke in {!sabhā!}, the sādhus questioned, ‘Who told you this?’ I replied, “Swāminārāyan told me. Who else will tell me?’ Mahārāj has said this in Gadhadā II-9, Gadhadā III-38, Gadhadā II-13, Loyā-14, etc.”\r\n[S.V. : 6/32]

12756.t: August 1959, Mumbai.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “There are four types of {!aushadhi!} [herbal medicines]: {!sandhini, varnaharni, vishalyakarni!} and {!sanjivani!}. Their four forms: {!dharma, gnān, vairāgya!} and {!bhakti!}. The four Vachanāmruts relating to these are Gadhadā II 28, Loyā 7, Gadhadā III 39 and Gadhadā II 10 respectively; these four Vachanāmruts should be perfected. \r\n[Y.M. : 2/600]

12776.t: After having Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 11 read, Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “If all householders understand this Vachanāmrut, they will remain at peace within.” \r\n[S.V. : 4/60]

12778.t:
Gunātitānand Swāmi says, “People do not become desireless through {!samādhi!}, but they become desireless through spiritual knowledge.”
Then Chaturbhujdāsji asked, “Why are both a {!sādhu!} and a householder described as being equally desireless?” Then Swāmi replied, “If a naked ascetic and a householder with all his possessions want to cross the ocean, then both will need a ship. Even though the ascetic is not even wearing a loincloth, it is not possible for him to swim across the ocean. Therefore, both the ascetic and the householder with all his possessions sit in the ship. The householder has his wife, children, buffalo and spinning wheel with him – and all will cross the ocean safely. But, without this ship, even one who does not touch money, observes eight-fold {!brahmacharya!}, is a great renunciant, but has not met God, does not attain liberation and does not cross {!māyā!}; whereas the householder attains liberation and crosses māyā.”
Then, after having Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 11 read, Swāmi said, “If all householders understand this Vachanāmrut, they will remain at peace within. But this talk is difficult to understand.” He then gave an example, “On seeing a householder who has a wife, eight children, sixteen ploughs, sixteen buffaloes and other things, one feels that he will not attain liberation; however, he has met God so he and everyone with him will attain liberation. This talk is just like one who has become ill by eating {!ghee!} and is cured by again eating {!ghee!}. Others cannot understand it; only Mahārāj can understand it. The answer to this question can only be given by Mahārāj, but not by anyone else. The very same qualities of {!rajogun, tamogun!} and {!sattvagun!} by which one goes to hell are the same qualities by which {!moksha!} can also be attained.” To illustrate, Swāmi quoted the shlok, ‘{!Āmayo yena bhutānām!}!’
[S.V. : 4/60]

12780.t: After having Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 11 read, Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “This Vachanāmrut should be understood by all householders; without understanding this Vachanāmrut, doubts will never be eradicated from one’s {!jiva!}.” \r\n[S.V. : 4/14]

12793.t:
Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Never let the joy of your {!brahmaswarup!} realisation wane for even a second. When thoughts of anger and passion arise, suppress them with spiritual knowledge. Threaten your mind, ‘If you entertain vulgar thoughts, then I will blow you to pieces.’ Read Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 12 which describes how to rule a kingdom [the body is the {!jiva's!} kingdom]. Then one will never have a single bad thought.”
[Yogi Vāni : 26/87]
[S.M. : 2/78]
[Y.M. : 1/213]

12817.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “If one understands the form of God as described in Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 13, only then does one attain liberation. The other means of liberation are like hands and legs, while this knowledge of the form of God is the head. Therefore, to understand all which has been said, a capable guru has to be accepted and only such scriptures which strengthen this knowledge should be read. By doing as stated above, the knowledge of his form should be attained.” \r\n[S.V. : 6/233]

12818.t:
Samvat 1953, Junagadh. 
Shāstriji Mahārāj once asked Bhagatji Mahārāj, “The {!darshan!} of the {!Brahmaswarup Sant!} is equivalent to the {!darshan!} of Bhagwān – such is stated in the Vachanāmrut many times; therefore, why is it necessary to achieve a state of {!ātmā!}-realization and experience Bhagwān in one’s heart if one has attained the {!darshan!} of the {!Brahmaswarup Sant!}?”
Hearing this question, Bhagatji simply gave Shāstriji Mahārāj a compassionate look for a few minutes. He then said, “{!Sādhurām!}, the external {!darshan!} of the {!Sant!} is the fruit of one’s spiritual endeavours from countless births. However, to experience that [external] {!murti!} into one’s heart constantly is an elevated state. Shriji Mahārāj has told senior {!sādhu-muktas!}, ‘When the inclination of the {!indriyas!} and {!antahkaran!} constantly remain withdrawn in one’s heart, one sees Bhagwān’s {!murti!} within the radiant light.’ In this way, when the inclination of the {!indriyas!} are retracted and remain focused on Bhagwān’s {!murti!}, that should be known as having achieved an elevated state.
“Shriji Mahārāj has explained in this Vachanāmrut [Gadhadā II-13], ‘In fact, you also see this form of Bhagwān, but you do not fully comprehend it.’ So do not think that, since you have seen the [external] form, you have understood it thoroughly. When you see that form completely in your heart, the tendency of the {!indriyas!} to remain on external objects will be destroyed and instead will remain constantly within. That is known as the state of {!sākshātkār!}. Muktānand Swāmi wrote: ‘{!Brahma thai Parabrahmane jue te jāne re’!} – One who sees Parabrahma having identified one’s form as Brahma knows Parabrahma.
“In this way, one who sees the [external] manifest form of Bhagwān [internally] within one’s heart knows Bhagwān thoroughly. Therefore, either in this very physical body or after one leaves the physical body, the only option is to achieve this state. Krupānand Swāmi, Swarupānand Swāmi, and Nityānand Swāmi, etc. had achieved that state.”
Then, Bhagatji Mahārāj added, “Among those who debate over scriptures or the pundits who study the scriptures, only a few can understand this philosophy. Others have no understanding in this matter. Therefore, for us, we should follow the path of the great. Having faith in the words of the Motāpurush is the greatest means to achieving {!sākshātkār!}.” Bhagatji Mahārāj left for his residence after answering Shāstriji Mahārāj’s question.
[S.M. : 1/186]

12825.t: After having Vachanāmrut Vartāl 1 and Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 14 recited, Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “If one understands like this, then a householder and a renunciant both attain the same [Akshardhām].”\r\n[S.V. : 5/89]

12827.t: After reading Vachanāmrut Vartāl 1 and Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 14, Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “If one understands like this, then a householder and a renunciant attain the same [Akshardhām]. A renunciant may stand out while a householder, like Parvatbhāi, may not stand out. But his state was such that he could advise Mahārāj.”\r\n[S.V. : 5/89]

12833.t:
25 February 1963, Mumbai.
During the afternoon discourses, speaking on Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 15, Yogiji Mahārāj looked at a {!sādhu!} and said, “If [someone] smashes and breaks one glasses, and throws them away, one should still [only] look at their positive traits [{!guna!}]. ‘He has granted the glasses liberation,’ take such a {!guna!}! One should not get angry. One should not take {!abhāv!}.
“Shāstriji Mahārāj used to say, ‘When I was young and went to school, I had such a character that everyone always maintained respect. No one would play cards in my presence…’ Swami [Shāstriji Mahārāj] lived in Vartāl, but wherever he went, he made an impression. When he spoke, no one else spoke. He had such a nature from childhood. Such a person never falls from {!dharma!}. No one can shake his {!vairāgya!}. Such a person never falls himself, nor does he let others fall. He extends a hand in support and pulls one out.”
[Y.M. : 3/444]

12844.t: 25 February 1963, Mumbai. \r\nDuring the spiritual discourse based on Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 16, Yogiji Mahārāj explained in his unique style the importance of faith, “A person who does not abide by {!niyams!} lapses. One who possesses faith attains spiritual enlightenment early. One who does not have faith takes a long time [to attain enlightenment, like a] local train. One who has faith travels by the Punjāb Mail [to reach the state of enlightenment]. Fast! The earth shakes wherever one stands. Whereas [attainment] will take a long time for the one without faith. One with faith comes first. Conversely, ‘Who has seen it? It may happen, it may get done,’ - that is being slow. The one with faith goes for it with full force.\r\n[Y.M. : 3/445]

12848.t: October 1960, Gondal. \r\nAfter having {!darshan!} after Thakorji was awoken in the afternoon, Yogiji Mahārāj remarked, “If one understands Kāriyāni 8 and Gadhadā II 17, then one will experience Akshardhām in this very birth.” Yogiji Mahārāj repeated this statement thrice. \r\n[Y.M. : 3/127]

12865.t:
Gunātitānand Swāmi says, “Spiritual wisdom develops and the {!antahkaran!} becomes pure by engaging in activity. However, the {!indriyas!} do not become pure due to association.
Nathu Patel then asked, “Is there a difference in attainment?”
Swāmi replied, “There is no difference in attainment; it is the same. If we do not call those following the path of {!nivrutti!} as being superior, then you may believe it but others would not. Thus, we have to answer in that way. However, God does as he wishes. Does he have a master? Answers have to be given as appropriate.”
[S.V. : 5/96]

12870.t:
Samvat 1972, Nadiād.
Dolatrambhāi invited Shāstriji Mahārāj, Nirgundās Swāmi, and other sādhus to his house. Dolatrāmbhāi was going to have {!darshan!} of Swāmishri after ten years of separation from Vartāl. He was overjoyed to meet Swāmishri again.
He held Swāmishri’s hand and said, “Swāmi, this house is consecrated. My father had served food to Gunātitānand Swāmi, Gopālānand Swāmi, and other great {!sadgurus!}. He took the water from their {!pattar!}, spread it in the street, covered it with dirt, did his construction on it; this is how holy this place is.”
Swāmishri was pleased to hear this and said, “Your father understood the greatness of Gunātitānand Swāmi. The year Swāmi left for {!dhām!}, he had Swāmi bless this house.”
Dolatrāmbhāi then offered {!dhotiyā!} to the {!sādhus!}.
He then asked, “Swāmi, do you have thoughts of reuniting with Vartāl?”
Swāmishri immediately replied, “Yes, if they accept Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II-21, we are not opposed to reuniting.”
Dolatrāmbhāi was impressed with Swāmishri’s answer, which was devoid of any selfish motives. He said, “Swāmiji, I know you well enough to know that you would not separate without a good reason. So first, tell me what principle have you understood from Gadhadā II-21.” Swāmishri explained the principle of Akshar-Purushottam based on this Vachanāmrut.
Realizing the truth in Swāmishri’s explanation, Dolatrāmbhāi exclaimed, “Swāmiji, had you not done this, Mahārāj would have to come on the earth as another {!avatār!} to do it! Today, you have installed Mahārāj and Swāmi’s {!murtis!} made of metal, but in the future, your devotees will install your {!murti!} made of gold.”
[S.M. : 1/412]

12871.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi says, “Last night, the main principle was described: It is that God has been attained. This Purushottam [Swāminārāyan Bhagwān] has been attained, so then what is left? Even the {!Sādhu!}, who has realized him fully, has been attained. That is the main principle, which we possess. Now there is no worry.”\r\n[S.V. : 6/213]

12873.t:
Samvat 1972, Sārangpur.
Thakor Sāheb of Limdi requested Shāstriji Mahārāj to install the {!murtis!} of Rādhā-Krishna in the central shrine instead of the {!murtis!} of Akshar-Purushottam. Shāstriji Mahārāj boldly replied, “We have shaved our head [become sādhus] for Akshar-Purushottam.” Subdued by this answer, Thakor Sāheb simply folded his hands.
Swāmishri assumed his gentle nature and said, “Whoever is the subject of their {!upāsanā!}, they install their form and do {!pujān, archan!}, and {!dhyān!}; otherwise, he is not a genuine {!upāsak!}. Shriji Mahārāj has shown us the path of liberation in Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 21 so that we can become true {!upāsaks!}. Accordingly, the extent of greatness we understand of the non-manifest {!avatārs!}, such as Rām, Krishna, etc., and their {!bhaktas!}, such as Nārad, Sanakādik, Uddhav, Hanuman, etc., the same extent should be understood of the manifest {!Bhagwān!} Sahajānand Swāmi and his {!bhakta!} Aksharbrahma Shri Gunātitānand Swāmi. If one understands this much, they have attained the main principle of liberation. This is our true {!upāsanā!}. Hence, we have to understand the greatness of Swāmi and Nārāyan, or Akshar and Purushottam.
“Shriji Mahārāj manifested on this earth and established {!ekāntik dharma!} to liberate countless {!jivas!}. He also brought with him 500 {!ekāntik paramhansas!}. Even today, He left the {!Ekāntik Satpurush!}, who has a direct relationship with him, for his followers. One should recognize the {!Ekāntik Satpurush!} by his qualities and seek his refuge, so that one can develop firm conviction of Mahārāj. {!Sanskārs!} are only obtained from associating with and serving the {!Satpurush!}. The ultimate goal of this human birth is to imbibe {!ekāntik dharma!} by the association of a genuine {!Satpurush!}.”
[S.M. : 1/427]

12876.t:
Shriji Mahārāj talks about His account in Amdāvād: “When I went to Amdāvād to perform the installation ceremony of Shri Nar-Nārāyan Dev, thousands of people had gathered for the festival. Following the completion of the installation of Shri Nar-Nārāyan Dev, and after thousands of {!Brāhmins!} from Amdāvād had been fed, I departed from there and spent the night in Jetalpur. There, I began to think, ‘I want to forget all memories of all of those people and all of the activities that I saw.’ In doing this, My heart felt intense grief, and as a result, I became ill… While thinking, I forgot all of the activities, and dispelled all those thoughts in such a manner that it was as if I had not even stayed at Lake Kānkariā, and as if there had been no festival - no thoughts remained at all…”
There is a hidden history behind Shriji Mahārāj’s illness that He describes in this Vachanāmrut:
In this Vachanāmrut, Mahārāj says He became ill because He had to engage in the activity ({!pravrutti!}) of feeding {!Brāhmins!} during the {!pratishthā!} of Narnārāyan in Amdāvād. This itself is merely showing human traits ({!manushya-bhāv!}), since one who creates, sustains, and destroys countless {!brahmānds!} and is not disturbed cannot be swayed by such a small activity.
After installing Nar-Nārāyan Dev in Amdāvād, Nar-Nārāyan Dev became predominant in everyone’s mind and Mahārāj became secondary. Therefore, Mahārāj was dismayed that without understanding Mahārāj to be {!sarvopari!} and cause of all, all of the {!mumukshus!} will not attain ultimate liberation ({!ātyantik kalyān!}). It seemed people grabbed the branch of a tree (Nar-Nārāyan Dev) instead of its trunk (Mahārāj Himself).
Shriji Mahārāj’s intention was to curb {!bhaktas!} from the fault of practicing {!upāsanā!} of trivial deities. Yet, these {!bhaktas!} became bound to the {!upāsanā!} of deities as according to their natural tendency; which caused Mahārāj to become disheartened. Mahārāj’s illness stemmed from this thought.
[B.S. : 4/332-333]
Moreover, after installing Nar-Nārāyan Dev, Shriji Mahārāj said to the senior sādhus, “Narnārāyan is the king of Bharat-Khand. I have installed him for the sake of countless other {!jivas!}. However, you all should not be misled. In Badrikāshram, Nar-Nārāyan Dev meditates upon Me.” At this time, a {!haribhakta!} brought a {!murti!} of Narvir to consecrate it with Mahārāj touch and placed it in His hands. Mahārāj got up and, drawing attention to Himself, said, “Everyone in Badrikāshram meditates upon this {!murti!}.”
[Nirgundas Swāmini Vato : Page 79]
Even after clearly alluding to His own {!sarvopari upāsanā!}, Nar-Nārāyan Dev became predominant to everyone and they forgot about the eternal {!upāsanā!} of Shriji Mahārāj.
Additionally, after the {!pratishthā!}, Shriji Mahārāj held Ānandānand Swāmi’s hand and arrived in the courtyard of the Mandir where everyone resounded the victory toll of Nar-Nārāyan Dev. Near the gateway where Mahārāj often discoursed (currently there is a shrine on this spot), He asked Ānandānand Swāmi, “Swāmi, did you understand anything?” Ānandānand Swāmi simply looked at Mahārāj as if he understood nothing.
Mahārāj said, “Infinite Nar-Nārāyan Dev, Krishna-Nārāyan, Lakshmi-Nārāyan, and Vāsudev-Nārāyan offer {!upāsanā!} to this manifest Swāminārāyan. Everyone forgot My greatness because naturally everyone develops faith in the non-manifest form of God. But Nar-Nārāyan Dev is the deity of Bharat-Khand. Due to Durvāsā’s curse, he meditated upon Me. Therefore, I told him I will manifest on the earth to establish {!Bhāgwat-dharma!}. I have narrated this clandestine message several times; yet people still leave the cause (Shriji Mahārāj) and embrace the effect (deities and other {!avatārs!}).”
[B.S. : 4/324]
In conclusion, Mahārāj’s illness resulted from people not becoming attached to Mahārāj’s {!swarup!}.

12877.t:
24 October 1959, Mumbai. 
Prior to departing for his second Satsang tour of Africa, {!Brahmaswarup!} Yogiji Mahārāj noted in his diary, “Everyone should focus on the principle and perfect Gadhadā II 22. Shriji Mahārāj has blown the horns loud and clear. He has eradicated darkness in the form of ignorance and bestowed peace to all. One should keep {!agna-upāsana!} firm. This is my recommendation, so please imbibe it in one’s {!jiva!} and keep pride [{!khumarī!}] and never fall back; remain courageous. Mahārāj and Swāmi will inspire such strength.” 
Moreover, during the 1959 Satsang tour in Kampala, Uganda, Yogiji Mahārāj wrote New Year blessings in a letter to the devotees residing in India. He again wrote similar sentiments and instructed everyone to perfect this particular Vachanāmrut. 
[Chalo Chale Ham Akshardhām : 83]

12878.t: Pramukh Swāmi did {!darshan!} of all the holy places in Ganesh Dholkā (located near Kothya), where Mahārāj stayed during His illness. On December 8, 1990, he returned to Amdāvād. Here, Swāmishri explained Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II-22 (i.e. we never went to Kānkariyā lake, nor did we gather anyone there) and gave {!manan!} by saying, “In this incident of Amdāvād, Mahārāj gave all of the human beings in the {!brahmānd!} the method to remain happy. With this thought, we can remain peaceful and worry-free in our work.”\r\n[Chalo Chale Ham Akshardhām : 159]

12879.t: 14 January 1957, Reniguntā.\r\nDuring the spiritual discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “In Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 22, it says to become victorious. To be victorious means to understand Mahārāj and Swāmi’s true {!upāsanā!} and explain it to others.”\r\n[Y.M. : 2/194]

12881.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi says, “The God that has manifested here is very great; like other {!avatars!}, his {!sādhus!} and devotees have performed miracles. He has written about Nar-Nārāyan in the following way: If someone wants to go to an unknown village, they require the aid of a guide. Therefore, [God] has never come here before and {!Bharatkhand!} is considered to be [Nar-Nārāyan Dev’s], so he has taken him as a guide.” \r\n[S.V. : 6/54]

12908.t: In the Swāminārāyan {!Sampraday!}, the place where the {!sādhus!} and devotees eat is called the {!choko!}. ‘{!Choko!}-patlo’ refers to the cleaning and mopping of a kitchen floor after a meal has been eaten. Similarly, the understanding of one who has resoluteness in {!sankhya!} and {!yoga!} is pure. He realises, ‘With the exception of Akshardhām, the form of God and the liberated {!jivas!} residing in Akshardhām, everything else – all of the realms, the deities, and the opulence of the deities – is perishable.’ Thus, he does not develop love for anything except God.

12910.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Vachanāmruts Gadhadā II 24 and III 38 are all Vachanāmruts which contain the supreme type of spiritual knowledge.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 24/30]

12912.t:
23 February 1963, Mumbai.
Explaining Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 24 during the afternoon discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said:
“ ‘{!Prakruti-Purush pralaymā āve… Le vāt āvi tu lakhi re.!}’ There is no happiness anywhere in the world. If one has such an understanding, one will never experience disturbances, barriers or obstacles. Whether one is in the forest or alone, whether one is eating {!dudhpāk-puri!} or millet bread with buttermilk [{!chāsh-rotlo!}], one experiences only happiness. If the two ‘rivers’ of {!sānkhya!} and {!yoga!} come together, a greater force results.”
[Y.M. : 3/442]

12914.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “According to Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 24, without [the relationship of] Mahārāj, everything up to and including Prakruti-Purush is under the influence of {!māyā!}.  If we propagated the fact that all of the incarnations are bound by {!māyā!}, it would not be palatable to the general public; however, if we mentioned that, ‘{!Vairat!} [{!Brahma!}] has emerged from {!māyā’!}, fully aware of the fact that all the incarnations originated from {!Vairat Brahma!}, no one would object! All of the incarnations are contained within a pore of Aksharbrahma. No one [externally] can comprehend any knowledge above the fact that they consider Mul-Purush to be Purushottam. How can one get married even before one is born?” [i.e. How can scriptures reveal this fact even before the manifestation of Purna Purushottam on this earth?]\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 2/28]

12915.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “One with such attachment beholds God continuously. So, if one has this union [with God and his {!Sādhu!}], then it is fine, and when it is not present, then one needs {!sānkhya!}. And when one realizes the perishable nature of everything up to {!Prakruti!}, one can live without hindrance.” Based upon this, Vachanāmrut Panchala 2 entitled ‘{!Sānkhya!} and Yoga’ was read. Swāmi then added, “For this reason, learn this.”\r\n[S.V. : 6/85]

12929.t: August 1961, Mumbai. \r\nDuring the morning discourse, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “If one wants to attain {!moksha!}, one should perfect Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 26. Shāstriji Mahārāj would often explain this Vachanāmrut in Bochāsan to the newly initiated sādhus.” \r\n[Y.M. : 3/207]

13031.t:
Samvat 1979, Sārangpur.
After the {!kathā!} following {!mangalā ārti!}, Shāstriji Mahārāj routinely encouraged everyone to join in the construction {!sevā!} of the mandir. Harikrishnadās Swāmi had a zeal for {!kathā!} and {!sevā!}, but preferred {!kathā!} more. He believed that {!gnān!} was of greater importance in the {!sampradāy!}. Therefore, he once folded his hands to Swāmishri and said, “Swāmi, will {!upāsanā!} spread by lifting rocks [i.e. construction of {!mandirs!}]? That will only occur when you engage in {!kathā!} and spread {!gnān!}.”
Seeing Harikrishnadas’s enthusiasm for {!gnān!}, Swāmishri looked compassionately at him and explained the importance of {!dharma!} [that is related to Bhagwān [Gadhadā III 21] and {!bhakti!}:
“To achieve {!ekāntik dharma!}, Shriji Mahārāj commanded everyone to develop firmness in four types of {!nishthā!}: {!dharma-nishthā, ātmā-nishthā, vairāgya-nishthā!}, and {!bhakti-nishthā!}. He also explained the characteristics of these four types of {!nishthā!} [Gadhadā I 47]. When one develops firmness in these four types of {!nishthā!}, then one is called a {!Param Bhāgwat Sant!} and one can be said to have achieved {!ekāntik dharma!}.
“The firm {!swarup-nishthā!} of the two forms [Akshar and Purushottam] that we want to develop through {!kathā!} have been installed here. When one thoroughly understands the greatness of these two forms in one’s heart, only then will {!swarup-nishthā!} become firm.
“When one’s {!swarup-nishthā!} becomes firm, only then will one cultivate {!dharma, gnān!}, and {!vairāgya!}. So that the {!upāsanā!} of these two forms remain, Mahārāj relaxed the emphasis on {!vairāgya!} and built {!mandirs!}. If {!upāsanā!} perishes, then blindness follows in succession - meaning, everyone will forget that Shriji Mahārāj is Bhagwān, resulting in an end to the master-servant relationship with him. Consequently, one becomes the guru and the Bhagwān. Therefore, {!gnān!} without {!upāsanā!} is inauspicious.
“In Panchālā, Shriji Mahārāj pointed to Gunātitānand Swāmi and said, ‘There is no Bhagwān like me and there is no {!sādhu!} like him.’ Our only {!sevā!} and our only goal of {!gnān!} is that the knowledge of these forms and our {!upāsanā!} spread.”
Explaining this much, Swāmishri added, “{!Sādhurām!}, we are lifting rocks to spread the supreme {!upāsanā!} of Akshar and Purushottam. If we believe this labor as {!bhakti!} in the form of {!sevā!}, then that will strengthen our {!bhakti!}. However, if we believe we are simply lifting rocks, then that will surely hinder us on the path of liberation. Therefore, forsake this incorrect understanding and understand the greatness of the {!mandirs!} constructed for {!upāsanā!}.
[S.M. : 1/505]

13036.t: August 1959, Mumbai.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “There are four types of {!aushadhi!} [herbal medicines]: {!sandhini, varnaharni, vishalyakarni!} and {!sanjivani!}. Their four forms: {!dharma, gnān, vairāgya!} and {!bhakti!}. The four Vachanāmruts relating to these are Gadhadā II 28, Loyā 7, Gadhadā III 39 and Gadhadā II 10 respectively; these four Vachanāmruts should be perfected. \r\n[Y.M. : 2/600]

13037.t:
Samvat 1921. 
Gunātitānand Swāmi was travelling from Mahelāv to Dholerā. Bhagatji was discoursing to all the {!sādhus, pārshads!}, and devotees. His talks described the greatness of Bhagwān and his {!sādhu!}. Mān Gadhvi heard his discourses and asked him, “Prāgji, why do you keep going on and on about the ‘{!Sādhu!}’?” 
Bhagatji replied, “Gadhvi, I am not the only one who mentions this. Muktānand Swāmi has also spoken about this and even Bhagwān has said that ‘The {!Sant!} is in my heart and I am in his heart. I always reside there constantly.’ Bhagwān remains in the {!sādhu’s!} heart and the sādhu remains in Bhagwān’s heart. Therefore, the {!sādhu’s!} greatness is included when talking about Bhagwān’s greatness, and Bhagwān’s greatness is incorporated when talking about the {!sādhu’s!} greatness. However, while one still has ignorance, Bhagwān and the {!Sant!} are considered separate. Mahārāj has explained this in Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 28.”
Mān Gadhvi was dumbfounded when he heard this from Bhagatji. 
[B.M. : 107]

13038.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “You ask me to speak, so I speak. [Either] I say it in the assembly or in the end, I narrate a historical story, but I remove the sting from the {!ātmā!}. Therefore, serve the {!sādhu!} and do not speak ill of him.” On this, Swāmi narrated the discourse of Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 28 in detail.\r\n[S.V. : 6/134]

13061.t: After having Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 28 read, Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “A {!jiva!} may make mistakes, but by any means, to keep it on the path of God and not allow it to fall is the greatness of the great {!Sādhu!}.”\r\n[S.V. : 5/343]

13075.t: Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 28 was being narrated. During so, the line, ‘The only means for the {!jiva!} to please God is to serve God’s {!Bhakta!} through thought, deed and word’ was read. The means to displease God is by maligning God’s {!Bhakta!}.’ Upon hearing this Yogiji Mahārāj instantly said, “Would Mahārāj ever accept the devotion of one who maligns Gunātit and then performs his {!ārti!}?”\r\n“If one maligns Gunātit [who is God’s ideal devotee], one’s {!jiva!} will be destroyed and attain an inanimate state. Thereafter, regardless how much one worships Shriji Mahārāj alone and extravagantly performs his ceremonies as per the scriptures, Mahārāj will not accept one’s devotion. It is like someone beating a son and then performing {!ārti!} of his father. Would the father ever accept this? He would never accept it.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 15/12]

13082.t: August 1959, Mumbai.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “There are four types of {!aushadhi!} [herbal medicines]: {!sandhini, varnaharni, vishalyakarni!} and {!sanjivani!}. Their four forms: {!dharma, gnān, vairāgya!} and {!bhakti!}. The four Vachanāmruts relating to these are Gadhadā II 28, Loyā 7, Gadhadā III 39 and Gadhadā II 10 respectively; these four Vachanāmruts should be perfected. \r\n[Y.M. : 2/600]

13084.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi says, “Jadbharat said to King Rahugan that the path that the Vedas have shown – the path of the codes of conduct – does not even come into consideration for one who is {!brahmavettā!} [i.e. one who has realised the true knowledge of the {!atmā!} and God]. According to his understanding, one should only truly realise both {!atmā!} and Paramatma.” \r\nBased on this, he had Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 39 read and said, “The principle that Mahārāj establishes in this Vachanāmrut is also the same; that one should only truly have fervour for {!atmā!} and Paramatma.”\r\n[S.V. : 1/207]

13096.t: 15 November 1955, Gondal.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “When Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 28 is perfected, one will constantly have thoughts of whom we have attained ({!prapti!}).” \r\n[Y.M. : 2/22]

13102.t:
11 June 1962, Mumbai. 
During the afternoon discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Mahārāj has stated that he is a devotee of devotees. Who can be labelled a true devotee? Can one who possesses {!dharma, gnān, vairāgya!} and {!bhakti!} be called a true devotee?”
At that time, a question was asked, “What do you mean by a ‘true devotee’?”
Swāmishri answered, “A true devotee is one who would wash the feet of your son and drink that water. Such is the glory of a devotee of God. People who have found faults with devotees of God have fallen from high levels. Whatever good occurs is due to the service of a devotee of God. God is not just pleased if someone merely presses his feet. He is pleased if one pleases his devotee. Mānat Swāmi would take a vessel around with water for everyone to drink. He would serve everyone water. One has served God if one serves a devotee of God. God is not pleased if one remains in close contact with a devotee of God, but does not serve him.”
[Y.M. : 3/356]

13111.t: 17 January 1963, Gondal. \r\nYogiji Mahārāj was writing letters in the assembly hall. Sitting in front of him were some knowledgeable devotees. One devotee suggested that Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 13 be read. Whilst writing the letters, Swāmishri looked up slightly and said, “The main principle is in Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 28; therefore, please read that.” Thus saying, he continued, “What is that main principle? Shriji Mahārāj explains that the sole means to please God is to serve a devotee of God through thought, word and deed. The sole means of displeasing God is to insult his devotee.”\r\n[Y.M. : 3/430]

13141.t:
16 January 1958, Rājkot
