After having Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 28 read at 7:45am, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Mahārāj advises in this Vachanāmrut against finding faults in a devotee of God. What do we mean by this? Where do these ‘faults’ spring up from? Do they come from within or do they come from external association?”
Swāmishri answered his own question by saying, “Seeing a flaw ({!abhāv!}) in a devotee of God means that someone would shun a devotee of God and broadcast a detailed account of a mistake that that devotee may have made or if some adverse incident has occurred with that devotee. One who does this to the devotee breaks off all relations with that devotee, so much so that they do not even like the sight of that devotee. Perceiving faults ({!avguns!}) in a devotee of God is the fabrication and propagation of false stories and accusations about a devotee of God – who is actually free from flaws and does not act against the norms of Satsang.
“Such vices of perceiving faults are second nature to a demonic {!jiva!}. This dangerous vice would come and go for others [who are not demonic], and this displays the instability of one’s mind. If one hears inappropriate things about another devotee but does not see the actual event unfold, even then one would hold a dim view of that devotee. Furthermore, if one actively associates with bad company, one becomes as infectious as a rabid dog. They die and their {!jiva!} is destroyed i.e. they become wholly demonic.
“One can gain mental stability, divine sight and a liking for performing service if one accepts the words of the {!Motāpurush!} when he says, ‘This certain person is free of any flaws whatsoever.’ However, what becomes of one who will only accept the {!Motapurush’s!} words if one has to be told four or five times? The opinion of the great is the same as what Shriji Mahārāj has written on every page of the Vachanāmrut, i.e. one should refrain from finding faults. According to this, we do not have any right to find faults in others. Mahārāj himself does not do this; therefore, one should close and seal that ‘window’. This is the Vachanāmrut that describes a lifeline. Once that link has been severed, one is sure to die. One should consider this as the death of a {!jiva!}, just as the body perishes when there is no pulse.
“The vice of finding faults remains if one is only faring in Satsang based on his own efforts. If one fares on the strength given by Mahārāj then one does not see the need to find faults in others. One should not feel any scorn if one possesses detachment yet sees another eat more than necessary.
“Mahārāj says, ‘If one offers constant devotion to me, yet speaks ill of a devotee, then even if I want to maintain affinity for that devotee or feel like embracing him, I would not do so. I would think, ‘How will I even come to see the face of such a person!’ We feel such an aversion to that person. I would not listen if someone comes to poison my ears; however, I would evaluate a person for a long period of time and only then would I judge that person.
“We should engage ourselves in service without looking too much at the young or old. Mahārāj has shown only service as a means. One should become addicted to service, just like Ukā Khāchar. One should engage oneself in service so much that one destroys the whims of the mind. Mahārāj says that one who discerns the wishes of the {!Sant!} and serves after being told just once is the best. He is, whilst still alive, seated in Akshardhām and is near Mahārāj. One should not begrudgingly perform {!sevā!}, but should continually engage oneself in it. This is the means to become a worthy recipient of eternal grace.”
[Y.M. : 2/328]

13150.t:
24 March 1960, Livingstone, Zambia. 
During the discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “One whose focus is totally immersed in the form of God possesses the following qualities: If one is extremely fatigued, so much so that one’s back is aching and that one does not even possess the strength to sit up, then when there is a discourse, one would become extremely attentive as if nothing has happened.
“One would generally think, ‘We have travelled many miles by car and are thus tired; therefore, we do not want to engage in discourses.’ However, one who cannot remain without discourses would not feel any fatigue whatsoever. Such was the innate nature of Nirgun Swāmi.
“If one maintains the same amount of excitement for discourses as one would if one has gained hundreds of thousands of rupees, one would not feel ill or fatigued and one would not take any insult to heart. One would subsequently engage oneself in listening to the discourses. If someone forgets to serve yoghurt during one’s meal, one would take it to heart and say, ‘I have been left out. No one gave me any yoghurt.’ Even if one does not say anything, one will still take it to mind. However, if one instead starts praising the other items that one has been served, saying, “Oh wow, what curry! What vegetables!” How much joy would one experience? Thus, in the same way, if one becomes attentive during the discourses, one will enjoy them. Even if one is suffering from an ailment, has been insulted badly, or has been spoilt by earning much wealth, the minute one hears the discourses of God, one should act as if nothing affects them. One should reach this level when it comes to hearing the discourses of God. Mahārāj also mentions people who are ill in this Vachanāmrut – he has not left anyone out. He has included even the ill, the indulgent and the affluent, whoever they may be. Someone who is said to be immersed in God’s form must imbibe these qualities.”
[Y.M. : 3/64]

13155.t: Yogiji Mahārāj asked, “In Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 30, aside from the pure {!chaitanya!} Brahma which transcends Prakruti-Purush, which other Brahma is there?” Whilst answering his own question, he said, “As per Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 31, {!Mahāpurush!} [{!aksharmukta!}] is like Brahma and pairs up with Prakruti [in the creation of infinite universes].”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 24/11]

13167.t:
24 March 1960, Livingstone, Zambia.
After having Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 30 read, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Once, Gunātitānand Swāmi arrived in Ghoghāvadar. He took some rest at the small shrine of Shankar on the banks of the river and Jāgā Swāmi was reading the Vachanāmrut. He read Vachanāmruts Gadhadā I 23, Gadhadā II 30, Gadhadā II 45, Amdāvād 2 and Amdāvād 3. Swāmi then got up and said, ‘It is as if we have never heard these Vachanāmruts.’ Thus saying, he instructed Jāgā Swāmi to read them again. Did Swāmishri not initially hear them? He did; however, he was overflowed with love and wanted to speak on the basis of these Vachanāmruts, as the essence of all five Vachanāmruts is the same. One line of thought is discussed in all five Vachanāmruts.
“One will notice that Shriji Mahārāj is talking on the basis of the Bhāgwat. People worshipping the past incarnations will accuse the Swāminārāyan fellowship of having no scriptural underpinnings; however, Shriji Mahārāj bases his talks on the essence of all the scriptures. If it was a complete break-off, as others would suggest, would Mahārāj encompass others’ philosophies in his talks?... 
“Mahārāj clearly states in the Vachanāmrut, ‘Events only occur as the scriptures have foretold and not otherwise.’ It is said in the Shrimad Bhāgwat that the dark age ({!Kaliyuga!}) resides in gold – we have seen this first hand. There are goldmines here, within which the dark age is present; hence gold is the reason why no one wants to emigrate from this country. People end up fighting and destroying each others’ property. If one looks at the rich, they have an innate nature of showing off their wealth. It is all for show and they are unable to actually spend as much as they show.
“Therefore, understand women and wealth to be the source of extreme attachment. What do we mean by ‘extreme’? Once attached, one cannot remove one’s focus from it, to the extent that one becomes a ghost at the end of one’s life to hover around the subject of one’s attachment. Mahārāj shows us a path whereby one can be free of all attachments.
“Consider one’s own form to be that of the pure, luminous Brahma. Who is that person? One who possesses the true knowledge that ‘Gunātitānand Swāmi is Mul Akshar.’ If one does not understand accordingly, one is tainted! One may consider oneself to be Brahma; however, at the same time, they do not possess a single quality of Brahma. Therefore, it is vital to understand that one cannot attain the {!brahmarup!} state unless one realises the truth that Gunātit[ānand Swāmi] is Mul Akshar. One cannot attain such an elevated spiritual state through considering oneself to be {!brahmarup!} based on the previous incarnations of God. One must have attained Shriji Mahārāj, Aksharbrahma or the manifest form of Akshar currently on this earth in the form of a {!Sant!}. One can only tread this path if one contemplates deeply on these words. We do not become {!brahmarup!} the minute we start considering ourselves to be so; however, one will eventually attain that state. We point out someone who has just started the sixth standard by saying, ‘They are in the sixth standard’; in the same way, when we are still in the process of learning the lessons of Akshardhām, we can start considering ourselves to be {!brahmarup!} and eventually we will reach that state.
“After this, one should sit idly, right? No! One should continually worship God, considering no one else to be above God. Secondly, one considers the creations of Prakruti-Purush to be perishable, false and insignificant; therefore, not worth pursuing. Thus, one would take an adverse view on the pleasures of this world and also not think that there is any point in pursuing worldly happiness. [One reaches a stage so significant that] one’s mind would not waver in the slightest, even if given millions of tonnes of gold.”
[Y.M. : 3/65]

13192.t:
25 January 1965, Mumbai. 
During the morning discourse, whilst explaining Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 32, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “To recognise God and the {!Sant!} is knowledge. To think about their glory is meditation.”
“What is immense greatness? To become like Gunātit. “
“What is knowledge of the {!pratyaksh!} form? Harshadbhāi! Give the answer!” 
Harshadbhāi replied, “You give the answer Bāpā!” 
Yogiji Mahārāj said, “You won’t give the answer. You know it! The whole Satsang reads this Vachanāmrut but they misunderstand it. In this universe, many kids are studying. However, before they attain a Bachelor of Arts, they must study at a lower level. How can they know about Akshar Purushottam? The deficiencies of infinite births can only be eradicated if one has past merits. It is difficult to understand [Swāminārāyan Bhagwān’s] supremacy. We have attained that same Shriji Mahārāj who resides in Akshardhām. That is the understanding of [Mahārāj’s] profound glory.
[Y.M. : 3/720]

13211.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Without observing the vow of non-lust, even if one has attained knowledge and studied the scriptures, it will amount to nothing. This knowledge will fall in vain. If one develops worldly desires, they should start turning a {!mālā!} immediately. If one maintains desires for the opposite gender, everything [on the spiritual path] becomes futile. On the contrary, one does not develop a desire to become {!ekāntik!}. A renunciant who craves worldly desires should be considered a fool… The summit of a mountain looks beautiful from a distance, but once up-close all one can see are stones. Mere stones! Mahārāj has told the {!paramhansas!} that one will go to hell if one craves and indulges in worldly pleasures. Thus by eradicating one’s inner desires for women and wealth, one is already sitting in Akshardhām… The bodies of men and women are full of {!māyā!} and dirt. They are composed of bone and nothing else. Why would a pure aspirant like a {!paramhansa!} desire such things? Mahārāj imposed an order on this; thus one should develop an aversion to worldly objects.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 28/4]

13214.t:
Shriji Mahārāj says in this Vachanāmrut: “… all of My divine actions and incidents, as well as the chanting of My name, are redemptive. When I explained this to Swarupānand Swāmi, the agonising pain in his body due to his illness was completely relieved, and he felt profound peace. In fact, he could see his own {!ātmā!} very well, yet it was of no use…”
The history behind these words is as follows:
When Mahārāj arrived to Gadhpur from Vartāl, Swarupānand Swāmi was ill. He was resting at the place Jivā Khāchar had made for sādhus. Mahārāj regularly visited him every night wearing a sky-colored {!reto!} from Jamnagar, tied a red-colored Burānpur {!reto!} with golden thread embroidery on the ends to His head; and carried a golden sword and dagger. He also tried another {!reto!} around his waist. Golden rings adorned His fingers. He tied a {!bukāni!} around His head and sat with support of cushions. The brave {!pārshads!} Bhaguji and Jasoji brought Mahārāj to Swarupānand Swāmi at night. Mahārāj spent about 1½ hours (four {!ghadi!}) narrating novel talks; yet the sādhus never felt satisfied listening. At daybreak, the {!pārshads!} would prompt Mahārāj to leave, so Mahārāj would return and sleep on His cot. Thus, He would talk at times, have Premānand Swāmi sing {!kirtans!}, or talk about Rāmānand Swāmi. Sometimes He spoke about His {!van-vicharan!} or His childhood {!lilā!} in Ayodhyā that no one had heard before. During these activities, Swarupānand Swāmi was at peace; otherwise, he was in agonizing pain. Other sādhus sprayed fine mist of water or had him drink soothing water mixed with grapes or {!sākar!} or applied {!chandan!} on his body. Mahārāj would prepare {!chandan!}, fill it in a pot and apply it on Swarupānand Swāmi. None of these remedies caused any difference in Swarupānand Swāmi.
Thus, Mahārāj said, “You are very powerful. You behave above the three bodies ({!sthul, sukshma, kāran!}) and the three states ({!jāgrat, swapna, sushupti!}). Such is your accomplished state, so what is causing your distress?”
Swarupānand Muni folded his hands and said, “You saved me from the ego of my achieved state. You are the all-capable Bhagwān. If you don’t point out mistakes, then even the deities will not be able to see their own mistakes. No one is comparable to you… I only ask that I never forget your {!murti!} and your {!lilā charitra!}.”
Mahārāj said, “I have sprayed colored water countless times in Jivā Khāchar’s and Dādā Khāchar’s {!darbār!}. I have also discoursed to sādhus and {!haribhaktas!} innumerable time. Contemplate on all that you have witnessed.”
Swarupānand Muni heeded to Shriji Mahārāj’s advice and felt peace in his heart. Shortly, he abandoned his physical body to permanently sit in Akshardhām. Those sādhus who were present witnessed Swarupānand Swāmi going to Akshardhām.
[H.C.S. : 15/47]

13237.t:
In this Vachanāmrut, Shriji Mahārāj elucidates the characteristics of a genuine {!Sant!}: “… one whose mind remains unmoved - that is, it does not become ‘hot’ upon experiencing repulsive {!vishays!} and does not become ‘cold’ upon experiencing pleasurable {!vishays!} should be known as a {!Param-Bhāgwat Sant!}.”
In this short Vachanāmrut, Mahārāj has defined the characteristics of a genuine {!Sant!} twice. This Vachanāmrut was spoken on Jyeshth sud 11 of Samvat 1878 (Bhim Ekādashi). Prior to this day, the incident that took place is as follows:
One {!haribhakta!} came from the port city of Diu to see Mahārāj. After Mahārāj called him, he prostrated and sat in front of Mahārāj. Mahārāj inquired as to why he had come so urgently.
He folded his hands and explained, “Mahārāj, an impostor has come to our city. He claims to be the {!avatār!} of Nar, and Nārāyan, who is Sahajānand, is my brother. He knows the names of all of the {!sādhus!} of the {!sampradāy!}. He also knows our {!niyams!}. The gullible among the people have developed faith in his words. He says women should not listen to talks of {!sādhus!} and shun their contact; however there is no objection in listening to his talks. Therefore, women serve him, which can likely lead to an immoral outcome. I just learned a few days ago that he is the {!Brāhmin!} Mulo Rājgor of Rājulā.”
“How long has he been there?” Mahārāj asked.
“It’s been about one month. Since the Portuguese control Diu, no one can enter Diu without their permission. {!Sādhus!} do not come to Diu, therefore, the people do not know the truths of satsang.”
Mahārāj questioned, “Mulo Rājgor had deceived Premābāi (see history for Kāriyāni 6), yet you still didn’t recognize him?”
The {!haribhakta!} said, “Mahārāj, he poses in different guises and can change his dialect accordingly. People are deceived by his tricks.”
Mahārāj consoled, “Do not worry. Krupānand Swāmi and Purnānand Swāmi are travelling in Vālāk Desh. I will send a message to them to go straight to Unā. From Unā, Hansarāj Sheth will bring them to Diu. When the imposter sees them he will immediately pack and leave.”
“But, Mahārāj. The Portuguese will not let Hansarāj Sheth enter.”
“Don’t worry about that. There is a barber named Haribhāi there. He is trusted by the Portuguese and he had served me once. Give him My name and tell him to go to Ghoghalā and from there to take Hansarāj Sheth and the {!sādhus!} to Diu… Caution the women not to become ensnared by him; otherwise, no good will come of it.”
So saying, Mahārāj sent the {!haribhakta!} off and sent a message to the {!sādhus!} by horseback. As soon as the sādhus arrived in Diu, Mulo Rājgor was alerted. He immediately packed and left by boat for Mumbai without speaking to anyone.
The {!sādhus!} spoke to the people of Diu. The women realized that if these {!sādhus!}had not come we would have transgressed our vow of fidelity. Hansarāj Sheth wrote a letter containing everything that transpired in Diu. Mahārāj had the letter read in the assembly and said, “To fulfill one’s desire for enjoying {!vishays!}, the sinners will pose as God. Therefore, in practising Satsang, one should forsake being too gullible and too over-wise.”
[B.S. : 4/354-357]
The preceding incident occurred immediately before Gadhadā II 23. Therefore, Mahārāj is cautioning against such pseudo-{!sādhus!} by repeatedly and emphatically illuminating the faults of a pseudo-{!sādhu!} in order to establish the characteristics of a genuine {!sādhu!}. The background of this discourse seems to be Mulo Rājgor’s incident.

13256.t: 25 October 1956, Gondal. \r\nDuring the discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 37. When I first came to Krishnacharandas Swāmi to become a {!sādhu!}, at that time he made me memorise this Vachanāmrut and made me put it into practice.” \r\n[Y.M. : 2/134]

13258.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Harsh words are the most intense of the intense and have such intensity that they have the potential to burn one’s hair. As per Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 37, ‘No matter how painfully strong the {!Satpurush’s!} words seem, one accepts those words to be for one’s own benefit.’ We are not saying this; these are Mahārāj’s own words. One who, as a result of these harsh words, does not even experience inner unhappiness ranks first. One who experiences unhappiness ranks second. We do not have an aversion towards anyone and, thus, are at peace. An ignorant person who develops an aversion towards others does not run away but stays in Satsang – albeit gradually deteriorating over time. When a senior is reading the Vachanāmrut and one thinks, ‘I totally understand this Vachanāmrut’ – this is known as possessing ego of one’s own virtues.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 15/25]

13260.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “What is the difference between contempt and harsh words? Contempt means one is driven away; one’s base instincts are stung in the form of harsh words.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 24/219]

13261.t:
10 January 1962, Mumbai. 
After having Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 37 read in the afternoon assembly, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “It is said in the Gitā that even a knowledgeable person acts according to his nature. On the basis of this Vachanāmrut, we should look within ourselves, not at others. We should become fearless and remove the bad habits that we may have in our lives. If one trusts the {!Satpurush!} in whatever means he employs to rid us of our flaws, one will pass the test with first class honours; otherwise one will not pass even after two years. One should act according to the {!Satpurush’s!} wishes. The {!Satpurush!} is never silent. He will speak. One should trust every word he says. True love is to continually take in his words. If one considers the {!Satpurush’s!} words to be beneficial even if the {!Satpurush!} rebukes one, then any [adverse] base nature will not remain. Whoever has a desire for liberation should employ this technique, despite facing any level of insult. Is this measurable? Is this talk for anyone else? It is for us. One should not feel any grief in one’s heart.
“What is the difference between harsh words and insult? Insult is where one is thrown out, ‘Go away from here! I do not want to even see your face!’ Harsh words is when one is called a fool. One experiences grief after hearing a few words like this. Even though Mulji and Krishnaji were driven out after being rebuked, they went outside and started singing devotional songs. Such faith! True devotion is to follow the words of the {!Satpurush!}. Even if one possesses the quality of detachment, if the {!Motāpurush!} instructs one to eat, then one should eat without questioning.”
[Y.M. : 3/279]

13271.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “What are the fruits of having a human body? To remain in good company and forsake one’s base instincts. One has attained good company, but is still hindered by one’s base instincts. One can overcome one’s base instincts by perfecting Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 37. This solution is not mentioned in the Gitā or the Bhāgwat. Mahārāj says that even if the discourser [the {!Satpurush!}] speaks harsh and difficult words, one should accept them as beneficial. Even if one is insulted and thrown out, one should not be upset by this in any way.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 9/30]

13272.t: Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 37 states: “Even a person possessing spiritual knowledge behaves according to one’s nature. When the {!Satpurush!} gives guidance and utters harsh words for the benefit of the devotee, if the devotee has total faith in these words, has deep affection for the {!Satpurush!} and accepts these words to be for one’s own benefit, then one’s innate natures will be eradicated. Therefore, one should not get over-excited by these words. By developing such excitement, one’s innate natures cannot be eradicated. If the {!Satpurush!} utters harsh words and one forsakes such feelings, and acts as per the {!Satpurush’s!} commands, only then will one’s innate natures be eradicated.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 13/4]

13273.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “One who becomes disturbed is unable to become {!ātmārup!}. How can the {!Satpurush!} maintain trust in us? Only if one sacrifices themselves for his sake. The {!Satpurush!} thus recognises the strength of one’s {!jiva!} by believing, ‘Regardless of the harsh words I may utter to this individual, he will not leave the Satsang.’ He may pull away one’s eating bowl. If {!dudhpāk!} is on the menu and he commands one to undertake a fast, one becomes disturbed and thinks ‘I will do the fast tomorrow.’ But if one is firmly told, ‘You must observe the fast today!’, then only one who craves liberation is able to endure this; others would run away. Consequently one’s prospects for liberation are spoilt. One who possesses a deep spiritual desire will maintain a wish to eradicate one’s base instincts. If one is able to pass through such testing times, one will attain the foremost position for liberation. One should never become pained during testing times. One should perceive virtues in the person who advises him, not perceive their faults. If one behaves like this, even if one has a mischievous nature, it will be eradicated.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 28/26]

13278.t:
30 March 1970, Mwanza, Tanzania.
After having Gadhadā II 37 read at 1:30pm, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “There are three vices that are the superintendent of all: obstinacy, ego and jealousy. These are the three most dangerous vices that lead to one’s downfall from the path of liberation. Other vices do not necessarily divert one from the goal of liberation. One may have a whole range of bad habits, for example overeating and oversleeping; however, these are the only three vices that prove to be an obstacle on the pathway to liberation. People may have differing levels of {!matsar!}, however, it does not detract one from achieving liberation. The three [devotees] who falsely attributed these vices to Shriji Mahārāj backtracked on the path of Satsang. One who is obstinate does not listen to anyone. How did Faibā falter? She ensured her downfall through obstinacy. Alaiyā Khachar left due to his ego and Jivā Khachar was unable to leave his jealousy. One should have a straightforward nature and follow every instruction of the {!Motāpurush!}]. Such people will not fall from the path of Satsang. If one is forced to renounce the whims of one’s mind and subsequently takes offence, one will surely renounce the path of Satsang at some stage. One should thus endeavour to eradicate one’s vices.
“This is an essential Vachanāmrut. The essence of what is to be understood is that one should renounce their base natures. One should thus not harbour obstinacy, ego and jealousy.
“There was a {!brahmachāri!} based in Junāgadh called Ishānand. A {!parshad!} once asked Ishānand, ‘Please kindly let me know if you see any vices in me.’ He had a habit of dozing off and once dozed off in the assembly to the extent that his head ended up touching the ground. [{!Brahmachāri!}] remarked in the assembly, ‘Why are you dozing off?’ The {!parshad!} took offence to this, thinking, ‘[He] had the guts to tell me off in {!sabhā!}? He should have told me off privately.’ Thus, he got angry on the [{!brahmachāri!}]. He did not renounce his anger. If one truly desires liberation, one will renounce one’s vices. If one does not have any eagerness to do this, one will feel offended every so often.
“We read the Vachanāmrut every day; however, when the time comes, we are unable to put it into practice. Everything ends up going wrong when the time comes to apply these Vachanāmruts.”
[Y.M. : 6/118]

13279.t: 25 October 1956, Gondal. \r\nDuring the discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “One should be eager for two things – one is liberation and the other is renouncing one’s vices. This is in accordance with Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 37. When I first came to Krishnacharan Swāmi to become a {!sādhu!}, he made me memorise and perfect this Vachanāmrut. One should have great faith and conviction in the words of the {!Satpurush!}; considering whatever he says to be beneficial to oneself, continually see the good in the person talking to oneself.”\r\n[Y.M. : 2/134]

13296.t: March 1959, Advāl.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “One should renounce one’s bad habits. There are two Vachanāmruts that talk of this: Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 37 and Gadhadā III 35; master these. One who is good will find faults within oneself, despite the fact that one feels perplexed when one’s habits are spoken about. One who finds faults in the {!Sant!} never progresses [in Satsang]. One’s bad habits can be eradicated if one tries.”\r\n[Y.M. : 2/530]

13322.t: 8 September 1967, Mumbai. \r\nExplaining Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 38 during the morning discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “To not be able to stay without God is {!ekāntik bhakti!}. What does it mean to merge? To develop such a feeling is to merge. One’s own awareness does not remain. Just as a father says, ‘Look, son, here comes mother!’ But whose mother, the father’s or his son’s? That is merging with your child… Just as Vignāndas constantly remembered Bhagatji, similarly we should constantly remember like that.”\r\n[Y.M. : 4/521]

13348.t: 19 April 1970, Mombasa. \r\nExplaining Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 40 during his afternoon discourse at 1pm at Ravibhāi’s house, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “To maintain one’s reputation with others, one maligns the {!Gunātit Mandal!}. They look good to others and want good food. Shukmuni Swāmi had goodwill for Gunātitānand Swāmi. Thus, Siddhānand Swāmi remarked, ‘What does Shukmuni know? He is a parrot.’ Siddhānand Swāmi said to Shivlal Sheth, ‘There are very hard black stones in Junagadh. Take an oath that you will not go there. Hold my feet.’ Shivlāl responded, ‘I will only hold your feet if I don’t go to Junagadh.’ In this way, many knowingly maligned the {!Motāpurush!}. If offence is caused amongst yourselves, then seek forgiveness. Don’t think, ‘What does he know?’ Always remain as a servant of a servant with God’s devotees.”\r\n[Y.M. : 6/165]

13354.t: 24 June 1962, Mumbai. \r\nExplaining Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 40 during the afternoon discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “We should always do 10 prostrations and one extra. Five for liberation and six as per the {!niyam!}. Don’t do prostrations like a frog. Offer eight-fold prostrations.”\r\n[Y.M. : 3/364]

13371.t: August 1966, Atlādrā.\r\nOnce, after lunch, Yogiji Mahārāj had Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 40 recited and said, “I don’t know how to harm a devotee of God. I don’t know how to gossip. I don’t have such intellect. I only know how to perform {!sevā!} and that is all I have done.”\r\n[Y.M. : 4/283]

13396.t:
6 April 1959, Dāngrā. 
After completing his usual morning routine, Yogiji Mahārāj lucidly explained Vachanāmruts Gadhadā II 41 and Gadhadā II 44 in detail by saying, “The eminent devotee Kuberbhāi, who hailed from Bhavnagar, would say, ‘When we go to the {!mandir!}, does {!Thakorji!} verbally welcome one into the {!mandir!}? Despite this, we maintain divinity in {!Thakorji!}. In the same way, even if a {!sādhu!} ignores one, at least consider him to be like a deity! If the {!Satpurush!} ignores one, one may not perceive faults in the {!Sant!}; however, a doubt still crosses one’s mind. However, one should renounce doubtfulness and maintain divinity. It is a good thing that [the {!Sant!}] does not go as far as rebuking one; ego can only be eradicated if one still does not feel insulted despite the {!Sant!} scolding one. Disregarding those of a smaller stature and only looking after those with stature amounts to {!manushyabhav!}.
“Even if one is so detached to the extent that one would not even keep a wooden peg in their possession, if one starts to find faults in others, then it is all in vain. Of what use is such detachment? Therefore, [Gunātitānand] Swāmi used to say, ‘It is acceptable if one is not able to perform austerities, but, one should not find faults in others.’ However much others eat, never perceive faults. One may end up fasting for five consecutive days, even without water. One’s ego would inflate by thinking, ‘Oh, see how much penance I am performing.’ What is the point of that? Even if one eats heavily three times a day, maintaining divinity in others even if rebuked, then ego is said to be eradicated. Mahārāj calls such a devotee ‘ego-free’.
“Ego has many ‘customers’. If everyone considers everyone else to be of inferior intelligence, who is going to remain humble and bow to others? Thinking in this way, one would not gain any peace.
“Normally, everyone talks about humility. However, one’s humility is truly tested when the time comes. It is for this reason that Mahārāj advises all to associate [with Satsang]. True association is defined as maintaining divinity in one another and not not find any faults in others, despite staying together.”
[Y.M. : 2/557]

13428.t: 18 January 1964, Mumbai. \r\nDuring the afternoon assembly, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “So that the {!Satpurush!} is not displeased and so that he remains pleased forever, one should ponder over Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 45.” \r\n[Y.M. : 3/578]

13429.t:
In Samvat 1919, Gunātitānand Swāmi started his journey toward Vartāl for the {!samaiyo!} of Chaitra sud 15 [{!Punam!}]. He stayed one day in Gondal and then arrived in Goghāvadar, a village nearby. He stayed at the Shiv Mandir on the river bank. While resting in the afternoon, he had Jāgā Bhakta read the Vachanāmrut. Jāgā Bhakta read five Vachanāmruts: Gadhadā I-23, Gadhadā II-30 and 45, Amdāvād 2 and 3. Hearing these Vachanāmruts, Swāmi sat up and said, “It is as if I had never heard these Vachanāmruts.” He said, “Read them again.” Jāgā Swāmi read them again.
Then Swāmi said, “Listening to these Vachanāmruts, I have concluded that even after millions of years, without behaving in this way, there is no final release. So, for us, there is no alternative but to do this. Also, even if one is an {!āchārya!}, a son of Bhagwān, an {!ishwar!}, or some small or big deity, still there is no release without behaving in that way. Since, that is Mahārāj’s belief.” Based on this, Swāmi recited some couplets quoted by Mahārāj: ‘{!Nijātmānam brahmarupam…’!}, ‘{!Brahmabhutah prasannātmā…’!}, ‘{!Parinishthitopi nairgunye…’!}, ‘{!Atmāramāshcha munayo’!}.
After reciting many such couplets, he said, “When one becomes like this, then Bhagwān resides in one’s heart.” Then, looking at a devotee, he said, “You do have a {!murti!}, but without a {!mandir!} where will you install it? So, if you want to install Bhagwān, then learn to prepare a {!mandir!} as described here, then Bhagwān will stay.”
Then he continued, “When the {!sādhus!} went to get the {!murtis!} for this mandir [Junagadh], the sculptor asked, ‘What type of {!murtis!} shall I make for you?’ Then the sādhus said, ‘Make them according to these designs.’ Then the sculptor said, ‘These {!murtis!} are suitable only for a mandir worth hundreds of thousands of rupees.’ Then the sādhus said, ‘We’ve come to take {!murtis!} in accordance with such a mandir.’ So the sculptor said, ‘Then I’ll make them.’ Then the sculptor sculpted the {!murtis!}. Similarly, without becoming {!brahmarup!} where will we install Purushottam? So, if you want to install Purushottam, you have to become {!brahmarup!}.” Having said this, he got up. Then he held a devotee’s wrist and while walking told him, “Beware, never have any [worldly] desires.” Then that devotee’s desires stopped. And Swāmi said, “If one can remain like this all the time, doubts, strong attachments to one’s karma, desires, affection for worldly relations, body-consciousness, etc. and countless other strong material bonds are destroyed and one can continually stay focused on Bhagwān.”
[S.V. : 3/13]

13484.t: 17 November 1965, Gondal. \r\nThe morning discourses were ongoing. Yogiji Mahārāj suddenly looked up whilst reading letters and spoke, “Read Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 45. The whole world can be conquered. The fifty one {!bhuts!} can be expelled.” \r\n[Y.M. : 4/157]

13500.t: 14 July 1964, Mumbai. \r\nExplaining Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 45 during the spiritual discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “In this [Vachanāmrut], Mahārāj has described 51 ghosts. In addition, inappropriate {!swabhāvs!} plus desires give a grand total of 53 ghosts that have clung to the {!jiva!}.”\r\n[Y.M. : 3/661]

13507.t:
In this Vachanāmrut, Shriji Mahārāj says: “A {!Satpurush!} living in this world is not pleased or pained upon seeing the worldly progress or regress of a person. However, when someone’s mind recedes from the path of God, he does become grieved. After all, life is so short; and if a person’s afterlife is ruined, it would indeed be a great loss for that person… For such {!ekāntik bhaktas!}, leaving the body is not considered to be death; rather, for them, falling from that {!ekāntik dharma!} is true death. This occurs when an aversion arises in one’s heart towards God or His {!Sant!}. It is then that that devotee should be known to have fallen from the {!dharma!} of {!ekāntik bhaktas!}… Therefore, to perceive flaws in God and His {!Bhakta!} is a graver sin than committing the five grave sins.”
When we scrutinize Mahārāj’s words, we remember Āmbā Sheth’s incident; since, during this time, Āmbā Sheth suffered a drawback from Satsang when he perceived human traits in Shriji Mahārāj.
Mahārāj was leaving the women devotees’ assembly at Vāsudev-Nārāyan’s room after giving Jivubā and Lādubā {!darshan!}. He passed under the neem tree where Adibā approached from Panchālā. As He walked down the steps, Mahārāj touched Adibā’s shoulder. The momentary touch thrilled Adibā because Mahārāj had fulfilled her wish. Once, in Panchālā, Mahārāj said He wanted to get married – which was merely a {!manushya-charitra!}. Adibā was ready to wed Mahārāj; however, Mahārāj reversed His insistence on getting married and Adibā’s wish to marry Mahārāj remained unfulfilled. However, she secretly wished that at least Mahārāj bless her with His touch once. Mahārāj fulfilled that wish as He walked down the steps.
Coincidently, Āmbā Sheth of Gadhādi was also present and observed Mahārāj touching Adibā. His faith was shaken, “This is Bhagwān? Someone who touches a young woman, and yet preaches from the scriptures that this is forbidden?” Āmbā Sheth instantly turned back to Gadhādi. One who came daily from Gadhādi to Gadhadā for Mahārāj’s {!darshan!} stopped coming.
Mahārāj didn’t see him for five to six days, so He commented, “Has the mango tree ({!āmbo!}) dried up?” With that hint, He sent Muktānand Swāmi to investigate what happened to Āmbā Sheth. Muktānand Swāmi learned what had transpired and explained perceiving divinity in all of Bhagwān’s actions. Āmbā Sheth realized the truth and asked Mahārāj for forgiveness, “Mahārāj, forgive me. Bless me so that I do not develop {!manushya-bhāv!} is your actions.”
[B.S. : 4/423-429]
In this manner, Āmbā Sheth begged for forgiveness and invited Mahārāj to Gadhādi along with 50 sādhus. Mahārāj accepted so Āmbā Sheth left to prepare for Mahārāj’s arrival. Mahārāj, however, asked everyone to come along to Gadhādi. An entourage of over 500 gathered to go instead of just 50.
Seeing so many {!sādhus!} and {!haribhaktas!}, Āmbā Sheth became perplexed. Worrying about his own family, he requested, “Mahārāj, there’s ten of us in my family. Give us enough for the ten of us, and you can serve everyone as you please.” Once again, Āmbā Sheth became entangled in Mahārāj’s human-like actions. Mahārāj served 500 people from the food prepared. When Mahārāj departed, Āmbā Sheth saw the same amount of food left as before everyone ate. He realized his unbecoming selfishness and felt hurt from making a mistake again. He again asked Mahārāj for forgiveness and resolved in his mind: In no way should I perceive flaws in Bhagwān; whatever He does is appropriate.
Oscillating between Mahārāj’s divine and human-like actions, these two incidents of Āmbā Sheth occurred around the time of Gadhadā II 46. After both these incidents, we find the following references: Dādā Khāchar prepared to celebrate the festival of Vasant in Gadhpur. At that moment, a message came from Sundariyānā that Himrāj Sheth has passed away to {!dhām!}. Therefore, on the first day of the month of Māgh (Mahā) of Āshādhi Samvat 1880, Mahārāj departed for Sundariyānā with an entourage.
[B.S. : 4/430-431]
The incidents regarding Āmbā Sheth occurred prior to this departure according to the scriptures of the Swāminārāyan {!Sampradāy!} – these incidents must have occurred during the first half ({!vad paksha!}) of the month of Posh and this Vachanāmrut is dated Posh vad Ekādashi. We can conclude that Āmbā Sheth falling from Satsang was the basis for this Vachanāmrut.
Also noteworthy is that the preaching in the Vachanāmrut are not just empty words, but behind these words is a purification process for each and every {!bhakta!} and a resolution of their problems.

13510.t: 2 February 1955, Gānā. \r\nAfter reading Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 46 during the afternoon discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “The {!ekāntik!} [devotee] of God is the pathway to God. To have an aversion for him should be known as falling from the path of God. What is {!ekāntik dharma!}? [Understanding] that the {!Satpurush!} manifest on earth is {!ekāntik dharma!}.”\r\n[Y.M. : 1/539]

13513.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “In the Vachanāmrut titled ‘The Death-line’, Mahārāj explains that when an aversion arises in one’s heart towards God or his {!Sant!}, it is at that point that that devotee should be known to have fallen from {!ekāntik dharma!}. To fall from {!ekāntik dharma!} is death for an {!ekāntik bhakta!}. To develop an aversion for God and his {!Sant!} is a far greater sin than the five grave sins stated in the scriptures. Thus one should perform service, but never perform disservice, which is to develop an aversion.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 7/29]

13514.t: Explaining Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 46, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Regardless of how much one is worshipped or seated upon a grand dais or considered a {!sadguru!}, if one perceives faults in a person like Shāstriji Mahārāj, then one is considered dead despite being alive.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 24/257]

13535.t:
The following recollection appears in this Vachanāmrut: Premānand Swāmi was singing ‘{!Vandu Sahajānand ras roop, anupam sārne re lol!}...’ - devotional songs useful for meditation. After he had finished singing, Shriji Mahārāj commented, “The devotional songs you sang were very nice. After listening to them I thought in My mind, ‘Since this {!sādhu!} contemplates upon God’s form in this way, let Me get up and prostrate before him.’
The reason for Mahārāj praising Premānand Swāmi’s ability to write such verses is based on the historical account that follows:
Shriji Mahārāj was in Gadhadā when a {!Brāhmin!} devotee of {!Devi!} from Shakhalpur named Vijayshankar arrived. He folded his hands before Mahārāj and said, “Mahārāj, you are God but, if you allow me, I will sing a {!garbo!} of {!Devi!} that I worship.”
Mahārāj gave His approval and the {!Brāhmin!} sang:
{!Mā tu pāvānī paṭarāṇī ke, kāḷī kāḷikā re lol!};
{!Mā tāro ḍungarḍe chhe vās ke, chaḍavu dohyalu re lol!}.
{!Māḍī tārā mukhnī maroḍatā joī, harāṇo garva chandano re lol!};
{!Māḍī e mukhaḍu jovā kāj, āve chhe kunvar nandno re lol!}...
Shriji Mahārāj was pleased listening to Vijayshankar’s tune and gave the {!Brāhmin!} gifts in return. Later, Mahārāj said to Premānand Swāmi, “Did you listen to Mataji’s {!garbo!}?” The tune was nice and manner of singing was also nice. He sang the greatness of Mātāji. You also compose a {!garbi!} like that.”
Premānand Swāmi accepted Mahārāj’s {!āgnā!} and on the next day (Mahā vad 14), Premānand Swāmi sang his composition in the veranda of Dādā Khāchar’s {!darbār!}:
{!Vandu Sahajānand rasrūp, anupam sārne re lol!};
{!Jene bhajtā chhuṭe fand, kare bhav pārne re lol!}...
One by one, Premānand Swāmi sang 8 verses, which was reciprocated by Mahārāj’s praise.
[B.S. : 4/436]
Even today, all {!sādhus!} and {!haribhaktas!} sing Premānand Swāmi’s eight verses when singing {!cheshtā!} at night.

13537.t:
Yogiji Mahārāj said, “‘{!Vandu Sahajānand ras-rup, anupan sārne re lol’!} -Premānand Swāmi sang this {!garbi!} in front of Mahārāj. Mahārāj became pleased and said, ‘Ask for whatever you wish.’ Premānand Swāmi said, ‘Mahārāj, all I wish is that your {!murti!} remains with me constantly.’
“Mahārāj replied, ‘The means for that are different. When you become the form of Gunātit [{!akshar-rup!}], then My {!murti!} will remain with you constantly.’
“Without becoming {!akshar-rup!}, no one has the right to offer {!bhakti!} to Purushottam.”
[Yogi Vāni : 2/51]

13538.t: Samvat 1949, Gadhadā. \r\nWhen the devotees went to Bhagatji Mahārāj’s residence in the morning for his {!darshan!}, he said to them, “Even if I have to take 25 births, I will purify you and take you to Akshardhām, because only then will you be at peace. Shriji Mahārāj has also said in the Vachanāmrut, ‘Although there is no reason for me to take birth… I should make a reason and take birth in the company of such {!sādhus!}.’“ \r\n[B.M. : 381]

13541.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Mahārāj informed Premānand Swāmi that the means to constantly behold the divine form of God are different. What are those means? To recognise the {!Aksharbrahma guru!} and please him.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 24/276]

13551.t: 12 May 1963, Panchālā. \r\nAfter having Gadhadā II 48 recited, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “One who contemplates on anything other than God is completely lost. College and high school students are completely lost. Office workers, people working in law and police sub-inspectors are completely lost. Dogs and donkeys don’t have wedding ceremonies. It happens automatically. That [worldly] happiness can be found in all life forms. Cattle get grass and all other necessities, but is liberation attained? It is not attained. If you have a nice house, then install the {!murti!} of {!Thākorji!}. One can then offer devotion and contemplate. One who perceives worth in worldly affairs has worldly vision. Wherever Mahārāj and Gunātitānand Swāmi have eaten are extremely sanctified [places]. Did anyone insist that we go to Dharshibhāi’s house – where Shāstriji Mahārāj had come? Did anyone tell us to [go to his house]? Despite this, we still went. Wherever God and the {!Sant!} have been is [as good as] Akshardhām.\r\n[Y.M. : 3/478]

13553.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi says, “What does not happen even after ten million births of introspection, will happen in one month with the help of the great {!Sādhu!}. Such is the power of this association. Therefore, this is our principle and Mahārāj has also said, ‘By making some excuse, I wish to be born in the midst of this kind of {!Sādhu!}.’ Such a birth has been taken by us.”\r\n[S.V. : 6/53]

13561.t: 11 March 1963, Mumbai. \r\nExplaining Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 49 in the morning discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Gunātitānand Swāmi had this Vachanāmrut read by Yogeshvardās 11 times near the infirmary for the ill {!sādhus!}. Was there anyone else who was {!pratyaksh!}? Only himself [Gunātitānand Swāmi]. Still he spoke explaining its significance.” \r\n[Y.M. : 3/449]

13565.t:
11 March 1963, Mumbai.
Whilst explaining the meaning of Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 49 during the morning discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Gunātitānand Swāmi had Yogeshwardās read this Vachanāmrut 11 times near the clinic for the ill {!sādhus!}. Was anyone else ‘the manifest form’? It was Mahārāj himself! He was speaking very meaningfully. 
“ ‘{!Muj vina jānjo re, bijā māyik sahu ākār!}.{!’!}
“Consider all forms apart from mine to be bound by {!māyā!}.
“According to Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 24, everything up to and including Prakruti-Purush is under the influence of {!māyā!}. If we propagated the fact that all of the incarnations are bound by {!māyā!}, it would not be palatable to the general public; however, if we mentioned that, ‘{!Vairat!} [{!Brahma!}] has emerged from {!māyā’!}, fully aware of the fact that all the incarnations originated from {!Vairat Brahma!}, no one would object! All of the incarnations are contained within a pore of Aksharbrahma. No-one [externally] can comprehend any knowledge above the fact that they consider Mul-Purush to be Purushottam. How can one get married even before one is born! [I.e. How can scriptures reveal this fact even before the birth of Purna Purushottam on this earth?]
“It is futile if one continues to think about forms within the influence of {!māyā!}. By that, we are referring to past incarnations of God, not physical structures such as mountains and buildings. We see all that anyway. Have we fallen in hell? This talk pertains to {!upāsanā!}.
“One cannot sentence a petty thief to death; only someone who [commits a heinous crime, such as if one] kills a prince would be sentenced to death. This only relates to one who may have associated oneself with Purushottam and then wanders elsewhere. One’s chastity is said to have lessened. One cannot comprehend a high school examination if one is still learning the alphabet.
“One’s aim should be to affirm to oneself the conviction that the true {!upāsanā!} as propagated by Mahārāj himself is above and beyond all. One should not try to get ahead of oneself. One should develop an affinity for Mahārāj, who is supreme and the cause of all incarnations. Do not wander elsewhere. We should firmly understand this.
“One should have a liking for Mahārāj’s {!murti!}, his {!sādhus!} and his {!darshan!}. One should keep Purushottam Nārāyan at the forefront of one’s life. One attains such a state if one continues to ponder upon [and imbibe] the divine words [of God] – so much so that time cannot destroy the {!ātmā, karma!} cannot influence the course of the {!ātmā!} and {!māyā!} cannot absorb the {!ātmā!}. That {!ātmā!} is thus eternally granted a place in Akshardhām!”
[Y.M. : 3/449]

13626.t: 12 January 1962, Mumbai. \r\nDuring the afternoon discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Read Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 51. It is short, but it is of great importance.” \r\n[Y.M. : 3/279]

13627.t: On November 20, 1956, Yogiji Mahārāj went to Jhārolā for the opening of the high school. Here, Yogiji Mahārāj gave the accompanying youths an {!āgnā!} for the day of fast, “Memorize Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 51.” Yogiji Mahārāj then left to visit devotees’ homes.\r\nAfter he returned, Yogiji Mahārāj had the youths recite the Vachanāmrut to him. He then said, “Since you all memorized this Vachanāmrut, you behaved as the {!ātmā!}.” Saying this, he rang the small bell that was sitting on the table nearby and said, “If one follows the command of the {!Satpurush!} to just ring a bell, then even that is considered as behaving as the {!ātmā!}.”\r\n[Y.M. : 2/128]

13628.t:
12 January 1962, Mumbai. 
During the afternoon discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Open Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 51. It is short but very important. Our base natures are a part of {!rajogun!}. Keep a peaceful nature. Do not lapse. Do not behave like a child. Behave like Gunātit. A rich person’s son would not think of himself as poor; he would believe that he is rich. Similarly we are sons of Akshar. We should believe ourselves to be Akshar. Remove our body consciousness.
“We have been born in Akshardhām. Our relatives have all gone. They have all been burnt. There is only Mahārāj and Swāmi. Mumbai and Kolkata have been burnt. As long as the influence of the {!gunas!} remains within a person, one will still be unhappy, even if one has become a {!sādhu!}.
“The mind harasses one and brings one down. The mind is very bad. It is a thief. To behave as the {!ātmā!} means to become aksharrup. Do not do anything that goes against Mahārāj’s commands. With the {!Satpurush’s!} command, you can eat three times! However, to do as he says is to behave as the {!ātmā!}.”
[Y.M. : 3/276]

13637.t:
1955. Ānand.
Yogiji Mahārāj was explaining Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 52 during {!kathā!}. The following words were read: “That which befits a householder is not appropriate for a renunciant, and that which befits a renunciant is not appropriate for a householder.”
One youth said, “Bāpā, you ask us to observe the {!niyams!} of renunciants such as not touching women and mixing food with water before eating. How should we understand that?”
Swāmishri replied, “As long as you have not married you are considered a renunciant.”
A married youth then said, “Bāpā, what about me? I am married and yet you ask me to observe these {!niyams!} as well.”
Swāmishri became thoughtful and said, “Your {!jiva!} is a renunciant. Do you not want to go to Akshardhām? Engage in {!pravrutti!} by the command [of the {!Satpurush!}] and retire from {!pravrutti!} by his command. I want to make you all {!ekāntik!}, so I ask you to follow {!niyams!}. Am I asking anyone else?”
[Y.M. : 1/551]

13641.t:
In this Vachanāmrut, Shriji Mahārāj says: “When delusion pervades one’s heart, one simply cannot perceive one’s own flaws. Thus, not being able to perceive one’s own flaws is, in fact, the very definition of delusion… They feel, ‘Although He is a {!Motāpurush!} or God, this much He is not doing properly.’ Therefore, a person who perceives faults either in God’s divine incidents or in His understanding should be known to be a non-believer and a sinner.”
Shriji Mahārāj seems to poignantly criticize those who perceive faults in God. He doesn’t spare any words and continues to deride those who doubt the divine actions of God: “Moreover, everyone has extreme vanity of the wisdom that they possess, but they do not think, ‘I do not even know anything about my own jiva’ - that is, is the {!jiva!} within this body black, or is it white? Is it long, or is it short…? Yet they find faults in the {!Motāpurush!} or in God. They feel, ‘Although He is a {!Motāpurush!} or God, this much He is not doing properly.’ Though they find faults in this way, little do the fools realise that God sees all of the {!jivas!} and {!ishwars!} who dwell in the countless millions of {!brahmānds!} as clearly as He sees a drop of water in His palm. He is also the supporter of countless millions of {!brahmānds!}…”
It’s as if Shriji Mahārāj is harshly ridiculing these types of {!jivas!} with sarcasm; but the whole {!updesh!} in this Vachanāmrut seems to be a distinct incident that occurred during this time.
Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 53 was spoken on Vaishākh sud 5 of Samvat 1880. The incident that occurred surrounding this time frame is as follows:
Vastā Khāchar, the {!darbār!} of Kāriyāni arrived in Gadhadā for Shriji Mahārāj’s {!samāgam!}. Jivā Khāchar entreated Vastā Khāchar, “Come to my {!darbār!} for the night.” Mahārāj intervened, “Since he’s come here, let Vastā Khāchar stay with us.” But due to Jivā Khāchar’s insistence, Vastā Khāchar couldn’t let go of Jivā Khāchar’s friendship and told Mahārāj, “Bāpu (Jivā Khāchar) insists to I’ll stay there and return the next day.” After Vastā Khāchar departed, Mahārāj said, “Vastā Khāchar will not return.”
“Why do you say that?” Muktānand Swāmi asked inquisitively.
Mahārāj foreshadowed, “He will fall back hearing Jivā Khāchar’s and Budhā Dhādhal’s negative words. His conviction in My {!swarup!} will break and perceive flaws in Me…”
What followed is exactly as Mahārāj described. Jivā Khāchar and Budhā Dhādhal injected poisonous words in Vastā Khāchar’s mind such that he left for Kāriyāni without seeing Shriji Mahārāj. Nevertheless, Vastā Khāchar has a positive balance of {!mumukshutā!}; so Shriji Mahārāj went to Kāriyāni to explain the truth. Vastā Khāchar understood his mistake and asked for forgiveness. Dādā Khāchar, who had also accompanied Mahārāj, added, “Vastā! On hearing a despicable person like Budhā’s words you perceived human-like traits in Mahārāj?” Having reversed the poison, Mahārāj returned to Gadhadā.
[B.S. : 4/456-462]
A substantial proof that the above incident occurred around the preaching of Gadhadā II 53 is that on Chaitra sud 9 of Samvat 1880, Shriji Mahārāj celebrated the {!samaiyo!} in Vartāl as described below:
The Hari-navami {!samaiyo!} was celebrated with great fanfare. Thereafter, Mahārāj called Brahmānand Swāmi and the sculptors for some work related to Vartāl mandir. After briefing Brahmānand Swāmi, He said, “When enough work is completed such that {!pratishthā!} can be done, let Me know.” Mahārāj returned to Gadhadā via staying at several villages on the way back.
[B.S. : 4/451]
Based on the above narrative, it must have taken Mahārāj 10 to 15 days to reach Gadhadā from Vartāl, having stayed in several villages on the way. He must have reached Gadhadā at the tail end of the first half of Chaitra month. Vastā Khāchar arrives in Gadhadā within a few days of Mahārāj arriving in Gadhadā, as according to {!sampradāy!} scriptures. This means Vastā Khāchar arrived in Gadhadā at the end of Chaitra or beginning of Vaishākh. This is when he fell prey to Jivā Khāchar’s {!kusang!}. The date of Gadhadā II-53 is Vaishakh sud 15, which follows the above incidents. Having just witnessed the incident, Mahārāj, no doubt, delivers the powerful message in this Vachanāmrut so that no one will become ensnared in such talks by {!kusangis!} in the future.

13643.t:
July 24, 1970. Sārangpur.
While reading Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 53, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Mahārāj held an assembly on an auspicious day of the month of Vaishākh.”
“Bapa, you were born in the same month.”
“No. No. We do not have a birthdate.”
“Bapa, then come to Dhāri for the {!pratishthā!}.”
“No. No. {!Hare!}! What does this Vachanāmrut say?” Swāmishri instantly became engrossed in the {!kathā!}.”
[Y.M. : 6/402]

13644.t:
6 February 1970, Nairobi.
At 1:40pm in the {!mandir!} assembly hall, Yogiji Mahārāj had Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 53 recited and said, “Shāstriji Mahārāj has propagated {!upāsanā!} after understanding [the facts]. Those that see faults in what he has propagated are non-believers and sinners. The {!Motāpurush!} only acts according to God’s commands. God has divine incidents and keeping {!divyabhāv!} in them represents a devotee’s extraordinary understanding.”
Ambalalbhāi asked a question, “Bāpā! If the {!Sant!} prevents us from doing what our mind wishes then we should keep {!divyabhāv!}, right?” Yogiji Mahārāj replied, “Yes, these are all divine incidents. Nothing else.”
[Y.M. : 6/10]

13667.t: Bhagatji Mahārāj said, “Out of the 262 Vachanāmruts, Shriji Mahārāj has called Gadhadā I 54 and Gadhadā II 54 the Vachanāmruts of {!moksha!}. He also asked Dinanath Bhatt to consider both of these as particularly relevant to him.\r\n[B.M. : 513]

13669.t: May 1954, Gondal. \r\nAt the Akshar Deri, Yogiji Mahārāj had Vachanāmruts Gadhadā II 51, II 53 and II 54 recited and said, “This {!jiva!} is not able to look at itself and think, ‘What am I like?’ It is ignorant in this way. Despite this, it still finds faults in the actions of the {!Motāpurush!}. It is the most foolish of the foolish. Therefore, keep {!divyabhāv!} and {!nirdoshbhāv!} in even the most trivial of his actions. Such understanding is only possible if one develops {!ātmabuddhi!} towards the {!Satpurush!}.”\r\n[Y.M. : 1/490]

13671.t:
September 1896 (Samvat 1952), Gadhadā.
Bhagatji looked at one of the {!sādhus!} seated in the assembly. The {!sādhu!} then recited some Vachanāmruts by heart – Gadhadā I 54, Gadhadā II 54 and Gadhadā III 21. Having heard this, Bhagatji turned to Purushottamdās of Vaso and said, “The topic is life’s ultimate goal.” 
He then added, “{!Ātmabuddhi!} towards the {!Ekāntik Sant!} of God is the unique endeavour for {!moksha!}. Shriji Mahārāj has given the key to {!moksha!} to such a {!Sant!}; therefore, that {!Sant!} is known as the gateway to {!moksha!}. Serve such a {!Sant!} by thought, word and deed, and perfect {!ekāntik dharma!}, but never fall into the habit of criticizing people. Previously, those who had negative thoughts towards the devotees of God devotees have fallen from even the most exalted status.”
[B.M. : 552]

13680.t: Yogiji Mahārāj explained, “Shriji Mahārāj is present in Satsang through the {!Gunātit Sant!}. In Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 54, Shriji Mahārāj has instructed one to maintain the four types of intellect [{!pujyabuddhi, tirthbuddhi, ātmābuddhi, and svatvabuddhi!}] towards the {!Ekāntik Sant!} of God. One who does not possess this understanding should be regarded as a bullock and wild donkey. {!Sādhus!} from Muli arrived at the village of Khārvā. There were many devotees in the village who possessed the conviction of Akshar-Purushottam. They kept the sacred images of Mahārāj and [Gunātitānand] Swāmi in their daily pujā. On seeing this, the sādhus said, ‘Why do you keep the image of Swāmi in your pujā?’\r\nThe devotees were staunch and replied, ‘Swāmi, open Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 54.’ After making them read it, the devotees added, ‘We do not want to become like a bullock and wild donkey; thus we keep the sacred image of [Gunātitānand] Swāmi along with Mahārāj’s.’ If one keeps the four types of intellect towards the {!Ekāntik Sādhu!}, Mahārāj becomes bound to one [God becomes bound by the devotion of the devotee].”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 25/85]

13693.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “God is not pleased as much by other endeavours as he is by Satsang. Satsang is the extent of one’s goodwill towards God and the {!Sant!}. To attain it is rare.”\r\n[S.V. : 5/26]

13701.t:
1 April 1941, Rājkot.
Yogiji Mahārāj wrote, “One should continuously read Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 2, day and night; and one should learn to behave accordingly.”
[S.M. : 2/77]
[Y.M. : 1/213]

13709.t:
30 June 1968, Gondal. 
During the afternoon discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj had Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 54 recited and said, “What is {!ātmābuddhi!} ? To give [God’s] devotee your own food. To eagerly follow any command that he gives. If one has {!ātmābuddhi!} then strength remains. One remains elated. The commands are followed. If you eat, does hunger go or remain?
“This Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 54 talks about this. If one does not have such {!ātmābuddhi!}, one would be offended if called a donkey or a bull. They would not come to the {!mandir!}. However, they are labelled as such in the [Shrimad] Bhāgwat. Other Vachanāmruts may be mastered or not, but if this one is, then that is sufficient. A horse rider keeps his focus on three things. Similarly we should keep our focus on separating wheat from the stones. Listen to discourses and remove the stones.”
[Y.M. : 5/120]

13710.t: 30 June 1968, Gondal. \r\nAfter having Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 54 read during the afternoon discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “If many Vachanāmruts can or cannot be perfected, but if this particular Vachanāmrut is perfected, then it is enough.” \r\n[Y.M. : 5/158]

13711.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Gunātitānand Swāmi has explained in his spiritual discourses that maintaining {!ātmābuddhi!} is Satsang. It is not the intention to disregard spiritual rules, righteousness, renunciation and non-attachment to worldly objects; however, {!ātmābuddhi!} is the prime factor. If one possesses {!ātmābuddhi!}, one will maintain loyalty; this was [Gunātitānand] Swāmi’s principle.\r\n“Through the grace of God, one may be able to behold the constant {!darshan!} of God’s form and achieve great heights, even to the extent that people may offer prostrations to such an individual. But without {!ātmābuddhi!}, Mahārāj has revealed that grave shortcomings remain in a devotee. According to Vachanāmruts Gadhadā II 54 and Gadhadā III 11, one can only experience everlasting peace by maintaining {!ātmābuddhi!}. If a devotee is loyal and maintains {!ātmābuddhi!} in the {!Bhakta!} of God, one has attained their last birth.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 3/16]

13712.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “Where the {!Sant!} is present, moral codes are observed, {!dharma!} is practised and spiritual wisdom is attained. Also, where there is the {!Sant!} there are infinite virtues and also God. So, as a result, the {!jiva!} becomes pure. It is noted in this Vachanāmrut that God has said, ‘I am not as pleased by austerities, renunciation, {!yoga!}, observance of vows, donations or other endeavours as I am by the association of a {!Sādhu!} of complete inner purity.’ Having attained this Satsang, the merits are limitless. Ajāmil was a grave sinner, but he met the Sanakadik, bowed to them and said, ‘I am not capable of achieving anything.’ The sādhus were compassionate. His son was named Nārāyan, and in this way he attained liberation.”\r\n[S.V. : 1/181]

13750.t: November 1970, Gondal.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 57 is supreme. Swāmi [Shāstriji Mahārāj] often had this Vachanāmrut read. All should memorise this Vachanāmrut.” Yogiji Mahārāj said this three to four times. \r\n[Y.M. : 6/497]

13752.t: 25 November 1970, Gondal. \r\nDuring the morning discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 57 is supreme. Swāmi would often have it recited. Do not be a ‘cat-like’ devotee. Such a devotee is one who has affection for things other than God. Everyone in the world that does not worship God is ‘cat-like’. We are extremely fortunate. Remain blissful. We have attained this human body and a guru like Shāstriji Mahārāj. Now don’t have affection for anything else. Do not become a ‘cat-like’ devotee…”\r\n[Y.M. : 6/497]

13808.t: 10 July 1961, Mumbai.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj wrote in a letter of blessings for Swāminārāyan Prakāsh, “The important Vachanāmruts – Loyā 17, Kāriyāni 1, Gadhadā II 59 and Gadhadā II 28 – should all be perfected.”\r\n[Y.M. : 3/206]

13810.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Which actions of ours do you perceive {!manushyabhāv!} in? If I desire, I can sleep on the floor and my body would not ache. I would bathe with cold water. I would not eat. I would not allow my arms and legs to be cared for and yet nothing would happen. Hence, we might reveal what seems to be body-conscious traits, but one should not believe these. If we did not reveal them, how would you have an opportunity to serve?\r\n“As per Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 7 and II 59, one only excels by performing service. That is why we offer you the opportunity for service by caring for our arms and legs, bathing us and cooking our food. Otherwise if you sat idle, you will never excel. If you wish, I will not ask you to perform any service. One should always maintain {!divyabhāv!}, but one cannot excel without performing service. Do you all want to see a blaze of light? If so, I can ask Swāmi (Shāstriji Mahārāj) to show you a blaze of light, and he will. But then you will become {!sakām!} (have desires to see such things). Hence, it is better to always desire acquiring the spiritually knowledgeable state.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 10/115]

13814.t: Yogji Mahārāj said, “If one desires to please the {!Motāpurush!}, one should undertake the most menial of service. Ours is the supreme attainment. As per Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 59, there should be a mad rush of people wanting an opportunity to perform service. However, one assumes oneself to be great through one’s own devices. If one attempts to act like the {!Satpurush!}, one will be thrown into jail. Only one who has received the stamp of the {!Satpurush!} is truly great. Once cannot become ‘Mavjibhāi’ of one’s own accord. The {!Gunātit Sant!} of God is the only true {!Satpurush!}.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 18/12]

13821.t:
15 July 1956, Gondal. 
In the morning, Yogiji Mahārāj had Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 59 read and said, “What was said? What is the main point? Only God and his {!Sant!} are redemptive – not wealth, women and children. 
“Today, we see that Shiva, Brahmā and Hanuman are venerated in every town. Who is above even all of them? The {!Sant!}. Those of the {!Junā Mandir!} criticise us that there should be no image of a {!Sādhu!}. What does [Shriji Mahārāj] say in favour of the {!Sant!}? The {!Sant!} is above the likes of Brahmā and other deities. If we understand his glory to such a level, we would be able to perform his service, wouldn’t we? We have attained the {!Sant!}. What do we mean by attainment? The fact that we have attained him in this present, manifest form.
“The manifest form of God that we have attained is the most redemptive of all. There is nothing that is more redemptive than him. One only receives the opportunity to serve such a {!Sant!} after gaining many merits.
“Which forms of service? Even the likes of Brahmā are not worthy of receiving the opportunities to serve the {!Sant!} by bathing him, feeding him, washing his used utensils, collecting flowers for him, offering garlands to him and much more. Others do not receive this rare opportunity, that has been attained [by you] after gaining many merits.
“There are many children in Rājkot; however do any of them come here? They are freely roaming around and playing cricket with a ball and bat. No one would even consider coming closer. The fact that we are achieving that level of closeness [with the {!Sant!}] is a result of the many merits accumulated in past lives.”
[Y.M. : 2/87]

13859.t:
March 1970, Kampala, Uganda. 
One evening, the {!yuvaks!} presented a cultural programme in Yogiji Mahārāj’s presence. Thereafter, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “The youths talked on certain topics. One youth recited Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 61. This discussed the concept of {!niyams!}, faith in God and loyalty. What is true loyalty? If someone is unnecessarily harming a devotee of God, one should stand up for that devotee. Two {!Kāthi!} youths of Gundali stood up for the {!sādhus!} [of Swāminārāyan Bhagwān]. They were not devotees; however, they stood up for the {!sādhus!} understanding them to be ‘{!sādhus!} that my maternal uncle follows. Therefore, their names were noted in history [mentioned in Vachanāmrut Loyā 3]. According to Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 7, in no way should one abandon one’s loyalty to God and his {!Bhakta!}, regardless if one’s reputation increases or decreases, one is honoured or insulted, or one lives or dies. Many may keep loyalty; however, when relationships turn sour, they may end up rebuking the person they kept loyalty for by saying, ‘You don’t do anything for us, despite us continually standing up for you.’ That cannot be called loyalty.”
“One’s body and the relatives of the body become dearer to one than a devotee of God – this is why Mahārāj makes this point. If a {!sādhu!} arrives from afar and at the same time one of our relatives were to arrive, one who is not loyal [to {!Satsang!}] will say, ‘O {!sādhu!}! Listen, my relatives are here, so I will not be able to attend your discourses.’ However, the relatives should be given second priority. One has a lot of love for one’s son. If we ask for that son [to be initiated into sainthood], they would retort, ‘Swāmi! Take my money, but not my son.’”
“In short, we should not endear our bodily relatives to a higher degree than devotees who are associated with the {!Gunātit Sant!}. This concept will prove to be of immense benefit in the future.”
“Nandubhāi Mancharam of Amdāvād was incredibly loyal. Despite the fact that he was the secretary of the {!Junā Mandir!} in Kalupur, he would ensure that Shāstriji Mahārāj stayed at his home. He remained loyal, placing his head on the line. Maintaining such loyalty reduces the five grave sins to ashes. We have come from afar. Devotees should remain loyal to each other, through thick and thin. If another devotee is undergoing difficulties, one should not think, ‘He got what he deserved.’ What cannot be done for a devotee associated with Swāminārāyan [Bhagwān]? This is the concept described in Vachanāmrut Loyā 3.”
[Y.M. : 6/93]

13894.t:
The date of this Vachanāmrut is Māgshar sud 2 of Samvat 1881. When studying Shriji Mahārāj’s {!jivan-charitra!}, He is actually present in Surat because on Kārtik sud 12 of Samvat 1881, He had performed the {!murti-pratishthā!} of Vartāl. During the {!pratishthā!}, the devotees of Surat yielded their wish to post a flag over the shrine of Harikrishna Mahārāj’s shrine. (Brahmānand Swāmi had given his word to the devotees of Surat that if they give the opportunity to plant a flag over the Harikrishna Mahārāj’s shrine to the devotees of Vadodarā, Mahārāj would come to Surat.) In order to fulfil Brahmānand Swāmi promise, Mahārāj went to Surat on Kārtik vad 6 (Friday). Mahārāj gave the devotees the bliss of His presence and left Surat on the day this Vachanāmrut is dated. Therefore, it’s impossible for Mahārāj to be present in Gadhadā if He was just leaving Surat for Gadhadā on this day.
[B.S. : 5/51]
However, Shriji Mahārāj had assumed a second form and preached this Vachanāmrut in Gadhadā. This has been mentioned in Harililāmrut:
{!Bani e j divas ek vāt, e to āshcharyakārī aghāt!};
That same day, an incident occurred, certainly a wonder.

{!Gaḍhapur-jan ātur thayā, anna-jaḷ taji kaik to rahyā!}.
The devotees of Gadhpur became eager (for Mahārāj’s {!darshan!}) and stopped eating and drinking.

{!Kare vinati te gad-gad thaine, āvo he Kṛuṣhṇa sau sāth laine!};
They prayed passionately for Mahārāj to return with everyone else.

{!Nahī āvo jo Shyām sujāṇ, tajashu ame nishchay prāṇ!}.
If you don’t return, we will certainly abandon our body.

{!Tyāre bīje rūpe Mahārāj, gayā Gaḍhpur sahit samāj!};
So Mahārāj came to Gadhpur in a second form, along with the entourage.

{!Māgashar sudi bīje tyā Hari, beṭhā darabārmā sabhā bharī!}.
On Māgshar sud 2, Mahārāj sat in the assembly held in the {!darbār!}.

{!Bhrātṛuputroye pūchhiyā prashne, āpyā uttar enā Shrī Kṛuṣhṇe!};
The sons of Mahārāj’s brothers (Ayodhyāprasādji and Raghuvirji) asked questions and Mahārāj answered them.

{!Vachanāmṛut tenu lakhāṇu, nathi koīnu te to ajāṇyu!}.
A Vachanāmrut was written recounting this dialogue, it is not unknown to anyone.

Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 62 is a miraculous account recorded in history.
[Shri Harililāmrut : 8/35/16-19]

13895.t: 10 July 1961, Mumbai. \r\nYogiji Mahārāj wrote an inspiring letter from Mumbai for Swāminārāyan Prakāsh for the Satsang community. He wrote, “Become the servant of servants. The attributes of a true servant have been described in Gadhadā I 14 and Gadhadā II 62; one should read and think about this. Therefore, {!sādhus!} and devotees should keep the strength of Mahārāj and Swāmi, and perfect devotion with servitude.” \r\n[Y.M. : 3/206]

13897.t:
May 1941 (Samvat 1997), Mumbai.
Shāstriji Mahārāj had Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 62 read and then asked, “This Vachanāmrut mentions three inclinations: conviction of oneself being the {!ātmā!}, love and servitude. Are these three in some sort of order, i.e. highest, intermediate and lowest?”
Answering the question himself, Swāmishri said, “There is no order of highest, intermediate and lowest in those inclinations. If we consider it in that way, then Gopalānand Swāmi and Brahmānand Swāmi had the inclination of offering devotion with servitude. They would be considered to be the lowest; however, on seeing their spiritual state, one cannot say that about them. Therefore, all three of these inclinations are of the highest level. Thus, when one sees the highest level of all three inclinations in one person, then he is said to be {!ekāntik!} or {!Param Ekāntik!}. One should apply a similar understanding for the intermediate and lowest levels.”
[S.M. : 2/76]

13939.t: September 1956, Nārāyan Sarovar\r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “After becoming a devotee, we should learn saintliness and offer devotion with servitude. Based on this, think on these two Vachanāmruts – Gadhadā I 14 and Gadhadā II 62. In Gadhadā II 62, Shriji Mahārāj uses very subtle words: ‘One would like the {!darshan!} only of one’s {!Ishtadev!}; one would like to hear talks only about him; one would like one’s {!Ishtadev’s!} nature; one would also prefer to stay only with him.’ Despite behaving like this, one would be eager to follow any {!āgnā!}. Only such devotion with servitude is of value.”\r\n[Y.M. : 2/109]

13986.t: 1 January 1959, Amdāvād. \r\nWriting a letter of inspiration to the youths of Mumbai, Yogiji Mahārāj wrote, “All of you are not from this world, but you are from {!parlok!}. Be enthusiastic about it [{!teno kef rakhvo!}]. One should read and ponder over Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 63. Fountains of joy will sprout. Victory will resound.” \r\n[Y.M. : 2/470]

13988.t:
Samvat 1952, Mahuvā. 
Bhagatji Mahārāj had Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 63 recited by Ganpatram and then said, “This Vachanāmrut is about gaining strength. One should consider that one has imbibed Satsang from the time one recognizes the {!Satpurush!} and develops conviction towards him. This {!jiva!} gains strength in proportion to the amount of faith with which it attaches itself to the {!Satpurush!}. The focus of the {!indriyas!} and the {!antahkaran!} of such a strong devotee are guided by the {!jiva!}. Thus, the {!indriyas!} and the {!antahkaran!}, and the focus of the {!jiva!} do not remain separate. The focus of the {!jiva!} is the focus of the {!indriyas!} and {!antahkaran!}; both of them become one.”
“If a person has love for God and his {!Sant!}, possesses intense faith in serving them, and also engages in the nine types of {!bhakti!}, then his {!jiva!} will instantly gain strength. Thus, for making the {!jiva!} stronger, there is no method comparable to that of serving God and his {!Bhakta!}.”
“The {!jiva!} acquires strength from the following three endeavours: exceptionally intense service, deep faith and devotion with an understanding of God's greatness. Such strength is not attained even if one is able to discriminate between the {!ātmā!} and the body, and behaves as the {!ātmā!}. Mahārāj has explained further, 'Much better than behaving as the {!ātmā!}, is to stay within the fellowship of God and his devotees. It is indeed the very best spiritual endeavour. Can’t one behave as the {!ātmā!} and not return to this body again?' Mahārāj has celebrated festivals and played {!rās!} for this reason. He always kept his devotees close to him and taught them this type of devotion. In the past, those who were great have also behaved in this way. [Gunātitānand] Swāmi performed much service of {!sādhus!} who were unwell. We also followed Swāmi's inner wishes and served him in Junagadh. There is no merit greater than serving devotees of God. One should serve them with an understanding of their greatness. Never spite or keep any ill will towards them.” 
[B.M. : 517]

13990.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “We do not have strength like that of Krupānand Swāmi and other senior sādhus. Instead of comparing ourselves with them, we should observe the eleven [main] commands and we will become as strong as they are. The company [of this {!Sādhu!}] is such that {!upāsanā, dharma!}, etc. are all included. Nothing is left.” Based on this, Swāmishri then had Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 63 recited.\r\n[S.V. : 5/168]

13996.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “The means to acquire strength is explained in Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 63: ‘Firm faith in performing service, intense love for God’s {!Sādhu!} and the nine types of {!bhakti!} coupled with the knowledge of God’s greatness.’ One should fully imbibe these three principles and practice Satsang with a sense of purity. A sense of purity means to understand that the same Mahārāj that resides in Akshardhām, we have attained today in the form of the {!Sant!}. To practice Satsang with such conviction is to practice Satsang with a sense of purity. When this occurs, one acquires the virtues of {!dharma, gnān, vairāgya!} and {!bhakti!}; This can only be achieved through the association of the {!Ekāntik Sant!}. Hence one should identify the {!Sant!} and engage in {!bhajan!}.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 3/14]

14015.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “It is due to the glory of this {!upāsanā!} that one is able to feel fulfilled and accomplished. Without this {!upāsanā!}, one feels unfulfilled and remains wishful.” Swāmishri had the ‘Gangājalio Well’ Vachanāmrut [Gadhadā II 67] read and said, “One becomes what one believes Mahārāj to be [if one believes that Mahārāj to be free from all blemishes, one also becomes free from all blemishes]. Thereafter, how can one still be unfulfilled and have wishes remaining? They simply do not remain.”\r\n[S.V. : 3/66]

14017.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “Through the {!upāsanā!} of Purushottam, the {!ātmā!} becomes like Akshar, and if one associates with the {!Mota!}[{!purush!}], one attains much greatness. When lice reproduce, they produce tiny eggs; whereas when a female elephant gives birth, the infant is the size of a bull.” Based on this, the Vachanāmrut was read: ‘One becomes as one understands God to be’ [i.e. if one believes God to be free from all blemishes, one also becomes free of all blemishes].”\r\n[S.V. : 1/188]

14018.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “Acquire understanding in the way Shriji Mahārāj has said in the Vachanāmrut: believe oneself as {!brahmarup!} and remember God – this is what needs to be done. The quintessence of {!upāsanā!} is that one becomes as one understands Mahārāj to be. One attains that much power and strength.
