By understanding Mahārāj to be the source of all {!avatars!} and the Lord of Akshardhām, one attains Akshardhām. In the Vachanāmrut, Mahārāj said, ‘One becomes as one understands God to be, but God remains limitless.’ Therefore, to clearly understand this {!upāsanā!} is the main endeavour.”\r\n[S.V. : 2/2]

14024.t: 5 February 1965 (Maha Sud 4, Samvat 2021), Atlādrā. \r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “We have attained such a {!Sant!} [Shāstriji Mahārāj]. Regardless of how much of his glory we sing, it would still fall short. The amount of glory we sing is how much we will imbibe. In Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 67, [Shriji Mahārāj says] we become the way we understand [God]. Even if the ocean is filled with sweet water, only that [amount of sweet water] which we are able to fill up is useful to us. Similarly, the extent to which we understand his glory is the extent to which we become great. He is completely beyond comprehension!”\r\n[Y.M. : 4/11]

14171.t: After having Vachanāmrut Vartāl 1 and Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 14 recited, Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “If one understands like this, then a householder and a renunciant both attain the same [Akshardhām].”\r\n[S.V. : 5/89]

14173.t:
3 August 1968, Gondal.
After lunch and having Vachanāmrut Vartāl 1 read, Yogiji Mahārāj explained it meaning. He said, “What is the {!Gunātit!} state?” In praise or insult, happiness or misery, regression or progression there is oneness. If thousands of people insult us, even then there is no effect. If they praise us with a garland, even then there is no effect.” 
“What is firm conviction? [Doubts such as:] ‘It cannot be.’ ‘Is it true or not?’ Such thoughts do not arise.
“Mahārāj sat under a mango tree and remembered that tree. Whoever and whatever is prominent at the time should be remembered. If the tree is not remembered, then it would get upset and think, ‘Why wasn’t I remembered?’
“What is conviction? To understand that the all-doer, who has a divine form, who is supreme and is the ruler of Akshardhām, is this very supreme God that I have attained.”
Yogiji Mahārāj asked Dr Maganbhāi of Bharuch to explain the essence of this Vachanāmrut. Then Swāmishri himself said, “While seated in front of Shriji Mahārāj, if one is attached to him, whether a state of {!samādhi!} occurs or does not, it is in fact still {!samādhi!}. You should have animosity towards your mind. The mind is always wandering around, it is never still. The {!Satpurush!} is our true mind. The mind becomes conquered; it becomes one with the {!Satpurush!}.” 
[Y.M. : 5/211]

14200.t: Harishankarbhāi asked, “How should one understand of the {!Sādhu!} who is like the {!vadvānal!} fire?”\r\nGunātitanānand Swāmi replied, “In the Satsangijivan, the qualities of such a {!sādhu!} are explained as one who imbibes {!pushpahārāya sarpāya!} [understands a garland to be like a snake]. Moreover, he forever beholds the image of God in his heart and his characteristics are according to the true principles of Satsang. Furthermore, he inspires many {!jivas!} to worship God, remains completely pure and never disobeys the commands given by God. Others may encourage one to worship God due to the strength of God, yet forget about God themselves. Greatness should not be understood in this way. This type of greatness is found in worldly life. In the Vachanāmrut, greatness has been defined as having firm, unflinching faith in God and following his commands; such a person is great. If he is not like the {!vadvānal!} fire, then how can he remain unaffected, despite making so many people {!satsangis!}? Consequently, what we believe to be great is not [necessarily] great. Greatness is dependent on following Mahārāj’s command.”\r\n[S.V. : 5/142]

14227.t:
22 June 1962, Mumbai. 
In the morning assembly, whilst explaining the ‘Four Types of Eminent Spiritual People’ Vachanāmrut [Vartāl 3], Yogiji Mahārāj said, “’By what means can such extraordinary bhakti be attained?’ The questioner is indeed great. Instantaneous question and immediate answer. ‘Serve me’, why didn’t [Shriji Mahārāj] say that? The {!Sant!} is the protector and liberator of [Mahārāj’s] lineage. Offer devotion to him.
“What can a candle-like [small flame] person do? Can he grant liberation? When his nature comes to haunt him, he is put in his place. Even a torch-like {!sādhu!} cannot withstand the force of the wind [unforeseen circumstances]. All four are described as {!ekāntik!}, from which only one is accepted and the other three are rejected. The ‘Mail’ [train] goes forward, local trains remain. That one is the {!vadvānal!} fire.
“Just like Joban Vartāla, Hirabhāi Mukhi of Bochāsan never listened to anyone. Shāstriji Mahārāj transformed him. Through his help, Bochāsan {!Mandir!} was constructed. Even the worst sinners became pure through association. Such is the power of the {!Sādhu!} who is like the {!vadvānal!} fire. He makes bitter-like personalities sweet, that cannot be achieved by the lightning-like {!sādhu!}. You need to go to the supreme court to appeal as the high court is not good enough. You will end up losing your money if you go to the high court.
“The {!Param Ekāntik!} [{!Sādhu!}] will transform the worst of sinners and make them like himself, whereas the lightning-like [{!sant!}] can only inspire values.
“We used to sit with Swāmi [Shāstriji Mahārāj]. Everything became calm and peaceful. You have not seen him; he was a God-realised {!Sant!}. He is like the {!vadvānal!} fire. Mahārāj’s lineage will not end. This is the concept of the {!vadvānal!} fire.”
[Y.M. : 3/362]

14233.t:
Samvat 1952, Mahuva. 
Bhagatji Mahārāj spoke at great lengths with the devotees from the Charotar region. Chaturbhāi asked, “Mahārāj! If the {!murti!} forever remains in one’s heart, flaws are eradicated. How can this {!murti!} be grasped?”
Bhagatji Mahārāj replied, “Behold the {!murti!} using your {!vruttis!} as a thread. If you endeavour to practice in this way, you will experience happiness in all aspects of life.
“Read Vachanāmrut Vartāl 4 and endeavour in the way described. The {!murti!} is like a wish-fulfilling gem. It will fulfil all your desires; however, only if you have saintliness will you be able to behold this {!murti!}. God helped King Yudhishthir because of his saintliness. Hence, we should imbibe such saintliness and walk along its path.”
[B.M. : 537]

14246.t:
Samvat 1969, Sārangpur.
Rānābhāi Darbār of Jhinjhar said some harsh words to Sādhu Harikrishnadās who was doing {!sevā!} in Sārangpur. Harikrishnadās requested Rānābhāi to meet Shāstriji Mahārāj. After prostrating, he sat before Shāstriji Mahārāj and said, “I’ve heard many, many things about you; however, hearing words like: ‘you are all outcasts from Vartāl and all of you are {!bandiyās!} from those who oppose you, I never came for your {!darshan!}.”
Swāmishri subtly laughed and said, “You have great {!sanskārs!} from your previous life, hence you have been able to come here. Bring the Vachanāmrut.” Shāstriji Mahārāj had him read Gadhadā I 21 in which Shriji Mahārāj explains the two forms of Akshar, Gadhadā I 71 in which Shriji Mahārāj said Bhagwān manifests on the earth along with his Akshardhām, Gadhadā II 59 in which Shriji Mahārāj says only those who have accumulated a great number of merits from performing good deeds receive the opportunity to serve {!Bhagwān’s Sant!}, and Vartāl 5 in which Shriji Mahārāj says that if one performs services of the {!Sant!} [one possessing highest qualities] similar to the services one performs of God then even if he was a devotee of the lowest calibre and was destined to become a devotee of the highest calibre after two, four, ten, or even after 100 lives, he will become a devotee of the highest calibre in this very life.
Shāstriji Mahārāj had all these Vachanāmruts read and explained that such a {!Sant!} with the highest qualities is Gunātitānand Swāmi who is the eternal Aksharbrahma; and the fundamental principle of {!upāsanā!} is to offer {!upāsanā!} having identified one’s self as Akshar.
Hearing the clear principles from the Vachanāmrut, Rānābhāi understood {!upāsanā!} perfectly.
[S.M. : 1/383]

14276.t:
19 April 1970, Mombasa.
At the Lohānā Assembly Hall, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Nityānand Swāmi asked, ‘What are the characteristics of one who has taken refuge?’ Purushottam, himself, replied lovingly saying, ‘{!Sarvadharmān parityajya mām-ekam sharanam vraja!}! O Arjun! Leave your mind’s desires. Do as I tell you.’ Arjun followed God’s commands and became victorious. Therefore, Mahārāj installed the {!murti!} of Nar-Nārāyan in Amdāvād.
“There are three traits that define a person who has taken refuge: 1. Great misery, like the destruction of the universe, does not occur to that person. Even if it did occur, he would believe only God and the {!Sant!} to be capable of saving him; No one else would be capable. 2. He would only ask his choicest deity for whatever one wishes, no one else. 3. He would only act according to wishes of God. Mahārāj replied to Nityānand Swāmi in this way. 
“Shriji Mahārāj’s words are worth understanding. If you experience misery, so much so that the sky shatters, even then only believe that Shriji Mahārāj is capable of protecting you and no one else. Without his wish, even a dry leaf cannot move. Gunātitānand Swāmi has said in his talks, ‘If someone rushes at you in anger, think that no one has the ability to move even a dry leaf without my Swāmi's wish.’ Swāmi and Mahārāj have both said the same thing. We have attained them. If you have the highest form of conviction in Akshar and Purushottam, you will continually experience peace, peace, and nothing but peace.” 
[Y.M. : 6/163]

14277.t:
Samvat 1966.
One day, Ambārām Bhagat came to Bochāsan from Bhādaran. Harikrishnadās perceived him as a great {!sādhu!} and served him according to his ability. Once, when he was sitting with Ambārām Bhagat, he told him that he had seen immense light from the {!murti!} of Shāstriji Mahārāj. Ambārām Bhagat said, “You have been blessed by Swāmishri so he showed you his true form. Become one with him with a singular firmness.”
He then added, “Harikrishnadās! We are very fortunate that we have obtained the {!Sant!} who has a direct relationship with Shriji Mahārāj. I also have this firm faith. I once had doubts whether we can meditate on the form of the guru. Last year, I went to Kanthāriyā where I was engaged in {!mānsi!} and this doubt arose. Swāmishri, accompanied by Prabhudās Kothāri, instantly gave me {!darshan!}. Prabhudās Kothāri pointed to Swāmishri and said, ‘Bhagat, you will experience peace when you meditate on this form.’ From that day on, my doubts became uprooted. Now I experience such bliss that I cannot describe it. When you become one with Swāmishri - who is the manifest form of Shriji Mahārāj - you will also experience the same bliss.” 
[S.M. : 1/345]

14284.t: January 1957, Bodi.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “Vachanāmrut Vartāl 5 is about refuge. Shri Krishna Bhagwān said to Arjun to forsake his own interpretations of {!dharma!}. When Arjun acted in this way, he attained God’s {!rājipo!}. In this manner, if one acts according to the wishes of God, God will become pleased. Refuge alone is {!bhakti!}. This association that has happened is our greatest fortune. Otherwise, this association is not attainable even after performing penance for hundreds of thousands of years.” \r\n[Y.M. : 2/185]

14338.t:
March 1966, Mumbai.
During the daily discourses, Vachanāmrut Vartāl 10 was being read. Yogiji Mahārāj mentioned, “None of the {!sādhus!} that met Shriji Mahārāj are to be seen today. Where are the nand [paramhansas]? Whose refuge should I keep right now?
“One who has attained similar qualities to him is known to have truly met him – i.e. he becomes intuitive of his wishes and attains oneness with him. Seek refuge in him. Act according to his commands. What does refuge mean? ‘I am yours’.
“What should we do if we cannot currently met the one that has ‘met’ God? Should we sit at home? Such a {!Sant!} is currently always present. If you haven’t met him face to face, then behold the {!murti!} and worship it. Instant liberation is granted through {!darshan!} of the {!Ekāntik Sant!}.” 
[Y.M. : 4/239]

14353.t:
Vachanāmrut Vartāl 10 was read. It mentions, ‘When God is not manifest on this earth, then take refuge in the {!sādhu!} that has met God. It is through him the {!jiva!} attains liberation.’ 
The meaning of ‘the {!sādhu!} that has met God’ was explained by Yogiji Mahārāj in the following way, “In Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 27, Shriji Mahārāj has said that, ‘…The attributes of the {!Sant!} – being free of lust, avarice, egotism, taste, attachment, etc. – are also described in the scriptures. The {!Sant!} who possesses these attributes has a direct relationship with God. Therefore, one should develop the conviction of God based on his words. In fact, to have firm faith in the words of the {!Sant!} is itself the conviction of God.
“Here, ‘direct relationship’ refers to the {!Sant!} that has ‘met’ God. This refers to the {!Param Ekāntik, Gunātit Sant!}.”
[Yogi Vāni : 24/255]

14370.t: 6 April 1959, Advāl.\r\nEngaged in a discussion with the youths on the upper floor during early morning, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “One will only be able to achieve that which is to be achieved if one imbibes Vachanāmrut Vartāl 11… one will be able to accomplish anything if one really takes in [the message of] this one Vachanāmrut.”\r\n[Y.M. : 2/536]

14371.t: Shāmji Bhagat could not overcome the grief of Yogiji Mahārāj reverting to Akshardhām. Pramukh Swāmi Mahārāj consoled him, “Do you want to see the mass of light? You cannot see what is up there [meaning the form of {!Bhagwān!} in Akshardhām] and you do not have faith in this down here [referring to himself - the manifest form of {!Bhagwān!} on Earth]. So what will happen? Read Vartāl 11. Developing intense affection toward the {!Satpurush!} is the means to realizing one’s {!ātmā!} and having the direct realization of {!Bhagwān!}.”\r\nHowever, Shāmji Bhagat could not convince himself of this. He then saw Pramukh Swāmi Mahārāj in Yogiji Mahārāj’s place three times in his dream and realized there is no difference between the two. They are one and the same. That Shāmji Bhagat later became Sādhu Purushottamdās. \r\n[Y.M. : 6/437]

14382.t: Yogiji Mahārāj was asked a question, “How can one become {!brahmarup!}?” \r\nSwāmishri replied, “As per Vachanāmrut Vartāl 11, when one believes this {!Sādhu!} to be {!brahmarup!} and associates with him through thought, deed and word, one becomes {!aksharrup!}. Only then can one remain in the service of Purushottam. One should develop such feelings and affection. One should perfect Vachanāmrut Vartāl 11 – which details how to become {!brahmarup!}. If one possesses intense love for the {!Gunātit Satpurush!}, removes any barrier with him and attaches oneself to him with {!ātmābuddhi!}, then he will make one {!brahmarup!}.” \r\n[Yogi Vāni : 25/77]

14383.t:
12 March 1966, Mumbai. 
While explaining Vachanāmrut Vartāl 11 in the assembly, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “We should not keep ego in front of God and devotees with his association. Arguing with elders is ego. Don’t keep even a little ego. This is important. Feelings of ego may be present, but not showing them outwardly is good. Bow down!
“Once a person started performing penance; from that day onward, a cat [continually] sat in front of him. After a few days, the person performing penance lost weight, but the cat gained weight. The person performing penance asked the cat, ‘What do you eat that made you this big?’ The cat said, ‘I am your ego. You have lost weight, but the ego of your penance has increased. Due to this, I have become big.’ We perform penance and sacrifice, but the ego-like cat should not enlarge. We should remain humble. {!Bhāryo devtā nakhkhod kādhii nākhshe!} [The unseen embers cause more harm]. If one chants Swāminārāyan and keeps refuge, but still has hatred towards {!Gunātit!}, then one become demonic. If someone maligns others then I [Mahārāj] hate his sight. It is not nice to malign anyone, no matter how small they are; in the same way, if one maligns the {!Gunātit!} [{!Sant!}], how can [Mahārāj] like that? If love has been developed, then all the actions of the {!Satpurush!} are considered {!Gunātit!}. {!Gunātit!}! The Vachanāmrut that can make you {!brahmarup!} is being read.” 
[Y.M. : 4/228]

14389.t: 28 January 1955, Vasant Panchmi, Atlādrā. \r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “Until we accept that Gunātit is our {!ātmā!}, we will remain in a deficit. According to Vachanāmrut Vartāl 11, all of our defects are eradicated when we develop love for the {!Satpurush!}.”\r\n[Y.M. : 1/517]

14397.t: Whilst explaining Vachanāmrut Vartāl 11, Yogiji Mahārāj asked, “What is greater - {!ātmābuddhi!} or intense love?” Answering this himself, Swāmishri replied, “In a house, five people live together and they have {!ātmābuddhi!} for one another. However, if a dispute was to arise, then a barrier would emerge between them. On the other hand, if one possesses intense love, no barrier will arise. The intense love that the {!gopis!} possessed excel all [other types of love]”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 24/102]

14415.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Vachanāmrut Vartāl 11 states, ‘If one attains a spiritual state similar to that of the {!Motāpurush!}, one will understand his greatness.’ Which state is this? The spiritual state of {!nirdoshbuddhi!}.” \r\n[Yogi Vāni : 24/323]

14429.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “One who has affection for God and his great {!Sādhu!} has nothing left to do. Based on this, think about the Vachanāmruts Gadhadā II 9 and Vartāl 11. They both convey the same message.” \r\n[S.V. : 5/338]

14446.t:
6 April 1959, Advāl.
During the early morning, whilst doing goshti on the upper floor, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Only if we perfect Vachanāmrut Vartāl 11 will we be fulfilled. If we attain a state like the {!Satpurush!}, then we will be able to understand his glory. If you study English and swear at me [in English], how would I know? We need to attain realisation. What is this realisation? If we realise others as flawless, then we become flawless. Even if we are beaten into pieces, our mind does not detach. This is intense attachment. Mulji and Krushnaji were beaten and thrown out, yet they did not think ill of Mahārāj. This is love. So much faith! So much divinity! If you understand the greatness, then {!divyabhāv!} will also be realised. 
“There is only one method of understanding greatness. If you perfect this one Vachanāmrut, your endeavours will be complete. Therefore, what is the principle? Intense attachment. How? Even if we are beaten into pieces, our mind does not detach. The attainment, association and liberation that were present during Mahārāj’s time are all exactly present today. Hence, we should behave in such a way.”
[Y.M. : 2/536]

14452.t: 15 May 1959\r\nAt 4:30pm, whilst travelling in the local train from Pālej to Bharuch, Yogiji Mahārāj addressed the youths, “In Vartāl 11 it is said: develop intense love for the {!Sant!}. How can such love be developed? See him as flawless. The way he is present in Akshardhām is the exact same way he is also manifest in front of you. \r\n[Y.M. : 2/551]

14461.t: 6 June 1968, Gondal.\r\nGiving a unique explanation of this Vachanāmrut, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “The Vachanāmrut to attain the state of {!brahmarup!} – Vartāl 11.”\r\n[Y.M. : 5/82]

14466.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “If one attributes human traits to the actions of manifest form of God and his {!Sant!}, one’s spiritual progress vanishes like the new moon. If one attributes divine traits, one progresses spiritually like the waxing moon of the second day of the bright half of the lunar month. What actions do the {!murtis!} perform that one could perceive faults in them and regress? Therefore, only the talking and walking form of God [i.e. human form] is called manifest.\r\n“Only the great {!Sant!} can instil divinity in the {!murti!}. But the three – {!murtis!}, scriptures and pilgrim places – together do not equal the {!Sant!}. Such a great {!Sant!} is able to make all three – {!murtis!}, scriptures and pilgrim places. Therefore, such a {!Sant!}, in whom God fully resides, is the manifest form of God.”\r\n[S.V. : 5/392]

14484.t:
Both the question and answer in this Vachanāmrut are unique. Rāmchandra Vāghmodiā’s (of Vadodarā) characterization in Sampradāy’s scriptures is as follows:
Rāmchandra Vaidya (Ayurvedic doctor) of Vadodarā adhered to going to Dākor every Punam. He had no sons; so he had kept a belief of going to Dākor. He treated the poor for free; whereas wealthier people paid 100 rupees to have their pulse checked (i.e. diagnosis made). He had a substantial income; yet, being generous, he fed the {!brāhmins!} of his caste and taught Ayurvedic medicine to 10 or 12 students.
In Dākor, he stayed in the {!haveli!} for {!brāhmins!} and went for {!darshan!} of Ranchhodji twice a day without fail.
There were two rooms near Ranchhodji. Here, he witnessed an immoral act in this holy place and his spirit was dampened. He stopped his circumambulation and became afflicted with a fever. He sat in the loft of his residence and started chanting when he heard a divine voice from the sky, “If you have a desire for God, then Swāminārāyan is the manifestation of God today. His {!sādhus!} can be found in Amdāvād {!mandir!}. They can show you where He is.”
In the morning, he went to Amdāvād by horse with two or three others from his group and met the {!sādhus!}.
Nityānand Muni was present so the Vaidya requested, “I want to meet the God that you have attained.” The Vaidya stayed there four to five days. The {!sādhus!} then told him all the villages where he can spend the night on the way to Gadhadā. In this way, Rāmchandra came to Gadhpur and had {!darshan!} of Shriji Mahārāj. Offering a {!shrifal!} (coconut) and a rupee, he requested Mahārāj to give him {!niyams!} of a {!satsangi!}. Mahārāj talked to him about the ways of Satsang.
He stayed in Gadhpur for five days. One day, he had food prepared and served Mahārāj and the {!sādhus!} food and performed Mahārāj’s pujā. He took leave of Mahārāj thereafter. Mahārāj had Bhajānand Swāmi and Jayānand Varni accompany him to Vadodarā.
[H.C.S. : 22/108-111]
We can see that the Vaidya is a great {!mumukshu!} from his characterization. It has been passed by word of mouth that the person involved in the immoral act he witnessed later experience {!samādhi!} after coming into contact with Satsang. This caused Rāmchandra Vaidya to question: This person does not observe any {!dharmas!} of {!varna!} and {!āshram!}; yet how did he experience {!samādhi!}? {!Yam!} (restrain of one’s senses; living a pure life) and {!niyam!} (moral, spiritual discipline) are the first two steps of {!samādhi!}. How can one devoid of these experience {!samādhi!}?
But history says that this person was kicked out of the village. He built a hut in a desolate place for shelter. One day, some pseudo-{!sādhus!} beat Mahārāj’s {!paramhansas!}. This person served the wounded {!sādhus!}. From this one pious act, all his sins were burnt and he experience {!samādhi!}.
In His answer, Shriji Mahārāj says, “Everyone believes that one who infringes the {!dharma!} of one’s caste and {!āshram!} as prescribed in the scriptures is an ‘unworthy person’. However, if that unworthy person sincerely appreciates the virtues of God and His {!Sant!}, he earns great merits. As a result, the sins that he had committed by transgressing the {!dharma!} of his caste and {!āshram!} are eradicated, and his {!jiva!} becomes extremely pure. Thereafter, when his mind is fixed on God’s form, he attains {!samādhi!}.”
The background to the question and answer dialogue is the historical account as listed above.

14490.t:
In this Vachanāmrut, Shobhārām Shāstri of Vadodarā asks Mahārāj, “Mahārāj, there are two types of {!jivas!}: godly and demonic. Have they always been so since eternity, or have they become so due to association?”
It has been written about Shobhārām Shāstri: He had no worries about shortage of food, but only had the eagerness for God. He had profound knowledge. He ranked highest in {!vyākaran!} (Sanskrit grammar) among a thousand {!Shāstris!}. He was honoured by the Gayakwād of Vadodarā and the wealthy of that time. Despite being a great scholar, he did not bear arrogance. When {!sādhus!} spoke to him as according to their understanding, he would listen as if he knew nothing. He never let logic impede his understanding and always said that Shriji Mahārāj is God. He never bore deceit…
[H.C.S. : 20/20]
Shobhārām Shāstri was present in Vadodarā when Shriji Mahārāj arrived on Kārtik vad 3 of Samvat 1882. He must have witnessed all the ways the Diwān Viththalrāv Devāji tried to plot Bhagwān Swāminārāyan’s capture.
While Mahārāj was staying in Vadodarā, the Diwān sent three men who practised black magic to use their skill on Mahārāj. Their incantations failed to work on Mahārāj, so the Diwān sent three Africans to stab Mahārāj with daggers dipped in poison. Finally, he plotted Mahārāj’s capture or assassination in Mastubāug where Mahārāj was staying. However, the heavy rainfall foiled his plan. 
Despite failing multiple times, the Diwān never backed down. Even as Mahārāj was departing Vadodarā, he sent four generals to capture Mahārāj but even they were left empty handed.
Within three short days of Mahārāj’s stay, the Diwān tried four times to defame, capture, or assassinate Shriji Mahārāj – these thoughts must have certainly occurred in Shobhārām Shāstri’s mind. The length and breadth of the Diwān’s demonic nature begged the question that Shobhārām Shāstri asked Mahārāj because this Vachanāmrut was spoken right after these incidents.

14495.t: Yogiji Mahārāj was asked a question, “What is the cause of demonic traits in the {!jiva!}?”\r\nSwāmishri replied, “The main reason is that one who receives the grace of the {!Satpurush!} becomes divine. If one hurts the {!ekāntik bhakta!}, one will become demonic. The {!ekāntik!} [{!bhakta!}] does not become pained; however, God residing within him becomes pained.” \r\n[Yogi Vāni : 25/49]

14557.t:
In this Vachanāmrut, Shobhārām Shāstri makes the suggestion to Mahārāj that if he showed a miracle to an eminent man, it would be beneficial for the Satsang Fellowship.
The circumstances to this suggestion revolves around an incurable disease that afflicted Mahārājā Sayājirāv Gāyakwād of Vadodarā, despite trying several treatments. Shobhārām Shāstri saw the favourable affection the Mahārājā developed for Shriji Mahārāj when He spent a few days there. Moreover, Shobhārām Shāstri had a strong desire to increase Satsang. It has been written that, prior to hearing about Satsang, his mind remain detached from Satsang; however, after having contact in Satsang, his Satsang increased day by day. Whoever he spoke to, he mentioned that Swāminārāyan is God. Whether they believed him or not, he never withheld speaking about Bhagwān Swāminārāyan.
[H.C.S. : 27/20-21]
So, Shobhārām Shāstri wanted to increase Satsang. And he knows that Shriji Mahārāj can cure any incurable disease by merely a thought. He had witnessed these types of miracles while Mahārāj was in Vadodarā.
When Mahārāj was departing from Vadodarā in a procession, one {!satsangi!} name Ranchhod Bhāvsār exclaimed to his wife, “Look, Ganga has arrived to our house. Mahārāj is seated on an elephant. Behold his {!murti!} and do {!darshan!}!”
His wife said weeping, “You have eyes so you can do his {!darshan!}. I’m blind and have never seen God, so how can I behold his {!murti!}? If He is truly God, then He can give me {!darshan!}.”
When the wife said this, the film that developed on her pupil which obstructed her sight for 20 years vanished and she was able to see.
The procession marched forward toward Pānigate. There, on the royal path, there were some graves belonging to a particular caste of Muslims. A nude {!sannyāsi!} came out from that area. Mahārāj took a fistful of flower petals and threw them on the fakir. All the flower petals fell on the fakir. Instantly, the petals became a white {!alfi!} of cloth from Jāgānnāth which covered him up to his heels. Shobhārām Shāstri saw such miracles that Mahārāj performed.
On the one hand, Gāyakwād Sarkār has an incurable disease that Mahārāj has powers to cure. On the other hand, the Mahārājā has great affection toward Mahārāj and Shobhārām has the zeal to increase Satsang. If {!dharma!} has the support of the king, then Satsang would grow much faster. Seeing such benefits from all sides, Shobhārām Shāstri suggests Mahārāj to show an eminent man a miracle.

14566.t:
1896 (Samvat 1952), Mahuvā.
Bhagatji Mahārāj had Vachanāmrut Vartāl 16 read and said, “Shriji Mahārāj has mentioned his inner feelings in this Vachanāmrut. If we contemplate deeply and realize that if we have {!darshan!} just once, even for a second, and believe God truly to be God, then the cycles of births and deaths would dissolve.”
He continued, “In the past, no one who was considered great believed that there was happiness in kingship or women. In contrast, we have set ourselves up thinking there is happiness in that. Thus, how will we ever be able to get along with the {!Satpurush!}?”
[B.M. : 525]

14567.t: 26 September 1965, Mumbai.\r\nExplaining Vachanāmrut Vartāl 16 in the assembly, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “[We] do not get along with worldly, eminent people having to say, ‘Oh, please come…sit…’ No flattery, following him around or running after him. Shāstriji Mahārāj would never engage in flattery. Would a worldly, eminent person even acknowledge us? He wouldn’t look at us. A king has pride… Whereas [we] have pride for our renunciation and initiating others as sādhus. ‘I have pride for inspiring others to worship God’, is what Mahārāj is saying. ‘I have pride of renunciation and {!vairāgya!}.’ How can one use flattery on that?\r\n[Y.M. : 4/115]

14568.t: Gunātitānand Swami says, “[We] don’t like it when some worldly, eminent person comes on his horse – and feel ‘when will he leave?’ Even if he brings {!motaiyā lādus!}, so what?... [We] prefer [the company of] meek devotees of God.”\r\n[S.V. : 6/127]

14569.t: August 1897 (Samvat 1953), Junāgadh.\r\nBhagatji Mahārāj had Vachanāmrut Vartāl 16 read and said, “ ‘Compared to the bliss of worshipping God, the bliss of the 14 realms is said to be like that of hell.’ However, the {!jiva!} has developed an outward perspective and now it needs to turn this around. If one practices introspection and spiritually embraces God, one will be able to reminisce and enjoy the nectar of devotion to God. On the other hand, nothing will be achieved just by being complacent. By associating with the {!Satpurush!}, the {!jiva!} will overcome its belief of attaching value to the five senses, a belief that originated from a lack of understanding and discretion. The {!Satpurush!} will then be able to convince such a person about the value of God.”\r\n[B.M. : 583]

14581.t:
In 1872 (VS 1928) Bhagatji was residing in Vartāl. At that time, Shri Govardhanbhāi was the chief kothāri of Vartāl. His nephew, Shri Girdharbhāi, came into Bhagatji’s contact. From the beginning, Girdharbhāi was a genuine spiritual aspirant and had many saintly qualities. He had decided that if he found an accomplished and great {!sadguru!}, he would renounce the world, become a {!sādhu!} and stay with that {!sadguru!} in order to attain God-realization in this very birth. Earlier, he had associated with Shukānand Swāmi’s disciple, Dharmaprasād Swāmi. The latter had associated with Gunātitānand Swāmi and on the basis of Vachanāmrut Vartāl 19 would repeatedly tell Girdharbhāi, “Moksha is attained only through the company of Bhagwān or a Sant who has met Bhagwān.” When Girdharbhāi heard these words, he decided to find such a Satpurush to associate with. Therefore, he left Vartāl in order to travel around in Satsang to fulfil his quest.
At first, he stayed with Mana Bhagat in Gadhadā for three months. Next, he stayed in Kotadā for two-and-a-half months before going to Junagadh. He also stayed with Nirgundās Swāmi in Amdāvād for two months. Yet his mind would not accept them as, “Great,” as described by Mahārāj in the Vachanāmrut. 
After that, he stayed with Achyutdās Swāmi in Bhuj for two-and-a-half months. Achyutdās Swāmi could continually see his {!ātmā!}. Although he had attained such a state, Girdharbhāi still did not feel the peace he desired. Finally, exhausted and unfulfilled, he returned to Vartāl,
In Vartāl, Girdharbhāi stood on one leg and prayed in front of the {!murti!} of Shri Harikrishna Mahārāj in Vartāl. After some time, pleased with his devotion, Bhagwān Swāminārāyan granted him His {!darshan!}. Girdharbhāi was overjoyed and thrilled to have this divine {!darshan!}. He prayed emotionally to Mahārāj, “Mahārāj, please make my state such that I can continually experience the bliss of your form. Also, please remain in my heart forever.”
Mahārāj was pleased with his prayer and said, “Bhaktarāj! A person can attain this state if he serves the {!Param Ekāntik Satpurush!}. Only he can purify the {!jiva!} and remove it from the cycle of infinite births by destroying {!māyā!} and establish my form in the heart. At present, such a {!Satpurush!} is Prāgji Bhakta, so serve him!”
Having said this, Bhagwān Swāminārāyan disappeared. Girdharbhāi was stunned because, rather than a {!sadguru!}, Mahārāj pointed him towards the meek devotee Prāgji Bhakta - the one who spent the day sewing in the assembly hall. Prāgji Bhakta, a tailor! How could he possibly be the {!Satpurush!}? Girdharbhāi was confused and his mind was overshadowed by doubts. He lacked clarity and failed to trust Mahārāj’s words. He again offered the same devotion to Mahārāj. One month later, Mahārāj, pleased by his genuine devotion, gave him divine {!darshan!} again.
Girdharbhāi repeated the same prayer to Mahārāj, “Mahārāj, please bless me with your continual {!darshan!}. Bless me so that I can achieve Bhagwān-realization and can recognize the one who is {!ekāntik!}.” Mahārāj laughed and said, “Bhaktarāj! At present, Prāgji Bhakta is the {!Ekāntik Satpurush!}. Despite being under the guise of a tailor, he is the {!Satpurush!} who beholds my form continuously. He has already perfected {!ekāntik dharma!}. Put aside the pride of your caste. You will experience peace if you surrender to him.” Mahārāj said this and then disappeared. This reassurance was now enough for Girdharbhāi.
This marked the beginning of Girdharbhāi’s conviction in Bhagatji and the start of his spiritual association with him. Kothāri Govardhanbhāi also developed deep respect for Bhagatji. He now knew that Girdharbhāi would no longer wish to remain as a householder. He arranged for Girdharbhāi to be initiated into the {!sādhu!}-fold at the hands of Adbhutānand Swāmi and named him Vignāndās Swāmi.
[B.M. : 163]

14582.t: After having Vachanāmrut Vartāl 19 narrated, Yogiji Mahārāj explained, “In this, Mahārāj has said that all must listen as he is about to deliver a discourse about God. By merely saying this, all became alert. God was present himself, but Mahārāj spoke from the perspective of the non-manifest form of God, because the {!jiva!} does not have the same level of conviction for the manifest form as it has for the non-manifest form of God. However, God and his {!Sant!} are always present on this earth. Hence, Mahārāj explained that they are never non-manifest, but one is unable to recognise them.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 23/10]

14585.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “This human body should be utilized for worshipping God. A human birth in this {!Bharat-khand!} is not attained by merely a few spiritual merits. Even the deities say, ‘{!Aho amishām!}.’ After reciting this shlok, Swāmi explained, “Even the deities wish for the human body that has been attained by us. God and his {!Sant!} have also been attained. This is not a small attainment.”\r\n[S.V. : 6/16]

14586.t: 19 June 1962, Mumbai.\r\nDuring the spiritual discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Mahārāj said that we are talking about God. Everyone understood that Mahārāj was talking about God [up there] but no-one said, ‘Mahārāj, talk about yourself.’ Having attained the {!Satpurush!} is itself liberation and the attainment of Akshardhām for us. Through the grace and blessings of the great {!Sant!}, we can experience this.” \r\n[Y.M. : 3/360]

14595.t:
12 April 1959, Jambusar. 
Once at 11pm, Yogiji Mahārāj, speaking on Vartāl 19, said, “If one cannot recognise the {!Sant!}, then he cannot be called a devotee. What does it mean to recognise? We have understood the importance of rupees, so will we throw them away? No! We put them in our pockets. The {!Ekāntik Sant!} of God has {!dharma, gnān, vairāgya, bhakti!} and is flawless. If one develops love for him, then one is a devotee; otherwise one may sit in the {!mandir!} and turn a {!mālā!} but one is still not a devotee. God says no.
If Swāminārāyan {!sādhus!} are walking in the streets, people comment, ‘Swāminārāyan’s {!sādhus!} are walking’; however, they do not understand them in their full glory. This {!sādhu!} is capable of taking us to Akshardhām and is the granter of liberation. Doing as he says is definition of knowing him. Nothing else. We have understood Shriji Mahārāj to be God and {!Swāmi!} to be Akshar; therefore we must obey the five principal codes of conduct [{!vartmans!}]. When we experience the bliss of God’s {!murti!}, we consider the bliss of the world as insignificant. Once you have eaten {!dudkpak!}, would you desire the taste for anything else? The worms that live in faeces enjoy it, but would we believe happiness in that? 
What are wishes? We will go to Akshardhām. We will master {!nirdoshbuddhi!} and {!ekāntik dharma!}; we will master such wishes. Moreover, also of our work life, right?
The pleasure of the 14 realms is insignificant, like the droppings of a crow. Do you want this? God’s devotee means devotees [in other realms]? No, it means Mahārāj’s devotees. Crow droppings are faeces made up of other faeces. Having realised this, why we still not give up worldly attachment? Why can’t this be imbibed in our {!jiva!}? Because we haven’t ever heard such courageous talks.” 
[Y.M. : 2/539]

14610.t: 15 November 1955, Gondal.\r\nDelivering his New Year’s message in Gondal, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “True understanding is like having 200 armed guards in one’s protection. {!Swarupnishthā!} is like a bridegroom. One should formulate one’s understanding according to Vachanāmrut Vartāl 20. These are the 200 armed guards. If one has developed such a resolute understanding, then one does not feel the influence of adverse circumstances.”\r\n[Y.M. : 2/23]

14621.t:
In Samvat 1919, Gunātitānand Swāmi started his journey toward Vartāl for the {!samaiyo!} of Chaitra sud 15 [{!Punam!}]. He stayed one day in Gondal and then arrived in Goghāvadar, a village nearby. He stayed at the Shiv Mandir on the river bank. While resting in the afternoon, he had Jāgā Bhakta read the Vachanāmrut. Jāgā Bhakta read five Vachanāmruts: Gadhadā I-23, Gadhadā II-30 and 45, Amdāvād 2 and 3. Hearing these Vachanāmruts, Swāmi sat up and said, “It is as if I had never heard these Vachanāmruts.” He said, “Read them again.” Jāgā Swāmi read them again.
Then Swāmi said, “Listening to these Vachanāmruts, I have concluded that even after millions of years, without behaving in this way, there is no final release. So, for us, there is no alternative but to do this. Also, even if one is an {!āchārya!}, a son of Bhagwān, an {!ishwar!}, or some small or big deity, still there is no release without behaving in that way. Since, that is Mahārāj’s belief.” Based on this, Swāmi recited some couplets quoted by Mahārāj: ‘{!Nijātmānam brahmarupam…’!}, ‘{!Brahmabhutah prasannātmā…’!}, ‘{!Parinishthitopi nairgunye…’!}, ‘{!Atmāramāshcha munayo’!}.
After reciting many such couplets, he said, “When one becomes like this, then Bhagwān resides in one’s heart.” Then, looking at a devotee, he said, “You do have a {!murti!}, but without a {!mandir!} where will you install it? So, if you want to install Bhagwān, then learn to prepare a {!mandir!} as described here, then Bhagwān will stay.”
Then he continued, “When the {!sādhus!} went to get the {!murtis!} for this mandir [Junagadh], the sculptor asked, ‘What type of {!murtis!} shall I make for you?’ Then the sādhus said, ‘Make them according to these designs.’ Then the sculptor said, ‘These {!murtis!} are suitable only for a mandir worth hundreds of thousands of rupees.’ Then the sādhus said, ‘We’ve come to take {!murtis!} in accordance with such a mandir.’ So the sculptor said, ‘Then I’ll make them.’ Then the sculptor sculpted the {!murtis!}. Similarly, without becoming {!brahmarup!} where will we install Purushottam? So, if you want to install Purushottam, you have to become {!brahmarup!}.” Having said this, he got up. Then he held a devotee’s wrist and while walking told him, “Beware, never have any [worldly] desires.” Then that devotee’s desires stopped. And Swāmi said, “If one can remain like this all the time, doubts, strong attachments to one’s karma, desires, affection for worldly relations, body-consciousness, etc. and countless other strong material bonds are destroyed and one can continually stay focused on Bhagwān.”
[S.V. : 3/13]

14622.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “Mahārāj says that one should offer worship after bathing and washing, but not when one is unclean. But we do not understand this.” On this, he had Vachanāmrut Amdāvād 2 read and said, “Do what it says; and in all the Vachanāmruts, Mahārāj has talked of the {!Sādhu!}, Purushottam and {!ātmā!}-realization. Just as a thread follows the needle, similarly, he has described the essence. Understand in this way.”\r\n[S.V. : 6/97]

14627.t:
