14638.t: 13 February 1964, Mumbai. \r\nExplaining Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 1 at the Vyākhyān {!Mandir!} in the morning, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “One should remain detached from the workings of Prakruti-Purush. An ordinary level of detachment is defined as not being taken in by the sense pleasures of the body. However, a supreme level of detachment is defined as not seeing any value in anything other than [Shriji] Mahārāj. Everything else is mere packets of ash. Ash causes irritation in one’s eyes. Firm {!ātmanishthā!} is to become one with Gunātit. {!Gunātit!} knowledge depends upon firm {!ātmanishthā!} and detachment.”\r\n[Y.M. : 3/597]

14689.t:
January 1957, Departing from Mumbai.
A youth asked Yogiji Mahārāj, “Swāmi! How can one ensure that God looks upon one with grace?”
Yogiji Mahārāj replied, “If one does not consider bodily comforts whilst going through hardships and if one is constantly engaged in service, then one ensures that God looks upon one with grace; one does not become worthy of such divine grace just like that.”
Thereafter, Yogiji Mahārāj quoted Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 7, “If a person lacks detachment, but intensely serves a great {!Sant!} and obediently perseveres in his observance of the injunctions of God, then God will look upon him with an eye of compassion; as a result, all his vicious natures will be eradicated immediately. In comparison, if he were to endeavour in other ways, his nature may be eradicated, but only after a great deal of time and effort – either in this life or in later lives.”
[Y.M. : 2/205]

14713.t: 24 February 1968, Ānand.\r\nDuring the morning {!mangal pravachan!}, Yogiji Mahārāj said to the yuvaks of Ānand and Vidyanagar, “One possessing the highest level of {!nirvikalp!} faith realises that countless millions of {!brahmānds!}, each encircled by the eight barriers, appear like mere atoms before Akshar. Such is the greatness of Akshar, the abode of Purushottam Nārāyan. One who worships Purushottam realising oneself to be {!aksharrup!} can be said to possess the highest level of {!nirvikalp!} faith.” Such has been described in Vachanāmrut Loyā 12. If that is perfected, then there is nothing else left to achieve. This talk is so that one can become such a devotee. We want all to become as such. We want to confer the degree of {!aksharrup!} to all. \r\n[Y.M. : 4/641]

14720.t:
Someone asked, “Why can’t we make firm the highest level of {!nirvikalp!} faith?” 
Yogiji Mahārāj replied, “Sant Swāmi will provide the answer.”
Sant Swāmi explained, “If circumstances are good and if the speaker is highly experienced and if he is a {!jiva!} of outstanding faith, then he can perfect in this very birth.”
Yogiji Mahārāj then said, “That is the correct answer, but what did you understand of its underlying meaning? Explain that.”
Then he himself said, “It is clear that we have met a person like Shāstriji Mahārāj and got to know him; but one who could not dedicate his mind has distanced himself and is at a loss. Therefore, if we can dedicate our minds at the feet of the guru in a timely manner, then he – the Motāpurush – can instil the highest level of unblemished faith; of this, there is no doubt. Then he forever behaves enthusiastically; only fountains of peace, happiness and joy would flow; and everything up to Prakruti-Purush becomes insignificant, such that our attention is not drawn towards it. That is what he can make you achieve. If [one] does not surrender one’s mind, then how can one attain a spiritual state? Therefore, we need to make firm this concept under the guidance of a senior. This path of knowledge entails that we do things according to the words of the {!Sant!} and we keep awareness while doing it. This is difficult. We have to persevere and carry on.” 
[Y.M. : 3/539]

14722.t:
December 1959, Tabora, Tanzania.
A devotee asked, “How is it that one who initially was the best of the best and instilled faith in others changes for the worse?”
Yogiji Mahārāj replied, “He encounters layers. While doing Satsang, seven layers are encountered. A layer of perceiving human traits, a layer of divinity, a layer of {!ekāntik-panu!}; like that. He behaves according to the layer that comes and goes. First he comes to {!Satsang!}, he maintains divinity, he is exuberant; but if he stays for a long time, time ripens him and he sees actions, which is when he perceives human traits. Therefore, ‘The {!Sant!} is Gunātit in all his actions. He does everything to [help us] perfect {!ekāntik dharma!}, it is not worth seeing [{!manushyabhāv!}].’ If one behaves [with such understanding], then {!nirdoshbuddhi!} stays forever.” 
[Y.M. : 3/25]

14801.t: Whilst explaining Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 2, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Who is the eternal {!Satpurush!}? The answer is Gunātit. One attains {!sanskārs!} through the association of the {!Satpurush!}. One who has attained the association of such a {!Sant!}, yet cannot understand his glory as it is has an extremely dull intellect. An ant that climbs into a bag of sugar crystals will merrily keep eating them all the way to Kāshi. Thus one should sit in this bag [in the form of the {!Satpurush’s!} association]. Mahārāj says, ‘This is not an ordinary assembly. I regard this spiritual assembly higher than Golok, Vaikunth, etc.’ One should perform austerities, observe renunciation and religious vows. One should focus on the divine form of God. One should believe oneself to be {!Brahma!} and do {!darshan!}; this is service in itself. We may not believe what has been said; thus [Mahārāj] swore by everyone there that he saw a resplendence of divine light within everyone. What do we mean by that? It does not mean effusing a blaze of light, but it means that one becomes filled with inner divine light due to one’s association [with God]. Otherwise, we would perceive {!manushyabhāv!}.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 12/34]

14810.t: After having Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 2 read, Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “One who sees worth in anything else except Mahārāj, and desires to see something else is like one who lights a small lamp before the sun. Could he be called a {!satsangi!}? When this talk is understood, one will become mad. The fact that one does not become mad after understanding God’s glory is due to God’s will. Attaining the company of the {!Ekāntik!} [{!Sant!}] is rare. All the work that God can do, can be done by him. Not everyone has the company of God. Therefore, understand the virtues of the {!Ekāntik!} [{!Sant!}].”\r\n[S.V. : 5/112]

14817.t: 15 January 1967, Mumbai. \r\nAfter completing his morning {!pujā!} in Kapolvadi, Yogiji Mahārāj explained Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 2, “In this Vachanāmrut, Mahārāj has pointed everyone in the direction of Gunātit. One has to talk for a long time to help one recognise the {!Satpurush!}. Mahārāj was understood by all as a mere {!sadguru!}! Only Gunātit didn’t realize him as a {!sadguru!}. If someone was to come along and exclaim, ‘All five Pandavas have arrived at the seashore, five metres tall!’ Everyone would run. Once, a pipe burst in Rājkot and someone ended up exclaiming that the Ganges has ‘exploded’ [into existence there]. Everyone ran. Everyone ran to the Muslim individual in Jamnagar who [claimed that] he could cure tuberculosis! However, no one shows any astonishment at the fact that Gunātit, who hails from Akshardhām, sits here. Just as a son is in the lineage of his father, the lineage of Mahārāj is the {!Satpurush!}. What is the harm in recognising just Mahārāj? However, this is not what should happen; one has to also understand the {!Satpurush!}. Gunātit is still unfathomable even in this day and age. How can one see what is north and what is east if one has lost all sense of direction? There are only a few who remain close yet do not perceive any human traits.” In this way, Swāmishri spoke very meaningfully.\r\n[Y.M. : 4/376]

14823.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “Where the {!Sant!} is present, moral codes are observed, {!dharma!} is practised and spiritual wisdom is attained. Also, where there is the {!Sant!} there are infinite virtues and also God. So, as a result, the {!jiva!} becomes pure. It is noted in this Vachanāmrut that God has said, ‘I am not as pleased by austerities, renunciation, {!yoga!}, observance of vows, donations or other endeavours as I am by the association of the {!Sādhu!} with complete inner purity.’ Having attained this {!Satsang!}, the merits are limitless. Ajāmil was a grave sinner, but he met the Sanakādik, bowed to them and said, ‘I am not capable of achieving anything.’ The {!sādhus!} were compassionate. His son was named Nārāyan, and in this way he attained liberation.”\r\n[S.V. : 1/181]

14829.t: Shāstriji Mahārāj’s favourite Vachanāmrut is Gadhadā II 7, Yogiji Mahārāj’s favourite is Vachanāmrut III 2 and Pramukh Swāmi Mahārāj’s favourite is Vachanāmrut III 7. \r\n[Yogi Gita Marma : 188]

14838.t: August 1961, Mumbai.\r\nOne morning, Yogiji Mahārāj explained Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 2 saying, “If Mahārāj willed it, he would have placed everyone {!into samādhi!} (a trance) and shown them infinite light; however, he did not do so and swore instead [that this assembly is divine]. The reason was that if he showed [light] then everyone would become mad and divert from the path. Mahārāj says, ‘We are able to see [the divinity]; that is why I have to swear.’”\r\n[Y.M. : 3/220]

14862.t:
19 September 2016, Sārangpur. 
After completing {!darshan!} and prostrations at all of the sanctified places in the {!mandir!} complex, Param Pujya Mahant Swāmi Mahārāj entered {!sarvasva!} [his residence] from the steps facing the {!chiku vādi!}. 
Here, one {!parshad!} after another spoke, “Bhagatji Mahārāj’s favourite Vachanāmrut was Loyā 10, Shāstriji Mahārāj’s favourite Vachanāmrut was Gadhadā II 7, Yogiji Mahārāj’s favourite Vachanāmrut was Gadhadā III 2 and Pramukh Swāmi Mahārāj used to consider Vachanāmruts Gadhadā III 7 and Gadhadā III 11 as his favourite Vachanāmruts. What then is your favourite Vachanāmrut?” 
Swāmishri immediately replied, “Gadhadā III 5.”

14869.t:
1 January 1986, Sārangpur.
This Vachanāmrut is Param Pujya Pramukh Swāmi Mahārāj’s favourite Vachanāmrut. 
Once he was asked, “What is your most favourite Vachanāmrut? Also, for what reason?”
At that point, Swāmishri revealed, “In a way, all Vachanāmruts are dear to me; therefore there is no such thing as a particular favourite. However, I have a natural inclination towards Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 7. In this Vachanāmrut, Mahārāj says, ‘Those that aspire to achieve ultimate liberation should not consider anything in this world to be more blissful than God and the {!Sant!}.’ If we have resolutely fixed this thought process into our mind, we can maintain constant love and affinity towards the manifest form of God. It is for this reason that we have more of a liking for these words, due to the fact that it shows us what resolute conviction to have within. Thereafter, we should do whatever we have to do [to progress accordingly]. Therefore, our inclination lies towards the words of this Vachanāmrut, in that if we practice in our lives the principles described in this one Vachanāmrut, Mahārāj will be pleased.”

14870.t: August 18, 1956.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “There was a devotee named Dāmodar Bhakta from Kunkāvāv. He caused a disruption while reading Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 7. Gila Bhakta [who had met Shriji Mahārāj and possessed a constant vision of Mahārāj] was present in the assembly. He said, ‘Since there was a disruption in the reading, Mahārāj and Swāmi left.’ Therefore, Mahārāj and Swāmi are always present during {!kathā!}, and we should respect their presence by maintaining silence.”\r\n[Y.M. : 2/98]

14886.t:
24 June 1962, Mumbai.
During the morning {!mangal!} discourse, Yogiji Mahārāj spoke on Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 7, “The devotees are seated; however there are no {!sādhus!}. [Shriji Mahārāj] reveals his inner principles. There are only a few principles. There is nothing as valuable as God and the {!Sant!}, not even one’s [worldly] wealth. One should have total love for that which gives true joy – {!ātmabuddhi!} and loyalty [to God and the {!Sant!}]. Even if one stands to lose one’s head, one should not falter from taking the side [of God and the {!Sant!}]. On one hand, one would take [God and the {!Sant’s!}] side, but behind their back, one would find faults in them. One should keep loyalty and at the same time, one should not allow fault-finding to creep in. Mahārāj demonstrates the essence. There is only one conclusion of the 262 Vachanāmruts – one should not keep bodily relations as dear to oneself. One should do what Dada Khāchar and other eminent devotees have done. When the time comes, one does not endear one’s bodily relations.
“One can only keep loyalty if one understands the glory [of God and the {!Sant!}]. If glory is understood bodily relations are not seen as dear. [Shriji Mahārāj] is explaining the true knowledge of the place which gives out [eternal] luminance [i.e. Akshardhām]. What service does one perform in [Akshar]dham? To keep looking at the {!murti!} [of God] is one’s service. One thus experiences ever increasing joy!”
[Y.M. : 3/363]

14890.t: Shāstriji Mahārāj’s favourite Vachanāmrut is Gadhadā II 7, Yogiji Mahārāj’s favourite is Vachanāmrut III 2 and Pramukh Swāmi Mahārāj’s favourite is Vachanāmrut III 7. \r\n[Yogi Gita Marma : 188]

14946.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said: “One should read the Vachanāmrut, but also endeavour to imbibe its words too. One should not read it in haste. Moreover, one should make the most of this scripture. Many people discourse on Satsang, but if one studies and imbibes the teachings of Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 8, then Mahārāj will come to collect us to take us to Akshardhām [during one’s last moments].”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 24/336]

14948.t:
24 February 1963, Mumbai. 
During the discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj spoke on Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 8, “If one lets one’s senses loose, one is sure to experience misery. One who endeavours to achieve liberation would repent [at such an action]. One’s repentance is one experiencing misery. If one attains the grace of God and the {!Sant!}, then it is impossible for one’s senses to run off in different directions.
“Which one trait should one keep? Friendship. All five traits are encompassed within this. If one has kept affection [for the {!Sant!}], then even if [the {!Sant!}] were to utter harsh words to him or ensures that he follows {!dharma!}, he does not find fault. Friendship is the key.
“Whoever does not have the association of Akshar and Purushottam cannot be said to be a devotee. Others [people who follow past incarnations] are still treading that path [of becoming a devotee]. Gunātit is that ultimate devotee and is able to eradicate the deficiencies of 100 lifetimes from oneself. One should not find faults. [Shriji Mahārāj] has collectively called everyone a devotee just so that one understands their glory. We should identify our flaws and scrutinise our drawbacks. One remains near, yet stills  doubts whether or not ultimate liberation can be attained. One worships at home thinking [it is simply enough to] worship the {!murtis!} at home – such a person can be said to have broken off mentally [from the {!Satpurush!}]. They will refrain from coming to the {!mandir!} and not come for spiritual association. 
“Apathy can be defined as doubting whether one is able to achieve liberation here. One should not look at anyone else’s flaws. If one breaks off mentally, he is half gone; however, one with apathy is completely, 100%, broken off.”
[Y.M. : 3/444]

14954.t:
13 November 1967, Mumbai. 
Explaining the meaning of Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 8 in the assembly, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Some individuals become upset and aloof from God and the {!Sant!}. They do not like gaining the association of the {!Satpurush!} and will end up associating with one who has been excommunicated. What does that mean? One who does not follow the injunctions laid down by God is said to be excommunicated. These people who do not follow the commands [of God] have thus been excommunicated from the {!Sanstha!}. 
“It was like this in Mahārāj’s time as well. Mahārāj was all-knowin., Why then did he initiate the likes of Rolānand into sainthood? [Mahārāj] is the owner and could do as he wished. One cannot find fault in what he does. However, the natures of the likes of Rolānand and Nirvikalpānand were far from ideal. The fates of those who harboured bad intentions were such that they ended up leaving Swāmi’s [Shāstriji Mahārāj’s] {!Sanstha!} and ended up maligning.”
[Y.M. : 4/535]

14955.t:
13 November 1970, Rājkot. 
Whilst explaining the meaning of Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 8 during the {!parayan!}, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Today, we are all participating in the {!pārāyan!}. One easily remembers the Gitā and the {!Bhāgwat!}; however, this Vachanāmrut would not come to mind. These words can be considered on par with those from the {!Vedas!}. One who has been inspired by Shriji Mahārāj would be able to memorize all 262 Vachanāmruts. Presently, discourses on the Vachanāmrut being delivered, therefore one should imbibe the qualities described therein into one’s life. One would not be able to understand the essence if one does not read or subsequently contemplate on it. The words of Mahārāj and {!Mul Akshar Murti!} Gunātitānand Swāmi are supreme and to have discourses narrated about them is considered to be the best. One cannot be considered wise if one blindly spends one’s money on material objects. It is only worth it if one’s wealth is used in the service of God. Shāstriji Mahārāj used to have this Vachanāmrut, 'Remaining Eternally Happy', read often. Having understood this, one should put its principles into practice. Shriji Mahārāj’s desire for discourses was so strong that he would himself would arrange the seat and cushions and immediately commence his talks. Flowers that gave out a beautiful scent were dangling from his ears. Thus, the grandeur of the setting was excellent.
“Remaining eternally happy means being happy for some days and experiencing sadness on other days, right? No! Eternal happiness means to remain happy throughout one’s whole life. One is said to be a devotee [in the true sense of the word] if one has full conviction in Swāminārāyan. We are all practising Satsang in order to attain eternal happiness. How can one thus remain eternally happy? This is the question that was being asked.
“On that day, eminent {!sādhus!} such as Muktānand [Swāmi], Nityānand [Swāmi] and others were seated in that assembly. They were not of an ordinary stature; they were all incredibly learned; however, they were unable to answer the question satisfactorily. Thereafter, Shriji Mahārāj revealed the answer as, firstly, a devotee who has firm detachment. 
“What is firm detachment? Firm detachment is defined as complete indifference to the work of Prakruti-Purush. One does not feel a connection with anyone else but Mahārāj and Swāmi... One should maintain fidelity towards Mahārāj. One can speak to everyone else, understanding them to belong to Mahārāj. One may not be able to remain detached from the world; however, to maintain fidelity towards Mahārāj is incredibly difficult. One cannot be said to be chaste if one has accepted refuge in 18 different places. One person would turn five {!mālās!} in the name of ‘Jamiyā Dātār’, five in the name of Meladi Mātā, five in the name of Ganpati and five in the name of Mahādev (Shiva Bhagwān). Thereafter, a {!sādhu!} insisted so he said, ‘Since you are not going away, I will turn five {!mālās!} in the name of Swāminārāyan as well.’ Now, who will come to collect his {!jiva!} at his last breath? He did not have one master. If one has firm faith, Mahārāj will surely come to collect that devotee. One should have the firm faith that Shriji Mahārāj is above all and is the cause of all incarnations. In this way, one should keep firm detachment [from this world].
“One should imbibe the qualities of saintliness; otherwise if one is rebuked, one will definitely bid farewell and take the first train back. Thereafter, even if one has to suffer in the world, one will still not return.
“Mahārāj mentions intensely resolute {!dharma!}. Would it not have been fine if Mahārāj had just mentioned {!dharma!} on its own? However, he has chosen to emphasise it by talking about intensely resolute {!dharma!}. One should follow the five main vows understanding Shriji Mahārāj to be Purushottam. One should follow all of God’s commands, however big or small they may be. One should not drink unfiltered water. One should not watch dramas or movies. One should not eat out. One should not act in a manner that would give people leverage to think, ‘He is a devotee of Swāminārāyan; why is he engaging in such activities?’ How can it be said that {!dharma!} has been strengthened in one’s {!sadhus'!} life if one forsakes the company of a {!sadhu!} to go and see a circus? Our {!dharma!} is to follow the injunctions laid down in the three scriptures, namely Shikshāpatri, Dharmāmrut and Nishkām Shuddhi.
“Thus, two facets [of remaining eternally happy] have been discussed – resolute detachment and {!dharma!}. Through these two methods, one gains victory and control over one’s {!indriyas!}; one does not even harbour any desired to do anything immoral.
“The second endeavour shown to us is that of intense affinity for God and his devotees. By this, we do not mean that which is just superficail, but [we mean] the truest level of affinity, so much so that one cannot live without their company. Affinity is defined as following the commands [of God], right to the letter; one does not step out of line, even for the slightest moment. One should harbour love [towards God] coupled with the true knowledge [of his form], such that one would never perceive human traits in God and the {!Sant!}.
“Even if one only reads half of the Vachanāmrut, it is more important to imbibe it in our lives. One should not end up reading the whole Vachanāmrut if in haste. One should have their fill [of this knowledge].”
Thereafter, he addressed a devotee, “One may direct many towards the path of Satsang, but if one does just this much [imbibe the Vachanāmrut], Mahārāj will collect one [to go to Akshardhām at the end of one’s life]. The more places one takes refuge in, the more misery one is sure to experience. Shāstriji Mahārāj is our one and only guru; apart from this, even if many {!sadgurus!} appear, consider them to be the crowns of our heads. However, one should hold the firm conviction that Shāstriji Mahārāj is our [only] guru, Shriji Mahārāj is supreme and the incarnation of all incarnations, and Mul Aksharmurti [Gunātitānand] Swāmi is the eternal abode of Shriji Mahārāj. We listen to so much knowledge being discussed; however, this is true knowledge indeed. If one has intense love, when one is burdened, one will not say, ‘Swāmi! I am unable to do this.’ According to Vachanāmrut Loyā 3, one who understands the true glory will offer his head.
“The third endeavour described is intense friendship with God and God’s devotee.” Describing in detail the story of the prince and the son of the administrator, Yogiji Mahārāj spoke of friendship, “If one were to reach for the other’s neck in this manner, the other individual is sure to abandon one, as well as their friendship for good. We have many friends in the world; however, one should establish such a friendship with God and the {!Sant!}.
“The fourth endeavour described is never being upset with God and God’s devotee. However, if [the {!Sant!}] were to test him a little by giving him the slightest difficulty, one would inevitably think that the {!Sant!} has strained him and that he is fed up. Thinking in this way, he would simply leave and go home.
“Dada Khāchar hosted Mahārāj at his home for 30 years. Even if devotees from other places insisted that Mahārāj visit their town for just a few days, he would cry. Therefore, if God and the {!Sant!} give us a little difficulty, one should not become dejected. The situation now is that people would run away [from us] thinking that, ‘The {!sādhu!} is continuously asking.’ Despite the fact that Mahārāj gave difficulties to Jhinabhāi [of Panchala] and Dada Khāchar, they never became unhappy. Therefore, if we have truly recognised the {!Satpurush!}, we should never become unhappy despite the constant barrage of testing [that Mahārāj may take us through]. Does anyone become upset with their wife and kids, even if they beat him up with their shoes?
“The fifth endeavour is being pleased only when one is in the company of God and his devotee. 
“The sixth endeavour is renouncing the company of those that are excommunicated – those that are completely cut off from God. One is only receptive to the talks of those that are firm in {!dharma!} and faith. Who can be said to be excommunicated? Mahārāj has answered this by revealing in Vachanāmrut [Gadhadā] II 60 that such a person considers all {!sādhus!} to be the same. If one were to remain listening to degrading talks of God and his devotee in order to maintain one’s reputation in front of others, that can also be considered to be excommunicated. Also, one who considers God to be formless is said to be excommunicated. God forever possesses a form. His form is apparent here as well as in Akshardhām.
“In this way, whosoever perfects these six points into their lives will remain eternally happy in this world and in the world beyond [Akshardhām].
“Mahārāj has said that I will take care of the food, clothing, reputation and wealth of one who acts accordingly and I will also take him to [Akshar]{!dham!} when the time comes. Therefore, if one has not gained control over one’s {!indriyas!}, then even if he continually stays with Mahārāj and Swāmi, he remains unhappy. One may turn the {!mālā!}, meditate or serve in the {!mandir!}; however, one must keep one’s {!indriyas!} in check. One should be pained if any inappropriate thoughts enter one’s mind, thinking, ‘How can I think like this despite being a devotee of God!’ Subsequently, one does not follow that path. Many ask, ‘Why does God not control our {!indriyas!}? Why does God allow our senses to roam freely and indulge?’ but, ‘O fool of fools! Why do you let your mind engage in such indulgences?’ Even if one is sitting near God or the {!Sant!}, how can one attain happiness if one’s mind is wandering freely elsewhere?
“Mahārāj has said the same thing three times, each time in a different way. Therefore, if one acts accordingly, regardless of whether one is a {!sādhu, brahmachāri, pārshad, āchārya!} or householder, one remains eternally happy. If we tolerate when someone rebukes us, is there any misery in this? However, if one retorts, there is a possibility that a formal complaint would be lodged! Senior {!sadgurus!} organised the public humiliation of {!Anādi Mul Aksharmurti!} Gunātitānand Swāmi in Vartāl; however, he still tolerated it. When it was his turn to speak, he spoke on the supreme glory of Mahārāj and codes of conduct for a good three hours without even a hint of inferiority. Not one word was uttered about the insults that he had just had to bear. Even Pavitrānand Swāmi had to concede, ‘Bravo! You really are {!Gunātit!}!’ Thus, even he saw good in Gunātitānand Swāmi. Thereafter, everyone offered shawls and garlands to Swāmi in honour; after which he said, ‘I view both honours and insults as one and the same.’ Thus, one who acts accordingly is {!gunātit!} - above the three {!gunas!}.
“The {!sādhus!} have asked questions in the Vachanāmrut on our behalf. Muktānand Swāmi asked a question, ‘What is the greatest obstacle for a devotee when offering devotion to God?’ Mahārāj showed three obstacles, the first of which is that one cannot recognise one’s own shortcomings. The fact that we go to look for flaws such as anger or egotism in others despite not being able to recognise our own should be known as awkward natures. We should only look at putting out our own fire. That is enough. Why should one look at [the faults of] others?
“The second obstacle is that one’s mind remains detached from God and the {!Sant!} despite physically being present with them, just as oil remains separated from water despite being together in one container. However, we should immerse ourselves in them just as ‘{!Rasbas hoi rahi Rasiyā sang, jyu misri pay māhi bhali’!} – sugar gets immersed in milk.
“The third obstacle is that one becomes disinterested in the devotee of God. When the {!Sant!} gives one some difficulty, he would retort, ‘I have a {!mandir!} at home and I will turn the {!mālā!}.’ He would even go on to say, ‘Is ultimate liberation only attainable here?’ Thus, one who is disinterested does not like the actions and words of the {!Sant!}. Even if the {!Satpurush!} talks to him out of love, the disinterested individual would think, ‘He just had to pick me out, didn’t he?’
“The greatest of three obstacles is the feeling of disinterest. He would simply go home. Even if a fault-finder picks out flaws, he could still just about last in Satsang; however, the disinterested person can be said to have completely broken all ties and leave, never to return. Jivā Khāchar, Alaiyā Khāchar, Nirvikalpānand were those who didn't care and remained disinterested. One whose mind remains aloof would still just about pull along in Satsang; however, this disinterested-ness is of a completely different 'fashion'altogether. He would never even care to look back.
“Thus, [those described above] are the three most dangerous obstacles in performing devotion. Mahārāj has emphasised on the ‘most dangerous’ part. One must, therefore, eradicate these traits through the association [of God and the {!Sant!}].”
[Y.M. : 6/480]

14995.t: 27 February 1970, Kisumu, Kenya.\r\nAfter having had Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 9 read during the afternoon discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Awareness is defined as not perceiving human traits in God and the {!Sant!}. Awareness means not finding flaws in anyone. It is mentioned in [Vachanāmrut] Gadhadā II 46 that for a devotee of God, true death is not departure from the physical body; it is finding faults in a devotee of God. ‘Oh, what an elevated devotee Maganbhāi is!’ Awareness is the fact that one understands the glory of another devotee. One must see only good traits in others and overlook their flaws. The weight of their flaws is on them. Why don’t you look at God? God is the all-doer. If one seeks his refuge, then one is sure to be rid of all misery. Awareness is not being under the influence of anyone except Purushottam Nārāyan.”\r\n[Y.M. : 6/65]

14998.t: 7 January 1967, Mumbai.\r\nExplaining Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 9 in the assembly, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Externally, scholars may explain knowledge in one way or another; however, they are not understand by anyone. True awareness means that Akshardhām is manifest as a form [on this earth], within whom Mahārāj himself resides eternally. He gives {!darshan!} to all. One loses awareness if one perceives human traits in him.”\r\n[Y.M. : 4/365]

15007.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Two Vachanāmruts are worth imbibing in one’s life. Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 7 and III 11: An understanding like that of Sitāji. One may not understand all the Vachanāmruts, but one should always refer to their favourite Vachanāmruts [of their spiritual inclination] and imbibe their words.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 29/45]

15008.t:
Samvat 1946. Bhādrod.
One day, Sādhu Yagnapurushdāsji and Nārāyancharandāsji went to Talgājardā to beg for alms [{!jholi!}]. Afterwards, they sat at a spot where the Patel of the village arrived. Yagnapurushdāsji spoke to him. The Patel was impressed and said, “Wow! The {!sādhus!} who are worthy of being honoured on an elephant have to wonder around begging for alms. This is Prāgji’s doing.”
Yagnapurushdāsji replied, “Actually, Bhagatji preached to us extensively and taught us the ways to conform with Satsang. We were preaching on the Dharmāmrut and singing verses from the Chosath Padi and other scriptures freely. Others did not like our behaviour. So Bhagatji made us humble. Moreover, the devotees of Gujarat are attached to us but the other {!sādhus!} do not approve and cause discord. Therefore, Bhagatji kept us here and preaches to us; otherwise something detrimental would happen to our {!jiva!} and the whole Satsang would have opposed us. However, only because of Bhagatji’s company, everything is fine.”
Hearing this, the Patel said, “Is that so? I have heard talks against Bhagatji, but now I understand how virtuous he is.” He then gave the {!sādhus!} 5 kg of rice in their {!jholi!}.
Sādhu Nārāyancharandās told Bhagatji this incident. He was immensely pleased. He said, “Whenever all of you speak to others, do not speak of your own virtues; instead, speak of your own faults and the virtues of the great [{!Satpurush!}] and learn the understanding like that of Sitāji.”
[S.M. : 1/126]

15009.t:
17 May 1963, Sardārgadh. 
After having Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 11 read during the afternoon discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “How much glory did Sitāji possess [for Shri Rām]? She suffered a great deal of unhappiness; however, she sent a message to Shri Rām that she was experiencing no adversities whatsoever and that she would happily engage in devotion with love and not be detached [from Shri Rām].
“On the other hand, others would say ‘Jai Swāminārāyan’ and catch the first train out, never to return... Sitāji had plenty of time on her hands and could have found faults in Shri Rām should she have wished to; however, she refrained from doing so. This level of understanding has been praised [in this Vachanāmrut]. One of this stature would not engage in fault finding, even if rebuked for no reason.”
[Y.M. : 3/493]

15012.t: 24 February 1955, Saring. \r\nIn the evening assembly, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Only when one perfects this Vachanāmrut – Understanding like that of Sitāji – can it be said that one has gained a true understanding and that one has truly realised that God is forever free from flaws.”\r\n[Y.M. : 1/556]

15021.t: 17 May 1963, Sardargadh. \r\nYogiji Mahārāj had Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 11 read in the afternoon assembly and said, “This Vachanāmrut is worthy enough to be imbibed into one’s {!jiva!}. If one does this, one will be rid of all adversities. This is one worth imbibing.” \r\n[Y.M. : 3/492]

15024.t: Whilst explaining Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 11, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “To tolerate the words of others is also a type of austerity. To perform the austerity of tolerance is great. To remain within one’s spiritual state is also an austerity. Is going to live in forest austerity? No, but to enjoy fewer objects is austerity. One who constantly performs austerities will not sustain long [in Satsang]. If one performs {!dhārnā-pārnā!} for two months and then eats excessively, of what use is that penance?”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 14/12]

15026.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Gunātitānand Swāmi has explained in his spiritual discourses that maintaining {!ātmābuddhi!} is Satsang. It is not the intention to disregard spiritual rules, righteousness, renunciation and non-attachment to worldly objects; however {!ātmābuddhi!} is the prime factor. If one possesses {!ātmābuddhi!}, one will maintain loyalty; this was [Gunātitānand] Swāmi’s principle. Through the grace of God, one may be able to behold the constant {!darshan!} of God’s form and achieve great heights – to the extent that people may offer prostrations to such an individual. But without {!ātmābuddhi!}, Mahārāj has revealed that grave shortcomings remain in a devotee.\r\n“According to Vachanāmruts Gadhadā II 54 and Gadhadā III 11, one can only experience everlasting peace by maintaining {!ātmābuddhi!}. If a devotee is loyal and maintains {!ātmābuddhi!} in the {!bhakta!} of God, this will be one’s last birth.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 3/16]

15028.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “One should imbibe Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III-11, which is based on Sitāji’s understanding. One’s Satsang will only become firm if the {!Motāpurush!} gives one suffering without any reason and one does not ever perceive any faults in him.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 29/18]

15034.t: 10 July 1961, Mumbai.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj wrote a truly inspirational letter addressed to the entire Satsang community through Swāminārāyan Prakāsh. Within this letter, Swāmishri emphasised the resolute understanding that one should have by writing, “One should imbibe Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 11 – ‘Understanding like that of Sitāji’. We should only focus on good qualities, even if a person comes and rebukes us for no rhyme or reason. Therefore, all of us should read and perfect Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 11. If we do accordingly, then we will not see even a single fault in anyone; one will feel that this Satsang is divine and one is also sure to experience infinite peace. The important Vachanāmruts – Loyā 17, Kāriyāni 1, Gadhadā II 59 and Gadhadā II 28 – should all be perfected. The principle is to become a devotee of God with great humility. This is our only duty.”\r\n[Y.M. : 3/205]

15045.t:
March 1936, Sārangpur.
After having Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 12 read, Shāstriji Mahārāj lucidly spoke on behaving with humility, and about renouncing obstinacy, egotism and jealousy. 
He concluded by saying, “Therefore, all the {!sādhus, parshads!} and devotees should imbibe Shriji Mahārāj’s principle in their hearts. If one has not perfected this Vachanāmrut, then in five years, 10 years or even 50 years, one wil inevitably have to return home. Furthermore, in the end, any devotee who has not perfected this Vachanāmrut won’t be able to stay in Satsang. Therefore, ego, criticism and jealousy – these three will make the {!jiva!} fall.”
[S.M. : 2/4]

15053.t: After having Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 13 read, Gunātitānand Swāmi discussed the following question, How can one remain God-centric even when one's circumstances become adverse? Swāmi explained, “If complete faith remains, that is itself a characteristic of one who is God-centric. Just as, if the wish-fulfilling gem [{!chintāmani!}] remains and all other wealth is lost, then nothing is lost; but if the wish-fulfilling gem [{!chintāmani!}] is lost and all wealth remains, then nothing remains; similarly, if firm faith remains, everything remains; in the end, only that will remain, for that is the means to final liberation.”\r\n[S.V. : 1/203]

15055.t: After Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 13 was read, Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “Even under the influence of place, time, actions, etc, the true love of one who understands {!upāsanā!} while considering oneself to be Akshar is never diminished. Such a person does not get taken in by egotism. If one understands that even divine abodes such as Golok, etc. can be destroyed by {!kāl!} at any time, then even if one’s physical ability to worship God is rendered useless, one does not lose the affinity that one has with God.”\r\nSwāmi then gave an analogy, “If one loses all other wealth, but the wish-fulfilling gem [{!chintāmani!}] remains, then nothing has been lost; however, if one loses the wish-fulfilling gem then everything has been lost.”\r\n[S.V. : 5/215]

15058.t: 8 June 1968, Gondal.\r\nExplaining in short the importance of this Vachanāmrut, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Gadhadā III 14 is the Vachanāmrut of faith.” \r\n[Y.M. : 5/96]

15059.t:
In Samvat 1945, during the assembly at Mahuvā {!mandir!}, Fulchandbhāi asked, “Can you please you tell us the way in which you understand Bhagatji and what you have seen in him.” Shāstriji Mahārāj elaborated the qualities described in Gadhadā I 27 and established Bhagatji Mahārāj as the {!Param Ekāntik Satpurush!}. He then said Bhagatji Mahārāj has been insulted in Satsang without a fault of his own, yet his faith in Shriji Mahārāj never wavered, as mentioned in Gadhadā III 21.
Raghuvircharan Swāmi raised a doubt, “No one is ever insulted in Satsang without it being their fault.”
Yagnapurushdāsji replied, “If this were true, why did Shriji Mahārāj use the words, ‘No matter how much a firm devotee is insulted in Satsang and no matter how much misery befalls them...’? Therefore, Mahārāj permits one to be insulted as a test of their conviction.”
Supporting this, Vitthalbhāi said, “Swāmi! If these words are written in the Vachanāmrut, please reveal them. We want to clarify everything today.”
Yagnapurushdāsji read Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 11 and Gadhadā III 14 and explained, “Mahārāj has clearly said that, ‘Even if he is harshly insulted by Bhagwān and his {!Sant!} without any fault of his own, he still does not bear an aversion to anyone, and then he earns the trust of Bhagwān and his {!Sant!}.’
“Bhagatji has been insulted and has faced difficulties despite no fault of his own. Nevertheless, he has remained unaffected. Knowing him to be the {!Param Ekāntik Sant!} - who beholds Shriji Mahārāj in every way - we have attached our {!jivas!} to him by thought, word, and deed. We desire nothing but {!moksha!} from him. He is not of our community or {!āshram!} in life. Our regions are not same, nor our clothes, nor are our towns the same, and he does not give us anything. In spite of knowing Bhagatji’s background, we have still attached our {!jivas!} to him through trust in Mahārāj’s words and in accordance with the Vachanāmrut - because it is his command to attach one’s {!jiva!} to the {!ekāntik!}. We are confident that Mahārāj will never give us unhappiness. It may seem like unhappiness in this world, but even then we experience continual happiness in our hearts.”
[B.M. : 253]

15070.t: 31 March 1963, Kapolvadi, Mumbai. \r\nAfter much talk on Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 15 during the Sunday assembly, Yogiji Mahārāj explained its main point. “The fact that one sees no the shortcomings of others and can experience an elevated state of joy means that one is now on the right path. If one yearns for ultimate liberation, one will engage in nine types of devotion, such as {!shravan!} (listening to talks praising the glory of God), {!manan!} (contemplation), etc. One the correct path, one will notice [only] one's own shortcomings.”\r\n[Y.M. : 3/456]

15076.t:
12 March 1963, Mumbai. 
Once, Yogiji Mahārāj said in Kapolvadi, “...One will only gain entry into Akshardhām if one is chaste in one's conviction. All demigods are due to this God… If one feels confused, one should contemplate on Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 16 and Gadhadā II 5.
“One will only develop affinity for the {!Sant!} after understanding the true nature of God's form; otherwise, one will end up falling off [the path of liberation]. One should affirm the nature of the true form of God in one’s mind, after which one is sure to experience insurmountable joy. It is others that are the ones running after scraps, while we experience ultimate joy.
“Mahārāj will explain [this concept] to us through his inspiration. One should stick to one place. ‘If there are indeed two Gods, they will sort things out between them; what are we to gain from that?’ One should not even think along these lines. If one has truly understood this and subsequently imbibed it into their life, then all misunderstandings are cleared. One can only truly understand through faith… since you have affinity [towards me], renounce the whims of your mind.”
[Y.M. : 3/448]

15136.t:
Āshābhāi, Ishwarbhāi and Motibhāi jointly owned property and managed its affairs. One day, they went for Shāstriji Mahārāj’s {!samāgam!} from Purushottampurā to Radhu. Āshābhāi had built a new bungalow to stay in and to store cotton, grains and heaps of other items. In Samvat 1985, even during an unfavourable year, he had stored 1,200 kg of cotton, 1,400 kg of chickpeas, 20,000 kg of wheat and other items to sell.
One night, his middle son Ramanbhāi lit a match while playing and threw it to the ground. It fell near the heap of cotton, lighting it, and eventually, the entire bungalow on fire. The storage and the bungalow were reduced to ashes.
The news reached everyone in Radhu, but Āshābhāi’s facial expression did not change one bit. Shāstriji Mahārāj asked Ishwarbhāi and Motibhāi to go to Purushottampurā to check if anything was saved. They observed that nothing remained from the fire. Since the food also burned away, they brought {!khichadi!} from Radhu and served everyone. [Āshābhāi’s family had escaped the bungalow before it burnt down.]
Motibhāi returned to Radhu. Shāstriji Mahārāj asked if anything was saved. Motibhāi replied with folded hands, “Bāpā, nothing survived. We had to fetch {!khichadi!} from Radhu last night to feed everyone.” Motibhāi’s eyes teared up.
Swāmishri patted his back to console Motibhāi. Motibhāi said, “Swāmi, we served for ten years in Purushottampurā, yet our fortune did not turn around.”
Swāmishri said, “Your sins have been burnt away. From now on, everything will be better.”
Motibhāi asked again with folded hands, “Swāmi, we have been in your company for many years now, yet we still have sins remaining?”
Swāmishri laughed and answered, “For Bhagwān’s {!ekāntik bhakta!}, to have affection or desires for anything other than Bhagwān is a sin (Gadhadā III 17). By burning the bungalow, Shriji Mahārāj has taught you {!sānkhya-gnān!}. Now, even if your wealth increases, because you have {!sānkhya-gnān!}, you will not be attached to it.”
[S.M. : 1/581]

15137.t:
6 June 1962, Mumbai.
Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Bharatji renounced the kingship of the whole world in order to please God. However, it was a surprising miracles that a fawn proved to be a hurdle in achieving his objective. He formed a bond with the fawn – something that ended up shackling him down [on the journey to please God], despite possessing all knowledge to the contrary.
“One should not have a desire for women, wealth and or one's disciples. A true miracle is that one is able to eradicate them [from one’s mind]. One should only form a deep attachment towards God and the {!Sant!}, so much so that one becomes immersed in them constantly. However, it is regrettable that one is unable to do so here. What understanding should one have in order to free oneself from these worldly bonds? These will be eradicated through the true knowledge and the blessings [of God and the {!Sant!}].
“After listening to this incident, one should realise that one cannot, under any circumstances, form any such bonds. One should not have a soft spot for worldliness. What chance do we stand if even the greats have been taken in by this? They were shackled down due to their sins.
“There are many kinds of sin; however, the gravest sin for a devotee of God is to form a bond with anything or anyone else but God. What if one forms such a bond with the devotees of God? This is what we have to achieve - not to remain 'dry'. Through this, we are able to attain the {!ekāntik!} state.
“One should keep compassion for one another, but only to the extent of what is deemed necessary. One should not keep excessive compassion that it spoils one’s ultimate liberation.”
[Y.M. : 3/351]

15169.t:
28 December 1956. 
Once, whilst travelling overnight via train to Madrās, Yogiji Mahārāj called the youths and had Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 17 read. He then said, “Within this, the incident of Bharatji is described as miraculous; so what is that miracle? Bharatji renounced his kingdom and his relatives and he was also the son of Rushabhdev {!Bhagwān!}; despite this, out of compassion, he formed an attachment towards a mere deer. One should master the art of showing compassion – that one should only keep as much compassion as is necessary; however, not to the extent of forming such a deep attachment. It is indeed a grave sin for a devotee of God for his focus to remain anywhere else but God. One who is indeed a {!Motāpurush!} never attaches himself to any worldly actions and would not allow others to do so either.
“Gunātitānand Swāmi was the head ({!mahant!}) of Junagadh {!Mandir!}, however, he used to keep his {!jholi!} always hung on a hook. The sole reason for this being that if Mahārāj sent a letter from Gadhadā calling for him, he would be able to take his {!jholi!} and leave for Gadhadā without delay. Nishkulānand Swāmi looked after the affairs of Dholera {!Mandir!}; however, he used to say that he has left the burden of it all to [Mount] Sālemāl [i.e. left everything up to God]. One should engage in worldly affairs according to God’s wishes; yet, while doing so, one should forever remain mentally detached and free from any misery that may arise. One should not form an attachment towards these affairs – that is the true definition of being of an elevated spiritual state.
“One cannot be said to have rid themselves of one’s worldly desires if one continues to have thoughts about worldly affairs. Thoughts related only to God will remain if one’s worldly desires have been eradicated. Thoughts regarding worldly affairs cause one to forget the murti of God and also prove to be a great obstacle in performing devotion.”
[Y.M. : 2/174]

15213.t: 23 September 1970, Bhādrā. \r\nExplaining Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 18, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “If Pramukh Swāmi is discoursing and one starts to feel sleepy, what should one do? Should one go away and sleep, or sit and listen to the discourses? If one thinks, ‘Let us go to sleep,’ then understand that to be a worldly desire. If one has the firm resolve, ‘Even though I have arthritis, I am feeling sleepy and also I am also feeling feverish, I still want to listen to the {!kathā!},’ then it can be said that one’s inner desirous thoughts have degenerated. Such thoughts cannot be removed unless one has attained the grace of God and the {!Sant!}.”\r\n[Y.M. : 6/435]

15215.t: Whilst explaining Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 18, Yogiji Mahārāj said, ‘If one develops affection for the eternal {!Gunātit Satpurush!}, one’s worldly desires will be burnt away. The eternal {!Gunātit Satpurush!} never departs [from this earth]. What is the surety of one’s spiritual destiny if he were to depart?”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 12/53]

15232.t:
6 June 1962, Mumbai. 
During the morning discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “How can one's worldly desires degenerate? If one has a newspaper on one side and the Vachanāmrut on the other, one should not fee like leaving aside the Vachanāmrut to read the newspaper. Mādhā Patel of Mojidad was such a devotee that if he received any guests and it was time for discourses, he would invite them to come along and listen to the discourses. If the guests refused, he would show them the bedroom and say to them, ‘Here is a bed for you and here is a pitcher of water for you to drink if required. You are free to rest.’ How would they sleep just like that as a guest? They would have to come despite not wanting to. This is the definition of degenerating one’s inner desires.
“Should one go and make a profit of Rs. 10,000 in the marketplace or come here to Shāstriji Mahārāj? One can only be considered to possess great strength if one has thoughts relating only to God. Others are of an inferior level. One is said to be free of desires when one only keeps these thoughts relating to God while continuing to support one’s worldly affairs in accordance with God’s wishes. On the contrary, it can be said that one is still full of worldly desires if one is so deep into worldly affairs and cannot leave them even at the behest of the {!Motāpurush’s!}.”
[Y.M. : 3/353]

15246.t: Harshadbhāi Dave, a proficient scholar of the Vachanāmrut, used to say the following piece of history connected with this Vachanāmrut: “In this Vachanāmrut, Shriji Mahārāj Himself taught Shukmuni this question and had him pose it to Gopālānand Swāmi. Seeing Gopālānand Swāmi struggle to answer the question, Mahārāj laughed a great deal.”

15248.t:
Samvat 1952, Gadhadā.
During the Jal-Jhilani {!samaiyo!} at 2:00p.m., Bhagatji made his way to Āchārya Vihārilālji Mahārāj’s residence, where an assembly was in progress. During the discourses, Āchārya Mahārāj asked Moti Bhagat to read Vachanāmruts Gadhadā I 27 and Gadhadā III 21.
Āchārya Mahārāj then said, “Both of these Vachanāmruts seem to apply to Bhagatji. This is evident because Pavitrānand Swāmi insulted Bhagatji when Bhagvatprasādji Mahārāj went to Mahuvā. However, in the intense summer heat, Bhagatji would still sit on the sand opposite the tent and only got up after the evening discourse had finished. He is the only person in whom I have seen such enthusiasm for discourses and {!darshan!} of the {!sādhus!}. Everyone else was also convinced and felt, ‘There is no one else like this,’ when they witnessed his elevated state of humility and saintliness. I was also amazed to see his spiritual state. Only a golden thread remain firm throughout all seasons, whilst threads made from wax soften during the summer heat. Similarly, in Satsang, only those who possess such a spiritual state remain stable when insulted; whereas others end up leaving Satsang permanently.”
“All of this is due to [Gunātitānand] Swāmi’s grace,” Bhagatji replied.
[B.M. : 434]

15256.t:
Samvat 1945, Mahuvā.
Yagnapurushdāsji had established Bhagatji Mahārāj as a {!Param Ekāntik Satpurush!} based on Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 27 and incidents from his life. While doing so, he had also referenced Gadhadā III 21 and said, “In Gadhadā III 21, Mahārāj says, ‘... a thread of gold remains the same in all six seasons; it does not become limp even during the heat of summer. Similarly, when one’s Satsang is firm and one’s mind never turns away from Satsang. Only such staunch {!satsangis!} are My kith and kin; and I wish to stay in the midst of such devotees during this life.’ Therefore, think - have you heard of anyone who has been humiliated in Satsang as much as Bhagatji and yet, his mind has not turned away from the {!sādhus!} and {!satsangis!} even slightly?”
Vitthalbhāi answered, “Truly, this Vachanāmrut completely applies to Bhagatji, because I have never seen anyone nor heard of anyone who has been insulted as much as him. Based on this Vachanāmrut, Bhagatji is the {!Param Ekāntik Satpurush!}.”
[B.M. : 253]

15258.t:
9 June 1962, Mumbai. 
Explaining Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 21, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “True {!bhāgwat dharma!} is when one singularly offers devotion to Purushottam Nārāyan with chastity.
“True devotion is to remain in the company of devotees of God and take on difficulties with a smile. It is of more benefit to remain in the company of devotees as opposed to staying in the forests or in the mountain ranges. Of what spiritual benefit is it if one wanders off to the forest? If one remains within Satsang, thousands will benefit.
“How can one eradicate one’s nature of fault-finding? Even if we have to use the toilet 45 times a day, we still do not find faults within our body. Why? This is because one has developed a bond and a feeling of oneness [{!ātmabuddhi!}] for the body. If we keep such a high level of love towards the devotees of God, we are sure to not find any fault in them. If one sees faults in the {!Ekāntik Gunātit Sant!} (who is above the three {!gunas!}), Mahārāj does not accept that person's devotion, even if one were to perform {!arti!}, {!pujā!} and remain in his service.
“The {!jiva!} has many mental ‘accidents’ of finding faults, similar to what happens when a traffic accident occurs. One should not engage in Satsang in a manner that one still maintains a sense of affinity towards one’s bodily relations. We should become like a thread of gold, i.e. despite having to face the fire of insults, however big or small, one would not backtrack from the path of spirituality. Many devotees in Mahārāj’s time did not backtrack despite the level of insults they had to face.
“Mahārāj used to say, ‘This is our true kith and kin.’ A true devotee is one whose mind does not retract in this manner when facing such situations. We currently only remain steadfast because we have not had to experience difficulties just yet. One who has become like a thread of gold [that does not become limp in any season] has acted as if they are the {!ātmā!}. One can become like Brahma only through one who is already Brahma.”
[Y.M. : 3/354]

15319.t:
12 June 1962, Mumbai. 
During the early morning {!mangal!} discourses, while having Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 25 read, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “These Vachanāmruts from around this time are the final teachings. Mahārāj, just before reverting to Akshardhām, gives one of his final teachings that one should understand the glory of God and his devotees, and understand all to be divine in order to experience eternal bliss.
“One is not able to fully dedicate one's mind because even though one may have determination, it is not coupled with the glory [of God and his devotees]. One fears ‘What if he initiates us as {!sādhus!}?’ Why would a {!sādhu!} want to take everything away from you? However, one still keeps this fear within. If {!sādhus!} were to visit a particular town, one would spread the rumour that the {!sādhus!} have come to collect funds; however, there is no place for fear for someone who has offered their all to God through mind, body and wealth. Everything belongs to God [anyway].”
[Y.M. : 3/357]

15321.t:
21 January 1964, Mumbai.
In the afternoon, Yogiji Mahārāj had Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 25 read and said, “Who can be considered to be a true devotee? One who falls back [from Satsang] after experiencing miseries such as a major illness, or not having clothes to wear, right? No. A true devotee is one who never retracts, but also becomes even more staunch despite having to face any level of misery! Am I correct in saying that one would think, ‘Bāpā has written these words for someone else; these words are for the {!sādhus!} and devotees that were present during Mahārāj’s time, and we have nothing to do with this?’ No, not at all. It is the same for the {!sādhus!} and devotees of present times too.
“Even if one were to experience miseries such as contracting a major illness, or falling ill whilst others are healthy, or not having a grain of food to eat or clothes to wear, whilst other non-devotees eat, drink and make merry, such an aspirant never falters, but becomes even more staunch.”
[Y.M. : 3/584]

15474.t:
10 March 1906, Ānand.
After leaving Vartāl in 1905, Shāstriji Mahārāj celebrated the festival of Fāgan Sud Punam in March 1906 at Keshavlāl Prāgji’s home in Ānand. Some 700-800 devotees had gathered for this historic festival – the first major one to be celebrated after departing from Vartāl. The decision to build the first {!mandir!} in Bochāsan was taken and Rs. 40,000 was collected within one hour. Eventually, Shāstriji Mahārāj had to stop collecting the pledges.
On this important occasion, after the fundraising for the {!mandir!} was complete, Swāmishri had Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 26 read and gave a discourse on it.
Hearing these words, Motibhāi Bhagwāndas of Ānand decided, “I will travel with Swāmi [Shāstriji Mahārāj]. If these attributes are indeed evident in Swāmi, we should realize that he is such a great {!Sant!} [as described in the Vachanāmrut].”
[S.M. : 1/293]

15522.t:
This Vachanāmrut is dated Kārtik vad 1 of Samvat 1885. Surā Khāchar asks Shriji Mahārāj, “Even after resolutely forming the conviction of God and the {!Sant!} as they truly are, what is the reason for someone suffering a setback?”
His question stems from the following historical account:
The {!murti-pratishthā!} of the Gadhadā {!Mandir!} being readied was determined to be Kārtik sud 12, Samvat 1885. With the eyes set on this date, the effort to have the {!mandir!} ready was in full force. Jivā Khāchar kept his microscopic eyes on its construction with a poisonous look. The {!garbh-gruh!} of the {!mandir!} was ready. Jivā Khāchar sent a message to the king of Bhavnagar, Vajesinha Bāpu: “Dādā Khāchar is constructing an armory in his {!darbār!}. He will be storing gunpowder and weapons. It’s worthwhile to err on the side of caution.”
Jivā Khāchar’s message was timed appropriately because, during that time, the Khumāns had turned to plundering. Among the Khumāns, Jogidās Khumān’s raids were most widespread. If the Khumāns and Khāchars collaborated, then they would cause even more trouble. Vajesinh became frightened at this thought. He immediately sent and army of 200 Arabs to halt the construction.
Shriji Mahārāj decided to leave Gadhadā the day prior to the {!pratishthā!}; and He actually did leave Gadhadā. After Mahārāj left, the Arabs came from Bhāvnagar and saw that there were no signs of an armory being built; instead it was a {!mandir!}. They returned back to Bhāvnagar. Nityānand Swāmi performed the {!ārti!} of the {!murti-pratishthā!} the next day.
[B.S. : 5/269]
Everyone must have felt some remorse over Shriji Mahārāj having to leave Gadhadā during the {!murti-pratishthā!}, the very place He called His own. Indeed, Jivā Khāchar’s malice has crossed the limits. What degree of animosity toward Shriji Mahārāj did he possess such that he dampened the spirits of the {!murti-pratishthā!} with such false rumors? At one time in the distant past, Jivā Khāchar held Mahārāj’s hand and brought him to Gadhadā; yet, now he is acting against Mahārāj.
Such thoughts must have spun in Surā Khāchar’s mind and sprang from his tongue, “Even after resolutely forming the conviction of God and the {!Sant!} as they truly are, what is the reason for someone suffering a setback?”
Hence, this question seems to be easily connected to this incident.

15524.t: While Yogiji Mahārāj was sick, Govindsinh Chudāsamā came to visit. He requested Swāmishri to discard his illness quickly. Swāmishri laughed and said, “We cannot pray for ourself, we cannot ask Mahārāj for that. Mahārāj has said in the Vachanāmrut (Gadhadā III 28) that, no matter what hardships one may encounter, a true devotee never becomes disturbed. Even if one was placed on a {!shuli!}, one cannot pray for themselves. Therefore, you all pray.” So saying, Yogiji Mahārāj laughed a great deal.\r\n[Y.M. : 3/168]

15557.t: 1950, Atlādrā.\r\nDuring his final illness, one night Shāstriji Mahārāj became cold and felt uneasy. Shāstriji Mahārāj said, “Out of all the Vachanāmruts, Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 9 is supreme. Following that, Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 13 and then Gadhadā III 30 and Gadhadā III 38. They are equivalent to one’s life force.” \r\n[S.M. : 2/344]

15576.t:
22 July 1965, Bochāsan. 
Yogiji Mahārāj had Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 31 read during the afternoon discourses and explained, “The time that has been written herein is to ensure that we meditate [in the true sense of the word]. At that time, what understanding would the {!sādhus!} have possessed regarding God, who was visible to all? Mahārāj himself is explaining his own glory, stating that ‘I am like this!’ At that time, wouldn’t anyone have asked, ‘Mahārāj! Who are you describing? Are you describing yourself or someone else?’ 
“Thereafter, on hearing the words, ‘The form of God in [Akshar]{!dham!} and the form of God that is present on this earth is above the {!gunas!},’ Swāmishri meaningfully laughed and said, “One should not perceive human traits in him.”
[Y.M. : 4/90]

15606.t: March 1959, Advāl.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “Eradicate one’s innate natures. Vachanāmruts Gadhadā II 37 and Gadhadā III 35 both refer to eradicating one’s innate natures. Both should be perfected.” \r\n[Y.M. : 2/530]

15651.t:
Samvat 1961.
Shāstriji Mahārāj was in Chānsad trying a milk-based remedy for canker sores. Mansukhbhāi Vaidya was called to Chānsad to treat Swāmishri. One morning, Swāmishri was sitting on a mat in the south-facing room of the Mandir. Devotees from Chānsad, Bhādaran, Dabhoi, Ānand, Bil, Sokhadā, etc. were seated in front of him. Kāshibhāi of Bhādran asked Swāmishri, “What are the means to liberation?”
Shāstriji Mahārāj had Gadhadā I 54 read by him and came across Muktānand Swāmi’s question: “How is that {!Bhāgwat Dharma!} upheld? Also, how can the gateway to liberation be opened?”
Swāmishri said, “The question you asked is the same question Muktānand Swāmi asked. Mahārāj answered: {!Bhāgwat Dharma!} is upheld by maintaining profound love towards the {!Ekāntik Sant!} of God, who possesses the attributes of {!swadharma, gnān, vairāgya!}, and {!bhakti!} coupled with knowledge of God’s greatness. Maintaining profound love towards such a {!Sant!} also opens the gateway to liberation.”
Swāmishri then turned to Hāthibhāi and said, “If you do this much, the gateway of liberation will open.”
Hāthibhāi folded his hands and replied, “With this answer, Shriji Mahārāj showed us everything is included in this one solution.”
Swāmishri told Kāshibhāi to read Gadhadā I 57 next. Again, Muktānand Swāmi’s question came, “Mahārāj, what is the most extraordinary means of attaining liberation?” Mahārāj had answered: “The knowledge of Bhagwān’s form [{!swarup!}] and the knowledge of Bhagwān’s greatness [{!māhātmya!}] are the two extraordinary means to attain liberation.”
From this dialogue, Swāmishri said, “Knowledge of Bhagwān’s form and knowledge of Bhagwān’s greatness can only be learned from a {!sādhu!} who has a direct relationship with Bhagwān. Mahārāj has said in Gadhadā III 27: ‘…the attributes of the Sant - being free of lust, avarice, egotism, taste, attachment, etc. - are also described in the scriptures. The {!Sant!} who possesses these attributes has a direct relationship with Bhagwān. Therefore, one should develop the conviction of Bhagwān based on his words. In fact, to have firm faith in the words of the {!Sant!} is itself the conviction of Bhagwān.’ Moreover, Bhagwān’s greatness and knowledge of his form spreads only though the {!Sant!} who has a direct relationship with Bhagwān.”
Finally, Swāmishri had Kāshibhāi read Gadhadā III 36 and explained, “Shriji Mahārāj asked all the {!paramhansas!} and devotees, ‘What is the most extraordinary spiritual endeavour for the liberation of the {!jiva!}, which, if practised, will surely guarantee liberation and prevent all other obstacles from hindering that liberation? Also, what is the greatest obstacle in that endeavour for liberation, on account of which one would certainly fall from the path of liberation? Please answer both questions.’ No one was able to answer Mahārāj’s question, so Mahārāj said, “The most extraordinary spiritual endeavour for liberation is to understand Purushottam Bhagwān, who is seated amidst the mass of light of Brahma, as eternally having a form. Furthermore, understanding that all avatārs emanate from him, one should accept the refuge of the manifest form of Bhagwān by any means possible. One should also offer {!bhakti!} to that Bhagwān while observing {!dharma!}, as well as associate with a {!Sant!} possessing such {!bhakti!}. That is the most extraordinary spiritual endeavour for liberation. One encounters no hindrances along that path.”
[S.M. : 1/253]

15657.t:
Samvat 1945, Mahuvā.
Bhagatji Mahārāj gave his disciples unparalleled bliss and commanded them to go to the Charotar region. During this time, Bhagatji Mahārāj and Shāmjibhāi went to Gopnāth {!Mandir!} daily to give the bliss of {!darshan!} and {!kathā!}.
On the last day, Bhagatji had Gadhadā III 37 read and said, “If one currently encounters the misfortune of having to eat cheap foods, when one remembers the expensive delicacies they had previous eaten, one can still remain happy. Similarly, the talks that have been heard from the {!Satpurush!}, the happiness from the {!darshan!} and {!prasādi!} that has been obtained should be remembered when one has to remain separated from him. Learn this method of earning bliss, but never become gloom.”
[B.M. : 256]

15668.t:
1882 (Samvat 1938), Junagadh. 
A festival was to be celebrated to mark the placing of the {!kalashes!} on top of the spires of Junagadh {!Mandir!}. Āchārya Vihārilālji Mahārāj wrote to Bhagatji inviting him to come to Junagadh for this occasion.
One day, Bhagatji Māhāraj was seated where Jāgā Bhakta normally sat. There was an assembly of {!sādhus!} and devotees around him. Bhagatji read Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 37 and said, “Whoever has served the {!Satpurush!} and has perfected {!ekāntik dharma!} by his grace, spontaneously remembers the service they have done, the association they have had, as well as his divine incidents and discourses. Jāgā Bhakta and I received such bliss through Gunātitānand Swāmi. When we met today, we experienced that joy again by recollecting some incidents from Swāmi’s time. However, what is there for someone who has not experienced the bliss of God? He may be in Satsang, but he is as ignorant as an animal. On the other hand, a person may experience such happiness just once in his life and perhaps be unable to keep such contact. However, if he recollects the bliss he has already experienced, he will never be unhappy.”
[B.M. : 186]

15676.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “The knowledge of God’s divine form and the knowledge of God’s greatness are key. What is the knowledge of God’s divine form? According to Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 37, {!Akshar!} is above {!jiva!}, {!ishwar!}, the {!avatār!}, Pradhān-Purush, Prakruti and Mahā-purush; and above this Akshar is Purushottam. One should fully understand God’s divine form in this way.\r\n“Just as a cow is produced from another cow and is its form, similarly the {!Sādhu!} who has ‘met’ God is the form of God. 'Met' God means to be one with God and not necessarily physically meeting him. The {!Sādhu!} who has ‘met’ God acts according to the wishes of God. He continues the great lineage of God and ensures {!ekāntik dharma!} does not fade.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 6/10]

15709.t: 1950, Atlādrā.\r\nDuring his final illness, one night Shāstriji Mahārāj became cold and felt uneasy. Shāstriji Mahārāj said, “Out of all the Vachanāmruts, Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 9 is supreme. Following that, Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 13 and then Gadhadā III 30 and Gadhadā III 38. They are equivalent to one’s life force.” \r\n[S.M. : 2/344]

15712.t:
Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “Without knowing Mahārāj as Purushottam, it is not possible to go to Akshardhām. And without becoming {!brahmarup!}, it is not possible to stay in the service of Mahārāj.”
Then Shivlal asked a question, “How should Mahārāj be known as Purushottam? And how can one become {!brahmarup!}?” 
Then Swāmi said, “Know that Mahārāj is supreme, the source of all incarnations and the cause of all causes.” Based on this, he had Vachanāmruts Gadhadā II 9 and Gadhadā III 38 read and said, “Today in Satsang {!sādhus!}, {!acharyas!}, {!mandirs!} and {!murtis!} are all supreme. So what is there to say in Mahārāj being supreme? One should understand that he is supreme. One can become {!brahmarup!} by believing this {!Gunātit Sādhu!} to be {!brahmarup!} and associating with him through one’s mind, deeds and speech. Then one becomes {!brahmarup!}.” Based on this, he had Vachanāmrut Vartāl 11 read and said, “When one becomes like this [{!Gunātit Sādhu!}] then one stays in the service of {!Purushottam!}.”
[S.V. : 3/12]

15716.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Vachanāmruts Gadhadā II 24 and III 38 are all Vachanāmruts which contain the supreme type of spiritual knowledge.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 24/30]

15738.t: 9 January 1957, Tiruchirappalli.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj narrated Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 38 and said, “If in this way, one has understanding of Shriji Mahārāj’s {!upāsanā!} coupled with supreme firm conviction, only then will one become brahmarup.”\r\n[Y.M. : 2/198]

15770.t: 6 June 1968 (Jeth Sud 10), Gondal.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 38 is the most supreme – offering the final teachings [of Mahārāj].”\r\n[Y.M. : 5/82]

15771.t:
16 January 1971, Gondal.
A week prior to Yogiji Mahārāj passing away to Dham, in the early morning he woke up and suddenly said “Read a Vachanāmrut.” 
The attendant {!sādhu!} recited Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 39 as per the daily reading. Yogiji Mahārāj listened joyously, while doing hand gestures at important sections within the Vachanāmrut. Halfway through the Vachanāmrut, he suddenly said, “{!Iti Vachanāmrutam!}” and went back to sleep. Thereafter, no opportunity came about for him to listen to any other Vachanāmrut before he passed away to Dhām. Therefore this is Yogiji Mahārāj’s sanctified Vachanāmrut. Throughout his entire life, he had narrated and discoursed on many Vachanāmruts giving divine joy to all, but this was to be his very last. 
[Y.M. : 6/539]

15772.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi says, “The {!ātmā!} is extremely luminous. Believing it to be separate from the gross, subtle and causal bodies, contemplate that ‘I am {!ātmā!} and this manifest Purushottam {!Bhagwān!} is ever present in me.’ And all these talks are stated in the ‘{!Vishalyakarani!} Herbal Medicine’ Vachanāmrut [Gadhadā III 39]. Such talks are, to some extent, in all the Vachanāmruts and may be absent in some. The contemplation of the {!ātmā!} in the mind should continue, ‘I am {!ātmā!}, I am Akshar.’ And if this is continually done, one attains the state of Akshar.”\r\n[S.V. : 6/22]

15773.t: Yogiji Maharaj said, “This {!jiva!} harbours worldly desires until its final moments. One should forsake these desires and desire only the divine abode. What does it mean to desire only the divine abode? One should constantly keep the wish to attain Akshardham and not retain any wishes to stay in this world. In addition, remain aware of {!ātmā!} and Paramātmā. According to Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 39, one should should be passionate of these two in such a way that one transforms internally; however, such passion can only arise from staying in the company of the {!Satpurush!} and understanding the glory [of God].”\r\n[Yogi Vani: 6/13]

15774.t: After having Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 39 recited, Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “What is mentioned in this Vachanāmrut should also be understood.”\r\n[S.V. : 5/303]

16501.t: Yogiji Mahārāj said, “In the Ashlāli Vachanāmrut, Mahārāj points out a flaw in the understanding of deities such as Prajāpati, etc. What was the flawed understanding held by deities such as Shiv, Brahmā, etc.? They regarded other incarnations and Mahārāj as the same; everything as the same. However, when Mahārāj manifested on this earth, all were able to understand the true principle and so did not rely on any other deities. They had no notion of conviction in any other deity as they had found the manifest form of Shri Hari. One who develops the conviction that they have attained Purushottam, achieves liberation in this very birth. As a consequence, one will not need to tolerate any further by taking any more births.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni: 23/23]

16510.t:
Samvat 2003, Sārangpur.
Shāstriji Mahārāj was speaking to a group of sādhus when Sanātandās Swāmi asked, “In Jetalpur 1, it is mentioned: ‘{!āpopu karvu’!}. How does one do that?”
Swāmishri stood up from where he was sitting and sat in Sanātandās Swāmi’s lap and said, “Forget your body and believe yourself to be the form that is sitting in your lap.” In this way, Shāstriji Mahārāj gave everyone an unforgettable memory while explaining the meaning.
[S.M. : 2/203]

16528.t:
August 1959, Mumbai.
Yogiji Mahārāj once said, “How can one define the knowledge of {!ātmā!} and Paramātmā? One can be said to be a true {!satsangi!} only if one has understood the knowledge of both {!ātmā!} and Paramātmā according to Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 39. One who has reinforced their status as a {!satsangi!} in this manner will never fall back. Such a {!satsangi!} never depends on his body; rather one remains dependent only on God. If one becomes worthy of receiving such knowledge, the great {!Purush!} would give one that knowledge and help one to attain that state of understanding.
“There are four types of {!aushadhi!} [herbal medicines]: {!sandhini, varnaharni, vishalyakarni!} and {!sanjivani!}. Their four forms: {!dharma, gnān, vairāgya!} and {!bhakti!}. The four Vachanāmruts relating to these are Gadhadā II 28, Loyā 7, Gadhadā III 39 and Gadhadā II 10 respectively; these four Vachanāmruts should be perfected.”
[Y.M. : 2/600]

17793.t: Once, {!Brahmaswarup!} Pramukh Swāmi Mahārāj was in the village of Ranu. Situated in the village is a shrine dedicated to Tuljā Mātā, where Nilkanth Varni had halted for one night during his travels. When Swāmishri proceeded there for {!darshan!}, the {!mahant!} of that {!mandir!} showed Swāmishri a quilt that had been sanctified by Nilkanth Varni. Thereafter, he offered the Hindi version of the Vachanāmrut that he owned to Swāmishri and requested, “Please kindly write your blessings in this Vachanāmrut and write which is your favourite Vachanāmrut.” Swāmishri wrote, ‘Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 7, Gadhadā III 11 and Vartāl 20.”
