18432.t:
August 1958, Surat.
Yogiji Mahārāj asked, “One is absorbed into {!Brahma!} and then emerges out again. What does this mean?”
He explained himself, “If conviction of {!divyabhāv!} in the {!Motāpurush!} is lacking, one keeps perceiving positive traits and flaws [in the {!Motāpurush!}]. Therefore, whenever {!satvagun!} is predominant and one perceives positive traits in the {!Motāpurush!}, then one acts according to his wishes. One doesn’t have affections towards oneself [and thus is associated with {!Brahma!}]. However, when {!rajogun!} and {!tamogun!} are predominant, then one perceives flaws in the {!Motāpurush!}. Such a person is said to have retracted from {!Brahma!}. In this way, if one’s awareness is firm, inappropriate thoughts ({!avgun!}) stop arising. Conviction of the {!Motāpurush’s!} form and {!divyabhāv!} in him becomes permanent and resolute.”
[Y.M. : 2/417]

19411.t: January 1964, Mumbai. \r\nDuring the month of January 1964, Yogiji Mahārāj was staying at Akshar Bhuvan in Dadar, Mumbai. One day during the morning {!maṅgaḷ!} discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj related a memorable incident [some {!smruti!}] related to Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 18 by saying, “Aksharpurush Swāmi often used to have this Vachanāmrut read. He would discourse on it for three hours. Once in Piplav, Swāmi Shāstriji Mahārāj was seated and said, “Read a Vachanāmrut.” This Vachanāmrut was read and it was not completed until 12.30am at night. I was also there. We enjoyed it so much.”\r\n[Y.M. : 3/569]

19483.t:
15 August 1965, Mumbai. 
At 7:30am whilst explaining Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 5, ‘One should meditate on Krishna together with Rādhikāji,’ during the morning discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Mahārāj has shown us the moon above the house. One who fails to understand this affixes one’s gaze to the house and not to the moon. The moon is in the sky. Similarly, meditating upon Purushottam along with Akshar is like this [the moon]. Meditating upon Krishna along with Radha is the example that has been given [the house]. This explanation refers to the {!upāsanā!} of God along with his {!Bhakta!} [choicest devotee].”
Someone asked, “Why did Mahārāj explain it like this [using Radha and Krishna]?” 
Swāmishri replied, “If at that time, people hesitated to say Mahārāj’s name [speak openly of his glory], then how could they have possibly been able to say the name of Akshar-Purushottam? Mahārāj explained this principle gradually. At first, in Gadhadā I 1, he spoke about meditating on himself [Mahārāj]. In Gadhadā I 3, he spoke of remembering the divine actions and incidents of God [Mahārāj]. He also spoke about remembering all devotees, sādhus and {!brahmachāris!}. In Gadhadā I 5 he speaks of meditating upon God [{!Purushottam!}] along with his choicest devotee [{!Akshar!}]. Therefore, in this way he gradually explained this principle to all.
“Some worship only Mahārāj and nobody else. In Gadhadā I 71, Mahārāj has explained the principle of Akshar-Purushottam and instructed everyone to speak about it to others, but nobody does this. Shāstriji Mahārāj left [Vartāl] and explained this principle [Akshar-Purushottam] to everyone. If this principle is understood, then everything has been understood.”
[Y.M. : 4/100]

19509.t: 20 January 1964, Mumbai. \r\nExplaining Vachanāmrut Loyā 10 at 8:20am, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “This Vachanāmrut relates to the divine knowledge that gives bliss. If one perfects it, then one will experience much happiness.”\r\n[Y.M. : 3/580]

19510.t: 1894 (Samvat 1950), Vansda.\r\nBhagatji Mahārāj asked for Vachanāmrut Loyā 10 to be read and asked the Diwānji to repeat the following five to seven times, “I have attained this {!gnān!} of the pure {!ātmā!}, which transcends {!māyā!}, by the grace of the {!Sant!}. That {!Sant!} is a devotee of God. Moreover, that God is the {!ātmā!} of even Brahma, who is the {!ātmā!} of all. He is the {!ātmā!} of Akshar and is also the {!ātmā!} of the countless millions of {!muktas!}. I am the {!brahmarup!} servant of that Parabrahma Purushottam Nārāyan.’ Bhagatji made him memorize this by repeating it and said, “If you perfect this Vachanāmrut, then you will reach the pinnacle of knowledge.” \r\n[B.M. : 440]

19511.t: 1888 (Shrāvan, Samvat 1944), Petlad.\r\nBhagatji Mahārāj asked for Vachanāmrut Loyā 10 to be read and said, “In this Vachanāmrut, Shriji Mahārāj has spoken about the divine knowledge that gives bliss. This is the knowledge of Ātma-Paramātmā. Those who perfect this knowledge attain bliss. There are two distinct types of knowledge mentioned here. Firstly, the theory of {!sankhya!} is mentioned and later the theory of {!sankhya!} and {!yoga!}.”\r\n[B.M. : 277]

19512.t: 27 May 1959, Rajkot.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “What is 16 annī [100%] Satsang? It is the perfection of Vachanāmrut Loyā 12.” \r\n[Y.M. : 2/560]

19513.t: Explaining Vachanāmrut Loyā 12, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “Countless millions of {!brahmānds!}, each encircled by the eight barriers appear like mere atoms before Akshar. Such is the greatness of Akshar, the abode of Purushottam Nārāyan. One who worships Purushottam realising oneself to be {!aksharrup!} can be said to possess the highest level of ‘{!nirvikalp!} faith’… I want to make you all like that.” Then, he pulled each {!yuvak’s!} hand one by one and repeated, “I want to make you {!aksharrup!} like that.”\r\n[Yogi Vāni : 29/5]

19515.t:
7 June 1965, Vadodara. 
Yogiji Mahārāj instructed the {!sādhus!} leaving for Mumbai to memorise Vachanāmrut Loyā 17 by heart before saying, “I will test you. Also teach the young {!parshads!}. Three things must be achieved: 
1. Perfect {!ekāntik dharma!}. 
2. Attain the Brahmic state. 
3. Be indifferent to the body.” 
[Y.M. : 4/77]

19517.t: After having Vachanāmrut Loyā 17 (Reverence and Condemnation) read, Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “When these talks are imbibed within, then just as one sees one’s clear reflection in the mirror, one’s behaviour is also transparent.” \r\n[Aksharāmrut : 6/33]

19530.t: March 1959, Advāl.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “Eradicate one’s innate natures. Vachanāmruts Gadhadā II 37 and Gadhadā III 35 both refer to eradicating one’s innate natures. Both should be perfected.” \r\n[Y.M. : 2/530]

19549.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi had Vachanāmrut Vartāl 11 read and said, “When one becomes like this [Gunātit Sādhu], one can stay in the service of Purushottam.”\r\n[S.V. : 3/12]

19550.t: 12 March 1966, Mumbai. \r\nExplaining the meaning of Vachanāmrut Vartāl 11 during the discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj mentioned, “We are currently understanding the Vachanāmrut through which one can attain the state of {!brahmarup!}.”\r\n[Y.M. : 4/228]

19554.t:
Samvat 1953, Junagadh.
Shāstriji Mahārāj once asked Bhagatji Mahārāj, “The {!darshan!} of a {!Brahmaswarup Sant!} is equivalent to the {!darshan!} of Bhagwān – such is stated in the Vachanāmrut many times; therefore, why is it necessary to achieve a state of {!ātmā!}-realization and experience Bhagwān in one’s heart if one has attained the {!darshan!} of a {!Brahmaswarup Sant!}?”
Hearing this question, Bhagatji simply gave Shāstriji Mahārāj a compassionate look for a few minutes. He then said, “Sādhurām, the external {!darshan!} of the {!Sant!} is the fruit of one’s spiritual endeavours from countless births. However, to experience that [external] {!murti!} into one’s heart constantly is an elevated state. Shriji Mahārāj had told the senior {!sādhu-muktas!}, ‘When the inclination of the {!indriyas!} and {!antahkaran!} constantly remains withdrawn in one’s heart, one sees Bhagwān’s {!murti!} within the radiant light.’ In this way, when the inclination of the {!indriyas!} are retracted and remain focused on Bhagwān’s {!murti!}, that should be known as having achieved an elevated state.
“Shriji Mahārāj has explained in Vachanāmrut [Gadhadā II 13], ‘In fact, you also see this form of Bhagwān, but you do not fully comprehend it.’ So do not think that, since you have seen the [external] form, you have understood it thoroughly. When you see that form completely in your heart, the tendency of the {!indriyas!} to remain on external objects will terminate and instead will remain constantly within. That is known as the state of {!sākshātkār!}. Muktānand Swāmi wrote: ‘{!Brahma thai Parabrahmane jue te jāne re’!} – One who sees Parabrahma having identified one’s form as Brahma knows Parabrahma.
“In this way, one who sees the [external] manifest form of Bhagwān [internally] within one’s heart knows Bhagwān thoroughly. Therefore, either in this very physical body or after one leaves the physical body, the only option is to achieve this state. Krupānand Swāmi, Swarupānand Swāmi, and Nityānand Swāmi, etc. had achieved that state.”
Then, Bhagatji Mahārāj added, “Among those who debate over scriptures or the pundits who study them, only a few can understand this. Others have no understanding in this matter. Therefore, for us, we should follow the path of the great. Having faith in the words of the Motā-Purush is the greatest means to achieving {!sākshātkār!}.” Bhagatji Mahārāj left for his residence after answering Shāstriji Mahārāj’s question.
[S.M. : 1/186]

19568.t: 13 November 1970, Gondal.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “‘Remaining Eternally Happy’ – Shāstriji Mahārāj used to have this Vachanāmrut read quite often. After hearing this, remember it and imbibe it into your lives.”\r\n[Y.M. : 6/481]

19591.t: 14 January 1957, Reniguntā.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “Vachanāmrut Gadhadā I 76 refers to renouncing obstinacy, egotism and jealousy and also tolerating hardships; Gadhadā II 22 refers to our aim. These two Vachanāmruts should be perfected.” \r\n[Y.M. : 2/194]

19592.t: 1950, Atlādrā.\r\nDuring his final illness, one night Shāstriji Mahārāj became cold and felt uneasy. Shāstriji Mahārāj said, “Out of all the Vachanāmruts, Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 9 is supreme. Following that, Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 13 and then Gadhadā III 30 and Gadhadā III 38. They are equivalent to one’s life force.” \r\n[S.M. : 2/344]

19596.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “Mahārāj told Gopālānand Swāmi in his dream, ‘If you do not spread the knowledge that I am Purushottam [i.e. that he is distinct from the other {!avatārs!} and is {!sarvopari!}], then I will keep you in the current body for one thousand years.’” Then Swāmi said, “Mahārāj had also told me [that he is {!sarvopari!}], I realized it from [reading] Mahārāj’s old documents, and knew it even before that. When I openly spoke in {!sabhā!}, the {!sādhus!} questioned, ‘Who told you this?’ I replied, “Swāminārāyan told me. Who else will tell me?’ Mahārāj has said this in Gadhadā II-9, Gadhadā III-38, Gadhadā II-13, Loyā-14, etc.”\r\n[S.V. : 6/32]

19597.t: Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “Mahārāj told Gopālānand Swāmi in his dream, ‘If you do not spread the knowledge that I am Purushottam [i.e. that he is distinct from the other {!avatārs!} and is {!sarvopari!}], then I will keep you in your current body for one thousand years.’” Then Swāmi said, “Mahārāj had also told me [that he is {!sarvopari!}]; I realized it from [reading] Mahārāj’s old documents, and knew it even before that. When I openly spoke in {!sabhā!}, the {!sādhus!} questioned, ‘Who told you this?’ I replied, ‘Swāminārāyan told me. 19628.t:
In Samvat 1919, Gunātitānand Swāmi started his journey toward Vartāl for the {!samaiyo!} of Chaitra sud 15 [{!Punam!}]. He stayed one day in Gondal and then arrived in Goghāvadar, a village nearby. He stayed at the Shiv Mandir on the river bank. While resting in the afternoon, he had Jāgā Bhakta read the Vachanāmrut. Jāgā Bhakta read five Vachanāmruts: Gadhadā I-23, Gadhadā II-30 and 45, Amdāvād 2 and 3. Hearing these Vachanāmruts, Swāmi sat up and said, “It is as if I had never heard these Vachanāmruts.” He said, “Read them again.” Jāgā Swāmi read them again.
Then Swāmi said, “Listening to these Vachanāmruts, I have concluded that even after millions of years, without behaving in this way, there is no final release. So, for us, there is no alternative but to do this. Also, even if one is an {!āchārya!}, a son of Bhagwān, an {!ishwar!}, or some small or big deity, still there is no release without behaving in that way. Since, that is Mahārāj’s belief.” Based on this, Swāmi recited some couplets quoted by Mahārāj: ‘{!Nijātmānam brahmarupam…’!}, ‘{!Brahmabhutah prasannātmā…’!}, ‘{!Parinishthitopi nairgunye…’!}, ‘{!Atmāramāshcha munayo’!}.
After reciting many such couplets, he said, “When one becomes like this, then Bhagwān resides in one’s heart.” Then, looking at a devotee, he said, “You do have a {!murti!}, but without a {!mandir!} where will you install it? So, if you want to install Bhagwān, then learn to prepare a {!mandir!} as described here, then Bhagwān will stay.”
Then he continued, “When the {!sādhus!} went to get the {!murtis!} for this mandir [Junagadh], the sculptor asked, ‘What type of {!murtis!} shall I make for you?’ Then the sādhus said, ‘Make them according to these designs.’ Then the sculptor said, ‘These {!murtis!} are suitable only for a mandir worth hundreds of thousands of rupees.’ Then the sādhus said, ‘We’ve come to take {!murtis!} in accordance with such a mandir.’ So the sculptor said, ‘Then I’ll make them.’ Then the sculptor sculpted the {!murtis!}. Similarly, without becoming {!brahmarup!} where will we install Purushottam? So, if you want to install Purushottam, you have to become {!brahmarup!}.” Having said this, he got up. Then he held a devotee’s wrist and while walking told him, “Beware, never have any [worldly] desires.” Then that devotee’s desires stopped. And Swāmi said, “If one can remain like this all the time, doubts, strong attachments to one’s karma, desires, affection for worldly relations, body-consciousness, etc. and countless other strong material bonds are destroyed and one can continually stay focused on Bhagwān.”
[S.V. : 3/13]

19629.t:
March 1863, Ghoghāvadar.
In Ghoghāvadar, Jāgā Bhakta read five Vachanāmruts, namely: Gadhadā I 23, Gadhadā II 30, Gadhadā II 45, Amdāvād 2 and Amdāvād 3. 
Extremely pleased with his selection of Vachanāmruts, Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “Oh, ho! It’s like I had never heard these Vachanāmruts. Please read them again.” Jāgā Bhakta read them again. 
Gunātitānand Swāmi then said, “Listening to these Vachanāmruts, it is clear that without imbibing these principles in our lives, no liberation is possible in infinite years. This is true not only for us, but one may be an {!āchārya!}, or the son of God, or an {!ishwar!}, or some minor or major god, but liberation is impossible without imbibing these principles. Why? Because this is also Mahārāj’s principle.” 
[S.V. : 3/13]

19655.t:
“Dādā, have you heard? Jivā Khāchar is playing his last card. He wants to seize your land and raise his flag over your {!darbār!} and make you all wander aimlessly...
“Muktānand Swāmi, Bāpu Jivā Khāchar has gathered and army of 2,000 for a big battle. He has requested an army of Arabs from Bhāvnagar for an attack tomorrow and may even take control of Dādā Khāchar’s share of villages.”
As Mahārāj was speaking, Meghji and Hasan arrived short of breath and burst out, “Mahārāj, calamity has struck. Our whole crop of sugarcane has been burned in Lakshmivādi. Everything is raging in flames.” 
Somlā Khāchar, seeing signs of an imminent battle, added, “Mahārāj, the Kāthis and Arabs are face-to-face in the courtyard of the {!darbār’s!} fort ready to clash. Please give us orders.”
Shriji Mahārāj gave His {!āgnā!}, “Somlā, you all have my blessings. With your swinging swords on the battlefield, the enemies’ heads will separate and fall like rain drops. Even if 100 or 200 heads are severed, as long as Dādā Khāchar [and his land] is protected, that is still not enough.”
(With Shriji Mahārāj’s {!āgnā!}, the Kāthis, {!pārshads!}, and few sādhus took up weapons to face the Arabs armed with rifles. The Arabs’ rifles failed to fire, allowing Kāthis to overcome the Arab army, which eventually fled. Hence, Mahārāj protected Dādā Khāchar and everyone who fought for him with loyalty.) 
[B.S. : 4/194-96]
The above incident is the background to Shriji Mahārāj words in this Vachanāmrut: “… everyone must have realised the state of their own {!antahkarans!} during the minor difficulty that recently befell Dādā Khāchar.” Dādā Khāchar’s uncle Jivā Khāchar had plotted to embezzle his land. To protect Dādā Khāchar, Shriji Mahārāj Himself had exposed this as a mere ploy by Jivā Khāchar. However, when these tactics were being played by Jivā Khāchar, many {!satsangi!} minds turned like ferris-wheels: “How can this happen in Satsang?” To ease their minds, Mahārāj Himself spoke: “The extent of one’s {!vairāgya!} and one’s understanding can be measured only when one encounters {!vishays!}, or in times of some hardship, but not otherwise. That being so, what can be said about situations of extreme prosperity or hardship? For example, everyone must have realised the state of their own {!antahkarans!} during the {!minor difficulty!} that recently befell Dādā Khāchar.”
The basis for Gadhadā I 74 seems to be the calamity that struck Dādā Khāchar. It should be noted that an army of 2,000 had reached Dādā Khāchar’s {!darbār!}; yet Mahārāj says, “… {!minor difficulty!} that befell Dādā Khāchar.” We learn from these words how firm the understanding that God is the all-doer is in His life.

19656.t:
On 25 January 1974, Pramukh Swāmi Mahārāj embarked on his first trip abroad in the morning from Mumbai. At exactly 10:15am, the Air India airplane “Gauri-Shankar” took off and disappeared in the sky. The airplane landed in Nairobi where many devotees gathered to receive Swāmishri with garlands. Swāmishri and the accompanying sādhus had not even disembark when an announcement was made: “Pramukh Swāmi will return back to India. The rest can deboard.” Hearing the announcement, Swāmishri’s facial expression did not change one bit. He simply said, “If that is Bhagwān’s will.” However, how could the other {!sādhus!} get off the plane without Swāmishri?
A few minutes later, another announcement was made: “Pramukh Swāmi and his party should all return to India.” Laughingly Swāmishri said, “This is Mahārāj’s wish.” All the other {!sādhus!} were astonished. Disappointed, they all sat back in their seats and were silent. Only Swāmishri was equipoised. Kothāri Swāmi [Bhaktipriya Swāmi], tasked with keeping the journal of the trip, asked Swāmishri to write something in his diary. Swāmishri wrote: “Whatever happens is according to Mahārāj and Bapa’s [Yogi Bapa’s] wish. Therefore, remain joyful. Never feel sorrowful. Offer {!bhakti!} to Mahārāj believing one’s self as Akshar – this way, no misery will be experienced.”
After returning to Mumbai, in the morning of the next day, Swāmishri explained Gadhadā I 74: “We should believe [Mahārāj] as {!kartā!} and {!hartā!}. We believe Him to be {!kartā!} [creative powers or power of giving] but have difficulty accepting His power of {!hartā!} [destructive powers or power of taking away]. When incidents like these arise, we question why He allowed the incident to happen. Why did He do it? But when everything happens according to His will, why should we experience grief? We should feel happy in every way. Whatever happens is for our own benefit… no matter what happens [even if it seems contrary]. We should understand that it is Mahārāj’s will and be glad… Perhaps after entering Nairobi, we were going to be hassled. Rather, it is better we came back alive and well. We are back alive and well and we are happy! If they [Nairobi officials] have to say something, they’ll say it; but what can they take from us? We should remain worry free and experience bliss… Others may talk big about their knowledge but when incidents like this happen, we realize their actual state.” 
In explaining this Vachanāmrut, Swāmishri solidified everyone’s understand of Bhagwān’s will. Everyone became elated with the bliss of listening to Swāmishri and forgot the turmoil they experience for having to return from Nairobi.
[Parabhakti : 90]

19703.t:
#1.)Continuously engaging one’s mind on the form of God:
##1.1)There is no spiritual endeavour more difficult than this.
##1.2)The scriptures state that there is no greater attainment than this.
#2.)By keeping one’s mind on the form of God, which is like a {!chintāmani!}:
##2.1)If he so wishes, he can see the forms of {!jiva, ishwar, māyā!} and Brahma.
##2.2)He can also see Vaikunth, Golok, Brahmamahol and the other abodes of God.
#3.){!Māyā!} is anything that obstructs a devotee of God while meditating on God’s form.
#4.)A devotee who has refuge in God goes to the abode of God and attains a body composed of Brahma.
#5.)One does not develop profound love for the Satsang fellowship if one bears an aversion towards the {!Sant!}.

19704.t:
#1.)Characteristics of one with the highest level of {!vairāgya!}:
##1.1)He is not affected by engaging in worldly activities like King Janak.
##1.2)He indulges in the most alluring of the {!panchvishays!} dejectedly and with total indifference towards them.
##1.3)His renunciation remains undiminished.
##1.4)He invariably views the {!vishays!} as flawed and treats them like enemies.
##1.5)He constantly remains in contact with the {!Sant!} and the sacred scriptures, and remains in the service of God.
##1.6)Even if he were to encounter adverse circumstances (eight factors of influence: places, times, company, etc.), his understanding would not diminish.
#2.)Characteristics of one with an intermediate level of {!vairāgya!}:
##2.1)He indulges in the best of the {!panchvishays!} but remains unattracted to them.
##2.2)If he were to encounter adverse circumstances:
###i.)He would become attached to those {!vishays!}.
###ii.)His level of {!vairāgya!} would diminish.
#3.)Characteristics of one with the lowest level of {!vairāgya!}: if he were to encounter ordinary or inferior {!vishays!}, he may indulge in them, but he would not become bound by them. However, if he were to encounter and indulge in appealing {!vishays!}, he would become bound by them.

19705.t:
#1.)Even one who can constantly see the form of God in his heart should recall the divine actions and incidents of God.
#2.)He should also maintain affection for the {!sādhus!} and {!satsangis!}, and should remember them.
#3.)Benefits of remembering the divine actions and incidents of God:
##3.1)If one forgets God’s form, then by remembering the divine actions and incidents performed by Him, then by that association, God’s form will also be remembered.
##3.2)Even if a sinner remembers these occasions at the time of his death, he will also attain the abode of God.

19706.t:
#1.)Devotees of God should not harbour jealousy amongst themselves.
#2.)If one is to harbour jealousy, one should imbibe the virtues of the person towards whom one is jealous, and should also abandon one’s own faults.
#3.)Nāradji harboured jealousy toward Tumbaru, so he went to Tumbaru to learn his virtues from him, and consequently God became please with him.
#4.)A devotee of God should totally abandon any form of jealousy that would result in harming another devotee of God.

19707.t:
#1.)One should meditate on God along with his ideal devotee
#2.)Even if one cannot behold the form of God within one’s heart, one should not lose faith and stop the meditation.
#3.)By persisting in meditation in this manner:
##3.1)One earns the immense grace of God.
##3.2)God is bound by their {!bhakti!}.

19708.t:
#1.)One who is wise ({!viveki!}):
##1.1)Finds flaws within himself and perceives virtues in God and His devotees.
##1.2)When God and His {!Sant!} utter harsh words of advice for his own benefit, he accepts them as beneficial.
##1.3)Steadily attains greatness in Satsang.
#2.)One who is not wise ({!aviveki!}):
##2.1)Perceives virtues within himself.
##2.2)When God and His {!Sant!} highlight his flaws and advise him, he perceives flaws in them due to his arrogance.
##2.3)Steadily declines and loses his reputation in Satsang.
#3.)When one renounces the vanity of his own virtues, becomes brave, and keeps faith in God and His {!Sant!}, then his ignorance is eradicated.

19709.t:
#1.){!Jiva!} and {!ishwar!}: their {!anvay!} form is when they are united with their three bodies and their {!vyatirek!} form is when they are distinct from their three bodies.
#2.)Brahma: {!anvay!} form is when Brahma pervades {!māyā!} and the entities evolved from {!māyā!} - the countless millions of {!brahmānds!}. Its {!vyatirek!} form is when Brahma is distinct from {!jivas, ishwars!}, and {!māyā!}.
#3.)Parabrahma: {!anvay!} form of God is as the controller of Aksharbrahma, the {!ishwars!}, the {!jivas, māyā!}. His {!vyatirek!} form is when He is distinct from these in His abode.
#4.)These five entities - Parabrahma, Aksharbrahma, {!māyā!}, the {!ishwars!} and the {!jivas!} - are eternal.

19710.t:
#1.)If the {!vruttis!} of the {!indriyas!} are engaged in the service of God and His Sant, then:
##1.1)The {!antahkaran!} is purified.
##1.2)Sins committed since time immemorial are destroyed.
#2.)If the {!vruttis!} of the {!indriyas!} are directed towards women and other {!vishays!}, then:
##2.1)The {!antahkaran!} becomes polluted.
##2.2)One falls from the path of liberation.
#3.)One should indulge in the {!vishays!} only as prescribed in the scriptures.
#4.)By keeping association with the {!Sant!} and shunning bad company:
##4.1)The sense of I-ness towards one’s body is eradicated.
##4.2)The sense of my-ness towards one’s bodily relations is eradicated.
##4.3)One develops profound love for God.
##4.4)One develops {!vairāgya!} toward everything except God.

19711.t: #1.)Even if a person has developed a conviction of the manifest form of God and offers {!bhakti!} to Him, but if he still does not consider himself fulfilled until he has seen the radiant form of God in His abode, then talks about God should not be heard from this person.\r\n#2.)If a person has firm faith in the manifest form of God and believes himself to be fulfilled merely by His {!darshan!}, then God Himself forcefully shows him His divine powers and forms in His abodes.

19712.t:
#1.)How Mahārāj served Sevākrām:
##1.1)Prepared a bed of banana leaves one-and-a-half feet high under a banyan tree.
##1.2)Sevākrām was suffering from dysentery, therefore Mahārāj washed him, brought ingredients, cooked, and fed him; but Mahārāj ate the food he got from begging. Some days Mahārāj fasted but Sevākrām never gave him food to eat.
##1.3)Mahārāj served Sevākrām until he recovered fully yet he would still make Mahārāj carry his belongings weighing 20 kg while he walked empty-handed.
#2.)Ungrateful:
##2.1)Is one who does not appreciate favours done by others.
##2.2)If a person has atoned for a sin as according to the scriptures, then whoever still considers him a sinner should himself be known as a sinner just like an ungrateful person.

19713.t: #1.){!Vāsanā!}: A desire within the {!antahkaran!} to enjoy {!vishays!} that have been previously seen, heard or indulged in.\r\n#2.){!Ekāntik Bhakta!}: A person who has no {!vāsanā!} except that of God and who offers bhakti to God realising himself to be {!brahmarup!}.

19714.t:
#1.)By understanding the nature of Purush, Prakruti, {!kāl!}; the 24 elements (including {!mahattattva!}, etc.), one is released from the bondage of one’s inherent {!avidyā!} ({!māyā!}, ignorance).
#2.)Four types of dissolution ({!pralays!}):
##2.1){!Nitya-pralay!}: The day-to-day death of the bodies of all living beings.
##2.2){!Nimitta-pralay!}: Destruction of the lower 10 realms of one {!brahmānd!}.
##2.3){!Prākrut-pralay!}: Destruction of Virāt Purush in the form of a {!brahmānd!}.
##2.4){!Ātyantik-pralay!}: Absorption of the countless {!brahmānds!}, which evolved from Prakruti, in the light of Brahma.
#3.)By knowing the process of the creation, sustenance and dissolution of the various realms:
##3.1)One develops {!vairāgya!} towards the world.
##3.2)One develops {!bhakti!} towards God.
##3.3)One attains the abode of God.
#4.)The abode of God is without a beginning and without an end ({!sanātan!}); divine, infinite and indivisible; characterised by eternal existence, consciousness and bliss.

19715.t: #1.)Question: When the branches of banyan, pipal or other trees are cut and planted elsewhere, the same type of tree grows there. Has that one {!jiva!}, which is whole and indivisible, been dissected into two, or has another {!jiva!} entered the new tree?\n#2.)Answer: God, in His {!antaryāmi!} form, resides in each {!jiva!} and grants birth to a {!jiva!}, through an appropriate body of another {!jiva!}, according to the relation of the {!karmas!} between the two {!jivas!}.

19716.t:
#1.)A true renunciant is one who, after renouncing worldly life, has no attachment to it.
#2.)A householder who is disinterested in worldly life is better than a renunciant who has desires for worldly life if:
##2.1)The householder observes all of the {!dharmas!} prescribed for a householder.
##2.2)He understands that the profound association of the {!Sant!} that he has attained is like a magnificent {!chintāmani!} and a {!kalpavruksh!}.
##2.3)He understands that his wealth, property, sons and daughters are all merely like a dream.
##2.4)He remains undeterred amidst any type of adversity that may come his way.
#3.)One who has attained the manifest form of God, even if he suffers an untimely death, will be liberated; whereas, a sinner may die while walking and talking but he will not be liberated.
#4.)‘Ante yā matihi sā gatihi |’ means “The outcome at the time of death is determined by the present state of the mind.”
#5.)A servant of God will certainly be liberated but those who have the {!darshan!} of him will also be liberated.
#6.)The characteristics of one who is a servant of God:
##6.1)He believes that the physical body is {!asatya!} (false) and the {!ātmā!} is {!satya!} (permanent, eternal).
##6.2)He harbours no desires to indulge in the objects that are intended for his Master.
##6.3)He never behaves contrary to the wishes of his Master.

19717.t:
#1.)A person whose heart is filled with {!bhakti!}:
##1.1)He has courage such that he feels, ‘I want to act only according to God’s and His {!Sant’s!} commands.’ 
##1.2)Even by mistake He never mistakenly believes or says: I will only be able to obey certain commands but not others.
#2.)One who behaves in the following manner is called an {!Ekāntik Bhakta!}:
##2.1)When meditating on the {!murti!} of Bhagwān daily, he does so with renewed faith and courage.
##2.2)He does not become discouraged (while meditating), even if it takes 100 years to behold the form of God.
##2.3)While trying to behold God’s form, if disturbing thoughts arise which cannot be supressed, then in that situation:
###i.)He understands the immense glory of God.
###ii.)He believes himself to be completely fulfilled.
###iii.)He falsifies his disturbing thoughts.
###iv.)He does not give up meditating on the form of God.

19718.t:
#1.)A wise devotee who can discern between {!sat!} (that which is imperishable, permanent) and {!asat!} (that which is perishable and not permanent) has the following characteristics:
##1.1)Recognizes his flaws and thoughtfully eradicates them.
##1.2)If he perceives flaws in a Sant or {!satsangis!}, he rejects them and only imbibes their virtues.
##1.3)He never sees flaws in God.
##1.4)He accepts whatever words of advice God and the Sant offer as the highest truth.
##1.5)He behaves as the {!ātmā!} - distinct from them all (mind, body, {!indriyas!} and {!prāns!}) - but never follows the instincts of his own mind.
##1.6)He identifies the objects and evil company that may cause bondage or raise deficiencies in his {!ekāntik!} {!dharma!} and shuns them; but he does not become bound by them.
##1.7)He imbibes positive thoughts and avoids negative thoughts.

19719.t:
#1.)One who talks discouragingly in this manner (described below) is called {!kusang!} (negative influence) in Satsang:
##1.1)“Who can follow God’s commands thoroughly? Who can possibly observe the religious vows perfectly?”
##1.2)“God is the redeemer of even the wicked, and so Even if we do not follow his commands he will grant liberation to us as well.”
##1.3)“Attempting to behold God’s form in the heart is not possible by one’s own efforts. It is only beheld by those whom God helps out of compassion.”
#2.)This type of {!kusang!} discourages others from practicing the spiritual endeavours for pleasing God.
#3.)To remove {!kusang!} from Satsang, Shriji Mahārāj has commanded:
##3.1)No one should utter such discouraging words; instead always speak courageously.
##3.2)On days when one speaks such discouraging words, one should observe a fast.

19720.t:
#1.)Without {!vartan!} (as described by Shriji Mahārāj in this Vachanāmrut), even by listening to, or studying and understanding the meanings of the four Vedas, six Shāstras, 18 Purāns, and the Mahābhārat and other Itihās scriptures, one cannot become a {!mukta!}.
#2.)The disturbance that a {!bhakta!} of God experiences in his heart is due to complacency of the {!antahkaran!} and the impure indulgences ({!vishays!}) of the {!indriyas!}.
#3.)Shriji Mahārāj is pleased with one who understands the following and acts accordingly; and he becomes a {!mukta!} and will reach Akshardhām:
##3.1)If the indulgences of the five {!indriyas!} are impure, then the {!antahkaran!} will become polluted.
##3.2)If the indulgences of the five {!indriyas!} are pure, then the {!antahkaran!} will remain pure and one will be able to constantly remember God.
##3.3)By associating with {!kusang!}, one’s intellect becomes polluted. Conversely, the company of God and the Sant purifies one’s intellect.
##3.4)No one has ever remained uninfluenced whilst associating with {!kusang!}; therefore, association with {!kusang!} should be shunned.
##3.5)Shriji Mahārāj is God and He is extremely pure (unaffected by impure {!vishays!}).
##3.6)All actions of Shriji Mahārāj are for the liberation of the {!jivas!}; therefore, no one should imitate his actions.
#4.)If one does not understand the above and act accordingly, then:
##4.1)He will not go to God’s abode.
##4.2)He will be reborn as a ghost or a demon and will have to suffer.

19721.t:
#1.)Those devotees seeking their own ultimate liberation should perfect all four virtues: {!ātmā!}-realisation ({!gnān!}), {!bhakti, vairāgya!} and {!dharma!}.
#2.)All four virtues are dependent upon each other:
##2.1)One may have {!ātmā!}-realisation, but if one does not have love towards God, then one does not attain the favour of God – such favour results in the great divine power of not being overpowered by the {!gunas!} of {!māyā!}.
##2.2)If one has love for God but has not attained {!ātmā!}-realisation, then due to the belief that oneself is the body, that love cannot be perfected.
##2.3)One may have both the virtues of {!ātmā!}-realisation and love for God, but if one lacks firm {!vairāgya!}, then the desires for worldly {!vishays!} will prevent the perfection of {!ātmā!}-realisation and love for God.
##2.4)One may have {!vairāgya!}, but if one lacks the virtues of {!ātmā!}-realisation and love for God, one does not experience the profound bliss associated with the form of God.
##2.5)One may have {!swadharma!}, but if love for God, {!ātmā!}-realisation and {!vairāgya!} are absent, then one will not attain God’s Akshardhām.
##2.6)One may have the three virtues of {!ātmā!}-realisation, love for God and {!vairāgya!}, but if {!swadharma!} is lacking, the other three cannot be perfected.
#3.)A devotee who has extremely firmly established these four virtues should be known as an {!ekāntik bhakta!}.
#4.)A devotee having any deficiency in these four virtues should overcome that deficiency by serving and profoundly associating with the {!Ekāntik Bhakta!} of God.

19722.t:
#1.)The {!jiva!} indulges in a countless variety of {!vishays!}, but:
##1.1)It does not indulge in the bliss of its own self, nor does it know its own nature.
##1.2)Therefore, it is the most ignorant of the ignorant, senseless of the senseless, most foolish of the fools and vilest of the vile.
#2.)For a person who has attained Satsang, realisation of one’s {!jivātmā!} lies in one’s own hands.
#3.)One who contemplates on the greatness of God and draws within oneself sees one’s own self as extremely pure and luminous; and in the midst of that luminance, one beholds the form of the manifest Purushottam Bhagwān.
#4.)All deficiencies, which remain in a devotee, are due to his own lethargy.

19723.t:
#1.)One who possesses {!dharma, gnān, vairāgya!}, and {!bhakti!} coupled with the understanding of God’s greatness is known as an {!ekāntik bhakta!}; and God is pleased through these four virtues.
#2.)One should contemplate on the form of God while performing all activities.
#3.)However if some internal disturbances arise while contemplating on God’s form then one should contemplate on one’s {!ātmā!}:
##3.1)One should realise his own self to be distinct from the body, {!indriyas!}, and the {!antahkaran!}.
##3.2)Just as one does not believe the bodies of those 8.4 million life forms to be one’s true body, similarly, one should not believe this present body to be one’s true self, nor should one believe the relations of this body to be one’s true relations.
#4.)In order to increasingly understand the profound greatness of God day by day, one should constantly keep the company of a {!sādhu!}.
#5.)After such an {!ekāntik bhakta!}leaves his body, he acquires the qualities similar to those of Akshar, and attains Akshardhām forever remaining in the service of God.
#6.)Akshar has two forms: first is Chidākāsh and second is the form that remains in the service of God in his abode.
#7.)All {!satsangis!} should develop the following singular conviction:
##7.1)We want to become an {!akshar-mukta!} and remain in the service of God in Akshardhām
##7.2)We do not want and be tempted by the temporary and vain worldly pleasures.
##7.3)We want to offer {!ekāntik!} {!bhakti!} to God.
##7.4)We want to eradicate our desires in this very life by thoroughly understanding the profound greatness of God.

19724.t:
#1.)One who does not remember God while singing:
##1.1)It is as good as not having sung at all.
##1.2)One does not attain peace of mind.
#2.)Singing devotional songs, reciting God’s holy name, chanting the {!dhun!}, etc. - one should only perform that activity while remembering the form of God.
#3.)One should practise maintaining one’s {!vrutti!} on the form of God while walking, eating, and drinking - in fact, during all activities.
#4.)Keeping the mind’s {!vrutti!} on God is like the digit 1. (A long row of zeros has no value, but when a single ‘1’ is placed before the zeros, the value of the composite figure is exponentially increased with each zero.)

19725.t:
#1.)There are two types of devotees of God:
##1.1)First has a complete conviction of God, yet worships God whilst identifying himself with the body. 
##1.2)The second believes his own self to be {!chaitanya!}, transcending the influences of the three states - waking, dream and deep sleep, and the three bodies - {!sthul, sukshma!} and {!kāran!}. This devotee worships God while beholding God’s form within his own self. He has attained an elevated spiritual state.
#2.)As long as one has not attained this elevated spiritual state, one is subject to obstacles, even if one is a devotee of God.
##2.1)One will succumb to the five {!vishays!}.
##2.2)One will perceive worldly attributes in God (he will perceive him as an ordinary human being).
#3.)If one has attained this elevated spiritual state, then one will not have doubts in God’s actions. Moreover, he understands: how can God have any ({!māyik!}) flaws if my own flaws were eradicated by worshipping him?
#4.)The means of attaining an elevated spiritual state is to maintain one’s {!vrutti!} constantly on God whilst engaged in pure or impure activities.
#5.)A pot that is filled with water and emptied somewhere daily will not form a pool of water; similarly, a person who at times worships God with a concentrated mind and, at other times, indulges in worldly thoughts does not develop such an elevated spiritual state.
#6.)When a devotee of God, who has attained an elevated state, focuses his {!vrutti!} on the form of God, that {!vrutti!} is divided into two:
##6.1)One {!vrutti!} affectionately focuses on the form of God.
##6.2)The other focuses within the worshipper himself by his thought.

19726.t:
#1.)Elevated state of {!gnān!}:
##1.1)Is when Prakruti-Purush and the entities evolved from them do not come into view, also known as {!gnān-pralay!}.
##1.2)Is attained by constantly maintaining one’s {!vrutti!} on the manifest form of God.
#2.)By understanding the greatness of God:
##2.1)Vicious thoughts cease.
##2.2)Just as when one has sucked many lemons, one would be unable to chew even cooked rice; in the same manner, when one has developed ‘sourness’ in the form of faith in God and an understanding of His greatness, one becomes incapable of chewing the {!vishays!} of the respective {!indriyas!} and {!antahkaran!}.
#3.)If a person realises God to be absolutely flawless, he himself becomes absolutely flawless.
#4.)Whatever types of flaws a person attributes to God will ultimately cause misery to the person himself.
#5.)The means to feel completely fulfilled:
##5.1)Believing one is extremely fortunate that:
###i.)The incarnate form of Purushottam has compassionately revealed His own form to me.
###ii.)He has freed me from lust, anger and all of the other vicious natures.
###iii.)He has placed me in the company of {!sādhus!}.
##5.2)Contemplating on the attainment of the manifest form of God and realising, ‘I am completely fulfilled.’
##5.3)When a fault is noticed in a devotee, thinking that he has attained {!Satsang!}, and appreciating their virtues with this understanding.
#6.)The following are major deficiencies of a devotee of God:
##6.1)Not contemplating on their great fortune and not feeling fulfilled, despite understanding the greatness of God.
##6.2)Not remaining extremely elated throughout the day.

19727.t:
#1.)Means to feeling completely fulfilled:
##1.1){!Ātmā!}-realisation coupled with {!vairāgya!}.
##1.2)Knowledge of God’s greatness.
#2.)He should also feel fulfilled by realising, “Now, I have no deficiencies remaining.”
#3.)One should not get carried away in the elation of this understanding, but he should also not feel unfulfilled.
#4.)There are two types of {!samādhi!}:
##4.1)One is controlling the {!prāns!} through {!prānāyām!}, one of the eight steps of {!ashtāng-yoga!}, whereby the {!chitt!} is also controlled
##4.2)The other is by controlling the {!chitt!}, whereby the {!prāns!} are also controlled – illustrated by the analogy: if the flow of twenty pails of water from a well is combined, then the resultant flow would become extremely powerful; similarly, when a person’s {!vruttis!} have become free of worldly desires, his {!chitt!} focuses only on God’s form.
#5.)When one observes one’s religious vows - which are God’s injunctions - God will be pleased with him.

19728.t:
#1.)A genuine amorous devotee:
##1.1)In the wakeful state in the physical body:
###i.)He is attracted to the five {!vishays!} related to only God.
###ii.)He bears an aversion to the worldly {!vishays!}.
##1.2)In the dream state in the subtle ({!sukshma!}) body:
###i.)He experiences bliss related to God only.
###ii.)He bears an aversion to other {!vishays!} similar to an aversion to vomited food.
#2.)A false amorous devotee:
##2.1)In the wakeful state in the physical body and in the dream state in the {!sukshma!} body, just as he experiences pleasure from God-related {!vishays!} he experiences equal pleasure from worldly {!vishays!}.
##2.2)His {!upāsanā!} and understanding are flawed.
#3.)When only thoughts of God remain, then one identifies one’s self as Brahma and sees form of God in his heart.
#4.)Affection towards only the form of God in this manner is called faithful {!bhakti!} ({!pativratāni!} {!bhakti!}).

19729.t:
#1.)God eternally resides in the heart of a person who possesses the following understanding:
##1.1)He understands that the cause of all wonders in the past, present and future is the incarnate form of God that I have attained.
##1.2)He has equanimity in honour and insults; beautiful woman or an unattractive woman; gold or stone.
##1.3)Possesses countless noble virtues, such as {!gnān, bhakti, vairāgya!}.
##1.4)He attains countless types of powers and liberates countless beings by the grace of God.
##1.5)Despite becoming powerful, he tolerates insults.
##1.6)That {!Sant!} is capable of empowering the {!indriyas!} of all {!jivas!} in the {!brahmānd!}, and therefore, is the sustainer of the world.
#2.)One who believes, “This woman is very beautiful; these clothes are extremely fashionable; this house is very nice, etc…” are petty-minded and do not develop the virtues of a {!sādhu!}.

19730.t:
#1.)One who is likely regress in Satsang:
##1.1)Vicious desires steadily flourish within him.
##1.2)Perceives flaws in all {!satsangis!}.
##1.3)Feels that all of {!satsangis!} lack understanding and considers himself superior to all.
##1.4)Smoulders like a half-burnt log.
##1.5)His anger never subsides.
#2.)One who is likely to progress in Satsang:
##2.1)Pure desires steadily flourish within him.
##2.2)Perceives virtues in all {!satsangis!}.
##2.3)Views all {!satsangis!} to be superior to him and considers himself insignificant.
##2.4)Experiences bliss 24 hours a day in his heart.
##2.5)The more he practises Satsang, he attains profound greatness.

19731.t:
#1.)Pure place, auspicious time, pious actions, and company of a {!Sādhu!} are ways to intensify the force of {!bhakti, dharma, gnān!}, and {!vairāgya!}.
#2.)The cause of one’s heart extremely becoming pure: {!prārabdha!}, grace of God, and personal endeavours.
#3.){!Prārabdha!} is the good or bad that happens due to one’s previous {!sanskārs!}.
#4.)The grace of God or the {!Ekāntik!} {!Sādhu!} occurs when he is pleased but one’s extremely pure sentiments.
#5.)Personal endeavour means purifying one’s self by keeping the company of a {!sādhu!} and one’s thoughts.

19732.t:
#1.)The reason for thoughts leaving a lasting impression is the influence of the {!gunas!}:
##1.1)When {!tamogun!} is predominant, a state similar to that of deep sleep is induced; and thoughts occurring in this state do not leave a lasting impression.
##1.2)When {!sattvagun!} prevails, thoughts that occur can be dispelled by contemplation and do not leave a lasting impression.
##1.3)Thoughts that arise when {!rajogun!} is prevalent leave a lasting impression in the mind.
#2.)Means to eradicate disturbing thoughts:
##2.1)Recognising which {!guna!} is predominant at a particular time and remaining aware of one’s thoughts.
##2.2)Reflecting on and imbibing the discourses of Satsang.
##2.3)Sincerely practicing Satsang by thought, word, and deed.
#3.)When one becomes free from all doubts, one is able to continuously concentrate on the form of God.

19733.t:
#1.)One who observes {!nivrutti!} (path of renunciation or path of inactivity from worldly pursuits) and one who offers {!bhakti!} to God:
##1.1)One who offers {!bhakti!} to God and may verbally hurt someone is better because he serves God and the {!Sant!}.
##1.2)The one who observes {!nivrutti!} without hurting anyone and is thereby unable to serve God and the {!Sant!}, should be known to be feeble.
#2.)Greatness is due to:
##2.1)One’s faith in the manifest form of God.
##2.2)Observance of God’s commands and offering {!bhakti!}.
#3.)One who forms a habit of perceiving flaws in God’s devotees:
##3.1)Will perceive flaws in God and His great devotees.
##3.2)His intellect becomes demonic.

19734.t:
#1.)Person who is attached to {!vishays!}: He enjoys only worldly {!vishays!} unrelated to God.
#2.)A devotee of God: He indulges in {!vishays!} related to God only.
#3.)A nest and a stake:
##3.1)Just as birds leave their nests to gather food and return to their nests at night to rest…
##3.2)Just as domesticated cattle return to their stake in the evening after grazing…
##3.3)Similarly, a devotee of God, after feeding on feed in the form of discourses, devotional songs, etc., should return to their nest in the form of God.
#4.)Technique of meditating on God:
##4.1)When different {!gunas!} enter the {!antahkaran!}, one should examine:
###i.)When {!sattvagun!} prevails, the {!antahkaran!} is pure and one can pleasantly engage in worship and remembrance of God’s form; therefore, one should meditate on God’s form.
###ii.)When {!rajogun!} prevails, the {!antahkaran!} becomes polluted and disturbing thoughts arise; therefore, one should not meditate on God’s form.
###iii.)When {!tamogun!} prevails, no thoughts arise at all, and one experiences a feeling of emptiness. One should not meditate on God’s form.
##4.2)When {!rajogun!} prevails:
###i.)One should not become dejected on noticing the many thoughts which arise.
###ii.)One should regard one’s self to be distinct from the thoughts arising in the {!antahkaran!} and believe one’s self to be the {!ātmā!}.
###iii.)One should believe God forever resides in one’s {!ātmā!} and engage in the worship of God.

19735.t:
#1.)The greatest endeavour to please God is the firm refuge of God.
#2.)Refuge is of three types:
##2.1)Blind faith: even if someone such as Brahmā were to attempt to deflect him from his refuge, he would not be deflected.
##2.2)Profound love for God: one does not become attracted to any object other than God.
##2.3)Understanding:
###i.)Understanding God’s form by utilising one’s intelligence.
###ii.)He does not harbour doubts when God, assuming a human form, exhibits divine powers or acts powerless.
###iii.)If someone tries to dissuade him, or even if he tries to dissuade himself, such a refuge in God never diminishes.

19736.t:
#1.)One becomes attracted to worldly objects instead of God because God set the world in motion in the form of {!māyā!} – affection toward relations of the body.
#2.)Means to overcome {!māyā!}:
##2.1)Developing {!vairāgya!} by maintaining an aversion for worldly objects.
##2.2)Knowing God to be absolutely blissful and keeping one’s {!vrutti!} focused on God.
#3.)The happiness and misery experienced by a non-believer is determined by his own {!karmas!}.
#4.)The happiness experienced by a devotee of God is due to observing His commands; and the misery experienced is due to lapses in observing God’s commands.

19737.t:
#1.)Despite being intelligent, if one perceives faults in God or His great {!Sant!}:
##1.1)Then his intellect is polluted.
##1.2)He is incapable of walking on the path of liberation.
#2.)Despite having little intelligence, if it is not polluted, then he will safeguard his liberation.
#3.)One whose intellect is polluted or demonic:
##3.1)Wherever he takes birth, he will always malign God or His devotees.
##3.2)Even if someone were to listen to his talks, the listener’s mind would also fall back from Satsang.
##3.3)Even the virtues of God and His devotees appear as faults to him.
##3.4)He becomes the king of some demons and worships God through animosity.
#4.)If one does not keep anger, arrogance, jealousy, and deceit with God or His {!Sant!}, his intellect will not become demonic.

19738.t:
#1.)Just as a wealthy man views a poor man to be a sinner, the great {!Ekāntik Sant!} views a renunciant who craves materialistic pleasures to be a sinner.
#2.)A renunciant who is like a poor man:
##2.1)Does not have affection for {!dharma, gnān, vairāgya!} and {!bhakti!}.
##2.2)Develops affection for perishable objects instead of God.
##2.3)His thirst for materialistic pleasures is never quenched 
#3.)A true renunciant:
##3.1)Views dirt and gold as equal.
##3.2)Never makes distinctions by thinking, “This object is pleasant, and this object is unpleasant.”
##3.3)Has affection only toward God.

19739.t:
#1.)Methods of abandoning affection for one’s birthplace:
##1.1)Believe one’s self to be the {!ātmā!}.
##1.2)View the relationships of the current body to be similar to the relationships of previous births.
##1.3)Just as the parents of the previous births have been forgotten due to ignorance, similarly the parents of this human body should be forgotten through knowledge.
#2.)Shriji Mahārāj speaks of his nature for the sake of revealing the ideals of a devotee:
##2.1)He has no affection toward any of His relatives.
##2.2)Even if a person serving Him is as virtuous as Nāradji, if he lacks {!bhakti!} for God, He does not like him.
#3.)For a person who has {!bhakti!} for God in his heart, understands God to be {!sākār!} and all-doer, Shriji Mahārāj bestows him 11 honours:
##3.1)He is dear to Mahārāj.
##3.2){!Kāl!} is unable to administer its power over him.
##3.3){!Karma!} is unable to administer its power over him.
##3.4){!Māyā!} is unable to administer its power over him.
##3.5)Mahārāj places the dust of his feet on His head.
##3.6)Mahārāj is afraid of harming him.
##3.7)Mahārāj longs for his {!darshan!}.
##3.8)He is wise because he wishes for liberation through the grace of God.
##3.9)After leaving his body, he attain a form of {!chaitanya!} in the abode of God and forever remain in His service.
##3.10)The {!darshan!} of such a true {!Bhakta!} of God is equivalent to the {!darshan!} of God Himself.
##3.11)He is so great that his {!darshan!} alone can redeem countless wretched {!jivas!}.

19740.t:
#1.)If one borrows money from a merchant and does not repay month-by-month, then it becomes difficult to repay the debt; similarly, one should examine their mind and eradicate their worldly desires little by little.
#2.)Method of eradicating worldly desires:
##2.1)Constant remembrance of God’s divine actions and incidents.
##2.2)Revealing one’s impure thoughts to one ({!Satpurush!}) who does not have impure thoughts of worldly desires, but instead is capable of eradicating others’ impure thoughts.
##2.3)Observing one’s own {!dharma!} and understanding God’s greatness, maintaining a constant effort to free their mind of worldly desires.
#3.)Importance of becoming free of worldly desires:
##3.1)No matter how much {!pravrutti!} one does physically, the mind should be pure and free of worldly desires.
##3.2)One who does not entertain worldly thoughts but entertains thoughts of God is eminent.
##3.3)It is Shriji Mahārāj’s principal that one becomes free from worldly desires.
##3.4)Even if one engages in austerities physically, if their mind is not free of worldly desires, then he does not benefit much.
#4.)A genuine renunciant and householder:
##4.1)A true renunciant is one whose mind never entertains a desire for objects that he has already renounced.
##4.2)One whose mind is free of worldly desires is a genuine householder.
#5.)The Ekādashi fast:
##5.1)The ten {!indriyas!} and the mind, the eleventh, should be withdrawn from their respective {!vishays!} and attached to God.
##5.2)Devotees of God should engage in this observance continuously.
#6.)The listener, speaker, the one who understands, and the one who knows is the {!jiva!}.

19741.t:
#1.)There are two states of those who become {!muktas!} by worshipping God:
##1.1)Those who have attained the {!savikalp!} {!state!}: They see {!jivas, ishwars, māyā!}, and their supporter, Brahma, as being distinct from each other.
##1.2)Those who have attained the {!nirvikalp!} {!state!}: They see {!jivas, ishwars!} and {!māyā!} as being one with Brahma - but they do not see them as distinct entities.
#2.)One with an incorrect understanding:
##2.1)Even though he has not attained the {!nirvikalp!} {!state!}, he believes he has attained such a state.
##2.2)Claims that the guru, the disciple, {!jivas, ishwars, māyā!}, the world, the Vedas, the Purāns, the Shāstras are all imaginary.
##2.3)Is extremely foolish and will be consigned to {!narak!}.

19742.t:
#1.)One who has attained {!savikalp!} {!samādhi!} still entertains pure desires.
#2.)One who has attained {!nirvikalp!} {!samādhi!} remains engrossed only in the form of God, having attained the attributes of Aksharbrahma.
#3.)Difference between {!bhakti!} and {!upāsanā!}:
##3.1){!Bhakti!} means worshipping God in the nine ways (mentioned in the Shrimad Bhāgwat: (1) {!shravan!}, (2) {!kirtan!}, (3) {!smaran!}, (4) {!pāda-sevān!}, (5) {!archan!}, (6) {!vandan!}, (7) {!dāsya!}, (8) {!sākhya!}, (9) {!ātmanivedan!}).
##3.2){!Upāsanā!} means having a firm conviction that God eternally possesses a form.
#4.)Characteristics of one with {!upāsanā!}:
##4.1)Even if he becomes {!brahmarup!}, conviction that God possesses a form never disappears.
##4.2)Even if he happens to listen to scriptures propounding the view that God is formless, he would still understand God to always have a form.

19743.t:
#1.)“Eko’ham bahu syām” means:
##1.1)As interpreted by Vedāntis: {!Jivas!} and {!ishwars!} were formed from God and are a part of Him.
##1.2)As according to Shriji Mahārāj’s principal: God enters {!jivas, ishwars!}, etc. as their cause and as their {!antaryāmi!} (but they were not formed from God).
#2.)God dwells in all entities, from Akshar to birds and animals. However, due to difference in capacities of the entities, there is a difference in their power.
#3.)God resides in Akshar in the greatest degree compared to other entities.

19744.t:
#1.)Understanding of Vedāntis: Only Brahma is {!satya!} and the moral do’s and don’ts are false and anything attained from these morals is also false
#2.)Understanding of Vedāntis is false because:
##2.1)Shankarāchārya ({!āchārya!} of all Vedāntis) propounded observance of moral do’s and don’ts and composed verses in praise of deities.
##2.2)Due to having attained the {!nirvikalp!} state, one may not see {!jivas, ishwars, māyā!}, etc. separately but may only see Brahma; however they all exist in reality.
##2.3)They (Vedāntis) meticulously performs all worldly activities, believing them to be real; yet, on the other hand, they falsify the moral do’s and don’ts which have been prescribed by the scriptures.
##2.4)If everything is Brahma, then the mutual affection husbands and wives have should cause them to become {!gunātit!}.
#3.)No matter how great one may be, bad company always leads to harm. No matter how grave a sinner one may be, maintaining profound association with God leads one to become absolutely pure and attain liberation.
#4.)Moral do’s and don’ts are true. One who falsifies them are consigned to {!narak!}.

19745.t:
#1.)Four types of liberation ({!mukti!}):
##1.1)Reside in the realm of God.
##1.2)Stay near God.
##1.3)Assume a form similar to that of God.
##1.4)Attain divine power similar to God’s powers.
#2.){!Sakām!} devotee:
##2.1)Desires the four types of liberation.
##2.2)Should overcome this deficiency by profoundly associating with a {!nishkām!} {!Ekāntik Bhakta!} of God.
#3.){!Nishkām!} devotee:
##3.1)Does not desire the four types of liberation if they are without the service of God.
##3.2)Only desires the service of God.
##3.3)God keeps him in His own service.
##3.4)God insistently grants him His divine powers and bliss.

19746.t:
#1.)Characteristics of one who as total affection for God:
##1.1)He has an unbroken remembrance of God.
##1.2)If he harbours thoughts other than those of God, then he experiences misery equivalent to being branded on the forehead by a red-hot branding iron.
#2.)Only by keeping profound association with the {!Satpurush!} can one develop intense love for God.
#3.)If one has a {!dagli!} sewn by a tailor and he believes the tailor is his father and the tailor’s wife is his mother, he would be considered foolish. Similarly, the {!jiva!} has obtained a {!dagli!} in the form of the physical body in 8.4 million life forms. A person who believes the body to be his true self and believes the parents of that body to be his own parents is called a fool.
#4.)As long as a person believes the body to be his true self, his understanding is totally useless.
#5.)As long as he continues to harbour vanity of his caste or {!āshram!}, he will never imbibe the virtues of a sādhu.
#6.)After discarding the feelings of I-ness and my-ness for the body and its relations, believing one’s {!ātmā!} to be {!brahmarup!}, and after forsaking all worldly desires, if a person worships God while observing {!swadharma!}, he should be known as a {!sādhu!}. No distance remains between Purushottam Bhagwān and a person who has cultivated such qualities of a {!sādhu!}.

19747.t:
#1.)God forever possesses a form:
##1.1)The Shrutis mention: “That God looked towards {!māyā!}.” One who sees has eyes; along with other parts (hands, feet, etc.). Therefore, God can be said to possess a (complete) form. 
##1.2)The Shrutis mention that God is without hands, feet, etc.; but that should be understood as {!māyik!} hands, feet, etc. In reality, God’s form is divine, not {!māyik!}.
#2.)God’s divine light is formless, but it is {!antaryāmi!}, governor of all, and grants the fruits of {!karmas!}; hence, it should be considered to possess a form.

19748.t:
#1.)Characteristics of Chidākāsh:
##1.1)It is one of the forms of Brahma and is extremely luminous.
##1.2)It pervades everything and is the supporter of all.
##1.3)It is eternal (without a beginning), not subject to change, and not subject to creation or destruction
#2.)The {!ākāsh!} that is one of the five {!panch-bhuts!}:
##2.1)Evolves from {!tamogun!} and is full of darkness.
##2.2)Is subject to change and subject to creation and destruction.
##2.3)Contracts during {!samādhi!} and becomes assimilated.

19749.t:
#1.)Characteristics of those who possess the four types of firmness:
##1.1)One with firmness in observance of {!dharma!}:
###i.)Abides by the disciplines related to the {!dharma!} of his caste and {!āshram!}.
###ii.)Lovingly engages in performing menial service to God and His devotees.
###iii.)Is inclined toward activities related to God.
###iv.)Offers bhakti to God without any form of pretence.
###v.)Enjoys listening to and reading scriptures expounding {!bhāgwat!} {!dharma!}.
##1.2)One with firmness in realising oneself as {!ātmā!}:
###i.)Always behaves as the {!ātmā!}.
###ii.)Understands God to forever possess a form, is all-transcending, and is divine; he engages in listening to and discoursing about this.
###iii.)Talks about and listens to talks expounding the pure nature of his own {!ātmā!}, as well as talks of Paramātmā. He also enjoys scriptures that contain such talks.
##1.3)One with firmness in {!vairāgya!}:
###i.)Has a dislike for all worldly objects except God’s form.
###ii.)Never remembers his home, his family or other objects that he has renounced.
###iii.)Likes the company of devotees who are renunciants.
###iv.)Offers {!bhakti!} to God in a manner that does not conflict with his renunciation.
###v.)Talks predominantly about renunciation and has a liking for scriptures propounding renunciation.
##1.4)One with firmness in {!bhakti!}:
###i.)Has intense love only for God.
###ii.)Is unable to focus his mind’s {!vrutti!} towards anything other than God.
###iii.)Enjoys listening to the human-like actions and incidents of God.
###iv.)Enjoys listening to scriptures describing God’s form.
###v.)Only develops affection towards devotees who have love for God.
###vi.)Always engages in some activity that is related to God.
#2.)When one person is firm in all four, he is known as {!Param-Bhāgwat!} or {!Ekāntik Bhakta!}.
#3.)This talk is like a mirror (in that it reveals one’s own inclination as it is); therefore, one should reflect on this talk and cultivate their inclination.

19750.t:
#1.)Four types of {!kusang!}:
##1.1){!Kudā-panthis!}: they will cause one to falter in their religious vows and make one impure.
##1.2){!Shakti-panthis!}: they will cause one to deflect from observance of {!swadharma!}.
##1.3){!Shushka-Vedānti!}: they will cause one to fall from {!bhakti!} and {!upāsanā!}.
##1.4){!Nāstiks!}: they deny the existence of God, thereby leading one astray from the path prescribed by sacred scriptures.
#2.)One should daily pray to God:
##2.1)May I never encounter the four types of {!kusangis!}.
##2.2)Protect me from the inner enemies of lust, anger, etc.
##2.3)Bestow upon me the company of your devotees.

19751.t:
#1.)A devotee of God finds it difficult to keep his {!vrutti!} on worldly objects.
#2.)A worldly person finds it difficult to keep his {!vrutti!} on God.
#3.)Means to become a devotee of God:
##3.1)Attending Satsang and listening to the talks of the sādhus, one gradually becomes a devotee.
##3.2){!Antardrashti!}: Constantly looking towards God, either internally within one’s heart or externally at the manifest form of God.

19752.t:
#1.)One with a sharp intellect:
##1.1)May possess little (worldly) intellect but safeguards his liberation.
##1.2)Constantly engages in worship of God.
##1.3)Indulges in {!panchvishays!} without interest in them.
##1.4)Attains God.
#2.)One with a blunt intellect:
##2.1)May be adept in worldly affairs and understand the meanings of scriptures; yet does nothing to safeguard their liberation.
##2.2)Does not worship God.
##2.3)Indulge in {!panchvishays!} with affection for them.
##2.4)Is a fool.

19753.t: #1.)God transcends all, is the all-doer, and the cause of all.\n#2.)Just as a diamond can only be cut by a diamond; similarly, if one who understands the greatness of the manifest form of God through the profound association of the Sant; then all of his {!māyik!} {!indriyas!} and {!antahkarans!} become {!amāyik!} (divine), and one develops conviction of God.

19754.t:
#1.)Sānkhya scriptures:
##1.1)Understanding: {!jiva!} and {!ishwar!} are included in the 24 elements and God is the 25th element.
##1.2)Drawback: when rejecting the 24 elements (because they are perishable), one understands the {!jiva!} to be God – the 25th element.
#2.)Yoga scriptures:
##2.1)Understanding: {!jiva!} and {!ishwar!} (25th element) are distinct from the 24 elements, God is the 26th element and possesses a definite form.
##2.2)Drawback: by believing God to possess a definite form, they consider Him to have limitations; they do not understand Him to be the {!antaryāmi!} of all and absolutely perfect.
#3.)Vedānt scriptures:
##3.1)Understanding: God pervades all, is the cause of all, is the supporter of all, is {!nirgun!}, and is untainted by {!māyā!} or divine.
##3.2)Drawback: God - who is described as the cause of all, pervading all and {!nirgun!} - is believed to be formless.
#4.)Panchrātra scriptures:
##4.1)Understanding: Parabrahma assumes an {!avatār!} on this earth and one attains liberation by worshipping Him.
##4.2)Drawback: human traits are perceived in the {!avatārs!} of God and God is understood as being present in only one place at any one time, but not as being the {!antaryāmi!} of all and absolutely perfect.
#5.)He who understands God using all four scriptures together is known as being completely enlightened.
#6.)He who acts according to his own mentally concocted interpretations of the scriptures:
##6.1)Even if he is a Vedānti or one with {!upāsanā!}, he cannot be said to have found the path of liberation.
##6.2)He should be viewed as a hypocritical {!gnāni!} and a hypocritical devotee.

19755.t: #1.)One who perceives virtues in the {!sādhu!} progresses and his {!bhakti!} and other virtues also flourish.\n#2.)One who perceives flaws gradually regresses and his virtues diminish.\n#3.)Only if there is a discrepancy in the observance of religious vows should one find flaws in others, but not for any other trivial reason.

19756.t:
#1.)By maintaining a profound association of an Ekāntik Sādhu, {!bhāgwat!} {!dharma!} flourishes and the gateway of liberation opens.
#2.)Characteristics of one whose {!dharma!} and Satsang remains firm even in adverse times:
##2.1)Diligent in following the commands of God.
##2.2)Does not disobey any major or minor injunctions of God.

19757.t:
#1.)If one encounters an adverse place, time, action and company:
##1.1)Resolve in worship, remembrance, and religious vows does not remain steady.
##1.2)Even the highest resolve is dissolved.
#2.)If the force of good deeds and merits from previous births are extremely powerful, then the resolve remains firm even in adverse circumstances.
#3.)Even in extremely favourable places, times, actions and company, one’s intellect may become polluted:
##3.1)If one has committed a grave sin.
##3.2)If one has spited a great devotee of God.
#4.)If one serves the {!Motāpurush!} diligently, his sins will be burnt and reduced to ashes.
#5.)One who associates with bad company and blames God by thinking, “Why did God not keep my mind stable?” is an utter fool.

19758.t:
#1.)Of the four types of devotees mentioned in the Gitā, a {!gnāni!} is the best because:
##1.1)He behaves as {!brahmarup!}.
##1.2)He thoroughly understands the greatness of God.
##1.3)He has no desires except that of God.
#2.)If a devotee of God:
##2.1)Exhibits {!gnān, vairāgya!}, and {!bhakti!} out of vanity:
###i.)That is a great flaw.
###ii.)Just as a no water will come in a well when a stone-cutter strikes a stone and it sounds solid (sparks fly), similarly, he will not acquire any great virtues.
###iii.)He sees God’s form residing in his heart with an expression of disgust.
###iv.)If he has any virtues, they will diminish.
###v.)His vanity only serves to strengthen his belief of being the body.
###vi.)The virtues of {!gnān, vairāgya!} and {!bhakti!} may make him appear virtuous superficially, but he does not have any inner-strength.
##2.2)Exhibits {!gnān, vairāgya!}, and {!bhakti!} with humility:
###i.)Just as plentiful water will come in a well when a stone-cutter strikes a stone and it sounds hollow; similarly, he will acquire many great virtues.
###ii.)God resides in his heart with a pleased expression.
###iii.)His virtues grow more powerful.
###iv.)He is the best.
#3.)Means to eradicating ego:
##3.1)Physically: realising the greatness of God’s devotees, bowing down to them, and serving them menially.
##3.2)Mentally: recognising thoughts of vanity when they arise in one’s heart and maintaining the force of thought.
#4.){!Upāsanā!}:
##4.1)Through the force of {!upāsanā!}, one attains countless types of greatness, highest state of enlightenment, and other powers.
##4.2)One realises the distinction between {!ātmā!} and non-{!ātmā!} and develops {!vairāgya!}.
##4.3)One should forsake dependence on the strength of other spiritual endeavours and rely on the strength of God’s {!upāsanā!}.
##4.4)One should increase the strength of their {!upāsanā!} of God by practising {!Satsang!}.
##4.5)One who has firmness in {!upāsanā!} believes, “However a grave sinner a person may be, if he utters ‘Swāminārāyan’ at the end of his life, he will attain God’s abode.”

19759.t:
#1.)Extraordinary means to attain liberation: the knowledge of God’s form and the knowledge of God’s greatness.
#2.)Two ways one develops affection for God:
##2.1)Love that develops due to blind faith (i.e. not applying any logic).
##2.2)Love that develops by realising God’s greatness – this is the best of all the ways.
#3.)Means to eradicate inappropriate {!swabhāvs!}:
##3.1)Develop an intense yearning for Satsang.
##3.2)Maintain enmity toward the {!swabhāvs!} that hinder one in practicing {!satsang!}.
##3.3)Think about one’s {!ātmā!}: the {!jiva!} is more powerful than the {!mind!} and the {!indriyas!}, therefore, whatever the {!jiva!} desires can be achieved.

19760.t:
#1.)The forces of the mayik {!gunas!}:
##1.1)If they arise due to the body, they are eradicated by contemplating on the {!ātmā!} and the non-{!ātmā!}.
##1.2)If they arise from bad company, they are eradicated by keeping the company of a {!sādhu!}.
##1.3)If they arise from unfavourable {!sanskārs!} of the past, they are eradicated by pleasing a {!Motāpurush!}.
#2.)By pleasing the {!Motāpurush!}:
##2.1)Unfavourable {!prārabdha!} becomes favourable.
##2.2)A beggar becomes a king.
##2.3)A disastrous misfortune one is to face is avoided.
##2.4)Unfavourable {!sanskārs!} from the past are destroyed.
#3.)To please the {!Motāpurush!}:
##3.1)One should behave honestly.
##3.2)Forsake {!swabhāvs!}.
##3.3)Behave with humility.
#4.)Whatever vices one perceives in the {!Motāpurush!} will dwell on the perceiver; and if one perceives the {!Motāpurush!} to be free of all flaws, then the perceiver becomes free of all evil natures.
#5.)Characteristics of a staunch devotee:
##5.1)Has a dislike for alluring {!vishays!}.
##5.2)Has firm faith in God.
#6.)Means to become a staunch devotee:
##6.1)Understanding the {!Motāpurush!} to be free of evil natures.
##6.2)Behaving as a servant of the servants of God and realising their greatness.
#7.)Benefit of becoming a staunch devotee:
##7.1)All of one’s evil natures are destroyed.
##7.2)The noble virtues flourish in him day by day.

19761.t:
#1.)If one has conviction in the manifest form of God’s the following type of understanding, then one develops extraordinary love for God:
##1.1)He who I have attained is undoubtedly God Himself.
##1.2)He is the master of all abodes, the all-doer, and {!antaryāmi!}.
#2.)One who has this type of conviction may appear to not possess extraordinary love for God. However one can realise the strength of his love by practising Satsang and listening to scriptures.
#3.)The person is the governing factor in determining whether places, times and actions are favourable or unfavourable.

19762.t:
#1.)When one naturally perceives pleasant and unpleasant {!vishays!} to be the same, then it should be known his worldly desires have been overcome.
#2.)Importance of overcoming worldly desires:
##2.1)Overcoming worldly desires is the greatest spiritual endeavour.
##2.2)To behave above the influence of worldly desires is the {!dharma!} of one who is {!ekāntik!}.
##2.3)Even if a slight worldly desire remains, it will draw him out of {!samādhi!}.
#3.)Means to overcome worldly desires:
##3.1){!Antardrashti!}: how much worldly desires do I have and how much affection do I have for God?
##3.2)Strengthen the realisation that one’s self is the {!ātmā!}.
##3.3)Realise the insignificance of the {!panchvishays!}.
##3.4)Understand the greatness of God.
##3.5)Reflect on the bliss of God.
##3.6){!Ekāntik!} {!dharma!} can only be attained by following the commands of a Purush who is free of worldly desires; it cannot be attained merely by reading books.
#4.)One’s experience after overcoming worldly desires:
##4.1)I have always been free of worldly desires.
##4.2)I never had any desires; whatever it may have seemed was some kind of illusion.

19763.t:
#1.)With {!ātmā!}-realisation, one remains stable in cold and heat, hunger and thirst, honour and insult, happiness and misery; but only refuge of God and firmness in {!upāsanā!} are helpful at the time of death.
#2.)What kind of devotee does God become bound to?
##2.1)Even if he attains Yogic powers, he desires nothing except God and remains free of worldly desires – such an {!Ekāntik Bhakta!}.
##2.2)One who has unparalleled devotion to God like King Bali.
###i.)He offered everything to God with {!shraddhā!}.
###ii.)God bound him without any fault of his own; yet King Bali did not falter from his {!bhakti!}.
##2.3)One who remains as a servant of God.
##2.4)One who becomes increasingly pleased as God imposes more and more hardships without becoming disheartened in the face of misery or for the sake of bodily comforts.

19764.t:
#1.)One who develops rapport with God by having the perfect conviction of God:
##1.1)Acquires the redemptive virtues of God.
##1.2)Becomes extremely capable and unattached just like God.
#2.)That perfect conviction should be like this:
##2.1)He realises that God is not like {!kāl, karma, swabhāv, māyā!}, or Purush (an {!aksharmukta!} involved in creation of countless {!brahmānds!}).
##2.2)He realises God to be distinct from everything, their controller and cause; despite being their cause, He is beyond their influence.
##2.3)Even if he hears misleading scriptures or talks of misleading philosophers, or if his own {!antahkaran!} raises doubts within himself, his conviction of God never wavers.
#3.)A demonic {!jiva!}:
##3.1)Will still not forsake his own {!swabhāvs!} even if he comes into contact with God.
##3.2)Suffers severely because he spites devotees of God.
#4.)The {!dharma!} of humble devotees of God:
##4.1)He does not retain the slightest arrogance due to remaining fearful of God.
##4.2)He does not pain even the smallest of being
##4.3)He behaves meekly.

19765.t:
#1.)Characteristics of one who has a deficiency in faith in God:
##1.1)Becomes disheartened when God does not display his divine powers.
##1.2)Blames God when he cannot eradicate his impure thoughts.
##1.3)Whatever flaws he harbours, he perceives the same flaws in God.
#2.)Characteristics of one who has total faith in God:
##2.1)Having attained the manifest form of God, he feels fulfilled, and believing he has attained all that needs to be attained, he remains in an elated state.
##2.2)He understands the greatness of the manifest form of God and his devotees.
##2.3)He may possess intense renunciation, yet he will willingly do any task on the path of {!pravrutti!} commanded by God.
##2.4)If he possesses any {!swabhāv!} that couldn’t be eradicated by a million means - if he senses God’s insistence in forsaking that {!swabhāv!}, he forsakes it immediately.
##2.5)He is unable to live without the discourses and devotional songs related to God and without the {!Sant!} of God even for a moment.
##2.6)He finds faults only within himself and thoroughly imbibes the virtues of the {!Sant!}.
#3.)A person who has realised the form of God perfectly:
##3.1)Has nothing left to realize.
##3.2){!Kāl, karma!} and {!māyā!} are incapable of binding him.
#4.)To realise the form of God perfectly means:
##4.1)Understanding the form of Akshar:
###i.)Akshardhām is superior to other abodes.
###ii.)Akshar is the cause of Prakruti-Purush.
###iii.)Countless millions of {!brahmānds!} float like mere atoms in each of its hairs.
###iv.)That Akshar is greater than all (Prakruti-Purush, Pradhān-Purush, {!mahāttattva, ahamkār!}, etc.) and possesses a divine form.
##4.2)The master of this Akshar is Purushottam.
##4.3)That God (who is greater than even Akshar) conceals his powers and becomes like a human being for their liberation.

19766.t:
#1.){!Ātmā!} and Akshar are the {!sharir!} (embodiment) of God and God is the {!shariri!} of {!ātmā!} and Akshar – this statement should be understood as:
##1.1)God is all-pervasive, independent, and all-powerful.
##1.2){!Ātmā!} and Akshar are pervaded by God, dependent on God, and are powerless without God.
#2.)God transcends even Akshar, who transcends everything. He is the inspirer of all and the controller of all.
#3.)Those who offer {!bhakti!} and {!upāsanā!} to God understanding Him to possess a divine form:
##3.1)Acquire the qualities similar to God.
##3.2)Acquire countless spiritual powers.
##3.3)Remain in the service of God.
#4.)Those who offer {!bhakti!} and {!upāsanā!} to God understanding Him to be formless are consigned to {!brahma-sushupti!} from which they never return.
#5.)These facts can be understood only from a person who firmly believes that God is forever divine and possesses a form.

19767.t:
#1.)The {!ākāsh!} that is one of the {!panch-bhuts!} is subject to creation and destruction; whereas, Chidākāsh, which is the supporter of all, is not subject to creation or destruction.
#2.)The arrangement of the body and the {!brahmānd!} are similar.
