#3.)In whatever state (wakeful, dream, or deep sleep) one focuses on the form of God, that state is dissolved first.
#4.)God possesses {!gnān-shakti!} (cognition), {!kriyā-shakti!} (conation), and {!ichchhā-shakti!} (volition):
##4.1){!Gnān-shakti!}: when the {!jiva!} enters the state of deep sleep and has no {!gnān!}, God awakens it and makes it aware of its actions.
##4.2){!Kriyā-shakti!}: whatever action a {!jiva!} engages in, it does so with the support of God’s {!kriyā-shakti!}.
##4.3){!Ichchhā-shakti!}: whatever object a {!jiva!} desires, it acquires with the help of God’s {!ichchhā-shakti!}.
#5.)A {!jiva!} cannot indulge in the fruits of its {!karmas!} according to its own will or as a direct consequence of its {!karmas!}. When God, who grants the fruits of {!karmas!}, allows it to indulge in the fruits of the {!karmas!} of that particular state that it is able to indulge in them.

19768.t:
#1.)When one encounters the talk of the four emanations of God in the Shrimad Bhāgwat:
##1.1)When the term {!nirgun!} is used, it is in reference to Vāsudev.
##1.2)When the term {!sagun!} is used, it is in reference to Sankarshan, Pradyumna, and Aniruddha.
#2.)The words of the scriptures cannot be understood in their true context by anyone except an {!Ekāntik Bhakta!}:
##2.1)“God is ‘God is formless’, ‘universally pervasive’,‘luminous’ and ‘{!nirgun!}.’ This means: He is devoid of {!māyik!} attributes; but possesses countless redemptive virtues.
##2.2) “God is an immense mass of light”: due to the immense light in God’s form, He appears to be just a mass of light; but that light emanates from the divine form of God.
##2.3)“God assumes a physical body” but the {!bhakta!} understands God:
###i.)Due to the powers of God, {!māyik!} objects become non-{!māyik!}; therefore, God’s physical body is also non-{!māyik!} – meaning divine.
###ii.)He transcends Akshar.
###iii.)He is the {!ātmā!} of countless millions of {!muktas!} and Akshardhām.

19769.t:
#1.)Characteristics of the {!Satpurush!}:
##1.1)Has no affection for the pleasures of this world.
##1.2)Desires only for the abode and form of God.
##1.3)For those who associate with him, he only wishes that they eradicate desires for this world and develop affection for God.
##1.4)All of the {!Satpurush's!} efforts are only for acquiring bliss after attaining the abode of God after death.
#2.)Only when one understands the virtues of the {!Satpurush!} this way are they acquired by an aspirant:
##2.1)Realise the {!Satpurush!} to be a form of God – i.e. maintain divinity in the {!Satpurush!}.
##2.2)Trust the words of the {!Satpurush!}.
##2.3)Imbibe the virtues of a {!Satpurush!} and forsake one’s flaws by feeling remorse.
#3.)One who perceives countless types of flaws in the {!Satpurush!} never acquires the virtues of the {!Satpurush!}.

19770.t:
#1.)God forever resides in the 8 types of {!murtis!} and in the {!Sant!}.
##1.1)A devotee maintains the same respect for murtis, the manifest form of God and the Sant.
#2.)One who does not respect the {!murtis!} of God or the {!Sant!}:
##2.1)Does not have faith in God.
##2.2)He will not be liberated.
##2.3)His devotion is like that of a hypocrite.
#3.)If one develops a {!nāstik!} attitude toward God’s {!murtis!} and the {!Sant!}:
##3.1)One develops a {!nāstik!} attitude toward the manifest form of God and his abode.
##3.2)He believes that the creation, sustenance and dissolution of this cosmos is due to {!kāl, māyā!} and {!karma!}, but not due to the will of God.
#4.)The cause of developing a {!nāstik!} attitude:
##4.1)Listening to the scriptures of {!nāstiks!}.
##4.2)Keeping the company of {!nāstiks!}.
##4.3)Not believing in the talks of a {!Sant!} when one is overcome by {!swabhāvs!} such as lust, anger, etc.
#5.)Means to overcoming a {!nāstik!} attitude:
##5.1)Listening to talks of the divine actions and incidents of God
##5.2)Understanding the greatness of God and the {!Sant!}.

19771.t:
#1.){!Dharma!} involving violence:
##1.1)Is for the attainment of {!dharma, arth!} and {!kām!}.
##1.2)Is for the purpose of limiting violence.
##1.3)Is for fulfilling worldly desires, but it is not for the attainment of liberation.
#2.){!Dharma!} not involving violence:
##2.1)Is the {!dharma!} of a {!sādhu!}.
##2.2)Is only for the attainment of liberation.
#3.)The {!dharma!} of a {!sādhu!}:
##3.1)Should not bear malice to anyone by thought, word or deed.
##3.2)Should not harbour arrogance.
##3.3)Behave as a servant of servants.
##3.4)Behave in a calm manner.
#4.)Having a hostile personality is the dharma of a wicked person.
#5.)There is no shortage of people with an arrogant nature. To be a {!sādhu!}, though, is indeed very difficult.

19772.t:
#1.)In the battle that occurs within one’s heart between the words of {!kusangis!} and the words of the Sant:
##1.1)When the strength of {!kusangis!} increases, then a desire to indulge in the {!vishays!} arises.
##1.2)When the strength of the {!Sant!} increases, the desire to indulge in the {!vishays!} disappears.
##1.3)If one wins the fight with {!kusangis!}, he will go to God’s abode.
##1.4)If one who dies while fighting with {!kusangis!}, then God will help him.
#2.)Ways to increase the strength of the {!Sant!} and decrease the strength of {!kusang!}:
##2.1)Avoid the company of external {!kusangis!}.
##2.2)Keeping the company of the Sant residing externally.
#3.)Faith in God:
##3.1)When one practices Satsang for the sole purpose of his liberation but not due to a desire for material objects, then one’s faith in God remains firm.
##3.2)If one practises Satsang while nourishing desires for some objects and those desires are not fulfilled, one’s faith will diminish.
#4.)When one with faith in God encounters misery, one should understand that God reduces the suffering of being executed on a {!shuli!} to a mere thorn-prick.
#5.)Shriji Mahārāj asked for these two boons from Rāmānand Swāmi:
##5.1)“If your {!satsangi!} is destined to suffer the distress inflicted by the sting of one scorpion, may the distress of the stings of millions and millions of scorpions befall each and every pore of my body; but no pain should afflict your {!satsangi!}.”
##5.2)“If the begging bowl is written in the {!prārabdha!} of your {!satsangi!}, may that begging bowl come to Me; but on no account should your {!satsangi!} suffer from the lack of food or clothing.”

19773.t:
#1.)Which mistakes does God not forgive?
##1.1)Spiting a devotee of God.
##1.2)Denouncing the form of God.
#2.)All entities that the manifest form of God accepts become divine.
#3.)The form of jealousy: One who is jealous of someone cannot tolerate that person benefiting in any way; in fact, he would be pleased if misery befalls that person.
#4.)One who worships the manifest form of God understanding him to be with a divine form and who behaves in accordance with the {!niyams!} of Satsang will attain liberation.
#5.)When God incarnates for the purpose of granting liberation to the {!jivas!}, He is always accompanied by His Akshardhām, His attendants - who are formed of {!chaitanya!} - and all of His divine powers; but they are not perceived by others. Therefore, a devotee of God should realise this and he should also explain this fact to others.
#6.)God accepts the service of his devotees:
##6.1)For their liberation.
##6.2)To give them His everlasting bliss.

19774.t:
#1.)One who has faith in God coupled with the knowledge of His greatness:
##1.1)Realises the greatness of the {!sādhus!} and {!satsangis!}.
##1.2)Cannot be harmed by both {!kāl!} and {!karma!} due to the force of his {!bhakti!}.
##1.3)Extols the human-like actions of God perceiving them to be divine.
##1.4)Understands in this manner:
###i.)From the very day I had the {!darshan!} of God, my liberation has been guaranteed.
###ii.)Any {!jiva!} who has my {!darshan!} or accepts my advice will assuredly be redeemed.
##1.5)He believed himself to be fulfilled.
##1.6)Whatever spiritual endeavours he performs is solely to please God.
##1.7)He attains the highest state of enlightenment.
#2.)One who is a non-believer or one who does not have a firm conviction in God:
##2.1)Does not benefit in any way, even if God wishes to do good for that person.
##2.2)Perceives flaws in God when He performs human-like actions.
##2.3)Remains doubtful that “I have met God but will I be liberated or not?”
#3.)God becomes like a human and exhibits human-like {!swabhāvs!}:
##3.1)To give devotees the bliss of His {!darshan!} and service.
##3.2)To liberate countless {!jivas!}.
#4.)To realise all of God’s actions and incidents as redemptive is the very {!dharma!} of a devotee, and only one who understands this can be called a perfect devotee of God.
#5.)Behaving this way, one incurs a sin equivalent to killing a {!Brāhmin!}:
##5.1)Oppressing the meek.
##5.2)Making false allegations against someone.
##5.3)Forcing five types of women to lapse in their {!dharma!}.
#6.)Three types of devotees:
##6.1)Greatest devotee:
###i.)Believes himself to be the {!ātmā!}, distinct from his body and sees God dwelling within his {!ātmā!}.
###ii.)Realises God and the Sant of God to be superior to {!ātmā!}-realisation.
###iii.)Harbours not even the slightest conceit of the {!ātmā!}-realisation he has attained.
##6.2)Average devotee: despite having knowledge of the {!ātmā!} and faith in God, becomes jealous of God and devotees of God and perceives faults in them.
##6.3)Lowest type:
###i.)Does not have {!ātmā!}-realisation.
###ii.)Has affection for God as well as for the affairs of this world.
###iii.)Having affection for affairs of this world, experiences joy and grief in the affairs of this world.

19775.t:
#1.)Whenever a thought related to women arises in the mind, semen is discharged through the genitals; if one does not allow this, he has conquered lust and is called an {!urdhvaretā!} {!brahmachāri!}.
#2.)Means to becomes free of lust by God’s grace:
##2.1)Maintain the strength of God’s {!upāsanā!}.
##2.2)Become free of desires from the {!panchvishays!}.
##2.3)Worship God.
#3.)Means to become free from worldly desires:
##3.1){!Ātmā!}-realisation, understand the greatness of God, and {!vairāgya!}.
##3.2)Become free of flaws by understanding the {!Motāpurush!} to be free of flaws.
#4.)When one becomes free from worldly desires, then his {!indriyas!} no longer remain sharp and his desire to enjoy worldly pleasures is eradicated.
#5.)Reasons for coming out of {!samādhi!}:
##5.1)If one still harbours desires for worldly pleasures, the worldly pleasures will draw him out.
##5.2)If one is extremely powerful, he can return according to his own will.
##5.3)If another person is much more powerful than himself, that person can bring him back.
#6.)When in {!samādhi!}, if one regards the form of the manifest Purushottam Bhagwān to be inferior and believes the light of Brahma to be superior, a breach in {!upāsanā!} is committed.
#7.)One who has surrendered his mind:
##7.1)He is enthusiastic in {!darshan!} of God and listening to the talks of God.
##7.2)He remains happy living according to the commands of God.
##7.3)Even if he is hundreds of thousands of miles away, he is near Shriji Mahārāj.
#8.)One who has not surrendered his mind:
##8.1)He may be staying close to Shriji Mahārāj, yet he is hundreds of thousands of miles away.
##8.2)Shriji Mahārāj is afraid of even giving advice to him as He fears, ‘Will he accept it positively or adversely?”

19776.t:
#1.)When one encounters {!vishays!} or encounters times of hardship, then the extent of one’s {!vairāgya!} and one’s understanding can be measured.
#2.)Understanding of God’s doer-ship:
##2.1)One should remain happy if God seats us on an elephant or a donkey.
##2.2)Satsang grows according to the wish of God, so one should not harbour grief or joy.
##2.3)One should worship God remaining dependent on Him.

19777.t: #1.)If all the members of a family in which there is a devotee keep affection for that devotee with an understanding of his greatness, then all of the members of that family will attain liberation; if they keep animosity towards that devotee of God, then their minds will become polluted and they will fall into {!narak!}.\n#2.)One who has {!gnān, vairāgya, bhakti!} and {!dharma!} should be known to have perfect faith. If one of these four factors is lacking, his faith is without the knowledge of God’s greatness.

19778.t:
#1.)Shriji Mahārāj speaks about His own nature for the sake of revealing the ideals of a devotee:
##1.1)Shriji Mahārāj does not get along with an angry, jealous, deceitful, or egotistical person.
##1.2)He does not believe that a lustful person is a {!satsangi!}.
##1.3)He effortlessly and naturally develops affection for one who is a perfect devotee.
#2.)Characteristics of one who is a perfect devotee:
##2.1)Has no deficiency in observance of the {!panch-vartmān!}.
##2.2)Remains totally undisturbed until the end of his life regardless of whatever stern commands God may impose - even if God compels him to forsake his preferences and enforce His own.
##2.3)Possesses perfect {!bhakti!} for God in his heart.

19779.t:
#1.)Whoever forsakes {!dharma!} - in the form of the five religious vows - solely advocating the strength of {!bhakti!} or {!gnān!}, is a blasphemer of the guru and guru’s word.
#2.)A person who has faith in God acquires the redemptive virtues of God and the 30 attributes of a {!sādhu!}, and therefore he is considered a true {!sādhu!}.
#3.)The fate of a non-believer and a devotee of God at the end of life:
##3.1)Even if a non-believer dies in a pleasant way, he will go to {!narak!}.
##3.2)A devotee of God will still go to the abode of God, whether he dies whilst walking or talking, babbling incoherently or silently, or whilst suffering.
##3.3)If one dies while thoroughly realising one’s {!jivātmā!} as transcending the three states and as being {!brahmarup!}, one passes away while displaying the powers of God.

19780.t:
#1.)The eight factors of influence become favourable or unfavourable due to the influence of God or His {!Bhakta!}, but not because of {!karmas!} of previous births.
#2.)Means to prevent a fault-finding attitude toward God and His {!Sādhu!}
##2.1)Unwavering faith in God.
##2.2)Thinking about the greatness of the servants of God.
#3.)By maintaining loyalty to Satsang:
##3.1)One’s foundation in Satsang becomes strong.
##3.2)Ego and other inner enemies are eradicated.
##3.3)One gains trust from God and the {!Sant!}.
#4.)To please God, one should:
##4.1)Not wish for bodily comforts.
##4.2)Not crave for the {!darshan!} of God.
##4.3)Do exactly as God commands.
##4.4)Follow the five religious vows completely.
##4.5)Endeavour to eradicate one’s {!swabhāvs!}.
#5.)“Wherever God and His {!Sant!} reside is the abode of God; and I reside in that abode of God” – one who understands this way: experiences awe all day and night and sways in an ocean of bliss.
#6.)God - who transcends Akshar, who is beyond mind and speech, and who is imperceptible - becomes perceivable to all people out of compassion.
#7.)How can one acquire the 30 attributes of a {!sādhu!}?
##7.1)Regard the {!Sant!} who possesses the 30 attributes as a guru and as a deity.
##7.2)Associate with that {!Sant!} by thought, word and deed.
#8.)God and the {!Sant!} bestows compassion on those who bear animosity toward their {!swabhāvs!}, so that:
##8.1)One experiences extreme bliss in their heart.
##8.2)One’s strength to walk on the path of liberation increases.
##8.3)The strength of one’s inner enemies decreases.
#9.)One still fears God even while away from God, if one understands this way:
##9.1)God dwells within every atom in His {!antaryāmi!} form just as He is in His manifest form.
##9.2)God is the all-doer, controller of all, and supporter of all.
#10.)The {!jiva’s!} liberation is cause by doing exactly as the {!Sant!} says without harbouring any doubts.
#11.)As one understands the greatness of the manifest form of God:
##11.1)One’s vicious nature is destroyed.
##11.2)One develops affection for God and His {!Sant!}.
##11.3)One remains unflinching in the nine types of {!bhakti!}.

19781.t:
#1.)One who has conquered the mind:
##1.1)Has no desires to indulge in the {!vishays!}.
##1.2)Has shunned the {!panchvishays!} with absolute resolution.
#2.)Means to defeat the desire for {!vishays!}:
##2.1){!Ātmā!}-realization: Subduing the affection for {!vishays!} with the understanding that one’s {!ātmā!} is distinct from the physical body.
##2.2)Understanding the glory of God in this manner:
###i.)This manifest form of God is the master of all (the realms of the deities and abodes such as Golok, Vaikunth, etc.) and forever resides in my {!ātmā!}.
###ii.)The bliss from the {!darshan!} of God for one second is greater than the pleasure derived from all the {!vishays!} of countless millions of {!brahmānds!}.
###iii.)The realms of the other deities are like {!narak!} compared to Akshardhām.
#3.)If one attempts to renounce the {!vishays!} without this understanding, then he will develop affection for the {!vishays!} in adverse circumstances (i.e. when he encounters an alluring {!vishay!}).

19782.t:
#1.)The mutual love that develops from the virtues of speech, deeds, and mind will not dissolve.
##1.1)How should one behave with their speech:
###i.)One should not hurt any living beings with one’s speech.
###ii.)One should purposely accept defeat before God and senior {!sādhus!}.
###iii.)If a command by God or His Sant seems inappropriate and leads to doubts, then one should, humbly and with {!bhakti!}, compromise with them or have a senior {!sādhu!} reach a compromise with them; but one should not immediately refuse to abide by it.
##1.2)How should one behave physically:
###i.)One should weaken the body by engaging in worship or by observing the {!chāndrāyan!} vow; but one should not take care of one’s own body.
###ii.)One should physically serve God and His devotees.
##1.3)How should one behave mentally 
###i.)One should do {!darshan!} of God with an attentive mind and concentrated vision and internalise that form exactly as it is in one’s heart.
#2.)When one does {!darshan!} or listens while keeping an attentive mind and a fixed gaze:
##2.1)One feels divinity of God in their mind.
##2.2)The {!darshan!} and discourses remains novel.
##2.3)The mind becomes stable.
#3.)When one does not do {!darshan!} or does not listen while keeping an attentive mind and a fixed gaze:
##3.1)God and the {!Sant!} are not pleased.
##3.2)He declines from Satsang day by day.
##3.3)He forgets the {!darshan!} he has done or discourses he has heard.
#4.)One should reprimand one’s eyes and ears to keep them under control whilst doing {!darshan!} of God.

19783.t:
#1.)If a person performs pujā of God emotionally and lovingly, then physical pujā and {!mānsi pujā!} are both superior; if pujā is performed without any emotions or love, then both physical pujā and {!mānsi pujā!} are inferior.
#2.)Characteristics of one who performs physical pujā or {!mānsi pujā!} with overwhelming love:
##2.1)He has intense {!shraddhā!} in performing the pujā of God and serving Him, in listening to discourses related to God, and in singing devotional songs.
##2.2)He also understands the profound greatness of God.
##2.3)With each passing day, his {!shraddhā!} and understanding of God’s greatness remain ever fresh, but never diminish.
#3.){!Shravan, manan, nididhyās!} and {!sākshātkār!}:
##3.1){!Shravan!}: listening to discourses of God.
##3.2){!Manan!}: having heard the talks, mentally pondering over the talk and retaining that which should be retained and discarding the rest.
##3.3){!Nididhyās!}: recalling the talks day and night.
##3.4){!Sākshātkār!}: recalling that talk exactly as it was - as if it were manifest before oneself - with absolute clarity and spontaneity.
#4.)The {!sākshātkār!} of the {!ātmā!} and Paramātmā:
##4.1)Can only occur by continuously doing {!shravan, manan!}, and {!nididhyās!}.
##4.2)Even if one does {!darshan!} or {!shravan!} for the rest of one’s life, one will not attain {!sākshātkār!} without {!manan!} and {!nididhyās!}.

19784.t:
#1.)Distinction between the {!ātmā!} and the non-{!ātmā!} (i.e. the physical body):
##1.1)The {!ātmā!} and the physical body are distinct.
##1.2)One should believe one’s self to be the {!ātmā!} and none of the characteristics of the physical body apply to the {!ātmā!}.
##1.3)After becoming totally free of worldly desires, one should believe oneself to be {!chaitanya!} (the {!ātmā!}) and contemplate upon Purushottam Bhagwān.
#2.)If one has not developed this firm distinction, he may think of the {!ātmā!} all day, but if he believes himself to be the body and fantasises about women, even for just a moment, then all of his thoughts are futile.
#3.)What happens if one dies without becoming totally free of worldly desires?
##3.1)The fate of a devotee of God:
###i.)He will attain the realms of the deities, which are described as comparable to {!naraks!} before the abode of God (but he does not enter the cycles of births and deaths).
###ii.)After indulging in the realm of deities, he will become a human again and attain God’s abode by doing {!bhakti!}.
##3.2)The fate of a non-devotee: He will go to Yampuri or re-enter the cycle of births and deaths.
#4.)Understanding a devotee of God should keep:
##4.1)If anything dies, it is this body; but I am the {!ātmā!}.
##4.2)One should not become discouraged seeing the force of worldly desires.
##4.3)Joyfully worship God.
##4.4)One should remain vigilant in trying to eradicate his desires for worldly pleasures.
##4.5)One Should maintain absolute faith in the words of God and the {!Sant!} of God.

19785.t:
#1.)Method of eradicating worldly desires from the heart:
##1.1){!Shraddhā!}.
##1.2)Faith in the words of God and His devotees.
##1.3)Affection for God.
##1.4)Understanding God’s greatness.
##1.5){!Bhakti!} coupled with the knowledge of God’s greatness is the most powerful method.
#2.){!Anvay-vyatirek!}:
##2.1){!Jiva!}: 
###i.){!Anvay!}: when the {!jiva!} is said to be the experiencer of births and deaths
###ii.){!Vyatirek!}: the uncuttable, unpierceable and eternal form of the {!jiva!}.
##2.2){!Ishwar!}: 
###i.){!Anvay!}: when {!ishwar!} behaves as one with its three bodies
###ii.){!Vyatirek!}: {!ishwar!} is described as transcending its three bodies.
##2.3)Akshar: 
###i.){!Anvay!}: the pervasive form in Prakruti-Purush, etc. and inspirer of all
###ii.){!Vyatirek!}: Akshardhām and the {!sevāk!} form in that Akshardhām 
##2.4)Parabrahma 
###i.){!Anvay!}: form is that which resides in the hearts of all as their witness. 
###ii.){!Vyatirek!}: is the form that resides in Akshardhām.
#3.)Who receives the fruits of chanting God’s name, the touch of God and the {!darshan!} of God?
##3.1)One who thoroughly understands God’s greatness.
##3.2)One who develops intense affection towards God.
##3.3)One who concentrates all his {!indriyas!} while engaging in God’s {!darshan!}.

19786.t:
#1.)That in which the {!jivātmā!} dwells when it indulges in the {!vishays!} is known as a ‘state’ ({!avasthā!}). The three states:
##1.1)Waking: {!sattvagun!} prevails
##1.2)Dream: {!rajogun!} prevails
##1.3)Deep sleep: {!tamogun!} prevails
#2.)The mode of indulgence in the three states:
##2.1)Waking:
###i.)With consciousness of one’s {!sthul!} body, the {!jivātmā!} indulges in the external {!vishays!} with discretion and according to its past {!karmas!}.
###ii.)It is the result of the sustenance state of {!ishwar!} and is located in the eye.
###iii.)Dream state within the waking state: {!jivātmā!} indulges in the pleasures of the external {!vishays!} inappropriately due to some misconception.
###iv.)Deep sleep within the waking state: {!jivātmā!} indulges in the pleasures of the external {!vishays!} without discretion due to sorrow, fatigue, etc.
##2.2)Dream: 
###i.)With the consciousness of its {!sukshma!} body, the {!jivātmā!} indulges in the {!vishays!} (via the mind) according to its past {!karmas!}.
###ii.)It is the result of the creation state of {!ishwar!} and is located in the throat.
###iii.)Waking state within the dream state: the {!jivātmā!} indulges in the {!vishays!} (via the mind) with discretion.
###iv.)Deep sleep within the dream state: the {!jivātmā!} indulges in the {!vishays!} (via the mind) without discretion.
##2.3)Deep sleep: 
###i.)The {!vruttis!} of the {!indriyas!} and the {!antahkaran!}, the desires for the pleasures of the {!vishays!}, as well as its sense of knowership and doership all become merged in the {!kāran!} body.
###ii.)It is the result of the dissolution state of {!ishwar!}.
###iii.)Dream state within deep sleep: the {!jivātmā!} indulges in {!vishays!} with a sense of doership.
###iv.)Waking state within deep sleep: the {!jivātmā!} indulges in {!vishays!} without a sense of doership.
#3.)God is whom the {!jivātmā!} obtains knowledge of these distinctions between the states, and who gives the {!jiva!} the fruits of its {!karmas!} accordingly within those states.
#4.)Four types of speech dwell in the body of {!jivas!}:
##4.1){!Parāvāni!}: explains the differences between {!jiva, ishwar, māyā!}, Brahma and Parabrahma and describes God’s divine actions and incidents.
##4.2){!Vaikhari!}: gives a complete explanation of worldly entities and {!vishays!} with discretion.
##4.3){!Madhyamā!}: gives an incomplete explanation of entities and {!vishays!}, thus creating confusion.
##4.4){!Pashyanti!}: blindly describes those entities and {!vishays!} as being the same, and which cannot be understood.

19787.t:
#1.)Naimishāranya Kshetra (in the form of the profound association of the {!Sant!}):
##1.1)When one commences pious deeds there, they flourish rapidly.
##1.2)One should seek liberation there.
##1.3)One should remain there with an absolutely resolute mind.
##1.4)The sharp edges (in the form of the ten {!indriyas!}) of the {!chakra!} (the mind) become blunt (are withdrawn from their {!vishays!}).
#2.)Characteristics of one whose {!indriyas!} have become blunt:
##2.1)Affection toward the {!panchvishays!} does not remain.
##2.2)A strong aversion toward the alluring {!vishays!}.
##2.3)No matter how alluring a {!vishay!} may be, one’s {!indriyas!} rebound from that {!vishay!} but do not get attached to it.

19788.t: #1.)Cause of jealousy: egotism.\n#2.)Characteristic of jealousy: one cannot bear to see someone greater than oneself being honoured.\n#3.)Extreme jealousy: One cannot bear anyone’s greatness.

19789.t:
#1.)The {!gunas!} are the reason the {!dharmas!} of the {!yugs!} prevail in one’s heart. The cause of the activities of those {!gunas!} are {!karmas!}.
##1.1)When pure {!sattvagun!} is prevalent, Satya-yug prevails in the heart.
##1.2)When {!sattvagun!} and {!rajogun!} are prevalent together, Tretā-yug prevails in the heart.
##1.3)When {!rajogun!} and {!tamogun!} are prevalent together, Dwāpar-yug prevails in the heart.
##1.4)When {!tamogun!} alone is prevalent, Kali-yug prevails in the heart.
#2.)A person in whom {!rajogun!} and {!tamogun!} are prevalent should:
##2.1)Utilise the strength of {!ātmā!}-realisation and God’s greatness.
##2.2)Not insist on meditating or concentrating.
##2.3)Engage in physical worship as much as possible.
##2.4)Physically serve God and the {!Sant!} with {!shraddhā!}.
##2.5)Abide by his {!dharma!}.
##2.6)Believe himself to be fulfilled.
#3.)If one has intense {!shraddhā!} and extremely firm faith in the words of God and the {!Sant!}:
##3.1)Whatever type of {!tāmasik!} {!karmas!} one may have performed will be destroyed.
##3.2)The {!dharma!} of Kali-yug will also vanish, and the {!dharma!} of Satya-yug will prevail.
##3.3)No fault will remain in one’s heart.
##3.4)One will become {!brahmarup!} in this very lifetime.
#4.)What can be called ‘sthān’?
##4.1)An individual’s {!dharma!} according to the four castes and the four {!āshrams!} 
##4.2)If a renunciant were to leave his fold and tread the path of householders, then he has diverted from his ‘sthān’.
##4.3)Even in the most difficult circumstances or if Shriji Mahārāj were to issue a command, one should not deviate from their {!dharma!}.

19790.t:
#1.)Two types of people:
##1.1)One who follows the path of righteousness:
###i.)Forsakes misdeeds, and fears God 
###ii.)Everyone trusts him.
###iii.)Likes the company of a true {!sādhu!} and stays within of disciples of {!dharma!}.
##1.2)One who follows the path of unrighteousness:
###i.)Engages in evil deeds.
###ii.)No one trusts him.
###iii.)Does not like the company of a true {!sādhu!} and spites those who do.
#2.)One who aspires to attain liberation should follow the path of righteousness and keep the company of a true {!sādhu!}.
#3.)From a physical perspective:
##3.1)The abode of God is very far away.
##3.2)Is not very beneficial.
#4.)From the perspective of the {!ātmā!}:
##4.1)God’s abode in not even an atom’s distance away.
##4.2)My {!chaitanya!} is distinct from the three bodies and God forever resides there.
#5.)The greatness of a {!Sant!} with the perspective of the {!ātmā!} 
##5.1)God and God’s abode it not even an atom’s distance away from him.
##5.2){!Darshan!} of him is the same as the {!darshan!} of God.
##5.3)He is fulfilled.
##5.4)If that {!Sant!} were to daily beat a person five times with a pair of shoes and he tolerates it, and in no way can he abandon his association with the {!Sant!}, then whatever that {!Sant!} attains he also attains.

19791.t:
#1.)One who endeavours personally:
##1.1)By the words of the {!Sadguru!} and the scriptures, his {!vairāgya, brahmacharya, shraddhā, dharma!} of non-violence, and {!ātmā!}-realisation become extremely firm.
##1.2)Is freed from the eternal ignorance of {!māyā!}.
##1.3)Is relieved from the burden of births and deaths.
##1.4)God’s grace is bestowed upon him, with which:
###i.)He becomes an {!Ekāntik!} {!Bhakta!}.
###ii.)He is not bound by pure and impure {!karmas!}.
###iii.)He attains Akshardhām.
#2.)One who has deficiencies in virtues such a {!vairāgya, brahmacharya, shraddhā!}, etc.:
##2.1)Does not attain Akshardhām.
##2.2)Does not become worthy of God’s grace.
##2.3)Does not enter the cycle of births and deaths; but instead attains the realms of the deities.
#3.)If a person becomes extremely determined and focuses his {!vruttis!} on God, then his deficiencies would be eradicated in the current lifetime.

19792.t:
#1.)Three virtues constantly remain in {!sādhus!}: 
##1.1){!Ātmā!}-realisation
##1.2){!Swadharma!}
##1.3)Faith in God ({!nishchay!}).
#2.)Understanding of a person with perfect {!gnān!}:
##2.1)The physical body and the {!ātmā!} are distinct
##2.2)He believes his {!ātmā!} to be {!brahmarup!} and Parabrahma forever resides in that {!brahmarup!} {!ātmā!} 
##2.3)His conviction of God remains forever steady.
#3.)The method of contemplating on the {!ātmā!}:
##3.1)When one is active in the {!sthul!} body, one should never look towards the desires arising in the {!sukshma!} body.
##3.2)When one is active in the {!antahkaran!}, one should become oblivious of one’s {!sthul!} body.
##3.3)The physical body and the {!ātmā!} are completely distinct. The traits of the physical body are not found in the {!ātmā!}, and the traits of the {!ātmā!} are not found in the physical body.
#4.)By applying a thought process, but not force, when one withdraws one’s {!vrutti!} from the {!vishays!}, the desires for {!vishays!} are eradicated.
#5.)As long as enemies in the form of the mind and the {!indriyas!} continue to trouble oneself, one should firmly contemplate on the distinction between the {!ātmā!} and the physical body.

19793.t:
#1.)The benefits gained from the scriptures:
##1.1)One develops faith in God ({!nishchay!}) because the characteristics of God and the {!Sant!} are described within.
##1.2)They are the inspiration behind the activities of {!dharma!}.
#2.)One who trusts the words of the scriptures:
##2.1)Develops unshakeable faith in God.
##2.2)Never turns away from God.
##2.3)Attains liberation.
##2.4)Never deviates from {!dharma!}.
#3.)One who does not have faith in the words of the scriptures:
##3.1)Loses his faith in God.
##3.2)Should be knows as obstinate and a {!nāstik!}.

19794.t:
#1.)God is extremely powerful:
##1.1)Without His wish, no one falls from His abode after having attained it.
##1.2)By His will, that which is {!jad!} (non-living, inanimate) can become {!chaitanya!} (possessing consciousness), and that which is {!chaitanya!} can become {!jad!}.
#2.)Those who have become enlightened through {!brahmacharya, vairāgya, ātmā!}-realisation, and {!bhakti!} towards God never fall from God’s abode.
#3.)Laziness and infatuation:
##3.1)Those who discard these two transgresses {!māyā!}.
##3.2)If one does not discard these two and behaves carelessly, then these will hinder a devotee.
##3.3)If a devotee remains vigilant, then he can eradicate both these; whereas, a non-believer cannot eradicate these.
#4.)The {!sthul!} body and the {!sukshma!} body:
##4.1)Both are interwoven with each other.
##4.2)For one who possesses the knowledge of the {!ātmā!}, he is not affected by the {!karmas!} of the {!sthul!} and {!sukshma!} bodies; therefore, when he discards his body, God grants him a divine body with which he resides in the abode of God.
##4.3)A person who identifies his self with the body is affected by all {!karmas!} related to the {!sthul!} and {!sukshma!} bodies, and he suffers the torments of Yampuri.

19795.t:
#1.)A devotee who has deep love for God but lacks {!ātmā!}-realisation and {!vairāgya!}:
##1.1)His {!bhakti!} may look extremely appealing, but in reality it is extremely inferior.
##1.2)When he comes in contact with bad company ({!kusang!}), then his intellect becomes polluted; he constantly craves {!vishays!}; and his love for God does not remain.
#2.)A devotee who has deep love for God along with {!ātmā!}-realisation and {!vairāgya!}:
##2.1)He may not seem outwardly enthusiastic for the {!darshan!}, touch, etc., of God’s form; however, the roots of his love are very deep and he is {!ekāntik!}.
##2.2)His love for God will not diminish even due to influence of bad company.
#3.)One who has thoroughly realised God’s greatness, then due to the power of that realisation, the virtues of {!ātmā!}-realisation and {!vairāgya!} naturally flourished in his heart.
#4.)The three types of {!gopis!}:
##4.1)Obstinate:
###i.)They would become upset with God.
###ii.)They would speak such harsh words to God, that one would feel they will fall from the path of God.
##4.2)Mediocre:
###i.)They would never become angry with God.
###ii.)They would not speak harsh words to God.
###iii.)Using their shrewdness, they would cunningly conceal their selfishness from others, thereby doing whatever they please, while also doing whatever pleases God.
##4.3)Mature:
###i.)They would do only that which pleases God.
###ii.)They would not do whatever they please using shrewdness to satisfy their selfishness.
###iii.)Their only wish is to please God.
###iv.)They would not become angry at or jealous of the other {!gopis!}.
###v.)They would not behave in any way that would displease God.

19796.t:
#1.)Out of Compassion, God performs austerities for the sake of his devotees, but not for those who are not devotees.
#2.)Due to the power of God’s austerities:
##2.1)The devotee’s virtues of {!dharma, gnān!}, etc., even if in lesser degree, flourish greatly in just a short span of time.
##2.2)The devotee has the {!darshan!} of God in his heart.
##2.3)The devotee attains liberation without any hindrances.

19797.t:
#1.)As the vision of a person who worships God becomes increasingly subtle:
##1.1)He realises the unlimited nature of God.
##1.2)He increasingly realises the greatness of God.
##1.3)His {!vrutti!} attaches itself more and more to God with love, 
##1.4)His {!upāsanā!} of God becomes even more firmly established.
#2.)As a devotee becomes worthy and his powers increase:
##2.1)He realises the greatness of God to a greater level.
##2.2)His master-servant relationship with God is further consolidated.
#3.)As a devotee worships God and the barriers are gradually overcome, he becomes increasingly luminous and powerful, whilst attaining immense bliss.
#4.)As obstacles in the form of {!māyā!} are overcome, and one increasingly attains the proximity of God:
##4.1)One realises the unlimited greatness of God.
##4.2)One’s sense of servitude towards Him is increasingly strengthened.

19798.t:
#1.)If a person with {!shraddhā!} develops {!shraddhā!} in the words of a true {!Sant!}, then:
##1.1)Redemptive virtues of {!swadharma, vairāgya, gnān, bhakti!}, wisdom, etc., would develop in his heart.
##1.2)Vicious natures of lust, anger, etc., would be burnt away.
#2.)Reasons for developing vicious natures such as lust, anger, etc.:
##2.1)If a person who has virtues of {!swadharma, vairāgya!}, etc., firmly rooted in his heart and who has not even the slightest desire for the pleasures of this world were to meet with evil company
##2.2)Youthful age.
##2.3)If one perceives faults in a {!Motāpurush!}, then all of those faults dwell in his own heart.
#3.)Means to eradicate one’s {!swabhāvs!}:
##3.1)Association of a {!Sant!} with {!shraddhā!}.
##3.2)Endeavouring to eradicate them with understanding and thoughtfulness.
##3.3)Keeping an account of {!swabhāvs!} like a merchant – have my vicious {!swabhāvs!} increased or decreased since entering the Satsang fellowship?
##3.4)Bearing an aversion to one’s {!swabhāvs!} followed by the grace of God
##3.5)Understands a {!Motāpurush!} to be {!nirdosh!} and imbibing His virtues.

19799.t:
#1.)When the conviction of God develops in the {!buddhi!}, one should realise conviction has also developed in the {!jiva!}.
#2.)The powers of the {!jiva!}: it is extremely subtle, yet it illuminates the body, {!indriyas!}, and the {!antahkaran!} at once.
#3.)Three types of conviction:
##3.1)Conviction in the {!indriyas!}: No doubts arise when God engages in appropriate or inappropriate actions.
##3.2)Conviction in the {!antahkaran!}: No doubts arise when God exhibits {!tamogun!}, (laziness, sleepiness, etc.);  {!rajogun!} (lust, anger, etc.); or {!sattvagun!} (tranquillity, self-restraint, etc.).
##3.3)Conviction in the {!jiva!}: No doubts arise when God behaves eccentrically and shows His {!gunātit!} state.
#4.)How can the {!māyik!} {!indriyas!} and {!antahkaran!} perceive God who is beyond the mind and speech; he is {!gunātit!}?
##4.1)Just as a bee captures a worm, stings it and then buzzes over it, and as a result, that worm is transformed into a bee; similarly, a {!jiva’s!} {!indriyas!} and {!antahkaran!} become divine by the profound association of the Sant, and the {!jiva!} is able to perceive the manifest form of God.

19800.t:
#1.)If one’s intellect is cursed, even if he has faith in God and the Sant, he will perceive flaws in them.
#2.)Reasons for one’s intellect being cursed:
##2.1)Having pained a great Sant.
##2.2)Having hurt a meek person.
##2.3)Not having served his parents.
#3.)Remedy for cursed intellect - observe {!niyams!} to a greater extent than everyone else.
#4.){!Karmas!} are without a form, but the fruits of those {!karmas!} have a form.

19801.t:
#1.)Virtues and faults cannot be discerned from an individual’s superficial behaviour; they can be discerned only after staying with him (i.e. observing the individual’s activities).
#2.)If a person is determined in his youth to eradicate vicious thoughts, then he progresses. Conversely, if he remains complacent instead of being alert, then he will not progress.
#3.)Characteristics of one who is virtuous in childhood:
##3.1)Does not like the company of immature children.
##3.2)Does not have an appetite for tasty food.
##3.3)Continuously restrains his body.
#4.)Faults due to the body and the mind:
##4.1)Faults of the body removed by imposing bodily restraints.
##4.2)Faults of the mind eradicated by contemplation, ‘I am the {!ātmā!}’.
##4.3)A great {!sādhu!} is one who restrains his body and contemplates on his {!ātmā!}. One remains like that due t the company of a great sādhu. 
#5.)If a renunciant desires to indulge in the worldly pleasures which are appropriate only for a householder, then:
##5.1)He is as good as an animal eating dry grass.
##5.2)He is a fool.
##5.3)He has not understood the talks of renunciation.

19802.t: #1.)The {!buddhi!} pervades the body from head to toe. The awareness of the {!buddhi!} is due to the awareness of the {!jiva!}.\r\n#2.)God resides within the {!jiva!}. The awareness of the {!jiva!} is due to the power of God’s awareness.\r\n#3.)While residing in Akshardhām with a definite form, God pervades the {!jivas!} through his {!antaryāmi!} powers. Even that {!antaryāmi!} form should be considered to possess a form.

19803.t:
#1.)Purpose of God assuming an {!avatār!} on earth:
##1.1)Having surrendered himself to his devotees’ bhakti. He grants bliss to devotees who have intense love for him.
##1.2)Fulfil all of the desires of His devotees.
##1.3)Grant liberation to innumerable {!jivas!}. 
##1.4)Establish {!dharma!}.

19804.t:
#1.)  God is pleased with a devotee who becomes free of lust, anger, avarice, deceit, egotism, jealousy and {!matsar!} and then offers {!bhakti!} to God.
#2.){!Matsar!}:
##2.1)Is the root of all vices.
##2.2)Is subtler than all of the other vices.
##2.3)Characteristics: if someone else gives and someone else receives, a person who possesses {!matsar!} burns with envy unnecessarily.
##2.4)Causes: women, wealth, sumptuous food, and ego.
#3.)A sādhu without {!matsar!} is worthy of possessing {!bhāgwat!} {!dharma!}.
#4.)Shriji Mahārāj speaks about His own nature for the sake of revealing the ideals of a devotee:
##4.1)He does not have even the slightest bit of lust, anger, avarice, egotism, {!matsar!} or jealousy in His heart.
##4.2)He experiences a strong aversion towards the {!panchvishays!}.
##4.3)He accepts food or clothes on seeing the {!bhakti!} of devotees, but not for His own physical pleasure.
##4.4)Just like {!ākāsh!}, he is unaffected by anything – those who constantly stay near Him know this.
##4.5)He has sacrificed His body for the sake of the devotees of God.
#5.)Characteristics of a perfect devotee of God:
##5.1)Possess resolute love only for God.
##5.2)Become dejected by enticing {!vishays!}.
##5.3)Indulge in ordinary {!vishays!} only to sustain their body.

19805.t:
#1.)How should a householder behave in order to fix his {!vrutti!} constantly on God?
##1.1)Thoughts of {!sānkhya!}: Just has one does not have any sense of my-ness for the relatives of one’s past lives, one should not keep any sense of my-ness for the relatives of this body.
##1.2)Maintain affection only towards God.
##1.3)Keep the company of a {!sādhu!}.
#2.)If one cannot abide by the above three resolutions (1a-1c), then they should:
##2.1)Abide by the {!dharma!} of Satsang.
##2.2)Rely on the strength of God and the Sant.
#3.)Hearing the words of the scriptures and the {!satpurush!}, one develops an obsession for {!vairāgya!} that does not diminish.
##3.1)If that obsession subsides, then he falls from both paths (i.e. path of renunciation and path of a householder).
##3.2)If that obsession does not diminish, he attains the highest state of enlightenment.
#4.)One who possesses the following understanding in the manifest form of God, then that itself is ultimate liberation:
##4.1)After the final dissolution ({!ātyantik-pralay!}), God forever remains in Akshardhām unaffected.
##4.2)God is divine, forever possesses a form.
##4.3)When He assumes a human form on the earth, He is still divine and {!gunātit!} (devoid of the {!māyik!} {!gunas!}).
#5.)One who has attained God-realisation through such a conviction experiences the following: Wherever he casts his eyes he sees the form of God (the same form in Akshardhām) as if it is before his eyes. 
#6.)The understanding of an ignorant fool: When God assumes a human form, He possesses {!māyik!} {!gunas!}.

19806.t:
#1.){!Sagun!} and {!nirgun!} aspects are the transcendental, divine powers of God.
##1.1)The {!nirgun!} form of God is much subtler than that which is subtle ({!sukshma!}). It is pure, untainted and unaffected by the five {!bhuts!} ({!pruthvi, jal, tej, vāyu, ākāsh!}), powerful and luminous.
##1.2)The {!sagun!} form of God is extremely vast such that the infinite {!brahmānds!} are like mere atoms in comparison. 
#2.)The manifest form of God, visible in a human form, is the eternal and original form of God.
#3.)If a devotee realises the {!nirgun!} and {!sagun!} aspects in God’s form in this manner, then {!kāl, karma!} and {!māyā!} would be incapable of binding him, and throughout the day he would continuously experience wonder in his heart.

19807.t:
#1.)Someone who has a spiteful obstinacy that develops into a grudge for someone and never forsakes that grudge but continues to be obstinate like a buffalo cannot be called a {!sādhu!}.
#2.)A person who possesses the {!bhakti!} of God in his heart and realises the greatness of God:
##2.1)Would never develop a spiteful obstinacy towards a devotee of God.
##2.2)Would never see faults of devotees, however minor they may be.
##2.3)Would never develop animosity toward the devotees of God.
##2.4)Would look upon the devotees who have come into contact with God as equivalent to deities.
##2.5)Should be known to be a perfect {!satsangi!}.
#3.)One who has not realized the greatness of God and his devotees:
##3.1)Develops animosity toward the devotees of God.
##3.2)Should be known as being half-fallen, even if he is a {!satsangi!}.

19808.t:
#1.)After noticing an illness in Mahārāj’s body, Muktānand Swāmi said, “Mahārāj it seems to be a serious illness. It seems that the times are tough for the {!satsangis!} right now; after all, Mahārāj! You are as vital to the {!satsangis!} as their lives, and any illness in Your body is the very definition of a difficult period for all {!satsangis!}.”
#2.)Austerities:
##2.1)A {!sādhu!} who is wise should also behave so as to deliberately induce suffering to his body and {!indriyas!}.
##2.2)Austerities are a means to please God.
#3.)God is the all-doer:
##3.1)Understanding this is the supreme cause of liberation.
##3.2)Not understanding this is the greatest sin.
#4.)One should immediately shun the company of those persons and those scriptures that refute the {!upāsanā!} of God and break one’s master-servant relationship with God.
#5.)One can become like {!Brahmā, Shiv, Shukji!} or {!Nārad!}. They may become like {!Prakruti-Purush!} or {!Akshar!}. But no one is capable of becoming like Shri Purushottam Nārāyan.
#6.)If the person who is offering {!bhakti!} to God with such lavish objects does so without any desires, solely for the purpose of earning God’s pleasure, then it is all right. If, on the other hand, he is tempted by those objects, viewing them to be God’s {!prasād!}, and, leaving God aside, if he develops affection for those objects, then by indulging in the {!vishays!}, he will become engrossed in them and corrupted by them.
#7.)A person who has great zeal in any endeavour would never be hindered, even if he were to face thousands of obstacles.

19809.t:
#1.)Characteristic of affection for God: One would never disobey the wishes of God, who is his beloved.
#2.)A devotee who has deep affection for God and treats the worldly {!panchvishays!} that are not related to God as vain:
##2.1)Wherever such a devotee goes by God’s command, the form of God also goes with him.
##2.2)God does not leave the heart of that devotee even for a fraction of a second.
##2.3)That devotee maintains a constant relationship with God.

19810.t:
#1.)Just as the skin of a tamarind seed is firmly attached to the seed, the {!kāran!} body is attached to the {!jiva!}.
#2.)Just as when a tamarind seed is roasted over a fire, the skin becomes detached and can then be peeled off easily, similarly, the {!kāran!} body is ‘roasted’ and becomes separated from the {!jiva!} easily if a person:
##2.1)Attains the company of the Sant and realizes the form of God through the words of the {!Sant!}.
##2.2)Meditates on that form of God.
##2.3)Imbibes the word of God in his heart.
#3.)Whatever one hears during the wakeful state, contemplates on it in the {!antahkaran!}, and the {!jivas!} endorses it, then that becomes thoroughly consolidated.
#4.)By listening to discourses of God with faith and love:
##4.1)The mind becomes stable and free of desires for {!vishays!}.
##4.2)All of his flaws would be eradicated.
##4.3)He becomes incapable of indulging in the {!panchvishays!}.

19811.t:
#1.)Anger:
##1.1)Shriji Mahārāj has an intense enmity toward anger.
##1.2)It makes the person appear ugly and makes one fall from the path of a {!sādhu!}.
##1.3)Even slight anger is a source of extreme misery.
#2.)Means to overcoming lust:
##2.1)Firm {!ātmā!}-realisation, firmness in observing the five religious vows ({!panch-vartmān!}), and fully understanding the greatness of God.
##2.2)Punishing the {!indriyas!} with austerities and the {!antahkaran!} with a thought process when they behave immorally.
#3.)Characteristics of devotees possessing the three levels of {!vairāgya!}:
##3.1)Lowest level: If he were to see a woman’s body, then his mind would get attached to that body, and he would not remain stable.
##3.2)Intermediate level: If he were to see a naked woman, then no disturbance would arise in his mind.
##3.3)Highest level: If he were to come across women and other worldly objects even in solitude, he would not be enticed.
#4.)Characteristics of devotees possessing the three levels of {!gnān!}:
##4.1)Lowest level: When he does not see God display powers, or when nothing untoward happens to an evil person who maligns God, then his conviction would not remain. Attains God-realization after countless lives.
##4.2)Intermediate level: When he sees pure and impure - seemingly human - actions of God, he would be deluded by them, and his conviction of God would not remain. Attains God-realization after 2-3 lives.
##4.3)Highest level: He would not be deluded even after seeing any type of pure or impure actions performed by God. Moreover, even if the person who initially convinced him of God loses conviction, his conviction would not diminish. Attains God-realization this life.
#5.)A person whose {!antahkaran!} burns due to the enemies of lust, anger, etc., would not believe himself to be fulfilled, even if he has faith in God.
#6.)Characteristics of one who has developed complete {!Satsang!}:
##6.1)Has extremely firm {!ātmā!}-realisation.
##6.2)Does not believe the actions of the body, {!indriyas!}, etc., to be his own.
##6.3)Behaves as {!brahmarup!}.
##6.4)Is firm in observance of the five religious vows and staunchly worships God maintaining a master-servant relationship.
##6.5)Realises the manifest form of God to be absolutely unaffected and understands His immense greatness.
##6.6)Serves God’s devotees menially.
#7.)Greatness of the {!Sant!}:
##7.1)The {!Sant!} follows the path of {!dharma!}.
##7.2)When the {!Sant!} sees a person treading the path of {!adharma!}, he rebukes that person. As a result, a person who identifies his self with the body will not know how to accept the advice positively and will harbour an aversion towards the {!Sant!}.
##7.3)One who harbours an aversion towards the {!Sant!} is unable to become pure by any form of atonement.
##7.4)He who perceives flaws in the {!Sant!} has had his head severed; he will certainly fall from {!Satsang!}.
#8.)If one has perceived flaws in the {!Sant!}, then the method to atone is:
##8.1)Maintaining intense {!shraddhā!}.
##8.2)Experiencing extreme remorse.
##8.3)Intensely perceiving virtues in the {!Sant!}.
##8.4)Pleasing the {!Sant!}with absolute humility.

19812.t:
#1.)There are four types of devotees of God who do not fear death, who feel completely fulfilled and are convinced of their liberation in this very life:
##1.1)One with faith ({!vishvās!}): He has established absolute faith in the words of God and His {!Sant!}.
##1.2)One with {!gnān!}: He has the strength of {!ātmā!}-realisation and believes, “I am {!brahmaswarup!} and a devotee of God.”
##1.3)One with courage: All of his {!indriyas!} and {!antahkaran!} tremble with fear. He is not afraid of anyone and does not transgress any of God’s injunctions in any way.
##1.4)One with affection: He has the inclination of a faithful wife – his {!vrutti!} is not drawn anywhere except in God.
#2.)A cause may be small and subtle, yet it is still capable of producing a vast effect – that is the very greatness of the cause. 
#3.)God appears like a human being, yet He is still the cause of everything and extremely powerful.

19813.t:
#1.)Characteristics of a person who has faith in God and His {!Sant!} coupled with the knowledge of their greatness:
##1.1)He would renounce his family, fear of public ridicule, a kingdom, pleasures, wealth, and wife/husband.
##1.2)He never disobeys the words of God; he does as God says.
##1.3)He has constant enthusiasm having attained God and his Sant.
##1.4)He is not elated or disappointed by the happiness or misery of the body; instead, he remains carefree and worships God.
##1.5)He increasingly understands the greatness of God and the Sant.
##1.6)He understands the difference in the death of a devotee of God and a non-believer. A devotee of God attains the abode of God, whereas a non-believer goes to Yampuri.
##1.7)He reaches Akshardhām with certainty but nowhere else.

19814.t:
#1.)While residing in His Akshardhām, God appears in countless forms in the countless millions of {!brahmānds!} for the sake of liberating devotees.
#2.)God is the greatest source of wonder and possesses all yogic powers:
##2.1)One who understands God as completely flawless ({!nirdosh!}) overcomes {!māyā!}.
##2.2)One who has doubts in God’s yogic powers (Why does God behave like that?) cannot be said to have overcome {!māyā!}.
#3.)The method for liberation is the same, but because of the levels and degree of {!shraddhā!} of devotees, many paths of liberation arise.
#4.)There is only one form of God; He is extremely powerful; and no one, including Akshar, is capable of becoming like God.
#5.)When Jhinābhāi became upset, Mahārāj gave the following teachings:
##5.1)While observing one’s own {!dharma!}, one should happily follow God’s commands.
##5.2)If one loves God but has a nature of becoming upset with him:
###i.)His love for God and {!bhakti!} will be lost in the end.
###ii.)The bliss God has given in the past will vanish.
###iii.){!Tamogun!} will envelop his mind and he will remain in a state of misery.
###iv.)He will not be able to carry out the commands of God completely.
##5.3)A devotee of God should remain ever joyful and should worship God with a cheerful mind. During adverse circumstances, one should not allow depression to enter his heart.

19815.t:
#1.)By revealing which thoughts to the Sant can one be considered to be honest, and by not revealing which thoughts can one be considered to be deceitful?
##1.1)Honest:
###i.)Any weakness in observing the five religious vows which cannot be overcome by one’s own thought process.
###ii.)Perceiving faults in the {!Sant!}.
###iii.)Any doubts in one’s conviction of God.
##1.2)Deceitful:
###i.)If any of the above thoughts are not disclosed to the {!Sant!}.
#2.)How can a deceitful and cunning person be recognised?
##2.1)By staying with him (keeping his company) – observing how he eats, drinks, etc.
##2.2)By having another person secretly observe him.
#3.)If a person attempts to eradicate an improper thought, but the thought still arises, then such a thought would cause him to fall from {!dharma!}. The same applies to one’s faith in God.
#4.)If one has the disposition of imbibing the virtues of a {!sādhu!}, then his foundation in Satsang becomes solid.
#5.)The method of controlling the {!indriyas!} and the {!antahkaran!}:
##5.1)By controlling the {!indriyas!}, the {!antahkaran!} can be controlled; but the {!indriyas!} cannot be controlled by controlling the {!antahkaran!}.
##5.2)From the scriptures: One should realise the greatness of God and His Sant.
##5.3)From the {!Sant!}: One should learn the techniques for controlling the {!indriyas!}.
##5.4)From one’s own thought process: look upon the techniques taught by the Sant positively as being for one’s own liberation. The one should behave accordingly.
##5.5)Means to controlling the {!indriyas!}: physical austerities, observance of {!niyams!}, listening to discourses of God.
##5.6)Means to controlling the {!antahkaran!}: contemplating on God’s glory, {!ātmā!}-realisation, and meditation.

19816.t:
#1.)To become {!ekāntik!} is an extremely difficult achievement.
#2.)Of the {!dharma!}-related endeavours, if one maintains the vow of non-lust ({!nishkām!}), all other endeavours will develop. Of the God-related endeavours, if one keeps the conviction of God, then all of the others will develop.
#3.)Thoughts related to conviction of God should never be altered. But on the advice of the {!Sant!}, one’s firm resolutions should be repeatedly altered.
#4.)Purifying one’s company:
##4.1)Whose company should be kept:
###i.)One who talks courageously with the backing of God’s strength and who is vigilant in eradicating one’s faults.
###ii.)A {!Sant!} who constantly reprimands one, talks about eradicating one’s faults, and does not pamper.
###iii.)A {!Sant!} who speaks harshly of one’s own relatives – one should listen to his words like {!amrut!}.
##4.2)Whose company should be abandoned:
###i.)One who has desires for worldly activities, identifies his self as the body, talks to others about the perceived flaws of God and the Sant.
###ii.)One who speaks discouragingly.
###iii.)One who emphasises his own efforts but does not acknowledge the strength of God.
###iv.)One who does not reprimand but pampers.
###v.)One who is lazy and sleeps too much.
###vi.)Out of vanity, one who boasts his virtues to be greater than virtues in others.
#5.)One should not maintain conceit before a staunch or meek devotee of God. One should maintain conceit before a person who has fallen back from Satsang.
#6.)One should follow God’s command and go wherever he commands one to go, but one should not keep any desire for the company of the Sant or God’s {!darshan!}. When God or a {!Sādhu!} have rebuked or expelled one and he is approached by a non-believer, then before him, one should exhibit tremendous affection towards the {!Sādhu!} and God.
#7.)If God were to give an order which seems to be full of {!adharma!}, then one should be hesitant in following it; that is, one should take some time and not accept it immediately.
#8.)When vicious thoughts arise, one should stop meditation and should clap and chant ‘Swāminārāyan, Swāminārāyan’ aloud, without shame. One should pray to God and remember the great {!sādhu!} of God.
#9.)One may be observing religious vows more resolutely than all; however, if as a result of this, another {!sādhu!} feels inferior, then that virtue should be renounced and one should behave on the same level as others.
#10.)All flaws reside in the flaw of identifying one’s self with the body. If that is abandoned, all flaws are abandoned. Furthermore, if the sole virtue of {!ātmā!}-realisation is developed, then all virtues will develop.
#11.)By indulging in God-related {!vishays!}, the mind is enlightened; and by indulging in worldly {!vishays!}, ignorance prevails in the mind.
#12.)One should not associate with the following even if it is God’s command:
##12.1)A place where he has frequent contact with his bodily relations.
##12.2)Adverse times in which one is suffering from beatings – one should leave that place.
##12.3)Company or activity in which there is the possibility of women being seen while having the {!darshan!} of God.
#13.)Scriptures which denounce God, even if they are written by someone intelligent, should not be read or heard.

19817.t:
#1.)Liberation is attained only with {!gnān!} - knowledge of God. The types of {!gnān!}:
##1.1)Understood from the scriptures.
##1.2)Understood from the external senses.
##1.3)Understood from the {!antahkaran!} (inner faculties: {!man, buddhi!}, etc.).
##1.4)Gained directly from experiential {!gnān!} of the {!jiva!}.
#2.)One who possesses complete/perfect {!gnān!}:
##2.1)Is one who knows God perfectly and knows the manifest form of God through the {!indriyas!}, the {!antahkaran!}, and experience.
##2.2)Is one who knows and sees God with an understanding of His greatness (described in 2.3) and is a perfect {!gnāni!}.
##2.3)Understands the manifest form of God to possess a divine form, is supreme, is the cause of all, and is the supporter of all; and having become {!brahmarup!} he worships Parabrahma.
##2.4)Even if he does not see the transcendental powers in God, he completely trusts God and believes himself to be fulfilled.
#3.)Only one who is {!brahmarup!} has the right to offer {!bhakti!} to Purushottam.
#4.)One who does not offer {!bhakti!} to Parabrahma after becoming {!brahmarup!} cannot attain ultimate liberation. Similarly, one who offers bhakti to Parabrahama without becoming {!brahmarup!} cannot attain ultimate liberation.
#5.)The understanding of contemporary Vedāntis: They believe themselves to be God and thus they are consigned to {!narak!}.

19818.t:
#1.)When does one perceive flaws?
##1.1)If a person is wise and has noticed an inappropriate {!swabhāv!} within himself, and while harbouring an intense aversion towards it, is continually endeavouring to overcome that {!swabhāv!}, then when he sees that very same {!swabhāv!} in another {!sādhu!}, he develops an aversion towards that {!sādhu!}.
##1.2)A fool does not overcome his own {!swabhāvs!}, but when he sees that same {!swabhāv!} in another {!sādhu!}, he perceives flaws in that {!sādhu!}.
#2.)In youth, if one’s food intake is decreased, and if one deliberately tolerates cold, heat, rain and hunger, and maintains profound association with the great {!Sant!}, the force of lust is weakened.
#3.)Addictions are developed by habit but not by {!prārabdha!}. If one maintains courage, keeps {!shraddhā!}, and becomes adamant on overcoming the addiction, then it can be overcome.
#4.)For the most part, a good or bad nature is due to the company one keeps, but in some cases, it is due to past {!karmas!}.
#5.){!Swabhāv!}:
##5.1)Formed recently:  can be overcome by staying in the company of a pious {!sādhu!} and by making a little effort to eradicate it.
##5.2)Formed previously: can barely be overcome, even after one makes a great effort to eradicate it, even if one stays in the company of a {!sādhu!}.
#6.)Means to overcoming the excitability of the {!indriyas!}:
##6.1)Punishing the {!indriyas!} by physical austerities and contemplating on one’s {!ātmā!}.
##6.2)Withdrawing the {!indriyas!} from their alluring {!vishays!} and engaging them on God instead.
#7.)If the tongue is fully subdued, then all of the other indriyas can be subdued.
#8.)If an overactive person wishes to become calm he should think, “I am the {!ātmā!}, Brahma, genderless, and stable.” If a person who is calm wishes to become more active, then he should realise the greatness of God and His devotees and performs the menial service of the devotees of God.
#9.)From the scriptures, among all of the incidents, only those incidents that match one’s own inclination should be imbibed.
#10.)One who has {!shraddhā!} in observing {!dharma!}, serving the {!Sant!}, listening to the talks of God, and has faith in the {!Sant!} progresses in Satsang.

19819.t:
#1.)Factors that lead to the development of {!dharma, gnān, vairāgya!}, and {!bhakti!}:
##1.1){!Dharma!}: Listening to the Smruti scriptures.
##1.2){!Gnān!}: Listening to the scriptures from a Satpurush.
##1.3){!Vairāgya!}: Knowing the four types of dissolution and the lifespans of all the {!jivas!}.
##1.4){!Bhakti!}: Listening to talks of God, his form, his abode, his divine actions and incidents with a sense of awe.
#2.)One becomes firm in observance of {!dharma!} first, then if one listens to scriptures that explain {!upāsanā!}, then {!gnān, bhakti!}, and {!vairāgya!} develop.

19820.t:
#1.)The level at which the {!indriyas, man!}, and {!jiva!} combine and indulge in an object, determine the force (mild, intermediate, intense) of the {!vruttis!} (towards the {!vishays!}). 
#2.)One develops affection for God by seeking favourable circumstances ({!deshkāl!} – the 8 factors of influence).
#3.)The means to not becoming disturbed (overcoming inappropriate thoughts):
##3.1)Firm understanding of the drawbacks in the {!vishays!}.
##3.2){!Gnān!} of {!ātmā!} and Paramātmā.
#4.)In an elevated state of {!gnān!}:
##4.1)One is devoid of a deep attachment to {!vishays!} and the mind does not become disturbed (have thoughts of enjoying {!vishays!}).
##4.2)One remains absolutely carefree in his own bliss.
##4.3)One feels equanimity in honour and insult.
##4.4)His vision becomes broad, in which he believes all worldly objects to be vain.
##4.5)One who has not achieved this elevated state of {!gnān!} but has intense faith in God and the {!Sant!}, he becomes blissful just like a {!gnāni!}.
#5.)For one who has faith coupled with knowledge of his greatness, {!māyā!} is not a cause of misery but a source of great happiness, because his {!indriyas!} and {!antahkaran!} all support the bhakti of God.

19821.t:
#1.)Understanding which an unholy person adopts from the holy scriptures:
##1.1)The male and female forms in the world are manifestations of God Himself; therefore, by meditating on those forms one attains instantaneous {!samādhi!}.
##1.2)If one perceives flaws in those forms, then one should believe that form to be Brahma and refute the perception of those flaws.
##1.3)The fruit of this type of understanding is consignment to the dismal regions of {!narak!} and the cycle of births and deaths.
#2.) Understanding which a holy person adopts from the holy scriptures:
##2.1)One should not meditate on deities such as Brahma, etc. nor meditate on the previous {!avatārs!}.
##2.2)One should meditate on the manifest form of God one has attained and maintain faithfulness (fidelity like that of a faithful wife) to that form.
##2.3)One should consider the human form of God equal to the divine form of God in His abode.
##2.4)One should perceive the devotees of the manifest form of God equal to the attendants of God’s abode.
#3.)One should only hear the sacred scriptures from a holy person but never from an unholy person.

19822.t:
#1.){!Savikalp!} faith:
##1.1)Lowest level: His faith remains as long as God exhibits {!swabhāvs!} to the same extent as other humans, but if He were to display more so than others, his faith would be shattered.
##1.2)Intermediate level: His faith remains firm even if God exhibits lust, anger, etc., to a double degree than that of humans.
##1.3)Highest level: Because he understands God to be the all-doer, if God were to indulge in some degrading deed, it would not affect Him.
#2.){!Nirvikalp!} faith:
##2.1)Lowest level: No matter what pious or impious deeds he witnesses being performed by God, he understands that in all actions God performs, He is still a non-doer.
##2.2)Intermediate level: One who becomes like the {!niranna-muktas!} of Shwetdwip - who are free from the six physical and emotional sensations - and worships Vāsudev.
##2.3)Highest level: One who worships Purushottam realizing oneself to be {!aksharrup!}. 
#3.)Reasons for the distinctions of faith:
##3.1)Association of a true or false guru.
##3.2)Effect of favourable or unfavourable factors of influence.
##3.3)Intensity of one’s {!shraddhā!}.
#4.)Means for developing highest level of faith from the lowest level:
##4.1)Keeping extreme {!shraddhā!}.
##4.2)Seeking favourable factors of influence.
##4.3)Seeking a guru with the highest level of {!gnān!}.

19823.t:
#1.)A person who has withdrawn his nādis and prāns, and by way of his {!nirvikalp!} state remains at the holy feet of God, would not be overcome by adverse places, times, company, etc.. However, one who has not developed such a state would be overcome by these.
#2.)There is a great difference between God and the {!muktas!}. One who believes them to be the same is a grave sinner; and one commits a sin equal to the five grave sins by having the {!darshan!} of such a sinner.
#3.)The greatness of God:
##3.1)Only Nārāyan is like Nārāyan and no one else is capable of becoming Nārāyan.
##3.2)He is the all-doer, cause of all, controller of all, extremely attractive, extremely radiant, and possesses {!kartum, akartum!} and {!anyathākartum!} powers.
##3.3)He can eclipse all of the {!muktas!} of Akshardhām by His own divine light and prevail alone.
##3.4)He is capable of supporting the countless {!muktas!} by His own power, without even needing Akshardhām.
##3.5)Because of his association with God, even a {!sādhu!} like Muktānand Swāmi can be considered to be like God; without God, however, even Akshar cannot be called God.

19824.t:
#1.)Shriji Mahārāj speaks about His own personal preferences for the sake of revealing the ideals of a devotee:
##1.1)He does not have a liking for the Advait philosophy.
##1.2)He has a liking for the {!upāsanā!} of Purushottam Bhagwān, who is above {!kshar!} (perishable) and {!akshar!} (imperishable).
##1.3)He likes the {!bhakti!} like that of the {!gopis!}.
##1.4)He likes {!vairāgya!} and {!ātmā!}-realization like that of Jadbharat and Shukji.
##1.5)He likes a renunciant who does not trust his mind.
##1.6)Purushottam Bhagwān in seated in His luminous abode Akshardhām, which is above all. He does not have a liking for the divine light but likes the {!darshan!} of the {!muktas!} along with God.
##1.7)One who does not have vices such as lust, one who observes {!dharma!}, and one who possesses {!bhakti!} toward God – he enjoys the company of such a person.
##1.8)He has a stronger dislike for those who have anger, egotism or jealousy than one who is lustful, because these three vices cause one to regress and fall from Satsang.

19825.t:
#1.)The {!jiva!} pervades the entire body from head to toe, but because of the purity of the {!indriyas!} and the {!antahkaran!}, its intensity and awareness is felt greater in the {!indriyas!} and the {!antahkaran!}.
#2.)Just as one who sees a part of a cow can be said to have seen the cow, but cannot be said to have seen the whole cow; similarly, as much one has realised the {!jiva!} through the {!indriyas!} and {!antahkaran!}, that is the extent of having realised his {!ātmā!}, but he cannot be said to have realised the {!ātmā!} completely.
#3.)God resides in the {!jiva!} with a definite form; but to keep the {!vrutti!} of the devotee’s mind confined within God, He cannot be seen.
#4.)Philosophy of Sānkhya:
##4.1)The {!jiva!} and {!ishwar!} are included in the 24 elements and God is the 25th element.
##4.2)The {!jiva!} attains a thought through endeavours that eventually leads to the realisation of its’ distinction from the elements (but not the forsaking of {!niyams!}). Then, realising oneself to be {!brahmarup!}, one engages in the worship of God.
#5.)Philosophy of Yoga:
##5.1)The {!jiva!} and {!ishwar!} are the 25th element and God is the 26th element.
##5.2)By fearing the {!vishays!}, one should forcibly keep their {!vrutti!} on God.
#6.)Philosophy of Vedānt (Upanishads): Only Brahma is {!satya!} and everything else is false, i.e. one who only sees Brahma perceives nothing else.

19826.t:
#1.)Worldly desires ({!vāsanā!}):
##1.1)Not become blunt: then the {!vruttis!} of the {!indriyas!} will cling to the {!vishays!} and will not dislodge even by a thought process.
##1.2)Become blunt: then the {!vruttis!} of the {!indriyas!} will not enter the {!vishays!} immediately; and if they do, they can be withdrawn instantly by a thought process.
##1.3)Become completely uprooted: then one is oblivious to the {!vishays!} during the waking state just as he is during deep sleep; and would behave as one who is {!gunātit!}.
#2.)One who has {!dharma, gnān, vairāgya!}, and {!bhakti!}, his worldly desires would become completely uprooted.
#3.)One who has {!bhakti!} toward God coupled with the knowledge of His greatness, then:
##3.1)All his flaws are eradicated.
##3.2)Attains {!dharma, gnān!}, and {!vairāgya!}
##3.3)That spiritual endeavour is the greatest of all endeavours.
#4.)One can discern the deceit of a deceitful person by knowing the company (i.e. company of an antagonist of Satsang) he keeps and how he behaves during adverse circumstances.
#5.)By spiting a devotee of God and by believing God to be formless, all of one’s virtues become faults.
#6.)The nature of an egotist:
##6.1)He perceives faults in the {!Sādhu!}.
##6.2)If someone praises him, even though that person may have a hundred faults, he would highlight a single virtue. Conversely, if a person does not praise him, then even though that person may have a hundred virtues, he would highlight an utterly insignificant fault and he would spite that person mentally, verbally, and physically as well.
#7.)How to eradicate ego: Thoroughly understanding the greatness of God and the {!Sant!}.

19827.t:
#1.)Perverted mind – one who spites a {!sādhu!} if He were to denounce his egotism or other {!swabhavs!}. Such a person would ultimately spite God as well and fall from {!Satsang!}.
##1.1)Causes for a perverted mind:
###i.)One who believes one’s self to be the body 
###ii.)One who does not have an intense aversion for the {!panchvishays!}
#2.)Means to eradicate consciousness that one’s self is the body and develop an aversion for the {!panchvishays!}:
##2.1)Becoming indifferent to the body.
##2.2)Firm realization that one’s self is the {!ātmā!}.
##2.3){!Vairāgya!} toward the {!panchvishays!}.
##2.4)Absolute faith in God coupled with the knowledge of His greatness.
#3.)A person who has an aversion toward the {!panchvishays!} would become troubled when he receives luxurious objects.
##3.1)Means to developing an aversion toward the {!panchvishays!}
###i.)Understanding God’s greatness
###ii.){!Ãtmā!}-realization
###iii.){!Vairāgya!}
#4.)God’s greatness:
##4.1)God is the creator, sustainer and destroyer of the world.
##4.2)The bliss of God is the highest bliss in comparison to all other bliss.
##4.3)If one understands God’s greatness this way then no object in the world will draw him away from the holy feet of God.
#5.)If one has realized the greatness of the {!Sant!}:
##5.1)He would behave as a servant of a servant.
##5.2)His foundation in {!Satsang!} remains firm.
##5.3)Even if the {!Sant!} scorns him, he does not become upset or hurt.
##5.4)Even if the {!Sant!} repeatedly physically mistreats him, he considers it his great fortune but does not perceive a fault in the {!Sant!}.

19828.t:
#1.)When a devotee who meditates on the manifest form of God goes to the abode of God, then he sees God in His original form but not the various forms/{!avatars!} God assumes in Mrutyulok.
#2.)When God assumes an {!avatār!}, He does not abandon His original form. That original form is characterised by eternal existence, consciousness and bliss; possesses a form full of divine light; is the source of all bliss; and is the controller of all.
#3.)Perceiving divinity in God means:
##3.1)One should believe God is divine along with his Dhām, powers, opulence and attendants.
##3.2)God’s form is supremely divine; He does not have a trace of human traits.
##3.3)One should perceive God as Purushottam, who transcends Akshar.
##3.4)Only one who perceives such divinity in God is said to have complete conviction.
#4.)Perceiving human traits in God means:
##4.1)Attributing lust, anger, and other feelings of the {!antahkaran!} to God.
##4.2)Attributing birth, death, and other characteristics of the physical body to God.
##4.3)One who perceives human traits in God without knowing His supreme divinity:
###i.)He repeatedly becomes upset and constantly perceives virtues and flaws.
###ii.)Even if he appears to have conviction of God, his conviction if flawed.
###iii.)His heart will regress day by day and he will surely fall from Satsang.
#5.)One should perceive divinity in devotees of God because they assume a divine form in God’s abode and become {!brahmarup!}.
#6.)Shriji Mahārāj’s insistence on this discourse about conviction:
##6.1)Regardless of whether you realise this fact today or you realise it after a hundred years, it must be realised. There is no alternative but to realise it and imbibe it firmly.
##6.2)One should discuss this principle of Mine at least once a day – that is My command.

19829.t:
#1.)One may have affection for God and firm resolution to observe {!dharma!}; however, if one has not applied a thought process then the extremely alluring {!vishays!} will never be considered equivalent to the extremely repulsive {!vishays!}, nor will they be considered inferior to them.
#2.)For the sake of revealing the ideals of a devotee, Shriji Mahārāj shares His thought process:
##2.1)God is the all doer (He is the creator, sustainer and destroyer of the world) and He possesses a definite form from the words of the scriptures.
##2.2)During the creation process, God grants {!indriyas!} and {!antahkaran!} to the {!jivas!} for the enjoyments of {!vishays!} and for liberation.
##2.3)God has created superior {!vishays!} for the purpose of alleviating the miseries of the inferior {!vishays!}.
##2.4)All of the happiness related to {!vishays!} which is apparent in this world is only due to some relation with God, and when coupled with {!dharma!}; but the bliss that is in God Himself cannot be found anywhere else.
##2.5)Therefore, an aspirant should realise, “The further away I am from God, the more miseries I will face and if I maintain close association with God, I will attain much bliss.
##2.6)Compared to the bliss of Golok and other abodes, the bliss of Akshardhām is immensely greater. One should keep this thought firm: Now I want to reach only the abode of God; I do not want to be tempted by the vain pleasures of the {!panchvishays!} along the way.
#3.)One who understands this way:
##3.1)Is intelligent.
##3.2)Mahārāj has affection for such a person.
##3.3)His mind remains dejected toward the {!panchvishays!}.
##3.4)He has no trouble in withdrawing his {!vrutti!} from the {!panchvishays!} and he easily perceives {!vishays!} as providing inferior happiness.

19830.t:
#1.)Philosophy of Yoga:
##1.1)The {!jiva!} and {!ishwar!} are the 25th element and Paramātmā is the 26th element.
##1.2)However much one contemplates upon the {!ātmā!} and non-{!ātmā!}, or however much one endeavours, without accepting the refuge of the manifest form of God, one cannot attain liberation.
##1.3)Drawbacks of Yoga philosophy:
###i.)Both {!jiva!} and {!ishwar!} are understood as equal.
###ii.)Prakruti-Purush, etc., are thought of as being the components of the all-transcending God.
##1.4)Resolving the drawbacks:
###i.)The {!jiva!} is minor (and limited) and incapable of sustaining the {!panch-bhuts!}; whereas, {!ishwar!} is all-knowing and capable of supporting the {!panch-bhuts!}.
###ii.)Only God is like God and He is indivisible; and Prakruti-Purush are His components in the sense that they are His devotees (but not a divisible component of God).
#2.)Philosophy of Sānkhya:
##2.1)The {!jiva!} and {!ishwar!} are included in the 24 elements and God is the 25th element.
