##2.2)When one understands the ultimate fate of all deities, humans, etc., and develops {!vairāgya!} for the {!vishays!} and realises one’s {!ātmā!} as transcending the three bodies, then one becomes a {!mukta!}.
##2.3)Drawbacks of Sānkhya philosophy:
###i.)The element that attains Paramātmā is not considered distinct from the 24 elements. Therefore, who attains that Paramātmā? That question is not resolved.
###ii.)All that is grasped via the {!antahkaran!} and the {!indriyas!} is false; therefore, they believe that the manifest form of God is also considered as being false.
##2.4)Resolving the drawbacks:
###i.)The {!jiva!} and {!ishwar!} have been included with the elements because they have attained oneness with the elements, but in reality, they are totally distinct from those elements.
###ii.)One should realise one’s own {!ātmā!} as being {!brahmarup!} and understanding the form of God that has manifested to liberate the {!jivas!} as being {!satya!}, one should meditate on Him.
#3.)Shriji Mahārāj’s principal: Become {!brahmarup!} through the path of Sānkhya and offer {!upāsanā!} to God through the path of Yoga.
#4.)Both philosophies depend on each other; hence, if both paths are followed, then one attains liberation.

19831.t:
#1.)One with intelligence:
##1.1)Realises all of his flaws and virtues, as well as the virtues and flaws of others, and maintaining an intense aversion towards his own flaws, he eradicates them.
##1.2)Accepts the advice of the {!Sant!} as beneficial to him.
##1.3)Even if he has a little (worldly) intelligence, his intelligence is useful in attaining liberation.
#2.)One who lacks intelligence:
##2.1)Acknowledges his own virtues but does not realise his drawbacks.
##2.2)He views himself as eminent like the Sanakādik, and he views other eminent people to be inferior to himself.
##2.3)His intelligence should be known as merely worldly and should be regarded as an utter fool.
##2.4)His worldly intelligence is not useful in attaining liberation.
#3.)Love:
##3.1)Definition: that which is the cause of the perpetuation of the world, and that which causes bondage and the cycle of births and deaths – the {!māyā!} of God.
##3.2)If one’s mind remains steady, without harbouring doubts, then that type of love toward God is not {!māyā!}; but if one’s mind does not remain steady, then that type of love is {!māyā!}.
##3.3)One who is intelligent should love God in the following way:
###i.)Develop love for God believing one’s self to be the {!ātmā!}.
###ii.)The {!indriyas!} and the {!antahkaran!} should be kept in a witness box and in chains in the form of the {!niyams!} of the five religious vows, and then they should be made to offer {!bhakti!} to God; but one should not perceive virtues in the {!indriyas!} and {!antahkaran!}, rather maintain enmity toward them.
###iii.)One should tempt the {!indriyas!} and the {!antahkaran!} with the bliss of God and divert them away from other {!vishays!}.
#4.)Method of contemplating on the {!ātmā!}:
##4.1)Thought: “I am not the 24 elements; I am distinct from them; I am {!chaitanya!}; and I am a devotee of God.”
##4.2)Reprimand the {!indriyas!} and {!antahkaran!}: If you do hanker after the {!vishays!} leaving God aside, then what is there between you and me? Who are you and who am I? I will have absolutely nothing to do with you. Whatever you do, you will have to bear the consequences.
##4.3)Prayer: “O Mahārāj! The fault lies with the {!indriyas!} and {!antahkaran!}; I am distinct from them. In fact, they are my enemies. So, please protect me from their influence.”

19832.t:
#1.)The original, eternal form of God narrated in the scriptures and the form of God manifest on the earth – one who develops a firm conviction of these two forms through intense {!shravan!} and {!manan!}, never harbours doubts in God when observing His human-like actions.
##1.1)God’s eternal, original and divine form is beyond the reach of the {!indriyas!} and {!antahkaran!} because God is divine and {!amāyik!} (cannot be perceived by the {!māyik!} {!indriyas!} and {!antahkaran!}).
##1.2)God is the king of the kings of countless villages in the form of {!brahmānds!}.
##1.3)When the chiefs of a {!brahmānds!} – Brahmā, Vishnu, and Shiv – pray to God and ask Him to visit their {!brahmānd!}, then God graces the {!brahmānd!} assuming a human body – behaving and possessing the {!swabhāvs!} of a human.
#2.)An intelligent person realises that there is something divine about that God, and with this understanding, he develops the conviction of Him being God.
#3.)If God were to behave with only divinity, one would not be able to comprehend that which is beyond the reach of the mind and speech.
#4.)God suppresses His own divine powers and gives {!darshan!} exactly like a human, so that His devotees can develop love toward Him; but at the same time He still remains present in His own abode.
#5.)If someone claims, “I have realised God, and I have the conviction of God,” but has not understood this discourse, then his conviction is imperfect.

19833.t:
#1.)Before one who spites or speaks derogatorily of God or His {!Sant!}:
##1.1)One should be conceited
##1.2)One should retaliate with words as sharp as an arrow.
##1.3)One should not become humble before him but rather maintain ego
#2.)Before God and His {!Sant!}:
##2.1)It is inappropriate to be conceited in front of them
##2.2)One should be humble
##2.3)One should become a servant of servant.

19834.t:
#1.)By giving Shri Krishna Bhagwān as an example, Shriji Mahārāj explains His self as the cause of all {!avatārs!}:
##1.1)There is no {!Avatār!} like this one.
##1.2)The other {!avatārs!} have shown limited strength, but this {!Avatār!} has shown complete divine powers and strength.
##1.3)This {!Avatār!} is the greatest of all.
#2.)If one has a firm conviction of the manifest form of God, and if that realisation never changes in any way, then even if one happens to commit a slip of conduct due to the influence of bad company, one would certainly attain liberation.

19835.t:
#1.)God’s form:
##1.1)The entities evolved out of the three {!gunas!} of {!māyā!}, namely the five {!bhuts!}, the {!indriyas!}, the {!antahkaran!} and their presiding deities are never present in God at any time - past, present or future.
##1.2)Just as the form of God in Akshardhām is resplendent with countless divine powers and divine light at the end of {!ātyantik-pralay!}, one should realise exactly the same regarding the manifest form of God.
##1.3)The perception of God appearing to possess human-like attributes is due to His yogic powers of creating an illusion, but in reality God remains absolutely unchanged – just as a magician who appears to have died and been burned is merely his illusion; similarly, one who understands God thoroughly, understands God to be eternal, imperishable and absolutely unchanging.
##1.4)The manifest form of Purushottam Nārāyan is the cause of all; He is forever divine and has a form. One should not perceive any type of imperfections in that form - it is like a {!murti!} made of sugar crystals (i.e. completely pure).
##1.5)One should meditate on, worship, and offer {!bhakti!} only to the form that one has seen.
##1.6)In whomever God ‘enters’ for the purpose of fulfilling many types of tasks, He eclipses that entity by His own divine light and exhibits His own divine light to a greater degree.
#2.)When one worships God with sincerity, having faith in the words of the {!Ekāntik Sant!} of God, one’s {!māyik!} vision disappears, and thereafter, one realises that same form of God as being the supreme {!chaitanya!}, characterised by eternal existence, consciousness and bliss.
#3.)One who understands God this way (i.e. never harbouring any doubts of {!māyā!} being present in the manifest form of God):
##3.1)He has understood God perfectly.
##3.2)He is called a {!gnāni!} and an {!ekāntik bhakta!}.
##3.3)His should be known to have perfect conviction ({!nishthā!}).
##3.4)If, by chance, he were to behave unbecomingly due to the influence of bad company or due to the influence of his own {!prārabdha!} {!karmas!}, he would still attain liberation.
#4.)One who does not understand God this way:
##4.1)He is a fool.
##4.2)Even if he is a staunch {!urdhvaretā!} {!brahmachāri!} and a great renunciant, attaining liberation would still be extremely difficult for him.

19836.t:
#1.)Infatuation: If God or the {!Sant!} criticise a {!vishay!} towards which one’s {!chitt!} has been lured, one would become upset with them and even malign them.
#2.)Characteristic of Infatuation: Loss of all sense of discrimination of what should be done and what should not be done.
#3.)Cause of Infatuation: weakness towards {!panchvishays!}.
#4.)Method to eradicate attachment to {!vishays!}:
##4.1)Consolidating the understanding that one’s true form is the {!ātmā!}.
##4.2)Thoroughly understanding the nature of how the cosmos is created, sustained and destroyed.
##4.3)Thoroughly understanding the greatness of God and contemplating on His bliss.
#5.)A person who no longer makes distinctions between pleasant and unpleasant {!vishays!}:
##5.1)Is free of infatuation and has overcome his weakness towards the {!vishays!}.
##5.2)Has understood God perfectly.
##5.3)Has an inclination like that of a woman who observes the vow of fidelity.
##5.4)Is a staunch devotee and should be known to possess {!gnān!}.
##5.5)Is extremely dear to God.
##5.6)Has attained God-realisation and has become fulfilled.
#6.)To eradicate infatuation, one should:
##6.1)Keep courage and persevere gradually.
##6.2)Make the following goal: I will eradicate as much attachment to the {!vishays!} as is possible in this life.

19837.t:
#1.)One who wishes to attain ultimate liberation should understand that:
##1.1)The {!jiva!} that resided in the physical body is separate from the {!indriyas, antahkaran, panchvishays!}, and the physical body.
##1.2)The desire to indulge in the {!vishays!} occurs through the {!indriyas!}, not through the {!antahkaran!}.
#2.)Methods for overcoming the weakness towards the {!panchvishays!}:
##2.1)Just as a well can be cleaned only when the small streamlets of water that flow into the well are clogged with cloth rags; in the same way, by controlling the external {!indriyas!}, the external {!vishays!} cannot enter the {!antahkaran!}.
##2.2)Contemplating that one’s self is the {!ātmā!} and remaining fulfilled.
##2.3)Beholding God’s form in one’s heart.

19838.t:
#1.)The path of amorousness and the path of {!brahma-gnān!} ({!ātmā!}-realisation) can lead to both liberation and downfall.
#2.)Reasons for falling from the path of liberation:
##2.1)In the path of amorousness: when God is described in the scriptures, women devotees are also described, which causes one’s mind to become infatuated with the women devotees.
##2.2)In the path of {!brahma-gnān!}: one develops the false understanding that Brahma assumes the mobile and immobile forms of creation; therefore he believes his own {!jiva!} to be God, which causes a breach in {!upāsanā!}.
#3.)Means for securing liberation:
##3.1)When offering {!bhakti!} to God in the amorous path, to prevent one’s mind from becoming infatuated one should consider the female devotees to be one’s mother, sister, or daughter.
##3.2)When offering {!bhakti!} to God in the {!brahma-gnān!} path, one should develop oneness between the {!jivātmā!} and Brahma, and then worship Parabrahma while maintaining a master-servant relationship with Him.
#4.)Brahma: the cause of and supporter of all (Prakruti-Purush, etc.) and pervades all through its {!antaryāmi!} powers.
#5.)Parabrahma: is distinct from Brahma and is the cause, supporter, and inspirer of even Brahma.

19839.t:
#1.)During adverse times, which should be maintained, {!dharma!} or {!bhakti!}? Which should be forsaken?
##1.1)When God is manifest, if He is pleased by upholding {!bhakti!}, then {!bhakti!} should be upheld; and if He is pleased by upholding {!dharma!}, then {!dharma!} should be upheld.
##1.2)When God is not manifest, one should constantly contemplate upon God.
#2.)When one realises the greatness of God and has {!shraddhā!}, then one will be able to constantly contemplate upon God.
#3.)One should understand the greatness of the manifest form of God in this manner: Despite that God may come into contact with {!māyik!} {!vishays!}, those {!vishays!} are not able to affect Him.
#4.)One who thoroughly understands the greatness of God:
##4.1)Is not enticed by alluring {!vishays!}.
##4.2)Views all of the attractive and repulsive objects in this world as being equal.
##4.3)If he understands this way, then he can maintain his {!dharma!}:
###i.)I want to constantly contemplate upon God and become an {!Ekāntik Bhakta!}.
###ii.)If my {!vrutti!} is drawn towards vicious natures such as lust, anger, avarice, etc., then that will be a hindrance in my contemplation of God.
###iii.)He remains extremely wary of treading the wrong path.
#5.)One who does not thoroughly understand the greatness of God:
##5.1)Will become attached to insignificant or worthless objects, such as a torn waist-cloth or a gourd.
##5.2)May endeavour in a million other ways, yet will not be able to constantly contemplate upon the form of God.

19840.t:
#1.)A devotee of God should maintain fidelity and courage.
##1.1)Just as a woman who observes the vow of fidelity would never sway upon seeing another man, a devotee of God should not let his mind sway towards anything other than God.
##1.2)If someone were to speak ill of one’s husband, then one should not remain timid and become subdued. Rather, one should reply very boldly. In this manner, a devotee of God should not become suppressed by evil people; he should be courageous.
#2.)It is generally said that a {!sādhu!} should view everyone equally, but this is not the principle of the scriptures.
#3.)One who does side with a non-believer will himself, either in this life or in the next, definitely become a non-believer as well.

19841.t:
#1.)Just as one acquires money from a draft written by a wealthy businessman, similarly, one attains liberation by abiding by the {!dharma!} expounded in the scriptures by a {!Motāpurush!}.
#2.)One who does not have faith in the moral do’s and don’ts should be regarded as a {!nāstik!} and grave sinner; his company should be shunned.
#3.)The {!chitt!} is extremely pure, therefore, it can visualise whatever object it recalls.
#4.)Whenever the {!chitt!} remembers good or bad objects, then while believing one’s {!ātmā!} to be distinct from the {!chitt!}:
##4.1)Worship God.
##4.2)Do not become frustrated by the pure and impure thoughts arising in the {!chitt!}.
##4.3)Always remain joyful.

19842.t: #1.)Just as a poor man may wish for sumptuous food and lavish clothes but he cannot acquire them; similarly, one who lacks {!vairāgya!} may wish in his heart to acquire the virtues of a {!sādhu!}, but he will not be able to acquire them.\r\n#2.)If a person lacks {!vairāgya!}, he should intensely serves a great {!Sant!} and obediently persevere in his observance of the injunctions of God. Then God will look upon him with an eye of compassion, and as a result his {!swabhāvs!} will be eradicated immediately.

19843.t:
#1.)How to observe the Ekādashi fast:
##1.1)Shun the indulgences of the eleven {!indriyas!}.
##1.2)Prevent the mind from having thoughts related to lust, anger, etc.
##1.3)Do not let the physical body engage in immoral activities.
##1.4)Observe all of the other {!niyams!}.
##1.5)Listen to the discourses of God, sing {!bhajans!}, and stay awake at night.
#2.)The principle of all scriptures is that liberation cannot be attained without performing sacrifices.
#3.){!Yoga-yagna!}: withdrawing the ten {!indriyas!} and the mind (the eleventh {!indriya!}) from whichever {!vishays!} they have become attached to and then offering them into the {!brahma-agni!}.
#4.)Gnān-{!yagna!} ({!antardrashti!}): 
##4.1)Physically engaging in God-related activities, such as having the {!darshan!} of God, performing His {!pujā!} or engaging in discourses, devotional songs, etc.
##4.2)To behold the form of God within one’s heart, perform His {!pujā!}, and bow before Him, etc.
#5.)The fruit of {!yoga-yagna!} and {!gnān-yagna!} is having a divine vision of Parabrahma within one’s own self, which is Brahma.
#6.)Manifest form of God:
##6.1)Everything that has a relation with God is called {!nirgun!}; anything that is not related to God is called {!sagun!}.
##6.2)Attaining the manifest form of God is itself the highest state of enlightenment.

19844.t:
#1.)If one does not understand the manifest form of God that one has attained to be supreme and instead understands him to be formless ({!nirākār!}) and like the other {!avatārs!}, then that is regarded as committing blasphemy against God.
#2.)One without firm conviction in God’s form:
##2.1)Will either go to the realm of Brahmā or to the realm of some other deity but he will not go to Akshardhām.
##2.2)Whenever he falters from {!dharma!}, he will feel, “I have fallen into {!narak!}.”
#3.)One who has the strength of conviction in God’s form:
##3.1)Will be protected from great dangers (in the form of {!adharma!}).
##3.2)Only he can be called an {!Ekāntik Bhakta!} and a staunch {!satsangi!}.
##3.3)Would never fall from the path of liberation.
##3.4)Even if he has to leave the {!Satsang!} fellowship or has transgressed God’s commands, he will go to Akshardhām.
#4.)It is difficult to understand talks related to God’s form, yet Shriji Mahārāj has made it easy for us to understand.

19845.t:
#1.)Those who do not have {!bhakti!} for God will understand God to be formless, even after reading scriptures that proclaim God to have a form.
#2.)God has a form because:
##2.1)Only one who has a form can create something that also possesses a form.
##2.2)Bhagwān pervades all through His {!antaryāmi!} power, but in his abode Akshardhām, He forever possesses a divine form.
#3.)Just as a woman who carries a foetus in her womb attains a child, one who carries a foetus in the form of faith in God attains God’s Akshardhām.
#4.)Between {!gnān, vairāgya!}, and {!bhakti!}, the greatest means for developing affection for God is {!bhakti!}. 
#5.){!Bhakti!}:
##5.1)Is to realise the redemptive virtues in God and to seek His firm refuge.
##5.2)Is perceiving divinity even in human-like actions of the manifest form of God.
##5.3)One who offers {!bhakti!} in this manner can be called a true devotee.
##5.4)Such {!bhakti!} is itself the highest state of enlightenment.

19846.t:
#1.)Many people perform pious {!karmas!} (such as sacrifices, observances, etc.) only for the attainment of {!dharma, arth!} and {!kām!}, however, by performing these pious {!karmas!}:
##1.1)They only enjoy the fruits of the three realms (Devlok, Brahmalok or Mrutyulok)
##1.2)They do not attain God’s Akshardhām.
##1.3)They do not escape the misery of the cycle of births and deaths.
#2.)By God’s command, if one performs pious {!karmas!} only to please God :
##2.1)All of one’s activities are performed to serve God and his {!bhakta!}.
##2.2)All of one’s pious {!karmas!} become a form of {!bhakti!} and aid in the attainment of liberation.
##2.3){!Karmas!} do not bind the devotee (i.e. the {!karmas!} do not determine one’s fate).
#3.)Whoever perceives flaws in in a devotee that by God’s command, performs {!karmas!} for the purpose of pleasing God, will have {!adharma!} and its retinue reside in his heart.

19847.t:
#1.)None of the vicious natures (such as lust, anger, and ego) lie within the {!jiva!}; the {!jiva!} has merely believed itself to possess them out of its own foolishness.
#2.)If a king possess little or no intelligence, the people in the village would not obey his orders. As a result, the king would become depressed, powerless, and sit idly. Similarly, the {!jiva!} in this body is like a king; but if the {!jiva!} becomes powerless, then the {!indriyas, antahkaran!}, and vicious natures would not let the {!jiva!} exercise authority.
#3.)One who aspires for their liberation should learn the art of ruling in the following way:
##3.1)Understand the greatness of God thoroughly.
##3.2)Believe one’s true self to be the {!ātmā!}, which is greater than the {!indriyas, antahkaran!}, and the five {!prāns!}; and I am their controller.
##3.3)Exercise control over one’s {!indriyas!}, allowing them to follow the path of God (sights, smells, words, tastes, touch related to God) but not on an unrighteous path.
#4.)Totally discarding timidity and vigilantly endeavouring in this way is the greatest of all spiritual endeavours for attaining liberation.

19848.t:
#1.)Shriji Mahārāj speaks about His own nature for the sake of revealing the ideals of a devotee: 
##1.1)Attractive {!vishays!} and the repulsive {!vishays!} are the same to Me. Praises and insults are the same to Me.
##1.2)My mind remains absolutely dejected towards the {!panchvishays!}. Whenever I forcefully engage My {!indriya’s!} {!vruttis!} towards objects, they remain there very reluctantly.
##1.3)I am not burdened by {!dharma, gnān!}, and {!vairāgya!}.
##1.4)The {!vrutti!} of my {!indriyas!} remains only on God.
##1.5)The reason for this elevated state is the realization of {!ātmā!} and Paramātmā.
#2.)The {!murti!} in Akshardhām, which transcends all:
##2.1)Is luminous, possesses two arms, and appears young like a teenager.
##2.2)Is Shriji Mahārāj Himself.
##2.3)Transcends Akshar and is divine. That {!murti!} is Parabrahma or Purushottam.
##2.4)Is the cause of all the {!avatārs!}.
##2.5)By meditating on this {!murti!} (which is Shriji Mahārāj himself) one transcends {!māyā!}.
##2.6)Everything becomes {!nirgun!} by His association.
##2.7)His manner of birth and discarding His body are not in accordance with the ways of this world (it is {!alaukik!} or divine).
#3.)Shriji Mahārāj’s points related to God’s form:
##3.1)Shriji Mahārāj is speaking (about God’s form) not out of any pretence, out of any self-conceit, or to spread His own greatness, but for the liberation of the {!jiva!}.
##3.2)If one understands God’s form, their {!jiva!} will benefit greatly.
##3.3)It is the essence of the {!shāstras!}, based on His own experience, and from what He has seen.
##3.4)Only from the {!Satpurush!} can one understand God’s form but not by one’s intellect alone or from the scriptures.
##3.5)When one comes to comprehend God’s form, one will not encounter any difficulty in subduing the desires for the {!panchvishays!} and {!swabhāvs!}.
##3.6)When one has a firm understanding of God, he has nothing left to accomplish; he is fulfilled and has reached the culmination of all spiritual endeavours.
##3.7)If one has completely understood God’s form (which is the essence of this discourse), then regardless of whether one is reborn in a base or elevated life form due to one’s {!prārabdha karmas!}, one will not forget this {!gnān!}.
##3.8)Without a firm understanding of the nature of God, one will never be able to overcome one’s weaknesses, regardless of their austerities or renunciation.
##3.9)One should keep this principle constantly new and fresh in their mind until the end of their life.

19849.t:
#1.)An unshakeable conviction of God’s form is achieved by the association of God’s Ekāntik Sant.
#2.)One who has an unshakeable conviction of God’s form:
##2.1)Whether he is a {!gruhasth!} or a renunciant, both become {!nirgun!}.
##2.2)Even if a small deficiency remains in him, he will be liberated.
##2.3)Even if he has only a feeble intellect, he should still be regarded as possessing much intellect. 
##2.4)He should be regarded as having attained {!nirvikalp samādhi!}.
#3.)One who does not have an unshakeable conviction of God’s form:
##3.1)Even if he is vigilantly striving to eradicate lust, anger, avarice, etc., he will not be able to eradicate those vicious natures.
##3.2)He will not be liberated.
##3.3)Ultimately, he will become evil and go to {!narak!}.
##3.4)Even if he has much intellect, he should still be known as having no intellect.

19850.t:
#1.)Methods to eradicate one’s {!swabhāvs!}:
##1.1)Just as one bears an intense aversion toward one’s enemy and would employ whatever means to harm him or would become happy if someone else were to harm him, similarly:
###i.)One should keep enmity toward their {!swabhāvs!}, such as lust, anger, etc.
###ii.)If a {!sādhu!} were to criticise and insult those internal enemies, then one should not develop an aversion towards that {!sādhu!}. On the contrary, one should be grateful to the {!sādhu!} and feel he is an extremely great benefactor.
#2.)Characteristics of one who would never deflect from {!dharma, vairāgya, gnān!}, and {!bhakti!}:
##2.1)He would not be suppressed by anyone’s personality.
##2.2)No one could mock someone or jest in his presence.
##2.3)No one could make even a mild sarcastic remark at him.
##2.4)He has zeal to attain liberation.

19851.t:
#1.)By maintaining resolute faith in God, faith in {!dharma!} will remain firm. However, by maintaining faith in {!dharma!} alone, faith in God declines.
#2.)Whether one has {!vairāgya!} or not, only by observing {!niyams!} can the desire for the {!panchvishays!} be conquered.
#3.)If the {!indriyas!} of one with feeble {!shraddhā!} are not under control, then one attains liberation after countless births.
#4.)Characteristics of one with strong {!shraddhā!}:
##4.1)His {!indriyas!} are under control.
##4.2)He attains {!gnān!} and immediately attains the highest state of enlightenment.
##4.3)When he wants to engage in God-related activities, he hastily carries out bodily activities.
##4.4)He remains eager for God’s {!darshan!} and to observe {!niyams!}.
#5.)By understanding the greatness of God, one’s feeble {!shraddhā!} will grow stronger.

19852.t:
#1.)God may accept the 24 elements of {!māyā!}, yet he remains unchanged and uninfluenced by them.
#2.)One whose faith in God’s form is firm:
##2.1)He understands God to be free from even a single trace of {!māyā!} (i.e. he does not believe this much of God has {!māyā!} and this much does not – He is totally free of {!māyā!}.)
##2.2)He never perceives flaws in God.
##2.3)He thoroughly understands the greatness of God’s devotees.
##2.4)He has an unflinching refuge of God.
##2.5)He understands God is not subject to change ({!nirvikāri!} – uninfluenced by vicious natures) and is absolutely uninfluenced by {!māyā!} ({!nirlep!}).
##2.6)He glorifies God’s weaknesses in exactly the same way that he glorifies His strengths. He also glorifies those actions and incidents of God that appear to be inappropriate in exactly the same way that he glorifies actions and incidents that are appropriate.
##2.7)Such a devotee should be known as being ‘{!sthitapragna’!}, entertaining no doubts regarding the nature of God’s strength and weaknesses.
##2.8)He has nothing left to understand.

19853.t:
#1.)A person who has committed any of the five grave sins can be redeemed at some point in time. However, one who has accepted either the beliefs of {!nāstiks!} or shushka-Vedāntis will never be redeemed.
#2.)Beliefs of {!nāstiks!}:
##2.1)They do not believe God is the all-doer, master of all, redeemer of sinners, and uplifter of the wretched.
##2.2)They believe their liberation is through their {!karmas!}.
##2.3)Their understanding is not in accordance with the Vedas, Shāstras, and Purāns.
#3.)Beliefs of shushka-Vedāntis:
##3.1)They believe they are God, as God Himself assumes the form of the {!jiva!}.
##3.2)They do not engage in any spiritual endeavour or worship God.
#4.)True {!gnāni!}:
##4.1)Engages in meditation of God, chanting His holy name, singing devotional songs, etc.
##4.2)Even though they are powerful, they remain as servants of God.
#5.)There is no deed greater than keeping the company of the {!Satpurush!}, conversely, there is no sin graver than keeping the company of ignorant people such as the shushka-Vedāntis.

19854.t:
#1.)After listening to the scriptures of shushka-Vedāntis, Mahārāj became extremely disheartened.
#2.)By listening to the scriptures of shushka-Vedāntis:
##2.1)One mistakenly believes that the {!jiva!} and God are equivalent, causing a breach in the {!upāsanā!} of God.
##2.2)One’s intellect becomes extremely corrupt.
##2.3)One begins to worship deities.
#3.)Even in the abode of God, the {!muktas!} worship God and offer {!bhakti-upāsanā!} with a master-servant relationship.
#4.)The letter that Shriji Mahārāj wrote:
##4.1)Reason for God assuming an {!avatār!}:
###i.)To establish {!dharma!} and uproot {!adharma!}.
###ii.)To give {!darshan!} to His {!ekāntik bhaktas!} and to protect them.
##4.2)The means to offer {!upāsanā!} to God:
###i.){!Upāsanā!} should be offered only to God, maintaining the vow of fidelity. One should perceive God to be free of all faults.
###ii.)One should engage in {!mānsi!} {!pujā!} and the nine types of {!bhakti!} with affection.
###iii.)One should strictly abide by the {!dharma!} of their caste and {!āshram!}.
##4.3)The {!bhakti!} of one who behaves in this manner will flourish.

19855.t: #1.)One who has mastered {!samādhi!}:\n##1.1)If he follows the path of {!nivrutti!}, then the power of his {!indriyas!} and faculty of knowing increases.\n##1.2)If he follows the path of {!pravrutti!}, then only the power of his faculty of knowing increases.

19856.t:
#1.)The essence of all the scriptures:
##1.1)The fruit of observing the {!dharma!} of one’s caste and {!āshram!} is {!dharma, artha, kām!}, worldly reputation, and physical comforts.
##1.2)For the purpose of liberation, one should realise God to be the all-doer.
##1.3)Just as one understands the greatness of the past {!avatārs!} of God and His {!bhaktas!}, if one understands the greatness of the manifest form of God and His Bhakta, then he has nothing left to understand on the path of liberation.
#2.)God is the giver of the fruits of one’s {!karmas!}; He creates experiences in the dreams of the {!jivas!} and {!ishwars!}, according to their {!karmas!}.
#3.)The understanding of a {!gnāni!}:
##3.1)Knows which of the influences (place, time, etc.) are predominant in any given circumstance
##3.2)The predominance of place, time, etc. prevail as long as God allows them to do so; but they cannot do anything against His wish.

19857.t:
#1.)When two armies prepare for combat and both have implanted their flags opposite of each other, those who are brave are not afraid of dying. A coward, however, harbours thousands of thoughts of fleeing, looting wealth and weapons, and dying.
##1.1)Brave devotees do not have any thoughts related to their body or of this world. They only think about attaining the abode of God.
##1.2)Cowardly devotees identify themselves as the body, and in their goal to reach the abode of God, they have a thousand thoughts such as ‘if the religious vows become strict, I will not be able to survive; only if they are easy to observe will I be able to survive.”
#2.)Shriji Mahārāj speaks about His own nature for the sake of revealing the ideals of a devotee:
##2.1)When He went to Amdāvād to perform the installation ceremony of Shri Nar-Nārāyandev, His heart felt intense grief and He became ill.
##2.2)After engaging in activities, one should attach to God in such a manner whereby one feels he has not done anything at all.
##2.3)One experiences bliss in their heart when one forgets all objects related to Devlok or Brahmalok, and while keeping courage against {!man, buddhi, chitt!}, and {!ahamkār!}.
#3.)Characteristics of an {!ekāntik bhakta!}:
##3.1)Believes himself to be {!brahmarup!}.
##3.2)Does {!bhakti!} of God while observing {!dharma, gnān!}, and {!vairāgya!}.
##3.3)Maintains no desire for any object other than God.
#4.)The {!Sant!} possesses the same majesty that God possesses.
#5.)There is no greater status than that of a {!sādhu!}.
#6.)If a devotee of God holds onto the {!chintāmani!} in the form of God’s form, then he will attain everything.

19858.t:
#1.)The nature of the mind:
##1.1)The instrument with which the {!jiva!} indulges in the {!vishays!} is the mind.
##1.2)Just as a person can die from heat or frost, similarly, when the mind travels towards the {!vishays!} that are full of miseries, the {!jiva!} becomes miserable and falls from the path of liberation; and if the {!vishays!} are pleasurable, the {!jiva!} becomes complacent (becomes attached to the {!vishays!} instead of God) and falls from the path of liberation.
#2.)One whose mind remains unmoved - that is, it does not become ‘hot’ upon experiencing repulsive {!vishays!} and does not become ‘cold’ upon experiencing pleasurable {!vishays!} should be known as a [!Param-Bhāgwat Sant!}.

19859.t:
#1.)A devotee who is resolute in yoga:
##1.1)Keeps his {!vrutti!} constantly fixed on the form of God.
##1.2)Somewhat lacks the strength of understanding and will experience hindrances when encountering adverse circumstances.
#2.)A devotee who is resolute in {!sānkhya!}:
##2.1)He appraises the pleasures of the 14 realms.
##2.2)He also appraises the miseries that subsequently follow those pleasures; therefore he develops {!vairāgya!} toward those pleasures, maintains profound love only for God.
##2.3)He possesses greater strength of understanding.
#3.)A devotee who is resolute in yoga and {!sānkhya!}:
##3.1)He realizes that, with the exception of God’s Akshardhām, the form of God in that Akshardhām and His devotees in that Akshardhām, everything else - all of the realms, the deities, and the opulence of the deities - is perishable and maintains profound love only for God.
##3.2)He never experiences any sort of hindrances whatsoever when encountering adverse circumstances.
##3.3)Just as a {!choko!} (kitchen: in the Swāminārāyan {!Sampradāy!}, place where renunciants and devotees eat) is mopped clean after a meal has been eaten, similarly, this devotee’s understanding is pure (i.e. he believes everything except God, Akshardhām and the {!muktas!} is wiped cleaned - perishable.)

19860.t:
#1.)When the renunciant who has worldly desires passes away, he will become a wealthy householder either in this Mrutyulok or in Devlok, where he will attain an abundance of {!vishays!} to indulge in. He will eventually develop {!vairāgya!} towards them; and then, feeling guilty in his mind, he will engage in the worship of God, become free of worldly desires and attain the abode of God.
#2.)Even though the householder has contact with a woman (his wife) and wealth, if he is free of worldly desires, he will attain the abode of God.
#3.)If one becomes addicted to serving God and His {!Sant!} to the extent that one would not be able to stay for even a moment without serving them, then all of the impure desires in one's {!antahkaran!} will be destroyed.
#4.)The means to extremely please God:
##4.1)Just as a poor householder is loving and humble with the {!Sant!}, he remains loving and humble if he were to attain the kingdom of Indralok or Brahmalok.
##4.2)Even after attaining powers similar to those possessed by God, if he can continue to menially serve all {!sādhus!} in exactly the same manner as he did when he was new and timid…
##4.3)Not impose one’s authority upon other {!sādhus!} or compete with them.

19861.t:
#1.)A devotee of God should never do anything that displeases God and His {!Bhakta!}.
#2.)Anything that hinders him in worshipping God:
##2.1)One should forsake his own relatives or any {!swabhāvs!} just as one forsakes one’s enemy.
##2.2)He should suppress even {!gnān!} of the {!ātmā, vairāgya!} or {!dharma!}.
#3.)One who perceives flaws in others and virtues in himself:
##3.1)He may be known as a {!satsangi!}, but he should be known to be half-fallen.
##3.2)No matter how great he may be, he will certainly encounter hindrances on the path of liberation.
#4.)One who perceives virtues in all {!satsangis!} and flaws in himself, his Satsang becomes stronger day by day.
#5.)When God gives advice to someone, if they accept it positively, He develops affection for them.

19862.t:
#1.)Shriji Mahārāj speaks about His own nature for the sake of revealing the ideals of a devotee:
##1.1)He does not become angry for his own sake.
##1.2)If someone transgresses his own {!dharma!}, if someone abuses the meek, or if someone sides with injustice, He becomes angry only for a brief moment and it subsides immediately.
##1.3)He never develops a grudge due to anger.
#2.)The harm caused by anger:
##2.1)If one becomes angry at the meek, then one may also become angry at God.
##2.2)If anyone hurts the meek, then God who resides in the meek will be offended.
#3.)Means to overcome anger:
##3.1)Contemplating on the greatness of God with {!Rājipāno vichār!}.
##3.2)Contemplating on the path of a {!sādhu!}.
#4.)If the {!Motāpurush!} becomes pleased, then the factors of place, time, etc. will not be angle hinder one in their path of liberation; if the {!Motāpurush!} is displeased, then even if the factors of place, time, etc. are favourable, they will hinder one in their path of liberation.
#5.)When no impure desires are left in one’s heart, the {!Motāpurush!} is pleased.
#6.)One should offer {!bhakti!} and {!upāsanā!} remaining within one’s {!dharma!} – to promote this principle, Shriji Mahārāj relaxed the emphasis on renunciation and built {!mandirs!}.

19863.t:
#1.)Shriji Mahārāj speaks about His own nature for the sake of revealing the ideals of a devotee:
##1.1)He has great compassion for devotees of God.
##1.2)He develops an aversion towards anyone who spites devotees of God.
##1.3)He does not feel like speaking to anyone who speaks ill of devotees.
##1.4)He becomes extremely pleased with one who menially serves the devotees of God.
##1.5)Only after He has observed a person for many days does He become pleased or displeased, but He does not become pleased or displeased with a person merely upon hearing someone else’s opinions of that person.
##1.6)If one is a genuine devotee of God, then He is a devotee of that devotee, and He does the {!bhakti!} of such devotees of God.
##1.7)In order to please God, He desires only to serve devotees of God in this life and all subsequent lives.
#2.)One who serves a devotee of God:
##2.1)God is pleased with that person.
##2.2)Only they go to the abode of God – Akshardhām.
#3.)One who spites a devotee of God:
##3.1)God is displeased with that person.
##3.2)They regress.
#4.)This discourse is the essence of all essences contained in all of the {!shāstras!} on the earth; It is the most fundamental principal and is a lifeline.

19864.t:
#1.)Characteristics of one who is attached to God: if one is exhausted from a prolonged walk, if one is suffering from an ailment and does not have the strength to sit upright, if one is insulted, or if one appears to be totally engrossed in the wealth and property one has attained; even so, the moment one hears talks of God, one behaves as if nothing happened.
#2.)The means to become firmly attached to God:
##2.1)Strong {!sanskārs!} from previous lives.
##2.2)Serving the {!Sant!} who has such firm attachment with God.

19865.t:
#1.)All of the sacred scriptures are truthful, and so reality reflects what is stated in those scriptures.
#2.)Gold and women are the source of extreme attachment. One does not become attached to these when:
##2.1)One becomes {!brahmarup!} and worships Parabrahma.
##2.2)One realises Prakruti and all of the entities which have evolved from it as being {!asatya!}, perishable and worthless and develops intense {!vairāgya!} towards them.

19866.t:
#1.)Cosmic evolution ({!Utpatti Sarg!}): Parabrahma > Aksharbrahma > Prakruti-Purush > Pradhān-Purush > Vairāj-Purush > Rām, Krishna, and other {!avatārs!}.
#2.)The {!jivas!} and {!ishwars!} are bound to {!māyā!}.
#3.)Only when Purushottam Nārāyan enters Vairāj-Purush are {!avatārs!} of God possible through Vairāj-Purush.
#4.)By associating with Brahma through constant contemplation, the {!jiva!} acquires the virtues of Brahma and the attachment to {!māyā!} in the form of unconsciousness is broken
#5.)By offering {!upāsanā!} to deities, such as Brahmā, etc., instead of God, one attains {!dharma, artha!}, and {!kām!} but not {!moksha!}.
#6.){!Jiva, ishwar, māyā!}, Brahma, and Parabrahma are the five eternal entities.

19867.t:
#1.)Just as the branch of a cactus, banyan, or a pipal tree is cut and planted elsewhere, it will grow into a new plant; similarly, when affection for a family member is cut, it will grow again.
#2.)Means to uproot affection for one’s family: discarding vanity of caste and {!āshram!}, believing one’s self to be {!brahmarup!}, and maintaining one’s {!vrutti!} on God.
#3.)The {!jiva!} transcends {!māyā!} and becomes {!brahmarup!} through the knowledge of the manifest form of God, meditation, devotional songs, spiritual discourses, etc.
#4.)Liberation is due to {!bhakti!} alone.
#5.){!Ātmā!}-realisation, {!vairāgya!}, and {!dharma!} are aides in offering unhindered {!bhakti!} to God.
#6.)By staying under the influence of adverse places, times, action, company, etc., one’s heart becomes polluted and one’s {!swabhāvs!} do not remains stable.

19868.t:
#1.)Shriji Mahārāj speaks about His own nature for the sake of revealing the ideals of a devotee:
##1.1)If it appears to Me that I have a liking for something, I would only be happy after I have discarded it.
##1.2)In no way do I ever experience an aversion towards a devotee of God.
##1.3)Even though I am persistently offered the {!panchvishays!}, I do not have any desire for them and push them away
##1.4)From when I was born to this very day, I have never harboured an improper thought regarding women or wealth, either in the waking or dream state
##1.5)Only the contemplation of God remains within My heart.
##1.6)One who firmly observes the vow of non-lust:
###i.)My affection for such a person never diminishes.
###ii.)I would be close to him, even if I were a thousand miles away from him.
###iii.)I like to be served by such a person.
###iv.)Such a person will be close to Me, both in this realm and beyond.
##1.7)If one transgresses the vow of non-lust, then:
###i.)I become extremely displeased with the person.
###ii.)I am a thousand miles away from him, even if I am physically close to him.
###iii.)I am extremely pained.
#2.)Means to firmly observing the vow of non-lust:
##2.1)Controlling the mind by engaging in the nine types of {!bhakti!} and by contemplating on one’s {!ātmā!}.
##2.2)Keeping the {!prāns!} under control by keeping one’s diet under control.
##2.3)Remaining within the {!niyams!} of Satsang.
#3.)One who discards lust, anger, greed, and other internal enemies to please God is a staunch {!sādhu!}.
#4.)What is impossible to achieve with this human body?

19869.t: #1.)The {!māyik!} elements in the form of the effect – body, {!indriyas, antahkaran!} – are {!jad!} (non-living; without consciousness).\n#2.)The presiding deities, who are the causes of the elements in the form of the effect, are {!chaitanya!} (living, possessing consciousness).\n#3.)The {!jiva!} pervades the body, {!indriyas!}, etc.; therefore, the {!māyik!} body, {!indriyas!}, etc. appear to be {!chaitanya!} (but in reality, they are {!jad!}).

19870.t:
#1.)Only by meditating on God can one attain {!ātmā!}-realisation.
#2.)The reason for developing {!ātmā!}-realisation is so one does not harbour any love for one’s body or their relatives and so there are no hindrances in the {!bhakti!} of God.
#3.)It is not possible to attain liberation by {!ātmā!}-realisation or {!dharma!} alone.
#4.)Regardless of how much a person may have mastered {!samādhi!}, or how thoughtful the person may be, if men and women begin to stay closely together, there is no way their {!dharma!} will remain.
#5.)The {!upāsanā!} of the manifest form of God, listening to and narrating the divine incidents of God, and chanting His holy name:
##5.1)If one stays within his {!dharma!} along with the aforementioned three attributes:
###i.)The {!jiva!} goes to God’s abode at the end of his life.
###ii.)He will remain peaceful even during times of physical misery.
##5.2)If one does not stay within his {!dharma!}, then his liberation is impossible.
#6.)One should listen to and sing the devotional songs and poems written by Muktānand Swāmi and other {!sādhus!}.
#7.)Shriji Mahārāj delivered this discourse for our liberation; therefore, by behaving accordingly, He will be extremely pleased.

19871.t:
#1.)One whose {!vrutti!} continuously remains on God is fulfilled and has nothing further to achieve.
#2.)Methods to continuously maintain one’s {!vrutti!} on the form of God:
##2.1){!Chitt!} has natural tendency to become engrossed in everything; therefore, employing the {!chitt!} to become engrossed in God.
##2.2)Become extremely brave.
##2.3)Fear birth, death, {!narak!} and the cycles of births and deaths.
##2.4){!Vairāgya!}.
##2.5)Grace of God.
##2.6)Intense affection for God.
#3.)Affection for anything other than God is {!māyā!}.
#4.)A person who has severed affection for his body, its relations and those who provide for his body is said to have transcended God’s {!māyā!}.

19872.t:
#1.)Means to eradicate one’s innate nature:
##1.1)Total faith in the guidance given by the {!Satpurush!}.
##1.2)Intense affection for the {!Satpurush!}.
##1.3)No matter how painfully strong the {!Satpurush's!} words seem, accepting those words to be for one’s own benefit and perceiving virtues in the {!Satpurush!}.

19873.t:
#1.)Whoever has faith in charms, spells or witchcraft, even though he may be a {!satsangi!}, should be considered to be half-fallen.
#2.)One who possesses the virtues of {!ātmā!}-realisation, {!vairāgya, dharma!}, and profound {!bhakti!} for God is called an {!ekāntik bhakta!}.
#3.)One who is an {!ekāntik bhakta!} ‘merges’ into God; but one who is not an {!ekāntik bhakta!} ‘merges’ into Brahmā or other deities.
#4.)One who has merged with God:
##4.1)He does not develop affection for anything except God.
##4.2)He continuously thinks of God.
##4.3)If he lives without God, he would pass his days in misery but would not be happy.

19874.t:
#1.)Shriji Mahārāj speaks about His own natural virtues for the sake of revealing the ideals of a devotee:
##1.1)He does not harbour any desire for the {!panchvishays!}.
##1.2)Regardless of how much {!pravrutti!} He is involved in, He still experiences profound bliss within.
##1.3)He has a very strong conviction that God possesses a divine form and is the all-doer.
##1.4)He becomes pleased only when He sees a genuine devotee of God and is only comfortable with such a person.
#2.)The senior devotees must absolutely observe the vow of non-lust, because the example set by the seniors is what is followed by everyone else.
#3.)The essence of the tenth canto of the Shrimad Bhāgwat: God that is mentioned in the scriptures, is the very manifest form of God before you.
#4.)The essence of the fifth canto of the Shrimad Bhāgwat:
##4.1)One should understand the greatness of the manifest form of God.
##4.2)God assumes different forms ({!murtis!}) to bestow bliss upon His devotees.
##4.3)One should abide by the {!niyams!} prescribed by God.
#5.)By narrating or listening to the divine incidents of God, one attains the highest state of enlightenment.
#6.)By believing God to be formless, one incurs a sin greater than the five grave sins. There is no atonement for this.
#7.)If a person who realises God to possess a form with firm conviction happens to commit a sin, by the grace of God, all of those sins will be burnt and his {!jiva!} will attain God.

19875.t:
#1.)Harming or spiting a devotee of God:
##1.1)If it happens knowingly or unknowingly through thought, word or deed, then to atone for this:
###i.)One should physically and mentally offer one extra prostration daily.
###ii.)One should verbally pray to atone.
###iii.)One should strive to avoid harming a devotee again.
##1.2)Can be caused by greed, egotism, jealousy, and anger.
##1.3)One who harms a devotee of God is not liberated but suffers intense misery.
##1.4)One who does not harm a devotee of God becomes extremely blissful.
#2.)A {!jiva!} is liberated by serving a devotee of God mentally, verbally, and physically; it is not liberated by any other means.

19876.t:
#1.)Serving God and devotees:
##1.1)Should be considered to be one’s extremely great fortune.
##1.2)Should be done only to please God.
##1.3)Should be done only for one’s liberation.
##1.4)Should be done with {!bhakti!}.
#2.)The nature of a {!jiva!} is such that he only enjoys doing that which satisfies his vanity.
#3.)When a dog chews on a dry bone, its mouth becomes abraded and bleeds. The dog takes pleasure in tasting its own blood. Similarly, the {!jiva!} takes pleasure in its own ego.
#4.)One who worships God having forsaken vanity is an extremely great devotee amongst all devotees.

19877.t:
#1.)Aksharbrahma:
##1.1)In its {!sagun!} aspect, it is much larger than even the largest of objects. Countless millions of {!brahmānds!} dwell like mere atoms in each and every hair.
##1.2)In its {!nirgun!} aspect, it is extremely subtle and smaller than an {!anu!} (an atom-like unit).
#2.)Parabrahma:
##2.1)Forever resides in His abode Akshardhām.
##2.2)His will always prevails ({!satya-sankalp!}).
##2.3)While remaining in Akshardhām, He manifests in whatever form is required in whichever {!brahmānd!}.
##2.4)Wherever Purushottam resides, that is the very centre of Akshardhām.
#3.)Aksharbrahma is the ‘key’ to unlocking (understanding) the greatness of Purushottam.

19878.t: #1.)A devotee who is {!brahmarup!} and behaves only as the {!ātmā!} still possesses love for God.\n#2.)One who loves God having become {!gunātit!} is {!brahmarup!}.

19879.t:
#1.)Due to the influence of adverse places, time, company, etc., one perceives more flaws in a devotee.
#2.)A godly devotee:
##2.1)Must have had the company of the {!Motāpurush!} or the {!darshan!} of God in his previous life.
##2.2)Perceives his own flaws but never perceives flaws in other devotees of God.
#3.)A demonic devotee:
##3.1)Never perceives his own flaws but perceives flaws in other devotees of God.
##3.2)Even if he stays in Satsang, he is similar to Kālnemi, Rāvan and Rāhu.

19880.t:
#1.)Shriji Mahārāj says that those who belong to Him:
##1.1)He does not want even the slightest imperfection to remain in them.
##1.2)He does not wish to allow any trace of the horde of 51 ghosts to remain. He does not wish to allow any influence of {!māyā!} to remain; on the contrary, He wants to make them realize their true self is {!ātmā!} and worship God.
##1.3)Therefore, all of you remain vigilant because even with a little carelessness, your footing in Satsang will not last.
#2.)God and His {!Sant!}:
##2.1)If they are displeased, then despite the fact that one had performed such {!karmas!} that would have led one to {!swarg!}, one would instead be consigned to {!narak!}.
##2.2)If they are pleased, then even if one were destined to fall into {!narak!}, all of one’s impure {!karmas!} would be destroyed and one would instead attain the highest state of enlightenment.

19881.t:
#1.)A {!Satpurush!} living in this world is not pleased or pained upon seeing the worldly progress or regress of a person. However, when someone’s mind recedes from the path of God, he becomes grieved.
#2.)God assumes {!avatārs!} upon earth for the purpose of establishing {!ekāntik!} {!dharma!}.
#3.)If one develops an aversion toward God or His {!Sant!}, then:
##3.1)He falls from {!ekāntik!} {!dharma!}.
##3.2)That is a sin greater than the five grave sins.
##3.3)That itself is death for that devotee.
##3.4)He does not attain God’s abode.
#4.)If one does not perceive flaws in God or His {!Sant!}, then all of one’s sins are destroyed and one dwells in the abode of God.

19882.t:
#1.)A {!sādhu!} aspiring for liberation ({!mumukshu!} {!sādhu!}):
##1.1)The more he is made upset or vishays {!denounced!}, he increasingly becomes overjoyed and perceives virtues.
##1.2)He eradicates his impure desires by the profound association of the {!Sant!}.
##1.3)He bears only one wish: To become {!brahmarup!}, offer devotion to God, and to attain God’s abode.
#2.)A {!sādhu!} who has desires for {!vishays!}:
##2.1)He remains with a senior {!sādhu!} due to the temptation of enjoying {!vishays!}.
##2.2)He should be considered like a wretched person or like a dog.
##2.3)He is worse than one who has committed the five grave sins.
#3.)Just as if the earth that has been split down to Pātāl, the gap can never be filled with water; similarly, the {!indriyas!} have never become satisfied by the {!vishays!}, and they never will be.
#4.)Renunciants and householders should mutually understand each other’s greatness.

19883.t:
#1.)Premānand Swāmi sang the “Vandu” {!kirtans!} in front of Shriji Mahārāj.
#2.)One who continuously contemplates on God:
##2.1)Shriji Mahārāj wishes to prostrate before such a person.
##2.2)He attains the highest state of enlightenment while alive.
##2.3)He and his parents become fulfilled.
##2.4)He is freed from the bondage of {!kāl, karma!} and {!māyā!}.
##2.5)He is the greatest among all of the devotees.
##2.6)He is called an {!ekāntik bhakta!} of God.
##2.7)He only enjoys the {!vishays!} related to God.
##2.8)Shriji Mahārāj wishes to be born amongst such a devotee.
##2.9)By his association, others also develop continuous contemplation of God.
#3.)One who contemplates on objects and {!vishays!} other than God:
##3.1)His misery never comes to an end even after countless millions of years.
##3.2)It should be considered he has become lost in the path of liberation.
#4.)The company of such a {!sādhu!} who is a knower of Brahma, as well as the direct {!darshan!} and contemplation of God are extremely rare.

19884.t:
#1.)There is a great difference between the manifest form of God and {!māyik!} forms, because:
##1.1)Those who do the {!darshan!} of the manifest form of God and contemplate upon it escape from the bondage of {!kāl, karma!} and {!māyā!} and become an {!akshar-mukta!} (attendants of God).
##1.2)Those who see {!māyik!} forms and contemplate upon it spend countless millions of years wandering in the cycle of births and deaths.
#2.)In order to guide His devotees, Shriji Mahārāj says: Just as My mind never becomes satiated with spiritual discourses, devotional songs, talks related to God or meditation of God, all of you should also not become satiated doing the same.

19885.t:
#1.)Shriji Mahārāj speaks about His principles for the sake of revealing the ideals of a devotee:
##1.1)I have kept My {!ātmā!} absorbed in the pure and perfect Aksharbrahma.
##1.2)I have continuous affection for God and His devotees.
##1.3)Worldly desires never arise in My heart, not even in My dreams.
##1.4)I do not wish to leave any trace of the world in the hearts of whosoever keeps My company.
##1.5)Only those devotees of God who are free of worldly desires are dear to Me.

19886.t:
#1.)As long as the influence of the {!gunas!} remains within a person, he will never experience happiness; only when he behaves as the {!ātmā!} does he become happy.
#2.)One who follows the commands of the {!Satpurush!}:
##2.1)Is behaving as the {!ātmā!}.
##2.2)Can be said to be under the influence of favourable circumstances.
#3.) One who does not follow the commands of the {!Satpurush!}:
##3.1)Can be said to be under the influence of adverse circumstances.
##3.2)Will never experience happiness.

19887.t:
#1.)That which befits a householder is not appropriate for a renunciant, and that which befits a renunciant is not appropriate for a householder.
#2.)A renunciant should think, “Which {!āshram!} do I belong to?” But he should not stray onto some inappropriate path like a fool.
#3.)If a wise person is scolded, he would consider the scolder’s virtues; however, if someone offers advice to a fool, the fool would be offended.
#4.)Shriji Mahārāj likes one who performs bhakti with {!shraddhā!} and without jealousy.

19888.t:
#1.)Not being able to perceive one’s own flaws is the characteristic of delusion ({!moh!}).
#2.)Egotist:
##2.1)He does not know anything about his {!jiva!}.
##2.2)He does not know the greatness of God.
##2.3)He perceives flaws in God’s divine incidents and His understanding.
##2.4)He should be considered a non-believer, a sinner, and the king of all fools.
##2.5)It is out of his own foolishness that he perceives flaws in God and His {!Bhakta!} and thus falls from the path of God.
#3.)God’s true {!Bhakta!}, the {!Satpurush!}, continues to act in a transcendental way.

19889.t:
#1.)God is not as pleased by any spiritual endeavours as much He is pleased by Satsang.
#2.)One who regards Satsang as the greatest spiritual endeavour is profoundly attached only to the {!Bhakta!} of God.
#3.)One who does not regard a {!Sant!} to be a place of pilgrimage, does not regard a {!Sant!} to be a venerable {!murti!}, does not regard a {!Sant!} to be one’s own relative, and does not regard a {!Sant!} to be one’s own self, should be considered to be like a donkey.
#4.)One who has profound attachment to God and His {!Sant!} will never attribute faults in them.

19890.t:
#1.)Shriji Mahārāj speaks about His inclinations for the sake of revealing the ideals of a devotee:
##1.1)In His childhood: Enjoyed going to {!mandirs!} for {!darshan!}, listening to spiritual discourses, keeping the company of {!sādhus!}, and going on pilgrimages.
##1.2)When He renounced His home: He did not like to keep clothes and liked to stay in the forest without fear.
##1.3)After joining Satsang:
###i.)He constantly has the thought that death is impending (and thus He doesn’t have an interest in objects or worldly life.)
###ii.)Constantly feels that {!māyik!} objects are perishable and insignificant.
###iii.)All of His activities are for the sake of the devotees of God; but not for His own personal enjoyment.
###iv.)He keeps a little fear for the benefit of Satsang.
###v.)A thought remains within His heart that: “I am the {!ātmā!}, distinct from the body; I am not like this body.” Also, His mind is always cautious, lest a portion of {!māyā!} in the form of {!rajogun, tamogun!}, etc. infiltrate his {!ātmā!}. He is constantly vigilant of that.
#2.)The mind, hands, speech, ears, and other {!indriyas!} of an {!ekāntik!} {!bhakta!} always perform activities related to God.
#3.)The heart takes the form of a goldsmith’s workshop. {!Māyā!}, in the form of the goldsmith, uses deceit for the sake of the {!indriyas!} and {!antahkaran!}, in the form of the goldsmith’s wife and children. {!Māyā!} steals the virtues of {!gnān, vairāgya!}, etc., in the form of gold, from the {!ātmā!} and replaces it with {!māyik!} flaws, such as the three {!gunas!}, attachment to {!panchvishays!}, etc., in the form of silver.
#4.)Just as gold can be purified from the silver that is mixed with it, the {!jiva!} should be filtered from the {!māyik!} flaws by contemplating on one’s {!ātmā!}; and one should remain vigilant that the {!māyik!} flaws are not mixed with the {!jiva!} again.

19891.t:
#1.)Only his love for God is true who never develops love for anything other than God.
#2.) The essence of all the scriptures:
##2.1)God is the sole source of eternal bliss and the supreme essence of everything.
##2.2)Excluding God, all other objects are absolutely worthless and totally unsubstantial.
#3.)Just as a lightly dyed cloth is ruined if it gets wet; similarly, when one who has love for the {!panchvishays!} encounters bad company, he will not remain stable.
#4.)To please God:
##4.1)Discard {!panchvishays!}.
##4.2)Abandon affection for objects other than God.

19892.t:
#1.)One should become {!brahmarup!} and develop affection for God.
#2.)The {!Ātmā!} has no {!māyā!}, but it may seem the {!ātmā!} has {!māyā!} due to ignorance.
#3.)The reason for cultivating {!ātmā!}-realization:
##3.1)So that in no way does one perceive any fault in God.
##3.2)Just as any insect that comes near a light is killed by a lizard; in the same way, the thought that rests within the light of the {!ātmā!} destroys everything apart from the {!ātmā!}.
#4.)The mark of true renunciation is that, if there were an object that appears to be dearer to him than God, he would completely discard it.
#5.)A person may outwardly renounce many other things but if he cannot discard an object that hinders him in worshipping God, then his renunciation is useless.
#6.)If a person truly loves God having realized God to be the source of immense bliss, he would never develop love for anything else.
#7.)A devotee who develops affection for objects other than God:
##7.1)Possesses an utterly petty mentality.
##7.2)Believes that there are pleasures in such miseries and thus develops affection for worthless objects.
##7.3)He is nothing but a ‘cat-like’ (deceitful) devotee.
#8.)A genuine devotee of God:
##8.1)There is no object dearer to Him than God.
##8.2)He possesses {!gnān, vairāgya, bhakti!} and {!dharma!}.
##8.3)He bears no cowardice in talking about God, even if he faces hindrances.
#9.) Whoever has even a little affection for God will not regress on the path of liberation.

19893.t: #1.)Only the scriptures that narrate the incidents of one’s Ishtadev will foster the {!sampradāy!}.

19894.t:
#1.)God and His {!Sant!}:
##1.1)Only they can grant liberation, which is the central principle of all the scriptures.
##1.2)God’s {!Sant!} is greater than even Bhava, Brahmā, and the other deities.
##1.3)Attainment of God or His {!Sant!} is itself ultimate liberation.
##1.4)Those who have accumulated a great number of merits from performing good deeds receive the opportunity to serve God’s {!Sant!}.
##1.5)If one develops affection for God’s {!Sant!} just as one has affection for one’s wife, son, parents or brother, then:
###i.)In no way would one perceive flaws in the {!Sant!}.
###ii.)The {!jiva!} becomes absolutely fulfilled.
#2.)A person who attained God and His {!Sant!} and served them in his past lives:
##2.1)His affection for God and His {!Sant!} would never diminish.
##2.2)Even if his disturbing thoughts related to lust, anger or avarice persisted, his faith in God would not dissolve.

19895.t:
#1.)The solutions to remaining happy amidst the difficulties encountered in life:
##1.1)Awareness of the {!ātmā!}.
##1.2)Awareness of the perishable nature of all worldly objects.
##1.3)Awareness of God’s greatness.
#2.)Just as one is loyal to one’s relatives, one should be loyal to the devotees of God.
#3.)A genuine devotee of God:
##3.1)Becomes distressed upon seeing the misery of another devotee of God.
##3.2)Never develops a grudge if a difficulty arises with another devotee of God.
##3.3)Maintains loyalty to God and His devotees.
#4.)One who does not feel misery seeing another devotee’s misery:
##4.1)Is a non-believer.
##4.2)Develops a grudge with a devotee of God, with feelings of enmity.
##4.3)Is never liberated, despite pursuing countless spiritual endeavours.
##4.4)Believes that all {!sādhus!} are equal.
##4.5)Does not show loyalty to a devotee of God when he hears someone speak ill of that devotee.
#5.)If one looks angrily at a devotee of God or hurts him, Shriji Mahārāj develops an aversion towards that person, but He does not feel any compassion for him.

19896.t:
#1.)A person who possesses these three attributes completely – {!niyam, nishchay!} (faith in God), and {!paksha!} (loyalty) – is a staunch {!satsangi!}.
#2.)The greatest among all devotees is one who:
##2.1)Has surrendered everything to God and His devotees.
##2.2)Would give his life for Satsang.
##2.3)Would immediately become a {!sādhu!} upon his Ishtadev’s command.
#3.)The greatest among all renunciants is one who, despite encountering wealth and women in his travels to other regions, remains unaffected and continues to firmly adhere to all of his {!niyams!}.
#4.)One who is considered to be respectable in society and worldly affairs should be treated accordingly so but should not be insulted.

19897.t:
#1.)If, when one engages in the worship of God, his {!indriyas, antahkaran!} and {!jiva!} all unite and become engrossed in worship, then even if he does so for half an hour, all of his sins will be burnt to ashes and he will be liberated.
#2.)When one places their body, wealth, home, family and relations in the service of God, then his {!jiva!} is liberated.
#3.){!Ātmā!}-realisation, fidelity, and servitude – if one has any one of these three inclinations, then their {!jiva!} is liberated.
##3.1)Characteristics of one with {!ātmā!}-realisation:
###i.)A thought, full of {!gnān!}, remains between one’s {!ātmā!} and the vicious natures of {!māyā!}.
###ii.)All of the {!vruttis!} remains absorbed in the {!ātmā!}.
###iii.)The {!jiva’s!} {!kāran!} body, which is full of worldly desires, is said to be destroyed.
###iv.)He has the realisation of himself as being {!brahmarup!}.
###v.)He also has the realisation of Parabrahma Nārāyan - who resides within his {!ātmā!}.
##3.2)Characteristics of one with fidelity:
###i.)He attaches his {!vruttis!} to God just as a faithful wife does with her husband.
###ii.)His mind would never become pleased upon seeing anyone else.
##3.3)Characteristics of one with servitude:
###i.)He only likes the {!darshan!}, talks, nature, and company of his Ishtadev.
###ii.)If his Ishtadev were to give a command that would force him to stay far away, he would happily stay there.
##3.4)Means to cultivate these three inclinations: Behave as a servant of the servants of a devotee who possesses one of these three inclinations and following his commands.
#4.)One should worship God after discarding a perverse nature, one’s personal likes and dislikes, and eradicating all desires other than those of God.
#5.)God Himself inspires hardships to befall upon His devotees in order to test their patience but not {!kāl, karma!} and {!māyā!}.
#6.)Realising it to be God’s wish, a devotee of God should remain cheerful in the midst of any misery.
#7.)One who has received the opportunity to serve God’s {!Bhakta!} should remain fearless and fulfilled.

19898.t:
#1.)If one’s {!jiva!} has become extremely powerful:
##1.1)He allows the {!indriyas!} and {!antahkaran!} to apply themselves wherever it is appropriate to do so and restricts them from doing as they please where it is inappropriate to do so.
##1.2)He would not have impure dreams.
#2.)By behaving as the {!ātmā!}, one’s {!jiva!} gains great strength; however, the greater and incomparable method to gain strength is:
##2.1)Developing an intense affection for God and His {!Sant!}.
##2.2)Maintaining intense {!shraddhā!} in serving them.
##2.3)Engaging in the nine types of {!bhakti!}.
##2.4)Sincerely serving God and His devotees by thought, word and deed.
#3.)During the final moments of life, when one has the {!darshan!} of God and His {!Sant!}, countless mental and physical miseries are expelled.
#4.)The greatness of the Bhakta of God:
##4.1)He is nothing but a form of Brahma, therefore, one should never perceive human traits in him.
##4.2)Spiting him is the greatest sin.
##4.3)Shriji Mahārāj does not even like to look at anyone who develops a grudge with God or His devotees. His anger with such a person never subsides.

19899.t:
#1.)Purushottam Bhagwān:
##1.1)Is the source of all {!avatārs!}, the master of countless {!brahmānds!}, and beyond birth.
##1.2)Despite residing in Akshardhām, through his yogic powers, He appears in countless places at once.
##1.3)He possesses all the skills and all the virtues.
##1.4)All of the wonders are due to His yogic powers.
#2.)God’s Akshardhām:
##2.1)In its {!vyatirek!} form, it transcends Prakruti-Purush.
##2.2)In its {!anvay!} form, it pervades everywhere.
##2.3)God eternally resides in Akshardhām.
#3.)Even while residing in one place - His Akshardhām – God appears in countless places in His pervasive form. But He is not pervasive in a formless way like {!ākāsh!}.

19900.t:
#1.)For the sake of accepting the {!bhakti!} of His devotees, God thoroughly indulges in the {!panchvishays!}. Seeing this, those who are over-wise perceive faults in God.
#2.)A {!sādhu!} who has realised the {!ātmā!} and has become {!brahmarup!} is not infatuated upon seeing any object of this world. Therefore, Parabrahma, who transcends even Brahma, is certainly uninfluenced by {!māyā!}.
#3.)God appears like a human, yet his transcendental greatness is not realised – that itself is God’s {!māyā!}.
#4.)If one has {!ātmā!}-realisation and {!vairāgya!} but does not have {!bhakti!} towards God, then he will not be liberated.
#5.)If one has {!bhakti!} towards God, but does not have the virtues of {!ātmā!}-realisation and {!vairāgya!}, then just as one has love towards God, one will also develop love towards other things.
#6.)When one possesses all three virtues of {!ātmā!}-realisation, {!vairāgya!} and {!bhakti!} towards God, one can be called a devotee with {!gnān!}, an {!ekāntik bhakta!} and a staunch devotee of God.

19901.t:
#1.)When a person offends a great devotee of God, his intellect becomes corrupted; therefore, he perceives faults in devotees without being able to realise his own faults.
#2.)Liberation is attained only by the refuge of God; whereas, spiritual endeavours and following God’s commands are for the purpose of pleasing God.
#3.)The form of the {!jiva!}:
##3.1)It is characterised by eternal existence, consciousness, and possesses the {!kāran!} body.
##3.2)It believes the {!sthul!} and {!sukshma!} bodies to be its own due to ignorance.
##3.3)When the {!jiva!} attains Akshardhām by worshipping God, by God’s will, the {!jiva!} receives a body composed of {!chaitanya!} {!prakruti!}.
#4.)Means to ensure that the manifest form of God and the {!Sant!} do not become secondary when one attains a state of enlightenment:
##4.1)One should look towards the {!Motāpurush’s!} words and conduct for inspiration.
##4.2)Just as when a man has been accused of something and has no witnesses to disprove the allegation, then he proves his innocence by holding a red-hot iron ball; similarly, if a fault cannot be realised, one should pray to God for the eradication of that fault: “Mahārāj, please be compassionate and destroy whichever faults I may have.”
#5.)If a person has absolute faith in God, then he would never have faith in anyone but God.
#6.)One who has attained God and His {!Sant!}:
##6.1)His days and nights are spent engrossed in spiritual discourses, devotionals songs, etc.
##6.2)He believes himself to be {!brahmarup!}.
##6.3)He develops an aversion toward objects other than God.
##6.4)He discards {!adharma!} and abides by {!dharma!}.
##6.5)When he dies, just like God, he also becomes free form {!kāl, karma!}, and {!māyā!}, and forever resides in the service of God.

19902.t:
#1.)A devotee of God who has acquired qualities similar to God understands that:
##1.1)God has granted me just as many divine powers and as much charm as I had realised in Him. Yet, God’s divine powers and charm appear to be totally limitless.
##1.2)Like me, countless others have also attained qualities similar to that of God, yet, His majesty does not diminish.
##1.3)No one is capable of becoming like God.
#2.)Even when a devotee of God becomes {!brahmarup!}, he behaves as God’s servant and engages in His worship.
#3.)Shesh, Shāradā, Brahmā, the four Vedas, and even God Himself cannot fathom the vastness of God’s greatness or His countless redemptive virtues.

19903.t:
#1.)Even if the {!prāns!} are not controlled, one is said to have attained {!nirvikalp!} {!samādhi!} if:
##1.1)One has taken a firm refuge in the manifest form of God.
##1.2)One has a firm conviction in the manifest form of God without any form of doubts.
#2.)Even if the {!prāns!} are controlled, it is still considered to be {!savikalp!} {!samādhi!} if:
##2.1)One continues to harbour doubts towards the form of God.
##2.2)One does not feel fulfilled by attaining the manifest form of God.
##2.3)One desires to see God residing in His abode.
#3.)One who takes fight with his mind:
##3.1)If he wins against the mind, then he attains {!nirvikalp!} {!samādhi!} and becomes an {!ekāntik bhakta!} of God.
##3.2)If he loses to the mind, he falls from his spiritual endeavours. Then, maybe after one life or two lives or even after many lives, ultimately, he will become an {!ekāntik bhakta!}.
#4.)One who aspires for liberation should develop enmity towards his mind.

19904.t:
#1.)God is pleased by understanding Him to be the all-doer and possessing a definite form. Not believing this is maligning God.
#2.)A complete {!gnāni!}:
##2.1)Understands God’s form through the four scriptures: Veda, Sānkhya scriptures, Yoga scriptures, and Panchrātra scripture.
##2.2)God is extremely pleased on such a person.

19905.t:
#1.)One who has {!dharma, gnān, vairāgya!}, and {!bhakti!} is called an {!ekāntik bhakta!} and is worthy of being made eminent in Satsang.
#2.)If one has intense {!bhakti!} for God coupled with the knowledge of His greatness, then {!dharma, gnān!}, and {!vairāgya!} are incorporated in {!bhakti!}; but they are not incorporated in ordinary {!bhakti!}.
#3.)Four types of eminent {!Purush!}:
##3.1)Like a small flame: they are extinguished by the wind in the form of the {!vishays!}.
##3.2)Like a torch: they are extinguished by stronger gusts of wind in the form of the {!vishays!}.
##3.3)Like lightning:
###i.)They are not extinguished even by rainwater in the form of {!māyā!}.
###ii.)They become an {!ekāntik!} {!sādhu!} by spiritual endeavours.
##3.4)Like the {!vadvānal!} fire:
###i.)Stays in the ocean without being extinguished by the ocean water.
###ii.)Transforms even the ‘salty’ {!jivas!} who are like the saline sea water, into ‘sweet’ {!jivas!}.
###iii.)He is God’s {!Param-Ekāntik Sant !} and is eternally enlightened.
#4.)If a person serves one who is like lightning or the {!vadvānal!} fire - by thought, word and deed, then {!bhakti!} coupled with the knowledge of God’s greatness develops in that person.

19906.t:
#1.)All spiritual endeavours for attaining liberation are incorporated in keeping the company - by thought, word and deed - of a {!Sant!} who possesses the 30 attributes of a {!sādhu!}.
#2.)When water goes into a fountain, it first revolves in a spiral and then spurts upwards; in the same way, the {!vrutti!} of the {!jiva!} revolves in a spiral in the {!antahkaran!}, which acts like the fountain, and then spurts out through the five {!indriyas!}.
#3.)A God’s devotee who is a yogi keeps his {!vrutti!} on God’s form in two ways:
##3.1)He contemplates on God residing in his heart as the witness.
##3.2)He contemplates on the external form of God in front of his eyes.
#4.)The method of beholding God’s form:
##4.1)Contemplating upon the whole form of God from head to toe; but not separately upon any single part of the body.
##4.2)Merging together both the form of God that resides in one’s heart as a witness, and the form of God that is outside.
##4.3)Becoming separate from one’s {!indriyas!} and {!antahkaran!} through a thought process and beholding God’s form residing in the {!ātmā!}.

19907.t:
#1.)One who has the firm conviction of God having realised that God transcends {!māyā!}, then he also becomes devoid of {!māyik!} qualities and transcends {!māyā!}.
#2.)A devotee who has sought total refuge of God:
##2.1)Abandons all other forms of {!dharma!} and accepts the refuge of God only.
##2.2)Even if he were to experience pain equivalent to that of final dissolution, he would not believe anyone else to be his guardian against such misery except God.
##2.3)Does not consider anyone but God to be the source of happiness.
##2.4)Behaves only according to the wishes of God.
#3.)One who does not have complete refuge of God:
##3.1)His deceit can be recognized only after staying and working together with him.
##3.2)He would not be able to tolerate the pressure of living with the fellowships of devotees.
#4.)If one serves God and his ideal {!Sant!} with utmost love, then if he were to be liberated after one hundred lives, he would instead be liberated in this very life.

19908.t:
#1.)During the period of creation, God, who is the giver of the fruits of {!karmas!}, gives the {!jivas!} residing in {!māyā!} their bodies according to their {!karmas!}.
#2.)The {!kāran!} body:
##2.1)The {!sthul!} and {!sukshma!} bodies reside in it like seeds.
##2.2)It is the form of ignorance, eternal, and retention of the {!sanchit!} {!karmas!}.
##2.3)The {!jiva!} and the {!kāran!} body have an eternal relationship.
#3.)Of the strength of {!kal, karma!}, and the will of God – the predominance of these should be considered according to the circumstances.

19909.t:
#1.)The godly {!jivas!} always become devotees of God.
#2.)The demonic {!jivas!} always remain opposed to God.
#3.)God’s form:
##3.1)If He associates with {!māyā!}, He makes {!māyā!} free of impurities, like Akshardhām.
##3.2)Even though God is {!anvay!} and pervades within {!māyā!} and the entities that have evolved from it; yet, He still remains uninfluenced by {!māyā!}.
##3.3)Even while pervading everything, He resides in His abode in His {!vyatirek!} form.

19910.t: #1.)Just as a spider stretches its web from one pillar to another, and then sometimes goes to one pillar, then to the other pillar, or sometimes sits between the two pillars, similarly, a meditating yogi sometimes becomes absorbed in God’s form; at times he stays within his own {!antahkaran!}; and at other times he stays between his {!antahkaran!} and God.\n#2.)One should believe one’s true form is {!brahmarup!}, separate from the three bodies, and keep their {!vrutti!} on God.

19911.t:
#1.)God’s {!nirgun!} bliss:
##1.1)Even if one experiences it for only a moment, one feels, “I’ve enjoyed the bliss of God in {!samādhi!} for thousands of years.”
##1.2)It is eternal and imperishable.
#2.){!Māyik!} happiness: Even if it is experienced for a long time, it feels temporary and perishable.

19912.t:
#1.)One who aspires for their liberation should recognise God in the form of a {!sādhu!} (39 characteristics of God’s {!avatars!} in the form of a {!sādhu!}) or the form of a king (30 characteristics of God’s {!avatars!} in the form of a king) and:
##1.1)Seek refuge in Him.
##1.2)Have complete faith in Him
##1.3)Perform His {!bhakti!} while remaining in His commands.
#2.)When God is not manifest on this earth, one should seek the refuge of the {!Sant!} who has the realisation of God.
#3.)When even such a {!Sant!} is present but one cannot recognise Him, one should keep firm faith in God’s {!murti!} and perform {!bhakti!} while observing {!swadharma!}.

19913.t:
#1.)If anyone harms (spites) God, a devotee of God, {!Brāhmin!}, or the meek, then:
##1.1)His {!jiva!} is destroyed.
##1.2)Shriji Mahārāj detests even the sight of him.
##1.3)Such a person will never attain Shriji Mahārāj’s company, either in this realm or in other realms.
#2.)One should never keep egotism of any sort before God or His devotee, because:
##2.1)Egotism is the cause of anger, {!matsar!}, and jealousy.
##2.2)The {!bhakti!} of an egotist becomes demonic.
#3.)Shriji Mahārāj commanded everyone to sing and memorize {!‘Mārā harji shu’!} and {!‘Mārā vahālāji shu’!} daily.
#4.)The pundits of the world do not understand the greatness of God and the {!Sant!} because:
##4.1)They do not have the refuge of God.
##4.2)They are overpowered by their inner enemies (ego, anger, lust, jealousy, etc.).
##4.3)They perceive God and His {!Sant!} to be flawed just like themselves.
#5.)When one develops intense affection for the {!Satpurush!}:
##5.1)One never perceives any kind of fault in the {!Satpurush!}.
##5.2)One will always believe the {!Satpurush's!} words.
