##5.3)It is the only means to realising one’s {!ātmā!}.
##5.4)It is the only means to realising the greatness of the {!Satpurush!}.
##5.5)It is also the only means to having the direct realisation of God.

19914.t:
#1.)Shri Purushottam Bhagwān, whose form is forever divine, while seated in Akshardhām, assumes the {!avatārs!} to grant liberation to the {!jivas!}.
#2.)One who develops faith in the manifest form of God through the profound association of a {!Sant!}, then:
##2.1)He progresses spiritually day by day like the waxing moon and finally becomes fulfilled like the full moon.
##2.2)Regardless of the type of action God performs, he does not perceive any fault in God.
##2.3)He becomes a fearless devotees.
##2.4)He is convinced of his liberation and also those who come into his contact.
#3.)One who perceives faults in God’s action due to influence of unfavourable place, time, etc. or due to identifying one’s self with the body, then he falls from the path of liberation.
#4.)One who does not have conviction of the manifest form of God coupled with the knowledge of His greatness:
##4.1)Does not develop conviction of his liberation.
##4.2)No one attains liberation by hearing even holy scriptures like the Gitā and the Shrimad Bhāgwat from him.

19915.t:
#1.){!Samādhi!} occurs in two ways:
##1.1)Anyone who does {!darshan!} of the manifest form of God with {!shraddhā!}, then all of their {!indriyas!} are drawn towards God and he instantly enters {!samādhi!}. 
##1.2)If God wishes to attract many people towards Him then He grants them {!samādhi!} due to His grace.
#2.)While possessing a definite form in His abode Akshardhām, God pervades everything due to His divine powers; but He is not pervasive in a formless way like {!ākāsh!}.

19916.t: #1.)By seeking the refuge of the {!Satpurush!}, regardless of how terrible a sinner a person may be, he becomes extremely pure.\r\n#2.)A person who maligns the {!Satpurush!} is a terrible sinner, regardless of how sincere he may seem to be in abiding by {!dharma!}.

19917.t: #1.)There are two types of {!jivas!}: godly and demonic.\r\n#2.)One becomes godly or demonic due to one’s company, {!karma!}, and the grace or wrath of the {!Satpurush!}.

19918.t:
#1.)Shriji Mahārāj speaks about His principles for the sake of revealing the ideals of a devotee:
##1.1)He does not get along with worldly, eminent men because they have pride of their power and wealth; whereas, Mahārāj has pride of renunciation and {!bhakti!}.
##1.2)Compared to the bliss of worshipping God, the bliss of the 14 realms is equivalent to {!narak!}.
##1.3)His only insistence is encouraging others to worship God and practice Satsang.

19919.t:
#1.)The means to develop an aversion to the {!panchvishays!}:
##1.1)Realising the miseries in the {!panchvishays!} and developing firm {!vairāgya!} toward them.
##1.2)Knowing the misery one will suffer by indulging in the {!panchvishays!}.
##1.3)Knowing the redemptive virtues of God.
#2.)Characteristics of one who has conquered his {!indriyas!}:
##2.1)He bears an extreme aversion toward the {!panchvishays!}.
##2.2)He spends his life in offering the nine types of {!bhakti!} to God.
#3.)A renunciant who follows the path of {!pravrutti!}:
##3.1)Should abide by the {!niyams!} given by God.
##3.2)Should abandon the vices such as lust, anger, etc.
##3.3)Should consider only the service and {!pravrutti!} related to God and His devotees as a form of {!bhakti!}.
##3.4)He is greater than a renunciant who only possesses {!ātmā!}-realisation.
##3.5)He becomes worthy of earning God’s grace.

19920.t:
#1.){!Satsangis!} should certainly know these facts:
##1.1)The customs of the Swāminārāyan {!Sampradāy!}.
##1.2)The succession of gurus.
##1.3)The eight scriptures that were accepted as authoritative by Shriji Mahārāj.
##1.4)The {!niyams!} of all {!satsangis!}.
##1.5)The manifest and non-manifest forms of God.
#2.)The form of God:
##2.1)Is {!nirgun!}.
##2.2)Whoever comes into contact with God also becomes {!nirgun!}.
##2.3)He is the source of all {!avatārs!}.
#3.)One should not make distinctions in the mode of {!upāsanā!} of God due to the differences in His divine actions.
#4.)Everyone should abide by their {!dharma!} and offer {!bhakti!} according to Shriji Mahārāj’s word, but no one should imitate His behaviour.

19921.t:
#1.)God and His {!Sādhu!} are always present on the Earth; however, only those who recognise them become a devotee of God.
#2.)A devotee of God:
##2.1)Does not wish for the pleasures of {!panchvishays!}.
##2.2)Regards the pleasures of the 14 realms to be extremely insignificant.
##2.3)Shows great indiscretion when he, out of ignorance, desires any object other than God.
##2.4)Bears affection toward God and God’s {!Bhakta!} by thought, word, and deed.
##2.5)Does not enter the cycle of births and deaths or go to {!narak!}.
##2.6)Is not able to describe the greatness of God and bliss enjoyed by a true devotee of God.

19922.t:
#1.)If the seeds of lust and other such vices are not burnt from one’s heart and one attains {!nirvikalp!} {!samādhi!}, then these vices will cause a disturbance.
#2.)If one has an understanding like that of King Janak:
##2.1)He remains unaffected and undisturbed even on the path of {!pravrutti!}.
##2.2)He can discern that which this is true and that which is false.
##2.3)He understands all worldly forms to be perishable and full of miseries.
##2.4)He realises himself to be the {!ātmā!}.
##2.5)The seeds of lust, anger, etc., in his heart will be destroyed.
##2.6)He is the greatest amongst all, whether he is a renunciant or a householder.
##2.7)Under no circumstances, should he associate with any type of evil influences.

19923.t:
#1.)The method of the miraculous meditation:
##1.1)Looking inwardly within one’s {!hrudayākāsh!} (inner self) by introspection.
##1.2)Looking toward one’s {!jiva!} and God that resides there.
#2.)Benefits of the miraculous meditation:
##2.1)One attains the {!darshan!} of God’s {!Vishwarup!} form.
##2.2){!Nāstik!} feelings are removed.
##2.3)The {!jiva!} gains strength.
##2.4)One becomes convinced of the scriptures.
##2.5)One attains the eight yogic powers.
##2.6)One attains enlightenment like Nārad, the Sanakādik and Shukji.
#3.)An {!ekāntik bhakta!} of God who practises this meditation can master it.

19924.t:
#1.)Four types of dissolution ({!pralays!}):
##1.1){!Nitya-pralay!}: {!Jiva’s!} deep sleep, when all of the {!jiva’s!} adjuncts are absorbed.
##1.2){!Nimitta-pralay!}: {!Ishwar’s!} deep sleep when all of the {!ishwar’s!} adjuncts are absorbed.
##1.3){!Prākrut-pralay!}: All of the entities that had evolved from Prakruti are assimilated back into Prakruti, in which one {!brahmānd!}, which is the adjunct of Pradhān-Purush, is destroyed.
##1.4){!Ātyantik-pralay!} - There are two types:
###i.){!Vāstavik-pralay!}: Everything up to and including Prakruti is eclipsed by the light of Brahma.
###ii.){!Gnān-pralay!}: By becoming {!brahmarup!}, one overcomes the influence of Prakruti.
#2.)One who worships God after becoming {!brahmarup!} by way of {!gnān-pralay!}:
##2.1)Is a superior devotee.
##2.2)Is never engulfed by the adjuncts of {!māyā!} again.
##2.3)If at any time he does assume a physical body, then just like God assumes a body by His own will, he also assumes a body by his own will.
##2.4){!Kāl, karma!} or {!māyā!} do not control his fate.

19925.t:
#1.)Even if the roots of a banyan tree, except for minor roots, are uprooted, the tree remains green. Similarly, one may have outwardly renounced the {!panchvishays!}, but if thoughts of them are entertained, then those thoughts become a cause of births and deaths.
#2.)For one who has attained the state of {!upsham!}, the {!panchvishays!} do not become a cause of births and deaths.
#3.)Methods of attaining the state of {!upsham!}:
##3.1)Main method: meditating upon God after {!ātmā!}-realisation.
##3.2)Second Method:
###i.)First: Understanding the greatness of God.
###ii.)Second: Doing {!darshan!} of God and serving Him and His {!Bhakta!} with extremely intense {!shraddhā!}.
#4.)God is pleased with one who serves him humbly.
#5.)Even if one does not have wisdom and understanding, yet has an intense yearning for liberation, then he still knows how to do whatever pleases God.

19926.t:
#1.)If one has firm {!ātmā!}-realisation and firm {!vairāgya!}, then no obstacles due to adverse circumstances will come in the way of one’s {!bhakti!}.
#2.)Due to firm {!ātmā!}-realisation, the {!māyik!} pleasures are negated; and due to firm {!vairāgya!}, all forms except for God’s form and all {!vishays!} are negated.
#3.)One who has an inclination of {!gnān!}:
##3.1)Understands the profound greatness of God.
##3.2)Understands God to be {!antaryāmi!}.
##3.3)Understands that God recognises a devotee’s inclination and speaks to him accordingly, but He does not act based on others’ advice.
#4.)One who has an inclination of affection:
##4.1)Cannot stay without God even for a moment.
##4.2)Would be willing to do whatever is necessary for God.
##4.3)Would never develop anger or jealousy toward or perceive a fault in God or His devotees.
#5.)One who perceives faults in God does not possess either the inclination of {!gnān!} or affection.
#6.)One should read the Shikshāpatri daily.

19927.t:
#1.)Means for developing love for God, making Satsang predominant in one’s heart, and developing {!vairāgya!} from the world:
##1.1)Worshipping God after realizing what their own inclination is.
##1.2)One should feel repentant when objects other than Satsang become predominant in one’s heart.
##1.3)Understand the greatness of Satsang.
##1.4)Developing conviction in the guru - who is the manifest form of God - in the same way that he has conviction in the non-manifest deities. As a result, he attains all of the {!arthas!} ({!dharma, arth, kām!} and liberation).

19928.t: #1.)Does one who has {!ātmā!}-realisation and {!vairāgya!} and is {!brahmarup!} harbour compassion and affection for God and His devotees?\r\n##1.1)One who has understood the greatness of God and His devotees through Satsang does harbour compassion and affection.\r\n##1.2)One who has gained {!gnān!} through {!kusang!} does not harbour these two.

19929.t:
#1.)Recalling the objects that one has falsified in one’s heart is called {!bādhitānuvrutti!}.
##1.1)One has {!bādhitānuvrutti!} as long as one does not attain {!nirvikalp!} {!samādhi!}
#2.)Regardless of whether a devotee of God dies in a disturbed state due to the influence of {!bādhitānuvrutti!} or while engaged in the chanting of God’s name, that devotee still reaches God’s abode.
#3.)A non-believer who dies with full consciousness will be consigned to {!narak!}.
#4.)The form of the {!jiva!}:
##4.1)It predominantly resides in and pervades the disc of flesh that sits in the heart.
##4.2)It is indestructible and luminous.
##4.3)It pervades the entire body.
##4.4)God resides in the {!jiva!} as a witness.

19930.t:
#1.){!Bhakti!} coupled with the knowledge of God’s greatness:
##1.1)With this type of {!bhakti!}, one does not encounter any obstacles of any form.
##1.2)If one does not have this type of {!bhakti!}, then one will encounter obstacles in his {!bhakti!}.
##1.3)Arises in one’s heart by serving and profoundly associating with eminent {!sādhus!} ({!Motāpurush!}).
#2.){!Sakām!} devotee: superficially appears to be a renunciant and free of other desires, yet he has desires other than a desire for the manifest form of God; hence, he attains less bliss (i.e. bliss of higher realms of deities but not God’s abode).
#3.){!Nishkām!} devotee: He may possess a lesser extent of renunciation and may become disturbed by desires; yet he does not desire for anything other than the manifest form of God; hence, he attains higher bliss in God’s abode.

19931.t:
#1.)One who wants to please God:
##1.1)Should not offer {!bhakti!} to please others (displaying it to others) or out of jealousy of someone.
##1.2)Should offer {!bhakti!} only for the sake of one’s liberation.
#2.)To blame the {!indriyas!} and {!antahkaran!} when one commits a mistake while offering {!bhakti!} is the foolishness of the {!jiva!}.
#3.)The {!jiva!} and the mind are mutual friends, because the mind never entertains thoughts that the {!jiva!} does not like.
#4.)One should develop intense hatred for {!adharma!} arising from one’s mind or by some other person, so one’s mind or the other person will not attempt to persuade him again.
#5.)If a devotee offers {!bhakti!} to God with this understanding, the evil influence of some non-believer or his own mind will not be able to affect him.

19932.t:
#1.)God and His {!Sādhu!}:
##1.1)Nothing in this world is more blissful than them.
##1.2)One should profoundly attach one’s self to them.
##1.3)One should remain absolutely loyal to them.
##1.4)One should not develop an aversion to them.
##1.5)One should not have as much affection towards one’s body or bodily relations as one has towards them.
#2.)For a devotee who behaves in this manner (as described in 1.1-1.5), even extremely powerful enemies such lust, anger, etc., are unable to defeat him.
#3.)In Akshardhām:
##3.1)God possesses a definite form.
##3.2)Devotees of God, who also possess a form, remain in His service.
#4.)Devotees who have taken firm refuge in the manifest form of God:
##4.1)Just as an iron nail that is firmly affixed to an iron surface can never be separated, similarly, their mind should be fixed firmly at the holy feet of God.
##4.2)They does not have to die to attain the abode of God - they have attained it while still alive.
##4.3)They attain God’s abode after they discard their physical body.
##4.4)They should not harbour the following fear in one’s mind: ‘What if I become a ghost or an evil spirit, or attain the realm of Indra or the realm of Brahmā after I die?’

19933.t:
#1.)Means to remaining eternally happy in this world and the realm beyond:
##1.1)Gaining control of the {!indriyas!} with {!vairāgya!} and {!swadharma!}.
##1.2)Relationship to God and his {!Bhakta!}:
###i.)Developing intense love and maintaining friendship with them.
###ii.)Never becoming indifferent towards them.
###iii.)Being pleased only by the company of them.
##1.3)Not liking the company of a non-believer.
#2.)Obstacles in {!bhakti!} toward God:
##2.1)Not realizing one’s own drawbacks.
##2.2)Becoming aloof from God and His {!Bhakta!}.
##2.3)Developing indifference towards the {!Bhakta!} of God.

19934.t:
#1.)The elevated state and understanding of Shriji Mahārāj and the senior {!paramhansas!}:
##1.1)They remain standing at the gateway of God’s abode in the form of awareness and engage in the {!darshan!} of God.
##1.2)They do not allow {!māyik!} objects to enter their heart where God dwells.
##1.3)Even if they encounter countless difficulties, they do not sway from their elevated state.
##1.4)While introspecting, they remain in the service of God and also perform their bodily activities.
#2.)Commands given by Shriji Mahārāj to His devotees:
##2.1)One should serve God with constant introspection.
##2.2)One should not develop an affection for any object except God.

19935.t:
#1.)During the final dissolution, everything that evolved from Prakruti-Purush will be destroyed; therefore, all the places on earth, including Vrundāvan and Kāshi, will also be destroyed.
#2.)Shriji Mahārāj elaborates on the fundamental principles:
##2.1){!Jiva, māyā, ishwar!}, Brahma and Parabrahma are eternal.
##2.2)By God’s will, when {!ishwar!} unites with {!māyā!}, then the {!jivas!} arise from {!māyā!} and assume their physical bodies; but new {!jivas!} are not created.
##2.3)The {!jivas!} are not a component of God.
##2.4)When a {!jiva!} seeks the refuge of God, it overcomes God’s {!māyā!}, becomes {!brahmarup!}, and attains the abode of God.

19936.t:
#1.)Means to conquer the {!indriyas!} 
##1.1){!Vairāgya, Swadharma!}, Austerities and {!Niyams!}.
#2.)Means to conquer the mind
##2.1)The nine types of {!bhakti!} coupled with the knowledge of God’s greatness.
#3.)If the devotee has profound attachment and deep love for God and His Bhakta, just like the attachment and love that he has for his own body, then:
##3.1)He forever experiences the type of bliss that prevails in {!nirvikalp!} {!samādhi!}, even without attaining that {!samādhi!}.
##3.2)Regardless of the adverse circumstances he may encounter, he will not fall from the path of liberation.
#4.)Understanding of Sitāji: Despite no fault of her own, Rām Bhagwān exiled Sitāji to the forest out of fear of public accusation; however she did not perceive any fault in Rām Bhagwān.
#5.)One should only keep the company and intense love for one who has an understanding like Sitāji (does not perceive faults in God and His Bhakta), even though that person’s {!dharma!} and {!vairāgya!} may be moderate.
#6.)One should not keep the company of one who despite having intense {!vairāgya!} and {!dharma!}, does not have an understanding like Sitāji (perceives faults in God and His {!Bhakta!}).

19937.t:
#1.)One who desires one’s own liberation:
##1.1)Should not harbour any form of vanity. Even with a meek {!satsangi!}, one should behave as a servant of servants.
##1.2)Should not malign God and His {!Bhakta!}.
##1.3)If he listens to or keeps affection for one who has perceived faults in God or His {!Bhakta!}, then he becomes a non-believer.
##1.4)Should not harbour deep affection for one’s bodily relations.
##1.5)Should become aloof from worldly life, harbour love for God, and continue to engage in the worship of God.
#2.)If one perceives a fault in God or His {!Bhakta!}:
##2.1)The demonic attitude is never eradicated from the heart.
##2.2)Will have to continuously die and be reborn for countless millions of years.
##2.3)Will never be able to walk on the path of liberation.
##2.4)No scripture describes methods to be released from such a sin (of perceiving fault in God and His {!Bhakta!}).
##2.5)Their {!jiva!} is destroyed.
#3.)This discourse is like a magical technique because by understanding this, one will never encounter obstacles on the path of liberation.

19938.t:
#1.)If one understands this way, then God protects one’s {!ekāntik!} {!dharma!} from unfavourable {!kāl!} and {!karma!}:
##1.1)Realises God’s greatness such that the slightest significance of riches, opulence, etc. does not remain.
##1.2)Does not bear affection for anything except God and attaches one’s mind to the holy feet of God.
##1.3)Develops intense love for God and His devotees, such that not even {!kāl, karma, māyā!}, nor one’s own mind can destroy that love.
##1.4)Believes God to be the sole controller of this body; therefore only does whatever pleases God.
##1.5)Never prays before God in this manner: “Mahārāj! Please relieve me of my misery.”
##1.6)Understands that the will of God is our {!prārabhda!} and there is no other {!prārabdha!} for us.
##1.7)Understands that whatever pain or pleasure we encounter is by the wish of God; thus one should not become disturbed in any way.
#2.)Shriji Mahārāj speaks about His preferences for the sake of revealing the ideals of a devotee:
##2.1)I like meditating on God in a secluded place; however, I have remained in Satsang seeing the fellowship of devotees.
##2.2)Even if a non-devotee tries to keep Me by a million means or serve me, I do not get along with him.
##2.3)I experience such ecstasy that I feel as if I shall become mad due to it.

19939.t:
#1.)Reasons for not developing deep affection for God:
##1.1)One does not have discretion, believing that the pleasures of women and other objects are extremely rare. Realising their immense pleasure, one develops affection for them.
##1.2)One has discretion, yet intense, sinful {!karmas!} have left impressions on his mind.
#2.)By performing intense, pure {!karmas!}:
##2.1)Influence of very intense, sinful {!karmas!} will be destroyed.
##2.2)One will develop affection for God.
##2.3)One acquires discretion and {!vairāgya!}.
#3.)Godly {!jivas!}:
##3.1)Always adhere to the path of God.
##3.2)Under the influence of favourable circumstances, their vicious nature is destroyed.
#4.)Demonic {!jivas!}:
##4.1)Always turn away from the path of God.
##4.2)Even under the influence of favourable circumstances, their vicious nature is not destroyed.
##4.3)If his wishes are not fulfilled and he is even slightly disturbed, he would intensely malign God or His {!Sant!}.
#5.)Of the nine types of {!bhakti!}, whichever type aids one in developing firm attachment to God is the best type of {!bhakti!} for that particular person.
#6.)A person earns the trust of God and His {!Sant!} when:
##6.1)Even if he falls severely ill and is not cared for very well during that illness, he still does not bear an aversion towards anyone.
##6.2)Even if he is harshly insulted by God and His {!Sant!} without any fault of his own, he still does not bear an aversion towards anyone.
##6.3)Maintains his resolve in observing {!niyams!} of Satsang:
###i.)If there were to be the slightest infringement, he would feel extremely repentant and would immediately perform atonement.
###ii.)Even if he were to entertain an evil thought in his mind, he would feel just as repentant and distressed as someone who had happened to physically infringe the observance of religious vows.
#7.)A devotee who has faith in God and totally accepts whatever God says is the best.
#8.)One who understands the greatness of God and His {!Bhakta!} behaves this way through thoughts, words, and deeds:
##8.1)Serves God and His {!Bhakta!} sincerely and lovingly.
##8.2)Physically bows and touches the feet of all of the {!sādhus!}.
##8.3)Serves {!sādhus!} who fall ill.
##8.4)Offers objects that he likes to the {!sādhus!}.
#9.)A {!Motāpurush!} possesses intense {!dharma, gnān, vairāgya!} and {!bhakti!}; yet sometimes, there may be some relaxation in his observance of dharma purely out of compassion for the {!jivas!}.

19940.t: #1.)Just as if an injured warrior’s wounds are not dressed with bandages (or wounds are not appropriately cared for), the pain of the wounds does not cease; in the same way, if a devotee who has been ‘wounded’ by the {!panchvishays!} due to the influence of unfavourable places, times, etc. does not offer {!bhakti!} according to his particular inclination, then he will not experience happiness whilst engaged in {!mānsi!} {!pujā!} or mediation because he will crave the {!panchvishays!}.\n#2.)One should engage in chanting God’s name, meditation, etc. having recognised one’s inclination.

19941.t: #1.)The solution to not develop affection for anyone other than God:\n##1.1)Just as a wife observes the vow of fidelity; similarly, one should not have affection for anyone else (even previous {!avatārs!} or {!mukta!} {!sādhus!}) except for the manifest form of God one has attained.\n##1.2)Abide by the wishes of one’s Ishtadev.

19942.t: #1.)Bharatji went to worship God in the forest, where he developed affection for a deer. Consequently, he was reborn as a deer in his next life. Therefore, developing affection for anyone other than God is an extremely grave sin.\n#2.)In his third birth, Bharatji behaved as a madman so that he would not develop affection to anyone except God, allowing him to fix his {!vrutti!} continuously on God. One should be fearful in the same manner such that they do not develop affection for anyone except God.

19943.t:
#1.)The dreams that springs forth are due to ingrained desires ({!vāsanā!}) generated by {!karmas!} performed in past lives.
#2.)By associating with the {!Satpurush!}, the ingrained desires gradually degenerate.
#3.)When the thoughts related to God defeat the thoughts related to the {!vishays!}, then it should be understood that one’s ingrained desires have degenerated.
#4.)One who is free of worldly desires only engages in worldly activities to the extent of the instructions given by God. One who is not free of worldly desires would not be able to detach himself from worldly activities through God’s instructions or even by his own accord.

19944.t:
#1.)Two undesirable traits of a renunciant: lust and affection for his relatives.
#2.)One should not keep affection for one’s relatives and for those who serve him, because:
##2.1)This type of person repulses Mahārāj.
##2.2)It is a sin graver than the five grave sins.
##2.3)His life becomes futile.
##2.4)One begins to have thoughts of {!māyā!} and becomes bound by {!māyā!}.
#3.) The means to eradicating these two undesirable traits:
##3.1)Understand: “I am the {!ātmā!}, distinct from this physical body; and I have no relationship with anyone.”
##3.2)Shun all those who obstruct one’s worship of God, knowing them to be {!avidyā!} (i.e. {!māyā!}).
##3.3)This discourse should be said and heard daily; and if one fails to do so, then one should observe a fast.

19945.t: #1.)The {!karmas!} that the {!jiva!} has performed during past lives, which have ripened and become assimilated with the {!jiva!}, are called {!swabhāv, prakruti!}, or {!vāsanā!}.\n#2.)By performing {!bhakti!} with {!ātmā!}-realisation, {!vāsanā!} is eradicated.

19946.t:
#1.){!Bhāgwat!} {!dharma!}:
##1.1)Is {!ekāntik!} {!dharma!} itself.
##1.2)Is related to God.
##1.3)God’s {!avatārs!} manifest for the purpose of establishing {!bhāgwat!} {!dharma!}.
##1.4)The {!jiva!} attains God’s abode through {!bhāgwat!} {!dharma!}.
##1.5)Its eminence is equal to that of {!bhakti!}.
#2.)Mere {!dharma!} of one’s caste and {!āshram!} is inferior compared to {!bhāgwat!} {!dharma!} and the fruits of the {!dharma!} of one’s caste and {!āshram!} are temporary.
#3.)Shriji Mahārāj gives His opinion for the sake of revealing the ideals of a devotee:
##3.1)If Mahārāj tries to develop affection to anything other than God and His devotees, He cannot do so.
##3.2)Mahārāj prefers to stay only in forests or mountains but not in large towns or cities. Despite this, He stays in the midst of thousands of people for the sake of God and His devotees.
##3.3)No matter how much {!pravrutti!} Mahārāj has to engage in, He does so for the sake of His devotees, understanding it to be {!nivrutti!}.
##3.4)One should not take note of minor flaws seen in devotees.
##3.5)If an argument arises with another devotee of God, one should derive pleasure in deliberately losing the argument.
##3.6)Whoever perceives flaws in devotees and speaks ill of them:
###i.)Mahārāj does not like to look at them.
###ii.)Mahārāj does not like food or water offered by their hands.
###iii.)Even if they are His relatives, Mahārāj develops an intense dislike for them.
##3.7)All of the {!satsangis!} are the same as the attendants of God residing in Akshardhām.
##3.8)Only those who have firm Satsang are Mahārāj’s true kith and kin.
##3.9)Mahārāj wishes to remain in the midst of such {!satsangis!} during this life and even after leaving His physical body.
#4.)One who offers {!bhakti!} without {!ātmā!}-realisation:
##4.1)Will be extremely distressed by lust, ego, and other internal enemies.
##4.2)Their true nature will be exposed in Satsang.
#5.)A thread of gold remains the same in all six seasons; similarly, when one’s Satsang is firm, regardless of the amount of misery that may befall one or however many times one is insulted in Satsang, one’s mind never turns away from Satsang.
#6.)A thread dipped in wax remains stiff in winter and monsoon, but it becomes slack during summer; similarly, when a devotee is insulted in Satsang or becomes physically distressed, he will withdraw from Satsang out of his own accord.

19947.t:
#1.)One who has {!bhakti!} characterised with profound love:
##1.1)Their attachment to {!panchvishays!} will diminish.
##1.2)They maintain {!ātmā!}-realisation without trying.
#2.)A devotee who has the same attachment for wealth and women as he has towards God:
##2.1)He is not a staunch devotee of God.
##2.2)This sin becomes ingrained in one, as if etched in iron.
#3.)To malign God and His {!Bhakta!}:
##3.1)Is the gravest of all sins
##3.2)There is no release from this sin.
##3.3)God becomes displeased by this sin and is hurt.
##3.4)One who commits this sin falls from his eminent position.
#4.)If one maligns a devotee of God knowingly or unknowingly:
##4.1)One should look at one’s own faults and look at the virtues of God’s devotees.
##4.2)One should bow to that person’s feet, pray to him, and act in a manner that pleases him.

19948.t:
#1.)One who performs {!mānsi!} {!pujā!} in various ways according to the three seasons has:
##1.1)His love for God increase.
##1.2)His {!jiva!} benefit tremendously.
#2.)When God or His {!Bhakta!} reprimands one:
##2.1)One should consider it to be his great fortune.
##2.2)One should believe that it will help in removing their flaws.
##2.3)One should not feel grief, nor get upset, nor regard oneself as being sinful.
##2.4)One should remain pleased.

19949.t:
#1.)One attains the service of God in Akshardhām through the sixteen spiritual endeavours - {!shraddhā, swadharma!}, etc.
#2.)One whose attention is constantly focused on all of God’s mandates, major or minor, should be known as one who would not fall from his {!dharma!}.
#3.)By practising Satsang for the fulfilment of one’s self-interest, one’s innate nature is eradicated.
#4.)Mahārāj develops love for a person who does not become disheartened when He repeatedly fires harsh words at them.
#5.)If {!vairāgya!} is coupled with {!gnān!}, then one does not become bound by {!vishays!} even during unfavourable circumstances.
#6.)Regarding discourses of God:
##6.1)The aversion one develops for the world and the extent to which one’s vicious natures are eradicated is proportionate to one’s attachment to listening to the discourses of God.
##6.2)If one has laziness in listening to the discourses of God, then one will not acquire noble virtues.
#7.)Male and female devotees should not understand the greatness of specific devotees of the opposite sex, instead they should understand each other’s greatness collectively (i.e. all of them are devotees of God).

19950.t:
#1.)When performing God-related activities, one should keep the desire for fruits in the form of pleasing of God.
#2.)A staunch devotee never falls back from his {!upāsanā, bhakti, niyams!}, and {!dharma!}; but becomes better, despite the extent of joy or misery he faces.
#3.)Shriji Mahārāj speaks of His likes and dislikes to show the ideals of a devotee:
##3.1)When speaking to God, Mahārāj dislikes one who speaks without discretion (i.e. speaks inconsistently, coarsely, interrupts, etc.).
##3.2)Dislikes one who is lazy, harbours an ego, or feels shame when performing God-related activities.
##3.3)Dislikes when one looks elsewhere while doing {!darshan!} of God.
##3.4)Dislikes one who is deceitful.
##3.5)Dislikes egotism, anger, and remaining suppressed by others.
##3.6)Dislikes devotees viewing each other as equal, thereby not giving respect to other appropriately.
##3.7)Likes female devotees who behave chastely by keeping their gaze downward and covering their bodies.

19951.t:
#1.)A {!Sant!} who is worthy of being worshipped on par with God:
##1.1)Suppresses the actions of the {!indriyas!} and the {!antahkaran!}.
##1.2)Only performs activities related to God.
##1.3)Is staunch in his observance of the five religious vows.
##1.4)Believing himself to be {!brahmarup!}, he worships Purushottam Bhagwān.
#2.)The characteristics of a person who does not become bound by the {!panchvishays!}, even during unfavourable circumstances:
##2.1)Has {!dharma!} predominant in his mind.
##2.2)Has the qualities of an {!āstik!} toward God.
##2.3)Is concerned about his own reputation.
##2.4)Has the attributes of genuine {!ātmā!}-realisation.
##2.5)Thoroughly understands the greatness of God.
##2.6)Firmly observes the five religious vows (vows of non-lust, non-avarice, non-taste, non-attachment, and non-egotism) in order to please God.
#3.)Shriji Mahārāj speaks about His own nature for the sake of revealing the ideals of a devotee:
##3.1)He does not like any form of vanity or hypocrisy.
##3.2)He does not like any person who, while worshipping God, eliminates the distinction between himself and God.
##3.3)He does not like a person who observes {!niyams!} liberally.
##3.4)He does not like a person who does not believe their true form to be the {!ātmā!}.
##3.5)If there is a devotee who thoroughly understands the greatness of God, observes dharma, and engages in the bhakti of God, he can be considered to be a staunch devotee. Despite having such virtues, if there is another devotee in the Satsang fellowship who does not understand anything yet has faith in God, then the former would consider the latter to be great. Shriji Mahārāj is extremely pleased with the former devotee.
##3.6)When speaking, he likes a person who never reveals even the slightest pride of his wisdom.

19952.t:
#1.)In God, one experiences the bliss of all of the {!vishays!} simultaneously; that bliss is extremely divine, eternal, and imperishable.
#2.)The happiness from the {!māyik!} {!vishays!} is extremely inferior, perishable, and ultimately the cause of misery.
#3.)A spiritual aspirant should develop {!vairāgya!} towards the worldly {!vishays!} and become totally attached to the divine and blissful form of God.
#4.)If a devotee has an intense yearning to engage in the {!bhakti!} of God and to associate with the {!Sant!}, then regardless of any {!swabhāv!} that he may possess, he eradicates it and behaves according to the {!Sant's!} will and command.
#5.)The obstinacy of observing the religious vows is essential to one’s life and is extremely beneficial. One should keep this type of obstinacy understanding its importance.
#6.)The obstinacy of one’s {!swabhāvs!} is inferior. If the {!Sant!} asks one to abandon it, it should be abandoned.
#7.)One who observes the religious vows keeping their {!swabhāvs!} is known as a {!rājarshi!} (a royal person who is below the elevated status of a {!brahmarshi!}). One who observes the religious vows and offers {!bhakti!} to please God is known as a {!brahmarshi!} and a genuine {!sādhu!}.
#8.)Egotism:
##8.1)The {!Sant!} does not have compassion for an egotistical person.
##8.2)Anger and lust arises from ego; therefore, it is a major vice.
##8.3)By keeping egotism, one falls from Satsang.
##8.4)By realising the greatness of God, egotism can be eradicated.
#9.)The {!Sant!} who possesses the attributes of {!panch-vartamān!} has a direct relationship with God. One should develop the conviction of God based on his words and that itself is the conviction of God.
#10.)Whoever has affection for a devotee with firm faith in God will be liberated.
#11.)If one does {!manan!} and {!nididhyās!} on the greatness of {!ātmā!} and Paramātmā, then one attains realisation and enjoys the same experience and bliss as one does in {!samādhi!}.

19953.t:
#1.)One falls from the {!bhakti!} of God by:
##1.1)Understanding God’s forms to be false from listening to scriptures by shushka-Vedāntis.
##1.2)Offering {!bhakti!} to God believing that one will enjoy pleasures of the {!panchvishays!} in God’s abode.
#2.)The {!jiva!} does not fall from {!bhakti!} by:
##2.1)Understanding that God is all-blissful, whereas the pleasures derived from the {!panchvishays!} have only a slight fraction of the bliss of God.
##2.2)Understanding that compared to the bliss of the abode of God, the pleasures of the other realms are like {!narak!}.
#3.)If one establishes conviction of God and the {!Sant!} without eradicating their deficiencies, then one may fall back from Satsang.
#4.)One who has realised the immense greatness of God:
##4.1)Will not harbour egotism, jealousy, and anger.
##4.2)Behaves as a servant of servants.
##4.3)No matter how much he is insulted, he will not abandon the company of God and the {!Sant!}.
#5.)If a devotee of God is placed on a {!shuli!} due to his {!karma!} and Shriji Mahārāj is standing next to him, if the devotee does not wish to be relieved of that misery and instead bears the hardships, then God becomes extremely pleased with him.
#6.)Only a person who does not believe the {!panchvishays!} to be his lifeline experiences God’s bliss. Only he is able to indulge in it. Only he attains it.

19954.t:
#1.)It is appropriate for one who has intense {!vairāgya!} to renounce from the stage of the {!brahmacharya!} {!ãshram!}.
#2.)If someone has developed profound attachment for the {!Ekāntik!} {!Sant!} and abides by His commands, then even if he does not have {!vairāgya!}, his renunciation will endure till the end.
#3.)Who does not sway from their {!dharma!} even during adverse times?
##3.1)One who is constantly aware of this thought: “If I do not remain alert and observe the religious vows, the love which Mahārāj has for us will not remain, and He will become displeased.”
##3.2)One who has intense {!vairāgya!}.
##3.3)One who has affectionately attached one’s {!jiva!} to a person who has intense {!vairāgya!}.
##3.4)One who keeps contact with Satsang, realises God to be {!antaryāmi!}, and behaves according to the {!niyams!} that have been prescribed for him.

19955.t:
#1.)For the sake of revealing the ideals of a devotee, Shriji Mahārāj talks about what he likes:
##1.1)He likes one who worships and offers {!bhakti!} to God with the firm conviction that God, forever possesses a form and resides in his abode Akshardhām.
##1.2)He likes one who engages in spiritual endeavours in order to please God without any form of pretentiousness.
#2.)For the liberation of His devotees, Shriji Mahārāj reveals His constant awareness of five thoughts:
##2.1)At this second, at this very moment, I will die and leave this body.
##2.2)Even though death is certain, this much work has already been accomplished and this much work is left, which I would like to complete.
##2.3)Have my desires for the {!panchvishays!} been eradicated from My mind or not?
##2.4)Have desires for the {!panchvishays!} in senior {!sādhus!} and devotees been eradicated or not?
##2.5)I should not become dejected, because it is by My association everyone happily engages in the {!bhakti!} of God.
#3.)Performing {!bhakti!} of God in this manner is the only great benefit of living.

19956.t:
#1.)The {!murti!} of Purushottam Bhagwān in Akshardhām:
##1.1)The {!avatārs!} occur from that form.
##1.2)Transcends both the perishable ({!kshar!}) and imperishable ({!akshar!}).
##1.3)Is the cause of all causes.
##1.4)Is currently manifest to liberate the {!jivas!}.
##1.5)There is no difference between the form residing in Akshardhām and the manifest form of God on Earth; just as the form in Akshardhām is {!gunātit!}, the human form of God is also {!gunātit!}.
#2.)Just as the changing position of the sun causes shadows to change; similarly, meditating on God’s form from various locations of the body causes God’s form to vary.
#3.)When the vision of a person who meditates on the human form of God develops extreme {!vairāgya!} from the {!panchvishays!} and remains engrossed only in the charm of God, then he does not notice any difference between the manifest form of God and the form in His abode.

19957.t:
#1.)If one who is in his youth behaves this way, then he will remain in Satsang:
##1.1)Reduces one’s diet and eats and behaves moderately.
##1.2)Lovingly engages one’s mind in the nine types of {!bhakti!}.
#2.)A genuine devotee:
##2.1)Just as he understands the greatness of God who resides in Akshardhām, he understands the greatness of the manifest form of God.
##2.2)With the exception of God, he understands all other worldly objects to be absolutely vain and perishable.
##2.3)He only develops affection for God.
##2.4)In order to please God, he abides by God’s commands.
#3.)A person with a corrupt mind:
##3.1)Believing God to be the uplifter of the wretched and the redeemer of sinners, he does not hesitate in committing sins under the pretext of knowing God’s greatness.
##3.2)Such a person is wicked and sinful.
##3.3)One should abandon the company of such a person.

19958.t:
#1.)The mind of one who has {!ātmā!}-realisation, {!vairāgya!}, and understands the greatness of God would not be affected by wealth, property, women, children, etc. 
#2.)If one receives honour, has the association of wealth, or encounters women, then even if he is a great {!sādhu!}, he would not be able to maintain his integrity. Therefore, one should shun its contact.
#3.)Characteristics of one who has ‘entered’ God:
##3.1)He has an intense affection for God.
##3.2)He has constant awareness of the form of God.
##3.3)He behaves as if he is infatuated with the form of God.
##3.4)He physically engages in the service of God.
##3.5)He remains attached to and has a yearning for God’s {!bhakti!} and other God-related activities.
#4.)If a devotee of God is vulnerable to women, wealth, {!swabhāvs!} and the belief that one is the body, then even if he is engaged in the {!bhakti!} of God, he will encounter hindrances in his {!bhakti!}. If one has any one of these four, one should abandon them with understanding.

19959.t:
#1.)The means to only have desires remaining for God:
##1.1)Love for God.
##1.2){!Vairāgya!} coupled with {!gnān!}.
##1.3)Faith in and the conviction of God.
##1.4)Renouncing the {!panchvishays!}, observing {!niyams!} related to one’s {!swadharma!}, and engaging in the nine types of {!bhakti!}.
#2.)Anger arises when one’s desires are not fulfilled or when one’s sense of my-ness for something is violated.
#3.)The great {!Sant!} may show anger in order to keep countless {!jivas!} within the disciplines of {!dharma!}. He is not bound by the consequences of this anger.
#4.)Means to overcome anger:
##4.1)Renouncing that object which causes anger to arise.
##4.2)Developing love for the great Sant and realising one will benefit by attaining liberation by staying with Him.
#5.)One should not become angry for the sake of worthless objects.

19960.t:
#1.)The characteristics of one whose refuge in God will not sway even in adverse circumstances:
##1.1)He understands the greatness of God and realises everything other than God to be worthless.
##1.2)He does not become disturbed when God or the {!Sant!} forcefully alters his innate nature, and he follows their commands in a straightforward manner.
##1.3)If he should become disturbed when his innate nature is altered, he perceives his own fault but never perceives a fault in God or the {!Sant!}.
#2.)If one’s desires are intense and God or the {!Sant!} alters one’s innate nature, then one will become disturbed and fall back from Satsang.
#3.)The path of a devotee consists of behaving as God likes, offering {!bhakti!}, and pleasing God and His devotees.
#4.)By maligning the {!Sādhu!}, God, who resides within his heart is maligned as well; however, by serving the {!Sādhu!}, God is also served.
##4.1)Characteristics of such a {!Sādhu!}
###i.)He believes God possesses a definite form, is the all-doer, and is always manifest.
###ii.)When he sees someone engage in the worship of the manifest form of God, he becomes pleased.
###iii.)He abandons any swabhāvs that interfere in remaining amongst the devotees.
###iv.)He is pleased by giving away precious objects to devotees.
###v.)He behaves frankly; his outward and inward character would be the same.
###vi.)He is quiet natured; however, he cannot tolerate the company of {!kusangis!}.

19961.t:
#1.)The extraordinary spiritual endeavour for liberation:
##1.1)Seeking refuge in the manifest form of God, understanding Him to possess a divine form, and understanding that He is the source of all {!avatārs!}.
##1.2)Offering {!bhakti!} while remaining within one’s {!dharma!} and associating with a {!Sant!} possessing such {!bhakti!}.
#2.)One encounters a great hindrance by associating with shuksha-Vedāntis.
#3.)Without the {!upāsanā!} of God, there is no possibility of having the {!darshan!} of the {!ātmā!} or Brahma through {!nirbij!} (‘seedless’ – without the association of God) Sānkhya and Yoga.

19962.t:
#1.)Just as a king who becomes poor will remember the expensive delicacies he ate; similarly, if one has thoroughly understood the knowledge and bliss of God’s form, then he will not forget these in adverse times.
#2.)The conviction of one’s liberation will develop if one understands the greatness of God in the following way:
##2.1)The powers of {!kāl!} (i.e. ability to destroy everything) does not affect God.
##2.2)Only God is like God, no one else can even compare to Him.
##2.3)God is {!nirgun!} and those who meditate upon Him also become {!nirgun!}.
##2.4)God is the giver of the fruits of one’s {!karmas!} and He is the life of all the {!jivas!}.
##2.5)He is the master of all yogic powers and countless other divine powers.

19963.t:
#1.)All forms that are the result of the entities evolved from {!māyā!} will be destroyed thus are false.
#2.)Supreme Purushottam Bhagwān who resides in Akshardhām:
##2.1)He and all of the {!muktas!} are {!satya!}, divine, luminous, possess two arms, and are characterised by eternal existence, consciousness and bliss ({!sachchidānand-rup!}).
##2.2)He manifests on this earth out of compassion for the purpose of granting liberation to the {!jivas!}.
##2.3)He is our Ishtadev and accepts our service.
##2.4)He is the lord of all of the {!ishwars!} and the cause of all causes. He reigns supreme, and He is the cause of all of the {!avatārs!}. He is worthy of being worshipped single-mindedly.
#3.)Means to remain eternally happy:
##3.1)Eradicating greed for wealth and the desire to associate with women.
##3.2)Eradicating cravings of the tongue for various tastes.
##3.3)Not believing one’s self to be the body.
##3.4)Not developing affection for {!kusangis!} and one’s relatives.
##3.5)Maintaining {!nivrutti!}.
##3.6)Not keeping the company of equals.
##3.7)Not indulging in {!vishays!} by abandoning one’s {!niyams!}.
##3.8)Attaching one’s {!jiva!} to and acting according to the commands (by thought, word and deed) of the great {!Sant!} who does not identify his self with the body, who possesses {!vairāgya!}, and who feels that he has transgressed a major injunction of God even if he has transgressed a minor injunction.

19964.t:
#1.){!Māyā!} is nothing but the sense of I-ness towards the body and my-ness towards anything related to the body.
#2.)It is the principle of all of the scriptures that one should eradicate {!māyā!} and develop love for God.
#3.)Understanding of {!ātmā!}-realisation:
##3.1)If it is firm, then one does not engage in perceiving faults in anyone.
##3.2){!Ātmā!} is full of consciousness.
##3.3)The {!ātmā!} has experienced death in countless ways, yet it has not perished and will never perish.
#4.)Greatness of God:
##4.1)He is the Lord of the lords of countless {!brahmānds!}.
##4.2)His bliss is extremely rare, extremely divine, imperishable, and eternal.
##4.3)Even the great such as Brahmā, Shiv, etc., apply the dust of God’s holy feet upon their heads.
##4.4)He possesses innumerable skills.
##4.5)Only God is like God.
#5.)By understanding greatness as such:
##5.1)One develops {!vairāgya!} towards all objects other than God.
##5.2)One develops affection for God.
#6.)The {!gnān!} of {!ātmā!} and greatness of God:
##6.1)One should apply it within one’s mind with great fervour.
##6.2)Just as the {!vishalyakarani!} herbal medicine removes the arrows that has pierced one’s body, similarly, with this {!gnān!}, desire to indulge in {!vishays!} is removed.
##6.3)This can only be understood by those who are pious but not by those who are demonic.
#7.)Shriji Mahārāj speaks for the sake of revealing the ideals of a devotee.

19965.t: 1.)Attaining a human birth in Bharat-Khand is extremely rare and is the best, because only with the human body can one perform spiritual endeavours for one’s liberation.\r\n2.)To attain liberation in Bharat-Khand: Seek the refuge of the manifest {!Satpurush!}, serve him, and worship God while keeping one’s body, {!indriyas!}, and {!antahkaran!} in accordance with his wish.

19966.t:
#1.)The greatness of God:
##1.1)God assumes a human body by His own will to liberate countless {!jivas!}, and he also discards His body just like other {!jivas!} discard theirs.
##1.2)Despite taking birth, God is still beyond birth. He is beyond ageing and death. He is {!niranjan!} (without blemishes of {!māyā!}). He possesses a definite form and is self-radiant. He is Parabrahma. He transcends Akshar. He is {!antaryāmi!}, the supporter of millions of {!brahmānds!}, and the controller of Akshar and countless {!muktas!}. He is the master of all.
##1.3)He helps other people eradicate their belief of being the body and accept the belief of being the form of Brahma.
#2.)One with a {!nāstik!} perspective:
##2.1)Becomes confused when seeing God’s divine actions.
##2.2)Believes God to undergo birth and death due to His {!karmas!}, just like the {!jivas!}.
##2.3)Will experience the cycle of births and death and the misery of Yampuri. 
#3.)A devotee with an {!āstik!} attitude:
##3.1)Believes the understanding of {!nāstiks!} to be wrong.
##3.2)Believes the body of God to be eternal.
##3.3)Believes physical changes to God’s body to be His divine actions and due to His yogic powers.
##3.4)Understands that {!kāl!} and {!māyā!} have no effect on God’s body.
##3.5)Becomes released from their {!karmas!} and the cycle of 8.4 million life forms.

19967.t:
#1.)The extraordinary characteristics of God:
##1.1)He can control the {!nādis!} and {!prāns!} of innumerable beings and grant them instant {!samādhi!}.
##1.2)He can influence hundreds of thousands of people by having them abide by {!niyams!}.
##1.3)He can control Akshar and the {!muktas!}.
#2.)The manifest form of God that resides in this {!brahmānd!} also assumes a body in countless other {!brahmānds!} to liberate {!jivas!}.
#3.)What should {!satsangis!} renounce?
##3.1)Desire for worldly ({!māyik!}) objects.
##3.2)Lustful desires and thoughts.
##3.3)Affection for one’s relatives.
##3.4)The sense of I-ness towards the body.
##3.5)Perceived faults in God and the {!Sant!}.
#4.)What should {!satsangis!} accept?
##4.1)Desires related to God.
##4.2)Desire for bliss related to God.
##4.3)Affection for the {!Sant!}, who is a servant of God.
##4.4)The attitude of being a servant of God.
##4.5)The virtues of God and the {!Sant!}.
#5.)Characteristics of {!dharma, arth, kām!}, and {!moksha!}:
##5.1){!Dharma!}: using wealth in Satsang for the purpose of {!dharma!} but not squandering it for other purposes.
##5.2){!Arth!}: Accumulating wealth or fulfilling one’s aim of liberation.
##5.3){!Kām!}: Keeping only one wife and regarding other women as either one’s mother, sister, or daughter.
##5.4){!Moksha!}: Observing all vows of Satsang diligently and keeping unfaltering faith in God.

19968.t:
#1.)If one understands the greatness of the manifest form of God this way, then one develops unfaltering faith and attains Akshardhām:
##1.1)He is the source of all the {!avatārs!} and is {!antaryāmi!}.
##1.2)He eternally possesses a definite form and is full of countless divine powers.
##1.3)He is the lord of countless {!brahmānds!} and is the cause of even Aksharbrahma.
##1.4)He dwells in Akshardhām and He is the master of Akshar and the {!muktas!}.
##1.5)He is manifest Shriji Mahārāj Himself.
#2.)Aksharbrahma:
##2.1)It is the abode of Purushottam Bhagwān.
##2.2)It is eternal, extremely radiant, and limitless.
##2.3)Its splendour is countless times greater compared to the other abodes.
##2.4)All objects there are divine and composed of {!chaitanya!}.
##2.5)Countless {!muktas!} reside there.

19969.t:
#1.)The greatness of Shriji Mahārāj:
##1.1)He is Purushottam Nārāyan, the master of that which transcends all - Akshardhām.
##1.2)He is the creator, sustainer, and destroyer of all the {!brahmānds!}.
##1.3)All of the deities, abodes, and other places are immersed in their tasks due to His powers.
#2.)One who understands Shriji Mahārāj’s greatness and develops faith this way:
##2.1)Has his mind becomes stable.
##2.2)Attains Akshardhām.
##2.3)Acquires powers equal to an {!akshar-mukta!}.

19970.t:
#1.)Anger destroys all virtuous virtues such as chanting God’s name, austerities, {!gnān!}, etc.; therefore, a {!sādhu!} should conquer anger.
#2.)Causes of anger: during a question-answer session, argumentative discussion, giving or taking some objects, reprimanding someone, maintaining partiality towards one’s attendant, when insulted, out of jealousy, possessiveness for one’s accommodation, when {!prasād!} is unequally distributed etc.
#3.)When one becomes angry or develops angry thoughts toward anyone, then considering the person to be a devotee of God; as a result, one should discard their ego, sincerely bow down to them, and pray. 
#4.)By atoning this way, God becomes pleased, one’s {!antahkaran!} becomes pure, and all vicious natures are eradicated.

19971.t:
#1.)If there are any shortcomings in understanding God’s form, these deficiencies will remain:
##1.1)One cannot experience the true bliss of God.
##1.2)One cannot become an {!ekāntik bhakta!}.
##1.3)One cannot attain Akshardhām.
#2.)The flaw that remains in the understanding of the creators of the cosmos (Brahmā, etc.) :
##2.1)They consider the strength of their own actions but not the strength of one’s refuge in God to be instrumental in their liberation.
##2.2)They do not realise that becoming {!aksharrup!} and serving Purushottam is in itself liberation.
##2.3)They believe the innumerable {!avatārs!} of God to be a part of God.
##2.4)At the time of a previous death, they were curious to understand how the {!brahmānds!} were created.
#3.)Only when one realises true {!gnān!} by profoundly associating with the {!Ekāntik Bhakta!} of God does one become {!brahmarup!} and attain the abode of God.
#4.)Characteristics of the three types of devotees:
##4.1){!Aishvaryārthi!} - He who worships God with the intention of earning powers to create the world – lowest type of devotee.
##4.2){!Kaivalyārthi!} - He who worships God only to experience the {!ātmā!} – intermediate devotee.
##4.3){!Bhāgwat-nishtārthi!} - He who has a constant and singular resolve for the service of the manifest form of God – he is the best devotee of all.

19972.t:
#1.)The {!karmas!} a {!jiva!} has performed become assimilated in {!māyā!}; therefore, one cannot be liberated by their pious {!karmas!} alone.
#2.)A {!Sant!} who has attained God:
##2.1)One should profoundly attach to such a {!Sant!} and believe he is one’s own self.
##2.2)By attaining that {!Sant!} or attaining God and seeking refuge in them, one transcends {!māyā!}.
##2.3)He has the ability to penetrate the barriers of {!māyā!}.
#3.)No matter how great one becomes, one with a rational understanding believes: “My greatness is not due to this status, but rather due to the {!ātmā!} and the association with the {!Sant!}.”
#4.)The greatness of a {!Sant!} is due to his {!bhakti!} and {!upāsanā!} of God, and his {!ātmā!}-realisation.

19973.t:
#1.)Characteristics of a ‘yati’:
##1.1)He firmly observes {!brahmacharya!}.
##1.2)He has control over all his {!indriyas!}.
##1.3)Even if he is faced with a situation that would cause his {!antahkaran!} to become impure, his {!antahkaran!} still remains pure.
#2.)Characteristics of the {!jiva!}:
##2.1)It is uncuttable, unpierceable, immortal, {!chaitanya!}, and the size of an {!anu!} (atom-like).
##2.2)It resides in the {!hrudayākāsh!} and performs different functions.
##2.3)It pervades the entire body from head to toe; yet it is distinct from it.
##2.4)By the grace of the manifest form of God, one can see the {!jiva!}.

19974.t:
#1.)If one harbours impure desires, then one cannot experience the bliss of God even while staying near him.
#2.)Methods to eradicate impure desires:
##2.1)Repeatedly chanting God’s name aloud.
##2.2)Offering the nine types of {!bhakti!} to God coupled with the knowledge of his greatness and while observing {!dharma!}.
##2.3)Not infringing the five religious vows knowingly; and if infringed unknowingly, then atoning for that sin immediately.
##2.4)Believing that “I am the {!ātmā!}, distinct from the body.”
##2.5)Not developing an aversion to the divine actions of God.
#3.)One should do that which pleases God:
##3.1)There is nothing greater than this.
##3.2)That is itself {!bhakti!}.
##3.3)Only then does one attain God.
#4.)To worship God with remembrance of the manifest form of God is equal to actually having the {!darshan!} of God.
#5.)Characteristics of one who is great in Satsang:
##5.1)Has {!vairāgya!} in which he considers all 14 realms to be insignificant.
##5.2)He has firm conviction of the manifest form of God.
##5.3)He is oblivious to the world in the waking state just as he is during the state of deep sleep.

19975.t:
#1.)The {!jiva!} is liberated by faith in the manifest form of God, His {!darshan!} and His constant remembrance.
#2.)Even if one has constant remembrance of God, but if one does not observe the codes of {!dharma!}, then:
##2.1)He does not become an {!ekāntik bhakta!}.
##2.2)He does not attain God’s abode.
##2.3)He cannot stay in the Satsang fellowship.
#3.)The greatness of the {!Sant!} who observes {!niyams!} and {!dharma!}:
##3.1)By sincerely feeding such a {!Sant!}, one earns the merits of performing millions of sacrifices and will ultimately attain liberation.
##3.2)By touching his feet, sins committed in millions of past lives are destroyed.
##3.3)By offering him clothes, one will attain ultimate liberation.
##3.4)Each river or lake he dips his feet becomes a place of pilgrimage.
##3.5)Any tree that he sits under or eats the fruit of will benefit greatly.
##3.6)By devoutly doing his {!darshan!} or bowing down to him, all sins are destroyed.
##3.7)Whomever he talks to or inspires to observe {!niyams!} will attain liberation.
##3.8)Since such a {!Sant!} has refuge in the manifest form of God, all his activities are redemptive.
#4.)So that one may experience the bliss of the manifest form of God, God suppresses one’s powers; therefore, {!māyik!} {!gunas!} still remain in a devotee of God.
#5.)Even if one has animosity toward God, if all of his {!vruttis!} are focused on the form of God, only then he is liberated. However, to worship God with {!bhakti!} is the best.

19976.t:
#1.)There is nothing greater than worshipping God.
#2.)For the sake of the liberation of His devotees, Shriji Mahārāj says:
##2.1)I am the Lord of Akshardhām – Purushottam Bhagwān and the all-doer.
##2.2)I have manifested along with the {!sādhus!} for the purpose of liberating {!jivas!} and to propagating {!ekāntik!} {!dharma!}.
##2.3)Even if one is a grave sinner, if he accepts My refuge and abides by the {!niyams!} and {!dharma!}, then I will give him {!darshan!} at the end of his life and take him to Akshardhām.
##2.4)The explanation for all of his efforts not yielding any fruits, or any miseries faced is that it is in direct proportion to his slackness in engaging in the worship of God.
##2.5)If you keep firm faith in Me and do as I say, then even if you were to suffer extreme hardships, I will protect you from them.
##2.6)Those who disregard this manifest form of God and worship other deities are like adulterous women.
##2.7)If you abide by My word, I will take you to My abode.
##2.8)Brahmā, Vishnu, and Mahesh come daily for the {!darshan!} of the assembly of {!sādhus!} and Me.

20013.t: June 1959, Bhadrā.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “If one develops {!uttam nirvikalp nishchay!} [the highest type of conviction] as per Vachanāmrut Loyā 12, then Satsang can be said to have been perfected as it is.” \r\n[Y.M. : 2/565]

20314.t: 9 December 1961, Mumbai. \r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “Shāstriji Mahārāj often used to have these Vachanāmruts read in the afternoon: Gadhadā I 15, Gadhadā I 16, Gadhadā I 17, Gadhadā I 21, Gadhadā I 58. Sometimes, he would discourse on them for three hours.” \r\n[Y.M. : 3/252]

20315.t: 10 July 1961, Mumbai.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj wrote in a letter of blessings for Swāminārāyan Prakāsh, “The important Vachanāmruts – Loyā 17, Kāriyāni 1, Gadhadā II 59 and Gadhadā II 28 – should all be perfected.”\r\n[Y.M. : 3/206]

20316.t: 27 July 1957, Mumbai. \r\nDuring the discourses, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “One should imbibe affection as per Vachanāmrut Kāriyāni 11; {!vishvas!} [faith] as per Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 11; and {!nishkapat!} [full disclosure] as per Vachanāmrut Loyā 5. If these three aspects are perfected, one can become {!brahmarup!}.\r\n[Y.M. : 2/257]

20319.t: After having the Vachanāmruts Gadhadā II 5 and Vartāl 13 read, Gunātitānand Swāmi said, “Keep your {!indriyas!} and {!antahkaran!} in your {!hrudayākāsh!} so your focus remains on God. You may not realize while alive, but endeavours do not go in vain. When you leave this body you will see [the fruits].”\r\n[S.V. : 5/152]

20320.t:
March 1970, Kampala, Uganda. 
One evening, the yuvaks presented a cultural programme in Yogiji Mahārāj’s presence. Thereafter, Yogiji Mahārāj said, “The youths talked on certain topics. One youth recited Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 61. This discussed the concept of {!niyams!}, faith in God and loyalty. What is true loyalty? If someone is unnecessarily harming a devotee of God, one should stand up for that devotee. Two {!Kāthi!} youths of Gundali stood up for the {!sādhus!} [of Swāminārāyan Bhagwān]. They were not devotees; however, they stood up for the {!sādhus!} understanding them to be ‘{!sādhus!} that my maternal uncle follows. Therefore, their names were noted in history [mentioned in Vachanāmrut Loyā 3]. According to Vachanāmrut Gadhadā III 7, in no way should one abandon one’s loyalty to God and his {!Bhakta!}, regardless if one’s reputation increases or decreases, one is honoured or insulted, or one lives or dies. Many may keep loyalty; however, when relationships turn sour, they may end up rebuking the person they kept loyalty for by saying, ‘You don’t do anything for us, despite us continually standing up for you.’ That cannot be called loyalty.”
“One’s body and the relatives of the body become dearer to one than a devotee of God – this is why Mahārāj makes this point. If a {!sādhu!} arrives from afar and at the same time one of our relatives were to arrive, one who is not loyal [to {!Satsang!}] will say, ‘O {!sādhu!}! Listen, my relatives are here, so I will not be able to attend your discourses.’ However, the relatives should be given second priority. One has a lot of love for one’s son. If we ask for that son [to be initiated into sainthood], they would retort, ‘Swāmi! Take my money, but not my son.’”
“In short, we should not endear our bodily relatives to a higher degree than devotees who are associated with the {!Gunātit Sant!}. This concept will prove to be of immense benefit in the future.”
“Nandubhāi Mancharam of Amdāvād was incredibly loyal. Despite the fact that he was the secretary of the {!Junā Mandir!} in Kalupur, he would ensure that Shāstriji Mahārāj stayed at his home. He remained loyal, placing his head on the line. Maintaining such loyalty reduces the five grave sins to ashes. We have come from afar. Devotees should remain loyal to each other, through thick and thin. If another devotee is undergoing difficulties, one should not think, ‘He got what he deserved.’ What cannot be done for a devotee associated with Swāminārāyan [Bhagwān]? This is the concept described in Vachanāmrut Loyā 3.”
[Y.M. : 6/93]

20321.t: March 1959, Advāl.\r\nYogiji Mahārāj said, “One should renounce one’s bad habits. There are two Vachanāmruts that talk of this: Vachanāmrut Gadhadā II 37 and Gadhadā III 35; master these. One who is good will find faults within oneself, despite the fact that one feels perplexed when one’s habits are spoken about. One who finds faults in the {!Sant!} never progresses [in Satsang]. One’s bad habits can be eradicated if one tries.”\r\n[Y.M. : 2/530]

21051.t:
The Vachanamrut is a sacred scripture containing Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s divine discourses. It is an ocean of wisdom and the essence of all scriptures. Read daily by thousands of spiritual seekers across the world, the Vachanamrut provides answers to life’s practical and spiritual questions.
Through easy-to-understand notes and explanations, this ‘Vachanamarut Study App’ sheds new light on eternal concepts.  Using the latest technology, this application gives users a new and convenient medium for reading and studying the Vachanamrut.  Allowing users to engage in the Vachanamrut in new and exciting ways, this application is an attempt to make it easier for curious minds to delve into the depths of the Vachanamrut. 
This application includes clear and informative explanations of difficult to understand paragraphs, phrases, and words.  Novel definitions of words have been explained with respect to their individual contexts.  The explanations have been supported by the words of the Gunatit Guruparampara to strengthen and clarify the reader’s understanding. Bhagwan Swaminarayan himself has said, “Discourses regarding the nature of God cannot be understood by oneself even from the scriptures. Even though these facts may be in the scriptures, it is only when the Satpurush manifests on this earth, and one hears them being narrated by him, that one understands them. They cannot, however, be understood by one’s intellect alone, even from the scriptures.” ((Vachanamrut Gadhada II-13)) Therefore these explanations of the Gunatit Guruparampara will help readers to grasp the true meaning of the words of the Vachanamrut. 
In addition, information about people, cultural expressions, idioms, examples, scriptures, sacred places, shlokas, kirtans, maps, references, summaries, history, and scriptural sources, etc. mentioned in the Vachanamrut have been given. Thus, an attempt has been made to give the reader all the information necessary to analyse and digest the deepest philosophical concepts with relative ease.
Started with the blessing of Brahmswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj, and completed by the grace of Brahmswarup Mahant Swami Maharaj, BAPS is pleased to publish the Vachanamrut Study App.

21052.t: BAPS is a global socio-spiritual organization committed to the moral and spiritual uplift of mankind. It was established in 1907 by Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj based on the Vedic teachings revealed by Bhagwan Swaminarayan (1781–1830). The organization’s global network of 1,100 mandirs, 4,290 Satsang centres and 17,000 weekly assemblies are perennial sources of moral, social, cultural and spiritual activities. The energies of the BAPS volunteer corps of 55,000 are channelled towards a variety of philanthropic activities.\r\nBAPS is an NGO in Consultative Status with the Economic and Social Council of the United Nations. Its world renowned cultural and spiritual complexes, like Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi and Gandhinagar, and Swaminarayan Mandirs in London, Houston, Chicago, Atlanta, Toronto, Los Angeles, Robbinsville and Nairobi are representations of its contributions to society.\r\nBAPS, under the inspiration and guidance of Mahant Swami Maharaj, has earned an endearing and unique place in the hearts of millions throughout the world.

21053.t: The Vachanamrut Study App team is continually trying to update the application with improvements and new features. If you have any suggestions regarding the features, content or the any other aspect of this application, please feel free to email them to info@swaminarayan.org.\r\nWe thank you in advance for any suggestions that will make this application better and thus improve everyone’s experience of the Vachanamrut.

21054.t:
“I, Purushottam, who is above Akshar, have taken birth in human form for the purpose of enlightening countless jivas by making them brahmarup, and leading them to ultimate liberation.”
Through these words, Bhagwan Swaminarayan states his life’s purpose revealing two things – that he was Parabrahma Purushottam Narayan himself, and that his lifework was focused on spirituality.
Bhagwan Swaminarayan initiated many spiritual and social projects to remedy society’s ailing conditions and reignite fading spirituality. He operated alms houses, built and recharged wells, introduced education for women and inspired all to live pure, addiction-free lives. He also actively campaigned to eradicate entrenched social practices of sati-burning, female infanticide and dowry. 
With a faithful following of paramhansas, renunciates of the highest order, he established the Swaminarayan Sampraday, introducing much-needed social reforms, serving the poor and needy, and challenging superstitions, addictions and blind faith. He cleansed and rejuvenated the impurities that had tarnished the celebration of Hindu festivals, such as Janmashtami, Holi and Ramnavmi, and transformed them into platforms for liberation. “That is why I perform grand Vishnu-yags; annually celebrate Janmashtami, Ekadashi and other observances… After all, even if a sinner remembers these occasions at the time of his death, he will also attain the abode of God.” ((Vachanamrut Gadhada I-3))
In a lifespan of only 49 years, Bhagwan Swaminarayan also built six majestic mandirs alluding to the Vedic Akshar-Purushottam philosophy. Revealing his purpose behind these activities, Bhagwan Swaminarayan says, “For the sake of preserving upasana, I have built mandirs of God… Thereby, even if only a little renunciation remains, upasana will at least be preserved, and through it, many jivas will attain liberation.” ((Vachanamrut Gadhada II-27))
Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s practical spirituality attracted people from all states of society, helping them regain their lost values and self-identity. He taught his householder disciples basic moral codes and inspired them to abstain from alcohol, meat-eating, dishonesty, adultery and improper habits of manner and diet. Such was his divine magnetism that over 3,000 spiritual aspirants accepted initiation from him into the sadhu-fold to lead a life of devotion and service to society. 
Also known as Sahajanand Swami and Shriji Maharaj, his was a life focused on promoting morality, moulding spiritual character and revealing the Vedic Akshar-Purushottam Upasana through his discourses. The profound wisdom imparted by him has been meticulously recorded in what is the most important scripture of the Swaminarayan Sampraday – the Vachanamrut.
Let’s now take a brief look into Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s personality, and how it is portrayed through his discourses in the Vachanamrut.

21055.t:
Bhagwan Swaminarayan is supreme God, cause of all the avatars and cause of all causes. He is Parabrahma Purushottam Narayan, who reigns in his divine abode, Akshardham. He is the all-doer, controller of everything, judge of all karmas and grantor of ultimate liberation.
Revealing his own true form, Bhagwan Swaminarayan says: “It is that same supreme Purushottam Bhagwan who manifests on this earth out of compassion – for the purpose of granting liberation to the jivas. He is presently visible before everyone; He is your Ishtadev; and He accepts your service. In fact, there is absolutely no difference between the manifest form of Purushottam Bhagwan visible before you and the form of God residing in Akshardham; i.e., both are one. Moreover, this manifest form of Purushottam Bhagwan is the controller of all, including Akshar. He is the lord of all the ishwars and the cause of all causes. He reigns supreme, and He is the cause of all of the avatars. Moreover, He is worthy of being worshipped single-mindedly by all of you.” ((Vachanamrut Gadhada III-38))
Offering tribute to Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s selfless life, great thinkers praise Bhagwan Swaminarayan as exemplary among all his contemporary luminaries, as someone truly worthy of being worshipped as God by spiritual seekers.
Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s talks are more than just words of experience, they are the words of God himself.

21056.t: The Vachanamrut encapsulates Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s divine discourses. Diving into this ocean of knowledge reveals two distinct faculties of Bhagwan Swaminarayan – a comprehensive understanding of all the scriptures, and a life of living the ideals contained within them. He has said that: “I, Myself, have listened to all of the scriptures which Vyasji has written regarding the attainment of liberation.” ((Vachanamrut Gadhada II-21))\r\nBeyond a being well-read in scriptural knowledge, Bhagwan Swaminarayan was an intellectually brilliant scholar who was able to gather the priceless pearls of wisdom from this ocean of knowledge. Describing his talks, Bhagwan Swaminarayan says: “What is this discourse which I delivered before you like? Well, I have delivered it having heard and having extracted the essence from the Vedas, the Shastras, the Purans and all other words on this earth pertaining to liberation. This is the most profound and fundamental principle; it is the essence of all essences.” ((Vachanamrut Gadhada II-28))\r\nAt the just 10 years of age, Bhagwan Swaminarayan attended a scholars’ conference in Kashi, where his creative genius led him to triumph in a philosophical debate. Such intellect makes the Vachanamrut a truly all-encompassing scripture like no other. To say that nothing remains to be read for one who he has read the Vachanamrut is no exaggeration.

21057.t:
Bhagwan Swaminarayan was not just a well-read scholar with the ability to understand and give that knowledge succinctly, but he lived by those ideals, through a life full of spiritual endeavour. His discourses were the based on his practical experience of these ideals imbibed in his life. He practiced before he preached. He has undergone whatever he has said regarding physical and mental spiritual endeavours, in fact much more. If something pierced his body, water would come out, but never blood, such was his severe physical austerity ((Vachanamrut Kariyani 3)). For months at a time he would remain without food or water while tolerating the the winter, summer and monsoon without any shelter whatsoever, wearing only a loincloth ((Vachanamrut Gadhada I-29)). During his 7-year pilgrimage across India, he turned down inviting offers of women, wealth and power in the form of Mandir Mahant-ships and even kingdoms. His sincere service of an ill sadhu named Sevakram gave new meaning to ‘selfless service.’ ((Vachanamrut Gadhada I-10))
Not just in physical endeavours, but Bhagwan Swaminarayan had also mastered the heights of thought related endeavours such as contemplating on the atma and sankhya etc. He mentions, “Even amidst the activities of all My indriyas, I do not lose awareness of [the] atma for even a moment” ((Vachanamrut Gadhada II-35)). Further, Bhagwan Swaminarayan reveals that: “I constantly regard each and every worldly object to be perishable and insignificant… For example, when considering the hairs of the armpit, which can be considered good and which bad?... Similarly, all worldly objects appear the same to me.” ((Vachanamrut Gadhada II-55))
Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s pure intention and divine sentiment echo through his words. He says, “I swear by the lives of these paramhansas that from the day I was born to this very day, I have never harboured an improper thought regarding women or wealth, either in the waking or in the dream state” ((Vachanamrut Gadhada II-33)). “Not even the slightest bit of lust, anger, avarice, egotism, matsar or jealousy enters my heart.” ((Vachanamarut Kariyani 6))
In this way, Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s Vachanamrut is not a product of imagination, assumption or other such intellectual exercises, but the ripened fruit of true knowledge plucked by hands of true experience. Bhagwan Swaminarayan says: “I deliver these discourses to you not from any imagination of My mind… I have experienced all that I have spoken about. In fact, I speak only that which I practise” ((Vachanamrut Gadhada III-39)). “This discourse is what based on what I have seen and realised through my own experience.” ((Vachanamrut Gadhada II-13))

21058.t:
Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s discourses were not for any self-benefit or any other ulterior motive. His own words reveal how the sole purpose of his talks was to reveal the path to ultimate liberation: 
#&)“What I am about to say to you, I say not out of any pretence, or out of any self-conceit, or to spread my own greatness. Rather, it is because I feel that amongst all of you sadhus and devotees, if someone can understand my message, it will tremendously benefit that person; that is my purpose in narrating it.” ((Vachanamrut Gadhada II-13))
#&)“All of you have faith in me. If I were to mislead you with unfounded talks, it would amount to throwing all of you into a well and sealing it with a stone slab so that there would be no hope of escape. However, if, because of your faith in my words, you are misled along the wrong path, then of what good would that be to me? Thus, these discourses are for the sake of your liberation.” ((Vachanamrut Gadhada II-35))
#&)“I do not want even the slightest imperfection to remain in those who are said to me mine” ((Vachanamrut Gadhada II-45)).
Such words reveal Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s compassion for jivas and passion for revealing the path to liberation.

21059.t: Speaking about the discourses he has given in his Vachanamrut, Bhagwan Swaminarayan says: “The reason I can behave in such a manner is that I have thoroughly realised [these discourses]… In fact, whoever realises them would also behave accordingly…” ((Vachanamrut Gadhada III-39)).\r\nBhagwan Swaminarayan didn’t preach utopian ideals, but gave timeless practical advice that can be followed by one and all. History notes the life transformation of Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s followers, the audience of his Vachnamarut, who uprooted their innate desires as a result of his discourses.\r\nCountless spiritual seekers have achieved the enlightened spiritual state of ‘jivan-mukta’ based on the Vachanamrut’s teachings. Spiritual seekers of today can too achieve that enlightenment and experience true eternal bliss.

21060.t: The Vachanamrut is a sacred scripture containing Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s divine discourses. These discourses were compiled by four of his scholarly renunciates - Gopalanand Swami, Muktanand Swami, Nityanand Swami and Shukanand Swami. These paramhansas even showed the manuscripts to Bhagwan Swaminarayan during its compilation, adding further authority to this unique scripture.\r\nThe compilers meticulously detailed all major aspects of the assembly setting. They noted the date, location and members of the audience congregated before Bhagwan Swaminarayan. In many instances they even mention his style of sitting, the direction he was facing in, his clothing and adornment etc.

21061.t: The primary emphasis of the Vachanamrut is ultimate spiritual knowledge, that is, explanation and analysis of the entities of Aksharbrahma and Parabrahma, as well as dharma, gnan, vairagya and bhakti – collectively known as ‘Ekantik Dharma.’ A variety of other topics are raised in the scripture, ranging from deeply philosophical subjects, such as the nature of God, creation of the cosmos and clarifications of classical Hindu philosophies, to more spiritually practical subjects such as liberation of the soul, good and bad company, the need for the Gunatit Satpurush and the means of attaining eternal bliss.\r\nThe Vachanamrut provides spiritual guidance on how to remain happy in this life and beyond, how to attain complete progress in life, how to overcome even the most difficult situations. \r\nEach page sheds new light, gives new inspiration, provides spiritual strength and gives constant encouragement. It exposes life’s root problems and offers lasting solutions.
