Revealing fundamental secrets of spirituality, eliminating the darkness of maya and giving new meaning and purpose to life, the Vachanamrut is an all-encompassing scripture like no other.

21062.t: The Vachanamrut is a unique work of prose in the Gujarati language. Despite its complicated spiritual subject-matter, Bhagwan Swaminarayan explains complex concepts through simple reasoning, scriptural allegories, proverbs, analogies and simple everyday examples. He imparted his wisdom in a clear and unique manner in a question and answer dialogue.

21063.t:
#$)The Gunatit Gurus have emphasised the importance of the Vachanamrut, for example:
##&)“This Vachanamrut text contains the essence of the four Vedas, six darshans and eighteen Puranas.”
((Swamini Vato 6/18))
##&)“Shriji Maharaj [Bhagwan Swaminarayan] has gifted us the essence of all the scriptures in the form of the Vachanamrut.”
((Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj))
##&)“Shriji Maharaj has revealed his philosophy through his 262 Vachanamruts. He has presented his own divine words. He has put the essence of all the scriptures in the Vachanamrut. It contains the essence of the four Vedas.”
((Brahmaswarup Yogiji Maharaj))
##&)“The Vachanamrut contains all knowledge. Nothing has been left out. There is no other scripture like it. To believe there to be value in anything else is delusion. In it, Maharaj [Bhagwan Swaminarayan] has revealed the essence of the Vedas and Vedant.”
((Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj))
#$)Well-renowned thinkers have praised the Vachanamrut:
##&)“To phrase it figuratively, you could say that the Vachanamrut is the Gita of Gujarat in the nineteenth century. I would even chance to say that the Vachanamrut is an extract of all of India’s teachings on faith and spiritual endeavour.”
((Raghuvir Chaudhari, writer))
##&)“The Vachanamrut is a matchless scripture... Its simplicity, clarity and logical reasoning captivate the reader. It speaks to the mind and settles in the heart. Whatever questions arise in the reader’s mind are resolved there and then, filling them with satisfaction and leaving no room for doubt… It is a simple and clear treatise on many seemingly difficult and incomprehensible subject-matters.”
((Chandravadan C. Mehta, writer))
##&)“Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s Vachanamrut is a jewel of Gujarati literature. For those seeking a spiritual and introspective life, it is impossible to ignore such a text in Gujarati. One who reflects and deeply contemplates on this text’s principles and teachings, and tries to imbibe them in his life, will no doubt achieve progress. It is unlikely that any other text such as this, revealing deep spiritual ideals and the practical guidance to realising them, exists elsewhere. Its language is direct, succinct, unambiguous, and easy to understand, giving clarification using examples where necessary. Just the right word is used in just the right place. You won’t find any confusing, doubtful or negative words anywhere. Page-upon-page you’ll experience the elevated spiritual state of the discourser.”
((Kishorelal Masharuwala, Gandhian philosopher))

21064.t:
The world will forever be indebted to the four paramhansas who collected and compiled Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s nectar-like discourses and presented them in the Vachanamrut scripture we have today – they are Sadguru Gopalanand Swami, Sadguru Muktanand Swami, Sadguru Nityanand Swami and Sadguru Shukanand Swami.
Despite few resources and many difficulties, these four paramhansas penned words of wisdom that have become the guiding light through every phase of a spiritual seeker’s life. How they scribed thousands of manuscripts with ink and quill, under the light of an oil-lamp, is near impossible to imagine in today’s technological age. Their creative and meticulous capturing of the date, place, occasion, audience, questions, answers, description of Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s dress, direction he was facing, and what he was holding etc. elevates the Vachanamrut to a class of its own.
All four compilers were authoritative and filled with integrity. When Sadguru Nityanand Swami presented Vachanamrut manuscripts to Bhagwan Swaminarayan, he certified their authenticity. ((Vachanamrut Loya 7))
The compilers have openly and honestly noted discourses that reveal their own shortcomings in the Vachanamrut Gadhada II-27, Gadhada II-31 and Gadhada III-33, just to name a few. Whenever faced with a decision on what to note and what to omit, without hesitation, they opted to include anything and everything, even if it may harm their reputation. In this way, the compilers ensured the integrity of the Vachanamrut remains beyond dispute.
Let’s take a brief look at these four compilers.

21065.t:
Born on 1 February 1781 (Maha Sud 8, Vikram Samvat 1837) in Todala (Idar, Gujarat), Sadguru Gopalanand Swami was a master in Ashtang Yoga. The murti in Shamlaji Mandir, a well-known pilgrimage place near Todla, would daily come to play with him in his childhood.
Whenever he offered oblations in a yagna, Yagnanarayan himself would give darshan. This great scholar paramhansa could literally move planets using the powers of Yoga and his austerity. Many great leaders and kings, including Sayajirao Gayakwad, became followers of Bhagwan Swaminarayan as a result of Gopalanand Swami’s knowledge and saintliness.
Despite his tremendous powers he was incredibly humble. He would easily forgive even those who insulted him.
The Shri Haricharitamrut Sagar says, “Other than Satsang, he regarded all of the universe’s objects to be akin to crow excrement. Shri Hari [Bhagwan Swaminarayan] praised his internal purity. He was complete in but not burdened by saintly virtues.” [Haricharitamrut Sagar : 20/22]

21066.t:
“Muktanand Swami’s shraddha and understanding of God’s glory are exactly the same today and just as fresh as they were when I first him in Lojpur; they have not diminished in any way whatsoever” ((Vachanamrut Sarangpur 3)). These are Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s words of praise for Sadguru Muktanand Swami, who was saintliness personified. By his mere darshan, one in a fit of anger would instantly become calm.
He was a gifted singer, musician, poet and dancer, as well an accomplished physician. After joining the Sampraday, Bhagwan Swaminarayan himself remained under Muktanand Swami’s instruction for nine months. Muktanand Swami’s academic triumph against scholars in Vadodara raised the Swaminarayan Sampraday’s profile.
Born in 1758 (Vikram Samvat 1814) in Amreli (Gujarat), he unceasingly served the Sampraday for 72 years. He wrote 30 scriptures in Sanskrit and prose, and composed thousands of kirtans. The arti he wrote in praise of Bhagwan Swaminarayan is sung across the globe today.
The Shri Haricharitamrut Sagar describes him as, “A ‘liberated sage’ could always tell Shri Hari’s [Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s] wish.” [Haricharitamrut Sagar : 8/48]

21067.t: “The essence of my [Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s] talks have been etched in his heart. He remembers such knowledge with natural ease. There is no limit to his intellect, yet he harbours no ego and remains humble before me. Even Brahmaji cannot fathom his unlimited intellect.” [Haricharitamrut Sagar : 9/47]\r\nBhagwan Swaminarayan uttered such praising words for Nityanand Swami, who was born in the north Indian village of Datiya (Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh) on 21 March 1793 (Chaitra Sud 9, Vikram Samvat 1849).\r\nRadiating with intellect, Nityanand Swami was undefeated in scholarly debates. He was a pragmatist with long-term vision and unshakeable faith in Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s supremacy.

21068.t: “This Shuk Muni is a very great sadhu. From the day he began staying with me, his enthusiasm has been ever increasing; in fact, it has never diminished. Thus, he is like Muktanand Swami” ((Vachanamrut Kariyani 3)). Bhagwan Swaminarayan uttered these words for Sadguru Shukanand Swami, who originally hailed from Nadiad but had settled in Dabhan. He was born in 1799 (Vikram Samvat 1855).\r\nOwing to his neat penmanship and in-depth knowledge of Gujarati and Sanskrit poetry and prose, he wrote, compiled and edited many literary works. Along with penning the original Vachanamrut and Satsangijivan manuscripts, Shukanand Swami was responsible for drafting many of the Sampraday’s legal and administrative documents.  This author of 17 scriptures in Sanskrit and prose also handled Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s letter correspondence.\r\nThe Shri Haricharitamrut Sagar notes that, “His personality pleased Shri Hari [Bhagwan Swaminarayan]. Wherever Shri Hari sat, this learned Brahmin would sit beside him and carefully note every letter Shri Hari dictated. Whatever he wouldn’t understand, he would ask and confirm. He had firm faith in the words of Shri Hari.” [Haricharitamrut Sagar : 16/2]

21073.t:
The Vachanamrut is a scripture comprising Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s divine words. In it, Bhagwan Swaminarayan has given solutions for all spiritual problems likely to be faced by aspirants. Thus, providing an obstacle-free spiritual path for all future generations. Hence, since the Vachanamrut is a source of the highest spiritual guidance in simple, lucid language, it is worthy of daily study by all aspirants.
The ‘Vachanamrut Study App’ enables more fruitful and effective daily study. This application captures the essence of decades of reflection, contemplation and experience guided by five generations of Gunatit Guruparampara. Aksharbrahman Gunatitanand Swami (1784–1867) discoursed day and night on the Vachanamrut. This tradition of spiritual discussions has been sustained over five generations by Brahmaswarup Bhagatji Maharaj (1829–1897), Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj (1865–1951), Brahmaswarup Yogiji Maharaj (1892–1971) and Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj (1921–2016).
To continually nurture in-depth learning in upcoming generations, in 1973, Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj initiated daily discourses and discussions on the Vachanamrut in the BAPS Sant Training Centre at Sarangpur. Here, for decades, under the counsel of the scholarly, experienced and spiritually accomplished Sadguru Santvallabhdas Swami, newly initiated sadhus engaged in detailed individual and group study of the Vachanamrut. Also, based on the insightful Vachanamrut discourses of Brahmaswarup Bhagatji Maharaj, Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj, Brahmaswarup Yogiji Maharaj, Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Pragat Brahmaswarup Mahant Swami Maharaj, the sadhus have engaged in comprehensive study of the Vachanamrut under the tutelage of experienced and scholarly senior sadhus.
This ‘Vachanamrut Study App’ is the fruit of such collective spiritual wisdom accumulated over many decades.
This application has been made to cater for the various features required to enable productive daily study of the Vachanamrut. The extensive materials collated and presented here by Pujya Brahmadarshan Swami and his team of sadhus at the Sant Training Centre in Sarangpur have been thoroughly checked and authenticated by senior scholarly sadhus of the Sanstha: Pujya Ishwarcharandas Swami, Pujya Viveksagardas Swami, Pujya Anandswarupdas Swami, Pujya Aksharcharandas Swami, Pujya Shrutiprakashdas Swami, Pujya Bhadreshdas Swami, Pujya Priyavratdas Swami, Pujya Adarshjivandas Swami, Pujya Atmatruptadas Swami, P. Priyaswarupdas Swami and others.
In addition, important aspects of doctrine and spiritual practice have been presented to Pragat Brahmaswarup Mahant Swami Maharaj and amended as per his guidance. In this way, every effort has been made to ensure the accuracy and authenticity of the content.
‘Vachanamrut Study App’ is the product of eight months of dedicated efforts by a team of over 30 scholarly sadhus, volunteers and technical experts of the BAPS. BAPS organization is thankful to all that have helped create this application. May the inspirers of this project, Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj and Pragat Brahmaswarup Mahant Swami Maharaj, shower their blessings on all.
We are confident that the ‘Vachanamrut Study App’ will be a valuable resource to assist all in the daily study of the Vachanamrut, and through such study will enable all to advance on the spiritual path.

21074.t:
Bhagwan Swaminarayan has repeatedly proclaimed the glory of the sant and bhakta in the Vachanamrut. In the Swaminarayan Sampraday, the words ‘sant’ and ‘bhakta’ have three meanings:
#1.)The guru who is the Aksharbrahma Satpurush
#2.)A liberated soul who has attained “Brahmi Sthiti”
#3.)A sant or bhakta who is devoted to Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the Aksharbrahma Satpurush
In many places the Sant and the Bhakta have been referred to as worthy of being served by aspirants, the gateway to liberation, a liberator like God, and the Satpurush who transcends others above maya. In those places, Sant and the Bhakta should be realised to mean the Aksharbrahma Satpurush. Yogiji Maharaj has said in his blessings for the Vachanamrut, “the Sant is described as the gateway to liberation.  That Sant is Mul Aksharmurti Gunatitanand Swami Maharaj.”
Clarification needs to be made here for those pursuing spiritual endeavours (sadhana). In the Vachanamrut, Bhagwan Swaminarayan has spoken descriptions of one who should be served, associated with, and should be not be spoken of negatively, etc. in reference to the Aksharbrahm Satpurush. Nevertheless, as the entire satsang is defined as a part of the Satpurush, the entire satsang is also included to somewhat extent in these contexts.  
For example, a lot has been written about the glory of serving the Satpurush. Any spiritual seeker who performs any service according to the command or wishes of the Satpurush is considered to the have served the Satpurush.  In addition, the scriptures say that one should understand philosophical concepts from the Satpurush, however, if one understands them from a sadhu or devotee by the command or wish of the satpurush, in accordance with the principles given by him, it should be considered the same. Bhagwan Swaminarayan also warns that to speak ill about or malign the Satpurush results in the jiva never attaining liberation. Within that command one should understand not to speak ill of those associated with the Satpurush either. In this way, in examples such as these the words Sant and the Bhakta should be understood as the Satpurush and those associated with him.

21075.t: All of the definitions in the application are based on the scriptures and authentic books. The references of these have been included alongside the definitions themselves. Nevertheless, in an effort to make the application easier to read, where there are extensive references, such as in the introduction to characters, the references have been mentioned elsewhere as an independent list. \r\nThe scripture, “Purushottam Bolya Prite” is a compilation of quotes from a handwritten manuscript of the “Shriharicharitamrutsagar.” Therefore Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s speech from “Shriharicharitamrutsagar” is referenced with “Purushottam Bolya Prite.”

21076.t:
Clicking on tagged words shows information about them. These display of these tags can be turned on or off from settings. Even when the display of certain tags has been turned off, clicking on those words will still provide the reader with the information. Nevertheless, some ‘essential’ words or sentences that are important to know will always be displayed. The supplemental information has been divided into the following categories: 
#*)People: Brief descriptions of all notable persons mentioned in the Vachanamrut are also provided. These include people contemporary to Bhagwan Swaminarayan as well as historical people such as those in the Purans. Examples include: Dada Khachar, Uddhavji, etc. 
#*)Scriptures: Short introductions to the books and scriptures mentioned in the Vachanamrut. Examples include: Gita, Bhagavat, etc. 
#*)Places: Short descriptions of places in the Vachanamrut. Examples include: Rameshwar, Golok, Gadhada etc. 
#*)Shlok-Kirtan: References and meanings of shloks/kirtans in the Vachanamrut.
#*)History: The historical events pertaining to questions and answers in the Vachanamrut. This information can also be seen by selecting history tag.
#*)Nirupan: Discourses relating to sadhana have been explained with supportive material from Purushottam Bolya Prite (a compilation of Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s quotes from Shriharicharitamrutsagar), Swami ni Vato, and the teachings of the Gunatit Guruparampara. This is not a definition of the words in the Vachanamrut but additional information that will benefit the reader. 
#*)Important Words: The definitions and explanations of important words. These words can be regional, scriptural or philosophical that may need further clarification.
#*)Other: Additional Information not included in the categories above such as the meanings of difficult sentences, questions, examples, references, idioms, sayings, etc.
#*)Essential: Even after turning off the display of all above information types, some essential tags will always remain displayed.
{{Other Features}}
#*)History:  History associated with the entire Vachanamrut. The history of the questions and answers within the Vachanamrut are featured here. 
#*)Glory: The greatness of the Vachanamrut in the words of the Gunatit Guruparampara.
#*)Nirupan: Any important explanations on the entire Vachanamrut in the words of the Gunatit Guruparampara.
#*)Prasang: Inspiring prasangs, relating to the Vachanamruts, as mentioned by the Gunatit Guruparampara and other santo-bhakto.
#*)Summary: A concise point by point outline of each Vachanamrut to help remember and review the Vachanamrut. 
#*)Quiz: A quiz to help self-assess knowledge gathered from the Vachanamrut. 
#*)Reading Lists: Reading lists allow you to follow a fixed course of Vachanamruts. Create your own custom reading list based on your preferences. Two reading lists have already been given to start you off. 
#*)Tag favourite Vachanamruts
#*)Write notes on each vachanamrut, and search through those notes
#*)Retrieve a count of how many times you have read each Vachanamrut
#*)Search the entire Vachanamrut for any particular word
#*)Read an English transliteration of the Vachanamrut and information included in the application

There are two types of transliteration schemes available:
##1.)The UN transliteration scheme
##2.)A simplified transliteration scheme
{The UN transliteration scheme is as follows:}
@transliteration_table.png@

{A simplified transliteration scheme}
#$)The simplified transliteration scheme follows the same rules but the words have been individually customized as pronounced commonly. E.g.: ભગવાન in UN scheme would be transliterated as ‘Bhagavan’, whereas in simplified transliteration scheme the final ‘a’ and the ‘a’ after ‘g’, which are commonly not pronounced have been removed to give ‘Bhagvan’.
#$)For easier readability, capitalisation rules of sentences and proper nouns have been attempted to be followed where possible.
#$)Occasionally ‘v’s have been changed to ‘w’s where felt it would be easier for the reader who is acquainted with reading the current rendering of the English Vachanamrut. E.g.: Bhagwan, Swaminarayan.
#$)The initial of the common names that are used as proper names have been capitalized. E.g.: Prakṛuti, Satpurush.
#$)The ‘anuswar’ (ં) in the UN scheme is transliterated as ‘ṁ’ but here it is transliterated as ‘ṁ’ when anuswar is pronounced as ‘m’ and as ‘ṅ’ when pronounced as ‘n’. E.g.: સંબંધ = saṁbaṅdh.
#$)The anuswar that is softly pronounced has been shown with a tilde (  ̃). E.g.: દાંત = dā̃t.
#$)Also the final anuswar which is usually not pronounced has been removed. E.g.: કરવું = karvu and not karvuṁ.
#$)In Sanskrut language words are pronounced as written, thus Sanskrut text is transliterated accordingly.
#$)The vowel ‘ઋ’ in the UN scheme is transliterated as ‘ṛ’ but for easier reading, in this scheme it’s transliterated as ‘ṛu’.
#$)For easier reading long Sanskrut and Gujarati words have been meaningfully broken into smaller words by placing a hyphen (-) in between the words. E.g: karuṇā-bhājan, guhya-bhāṣhaṇam.
#$)Names of places and persons have not been transliterated according to the rules above but have been spelled according to the English language. E.g.: દિલ્હી = Delhi and not dilhī.
#$)The English words widely used in Gujarati language have not been transliterated but spelled according to English and the ‘pratyay’ is separated by a hyphen (-) to avoid confusion. E.g.: કલેક્ટરની = collector-nī

Swami-Shriji Satya Chhe.
The Vachanamrut is the collection of divine nectar-like discourses of Shriji Maharaj. Shriji Maharaj will grant whoever drinks that nectar a place close to him. Therefore senior sadguru sadhus have said that if you read the Vachanamrut 108 times, then Shriji Maharaj himself will give you darshan. 
The Vachanamrut discusses five main principles: dharma, gnan, vairagya, bhakti and mahima, in which the sant is described as the sole gateway to liberation.  Maharaj has conveyed that that Sant is Mul Aksharmurti Gunatitanand Swami Maharaj.  Therefore, read the Vachanamrut all 12 months (a year). Mul Akshar Swami (Gunatitanand Swami) has said that people drink eternal nectar in Devlok but it can be found in the Vachanamrut. Swami would have copies of the Vachanamrut written himself, but now they are printed, so everyone should keep it in their homes. 
#Sadhu Gnanjivandas’
^Jay Swaminarayan
^3-10-1969 
^Mumbai.

21079.t:
@blessing_psm_page1.jpg@
@blessing_psm_page2.jpg@
#||Swami Shriji||
#09-07-1996
^Orlando, FL, USA
Purna Purushottam Narayan Shri Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s divine discourses, the Vachanamrut, is a priceless and unparalleled spiritual text. The essence of all the shastras are encapsulated within it. In the Vachanamrut, Bhagwan Swaminarayan has given extraordinary solutions to all problems faced by spiritual aspirants. Within it, any aspirant who wishes to realise God receives life-long guidance in easy-to-understand language. 
Bhagwan Swaminarayan himself came into this universe with his divine abode (Akshardham), the aksharmuktas and all of his divine power. That is explained in Gadhada I-71.  In addition, when explaining his fundamental principles he said, “Thus, only one who has become brahmarup is worthy of offering devotion to Parabrahma” (Loya-7). Bhagwan Swaminarayan brought Gunatitanand Swami with him in order to make jivas brahmarup. Shriji Maharaj propagated Ekantik Dharma and continued that mission through the Ekantik Sant, who is Akshardham personified. By explaining Shriji Maharaj’s principles in the Vachanamrut, Gunatitanand Swami spread true upasana and explained Shriji Maharaj’s form as it truly is.  
Shriji Maharaj says that even if these words are in the scriptures one cannot understand them by one’s self, one can only understand them from the Ekantik Satpurush.  The teachings of satpurushes like Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj have led countless to attain bliss, and continue to do so even today. 
Blessings that those that read this supreme scripture experience inner-peace, and that those that read it time and time again acquire great fervour for Atma-Paramatma and attain Akshardham.
#With Blessings
^Shastri Narayanswarupdas’
^Jay Swaminarayan

Out of compassion Bhagwan Swaminarayan has delivered discourses for the ultimate liberation of spiritual aspirants. Upon his command, the paramhansas compiled the Vachanamrut. It is the essence of all shastras. The Vachanamrut clearly propounds the concepts of Ekantik Dharma and becoming like Akshar and offering devotion to Parabrahma Purushottam.
Any aspirant seeking to become successful in his spiritual endeavours will find guidance from the Vachanamrut. 21083.t:
Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s first spiritual successor, Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami Maharaj was born in Bhadra in the Jamnagar district of Gujarat, on Sharad Punam, VS 1841 (17 October 1785). His father’s name was Bholanath and mother’s name was Sakarba. His childhood name was Mulji Bhakta.
From childhood, divinity sprung forth in every one of Mulji’s actions. Everyone was always surprised with his oneness with Bhagwan Swaminarayan. Mulji would explain deep philosophical and spiritual principles in a clear and easy manner, using incidents taking place around him as a base for practical application. 
On Posh Sud Punam, VS 1866 in the village of Dabhan, Bhagwan Swaminarayan initiated Mulji Bhakta in to sadhu-fold, naming him Gunatitanand Swami, and revealed his greatness as the incarnation of Akshar Brahma. Gunatitanand Swami was an ideal sadhu displaying saintly qualities such as austerity, selfless service, self-control, tolerance, forgiveness, following commands, and many more. 
In Samvat 1877, in Panchala, Bhagwan Swaminarayan applied a tilak to Gunatitanand Swami’s forehead. Speaking about Swami’s glory, he said, “There is no God like me and there no sadhu like him.” During many such incidents, Bhagwan Swaminarayan would sign the praises his unique sevak and successor, Gunatitanand Swami.
In VS 1884, Bhagwan Swaminarayan appointed Gunatitanand Swami as the mahant of Junagadh mandir and gave him the responsibility for the welfare of the Sorath region and its haribhaktos. As per Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s wish, Gunatitanand Swami served as the mahant for 40 years and revealed the full glory of Bhagwan Swaminarayan as supreme God through his continuous spiritual discourses. His spiritual discourses were later compiled in a work that is popularly known today as Swamini Vato. 
After returning to his Akshardham in Samvat 1886, Bhagwan Swaminarayan gave darshan to Gunatitanand Swami in divine form. He promised to remain ever-present through Swami.
Gunatitanand Swami transformed the lives and eradicated the internal deficiencies of people walking on a path of immorality and uplifted them to a higher spiritual level. There were 300 sadhus living in Junagadh under Swami’s instruction. He guided these sadhus in the way of saintliness (sadhuta), which prompted the term ‘Junagadhi Jogini Reet’ (the Junagadh Jogi’s way) to be coined.
When leaving Junagadh for the final time before returning to Akshardham, he acknowledged that he would remain ever-present through Pragji Bhakta of Mahuva (Bhagatji Maharaj). While travelling, he reached the town of Gondal and on Aso Sud 13, VS 1924 (11 October 1867) he left his mortal body of his own accord. A shrine was constructed on the land where Gunatitanad Swami’s final rites were performed. This shrine is famously known within the sampraday as the Akshar Deri and attracts hundreds of thousands of devotees and pilgrim-goers.

21084.t:
Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s second spiritual successor, Brahmaswarup Bhagatji Maharaj, was born in Mahuva, in Gujarat’s Bhavnagar district, on Fagan Sud Punam, VS 1885 (20 March 1829). His father’s name was Govindbhai Mandaliya and mother’s name was Maluba. His childhood name was Pragji Bhakta. 
From a young age, Pragji Bhakta lived an ideal life, steeped in devotion to God. Though a householder, he lived the life of a sadhu. He kept the company of Sadguru Gopalanand Swami for 13 years and Aksharbrahma Gunatitanand Swami for 15 years. Despite being the form of Akshar Brahman himself, he lived the life of an ideal spiritual aspirant, setting an example for all. Through association of Gunatitanand Swami, he imbibed Ekantik Dharma’s ideals of dharma, gnan, vairagya and bhakti in his life, attained the ultimate state of brahma stithi. Yet, he tolerated countless abuse and insults in propagating the true glory of Gunatitanand Swami. 
He instilled within the hearts of many souls the true glory of Akshar Purushottam, and raised them to his own elevated spiritual state. Overwhelmed by his divinity, many respectfully called him ‘Bhagatji Maharaj’. 
He imparted Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s upasana to the young and learned Shastri Yagnapurushdas. Having strengthened the knowledge of the Akshar Purushottam Upasana, he commanded Shastri Yagnapurushdas to propagate these principles across the world. On Kartik Sud 13, VS 1954 (7 November 1897) in Mahuva, Bhagatji Maharaj left his mortal body.

21085.t:
Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s third spiritual successor, Brahmaswarup Shastriji Maharaj’s birth took place in Mahelav, in the Anand district, on Vasant Panchmi VS 1921 (31 January 1865). His parent’s Dhoribhai and Hetba named him Dungar Bhakta. 
When playing with friends, young Dungar Bhakta would devotedly make Mandirs out of sand – thus displaying his life’s mission from a young age. At the age of 18, he renounced worldly life to join Sadguru Vignanand Swami; he was initiated by Acharya Viharilalji Maharaj and named Yagnapurushdas. His saintliness, scholarliness, intelligence and administrative prowess were unparalleled in the entire sampraday.
He kept faith and patience in the face of countless obstacles and insults he met in preaching these teachings. He responded to his opponents with forgiveness. In 1907, he began the Bochasanwasi Shri Akshar-Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) by installing the first murtis of Akshar Purushottam in Bochasan; which was followed by similar grand mandirs in Sarangpur, Gondal, Atladara and Gadhada. By bringing together Brahma and Parabrahma, and revealing the true and present form of this principle, he forever opened the gates of salvation countless jivas.
On 21 May 1950, in Amdavad, Shastriji Maharaj, as he came to be known, appointed Shastri Narayanswarupdas in his position as the president of BAPS, and handed the reins of Satsang to Yogiji Maharaj. Shastriji Maharaj passed away to Akshardham, aged 86, on Vaishakh Sud 4, VS 2007 (10 May 1951) in Sarangpur.

21086.t:
Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s fourth spiritual successor, Brahmaswarup Yogiji Maharaj was born in Dhari, in the Bhavnagar district, on Vaishakh Vad 12, VS 1948 (23 May 1892). His father’s name was Devchandbhai and mother’s name was Puribai. His childhood name was Jina Bhakta.
Since childhood, Jina Bhakta’s life was immersed in devotion and meditation. At the age of 19, he was initiated as Sadhu Jnanjivandas by Shripatiprasadji Maharaj of Vadtal. A life of selfless service and singular devotion to God combined with his enlightened spiritual state meant that after just one year everyone affectionately and respectfully called him ‘Yogi’. Thereafter, leaving Junagadh, he joined Shastriji Maharaj in propagating the Akshar Purushottam philosophy.
He was embodiment of tolerance, selfless service, saintliness and love. Having stayed in Gondal as Mahant for many years, he made a unique contribution to the development of Gondal Mandir. With his foresight he established activities for children, youth, regular weekly Satsang assemblies, reading of Vachanamrut and Swamini Vato, youth competitions, Satsang exams etc. 
Outside India, in Africa and England, he built Akshar Purushottam Mandir’s in order to keep Hindu traditions and devotion flourishing and put Hinduism and BAPS Sanstha on a global platform. He also set a new tradition in inspiring educated youths to renounce the world and become Sadhus.
‘Pramukh Swami is my everything…’ – with these words, Yogiji Maharaj handed over his spiritual responsibilities to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, and on Posh Vad Ekadashi, VS 2027 (23 January 1971), in Mumbai, reverted to Akshardham.

21087.t:
Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s fifth spiritual successor, Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj was born in Chansad in the Baroda district of Gujarat, on Magshar Sud 8, VS 1978 (7 December 1921). His father’s name was Motibhai and mother’s name was Diwaliba. His childhood name was Shantilal.
A life naturally detached from the world and devoted to God even in his childhood, Shantilal at the age of 18 renounced home based purely on a letter from Shastriji Maharaj, and was initiated as Sadhu and named Narayanswarupdas. As a sadhu, Narayanswarupdas served according to the inner wishes of his guru and earned his blessings.
After Shastriji Maharaj made him the President of the BAPS Sanstha at the tender age of 28, everyone lovingly referred to him as Pramukh Swami. Thereafter, his incomparable s	aintliness and immense efforts, has nurtured the unique growth of the organisation. Under his leadership, the BAPS Sanstha has initiated many social and spiritual activities. Having toured more than 17,000 villages, responded to more than 250,000 letters, and personally met millions of people, he has touched the lives of countless souls. Furthermore, with more than 1000 sadhus, over 1000 mandirs, Akshardham Monuments, and grand cultural festivals, he has raised the awareness of Indian culture throughout the world. 
Having blessed innumerable souls with God’s grace and presence, and having given the spiritual succession to Mahant Swami Maharaj, on Shravan Sud 10, VS 2072 (13 August 2016), in Sarangpur, he returned to Akshardham.

21088.t:
Bhagwan Swaminarayan’s sixth spiritual successor, Pragat Brahmaswarup Mahant Swami Maharaj was born in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh on Bhadarva Vad 9, VS 2089 (13 September 1933). His parents Manibhai and Dahiben name him Vinubhai.
A quiet and peaceful child, his tranquil and thoughtful nature meant everyone was naturally attracted to him. Father Manibhai, together with his family, would frequently visit his original home in Anand, Gujarat, where he came into contact with Brahmaswarup Yogiji Maharaj. Soon after, in Gadhada in 1961, Yogiji Maharaj initiated him as a Sadhu and named him Sadhu Keshavjivandas. Thereafter he was made ‘Mahant’ of newly initiated Sadhus – hence his name ‘Mahant Swami’. 
His life was an embodiment of penance, fasting, self-control, devotion, saintliness, humility and countless other such qualities combined with selfless service, he has pleased and earned the grace of Brahmaswarup Yogiji Maharaj and Brahmaswarup Pramukh Swami Maharaj. As per the wishes of his Guru, he has taken a unique and leading role in all the Sanstha’s activities whilst still remaining humble. He has made a unique contribution to the advancement of the organisation. He has inspired millions with his spiritual advice, and his God-centred and saintly life has and continues to motivate Sadhus, devotees, and countless well wishers. 
The leader of all of BAPS Sanstha’s social and spiritual activities, he continues to inspire innumerable souls on the spiritual path, as revealed by Bhagwan Swaminarayan.
